Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 1–2:

Surat an-Nisa' (The Women) – Madaniyyah (Medinan) ﷽

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul﴾ meaning Adam, peace be upon him, ﴿and created from it its mate﴾ meaning Eve, ﴿and dispersed from both of them﴾ spread and made to appear, ﴿many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another﴾ meaning, you ask one another by Him. The people of Kufa read it with the "s" (sin) lightened, by omitting one of the two "t"s, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and do not cooperate [tatawanu]﴾. ﴿And the wombs [al-arham]﴾ is the reading of the majority with the accusative, meaning: and fear the wombs, lest you sever them. Hamzah read it in the genitive, meaning: by Him and by the wombs, as one says: "I ask you by Allah and by the ties of kinship." The first reading is more eloquent, because the Arabs hardly coordinate an apparent noun with a pronoun unless they repeat the preposition, as in "I passed by him and by Zayd." Yet it is permissible, though rare. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Watchful over you﴾ meaning: Guardian.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And give the orphans their property﴾ Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning a man from Ghatafan who had much wealth belonging to a nephew of his, an orphan. When the orphan reached maturity he demanded the property, but his paternal uncle refused him. They brought their dispute before the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed. When the uncle heard it he said: "We obey Allah and we obey the Messenger; we seek refuge in Allah from the great sin," and he handed over his property to him. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul and obeys his Lord in this manner, Allah will make his abode [paradise] lawful for him," meaning: his Paradise. When the young man received his property, he spent it in the way of Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The reward has been secured and the burden remains." They said: "How does the burden remain?" He said: "The reward is secured for the boy, and the burden remains upon his father." [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 136, without an isnad, attributing it to al-Kalbi and Muqatil. See also: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5/8; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 3/159.]]

His saying, "And give," is an address to the guardians and executors. "Al-yatama" is the plural of "yatim," and the yatim is the name for a young person who has neither father nor grandfather. Property is only handed over to them after they reach maturity, and here He called them "yatama" in the sense that they had been orphans.

﴿And do not substitute [tatabaddalu]﴾ meaning: do not exchange, ﴿the bad [al-khabith] for the good [al-tayyib]﴾ meaning: their property, which is unlawful for you, for the lawful from your own wealth. They differed concerning this substitution. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri and al-Suddi said: The guardians of orphans would take the good from the orphan's property and put in its place the inferior, so one of them might take a fat sheep from the orphan's property and put in its place a lean one, and take a good dirham and put in its place a counterfeit one, saying: "A dirham for a dirham." They were forbidden from this.

It was also said: The people of the Jahiliyyah did not give inheritance to women and children, and the eldest would take the inheritance. So his share of the inheritance is good, while what he takes from the orphan is bad. Mujahid said: Do not hasten to take unlawful provision before lawful provision comes to you.

﴿And do not consume their property along with your property [ila amwalikum]﴾ meaning: together with your property, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Who are my helpers in the way of Allah? [ila Allah]﴾ meaning: together with Allah. ﴿Indeed, that is a great sin [huban kabiran]﴾ meaning: a great wrong.

[ila Allah]﴾ meaning: together with Allah. ﴿Indeed, that is a great sin [huban kabiran]﴾ meaning: a great wrong.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans, then marry from among women what seems good to you, two, three, or four﴾, to the end of the verse. The scholars differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is, "If you fear, O guardians of orphans, that you will not be equitable toward them when you marry them, then marry other women who are not orphans, two, three, or four."

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr used to narrate that he asked A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, about ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans, then marry from among women﴾. She said: "It refers to the orphan girl who is in the care of her guardian, who desires her beauty and her wealth, and wants to marry her while giving her less than the customary bridal payment given to women like her. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they gave them full bridal payment, and they were commanded to marry other women besides them." A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Then the people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for a ruling, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning them﴾, up to His saying, ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾."[1] Thus Allah the Exalted explained in this verse that when the orphan girl had beauty or wealth, they desired to marry her without giving her the customary full bridal payment; and when she was disliked for her lack of wealth and beauty, they left her and sought other women. He said: "Just as they leave her when they have no desire for her, they have no right to marry her when they desire her, unless they give her the fullest bridal payment and give her what is due to her."

Al-Hasan said: A man from the people of Medina would have orphans in his care, among whom was one he was permitted to marry. He would marry her for the sake of her wealth, though she did not please him, out of aversion to letting a stranger enter and share in her property. Then he would treat her badly and wait for her to die so that he could inherit from her. Allah the Exalted condemned that, and Allah revealed this verse.

Ikrimah said: A man of Quraysh would marry ten or more women. When he was unable to support his wives, he would turn to the property of the orphan in his care and spend it. So it was said to them: "Do not exceed four, lest you be driven to take the wealth of orphans." This is the narration of Tawus from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Some of them said: They were scrupulous about the property of orphans but lax regarding women. They would marry as many as they wished, and sometimes they were just and sometimes they were not. Then, when Allah the Exalted revealed concerning the property of orphans, ﴿And give the orphans their property﴾, He revealed this verse: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans﴾, meaning: just as you feared that you would not be just toward orphans, so too fear that you will not be just toward women. So do not marry more than you can fulfill their rights, because women in their weakness are like orphans. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi.[2] Then He permitted marrying up to four, saying: ﴿So marry from among women what seems good to you, two, three, or four. But if you fear that you will not be just﴾ toward them, ﴿then one﴾.

Mujahid said: Its meaning is: if you are scrupulous about guardianship of orphans and their property out of faith, then be likewise scrupulous about adultery. So marry lawful women in a good marriage, and then He specified a number for them, whereas they used to marry as many as they wished without any limit. As for His saying, ﴿So marry from among women what seems good to you﴾, the word "what" (ma) means "whoever" (man), as in His saying: ﴿By the sky and He who built it﴾ [al-Shams: 5], meaning "and He who built it," and His saying: ﴿Pharaoh said: And what is the Lord of the worlds?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 23]. The Arabs use "man" and "ma" each in place of the other, as in His saying: ﴿Among them is one who walks on his belly, and among them is one who walks on two legs﴾ [al-Nur: 45]. And "tayyaba" means: lawful for you from among women, two, three, or four. These numbers are formed as derivatives of two, three, and four, which is why they do not take nunation (tanwin). The "wa" (and) here means "aw" (or), indicating choice, as in His saying: ﴿That you stand before Allah in pairs and singly﴾ [Saba': 46], and: ﴿Possessors of wings, two, three, or four﴾ [Fatir: 1]. There is consensus that no one among this community may marry more than four wives. The allowance of more was among the special privileges of the Prophet ﷺ, and no one from the community shares it with him.

It is narrated that Qays ibn al-Harith had eight wives. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Divorce four and keep four." He said: "So I began saying to the wife who had not borne children, 'O so-and-so, turn away,' and to the one who had borne children, 'O so-and-so, come near.'"[3] It is also narrated that Ghaylan ibn Salamah al-Thaqafi embraced Islam while he had ten wives, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Keep four and separate from the rest of them."[4]

If a free man marries four free women, it is permitted. As for a slave, according to most scholars, he may not marry more than two women. Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ahmad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Sufyan informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, mawla of Abu Talhah, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abd Allah ibn Utbah, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "A slave may marry two women and divorce with two divorces, and a slave woman observes a waiting period of two menstrual cycles, or if she does not menstruate, two months or a month and a half."[5] Rabi'ah said: It is permissible for a slave to marry four women, like a free man.

﴿If you fear﴾ means "if you dread," and it was said: "if you know." ﴿That you will not be just﴾ among the four wives. ﴿Then one﴾ means: then marry one. Abu Ja'far read ﴿then one﴾ with a nominative ending (wahidatun). ﴿Or what your right hands possess﴾, meaning concubines, because no rights are binding upon them as are binding upon free women; they have no fixed turn, and there is no limit to their number. The mention of "right hands" is an explanation; its implied sense is "or what you possess." Some of the scholars of meanings said: "Or what your right hands possess" means what your oath can take effect upon, taking "right hand" as the oath of swearing, not the limb. ﴿That is closer﴾, meaning nearer, ﴿to your not being unjust﴾, meaning: that you not deviate or incline. It is said: "a balance that is 'a'il" meaning one that is unjust and inclined. This is the view of most exegetes. Mujahid said: "that you not go astray." Al-Farra' said: "that you not transgress what Allah has imposed upon you." The root of "awl" is transgression, and from it comes "awl al-fara'id" (the increase in the shares in inheritance). Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "that your dependents not increase." But no one else has said this; what is said regarding the increase of dependents is: "a'ala yu'ilu i'alatan," when his dependents increase. Abu Hatim said: "Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, was more knowledgeable in the language of the Arabs than us, and perhaps this is a dialect." It is said this is the dialect of Himyar. Talhah ibn Musarrif read ﴿"That you not be burdened"﴾ (an tu'ilu), and this serves as proof for the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah's pleasure be upon him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 4:

﴿And give the women their dowries as a free gift﴾. Al-Kalbi and Mujahid said: this address is to the guardians (awliya'). That is because the guardian of a woman, when he married her off, if she was among his kin, would not give her any part of her dowry, whether little or much; and if her husband was a stranger, they would carry her to him on a camel and would give her nothing of her dowry other than that. So Allah forbade them from this and commanded them to deliver the right to its people.

[Al-Hadrami said: the guardians of women used to give this one his sister on condition that the other gave him his sister, and there was no dowry between them. So they were forbidden from this and commanded to specify the dowry in the marriage contract. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "forbade shighar".

Shighar is that a man marries his daughter on condition that the other man marries his daughter to him, and there is no dowry between them.] [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Nikah, chapter on Shighar: 9/162, and Muslim in Nikah, chapter on the prohibition and invalidity of shighar, no. (1415): 2/1034, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/97.]]

Others said: the address is to the husbands, who were commanded to give their wives the dowry, and this is more sound, because the address before this was with those who marry. The sadaqat are the dowries, singular sadaqah. ﴿Nihlah﴾: Qatadah said: an obligation. Ibn Juraij said: a specified obligation. Abu Ubaydah said: nihlah is only something specified and known. Al-Kalbi said: a gift and a present. Abu Ubaydah said: from good pleasure of the soul. Al-Zajjaj said: as a religious duty.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us, al-Layth informed us, Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me, from Abu al-Khayr, from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The most deserving of conditions to be fulfilled are those by which you made lawful the private parts." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Shurut, chapter on conditions regarding the dowry at the marriage contract: 5/323, and also in Nikah, and Muslim in Nikah, chapter on fulfilling conditions in marriage, no. (1418): 2/1035-1036, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/53.]]

﴿But if they give you something of it willingly﴾: meaning, if their souls are pleased to give up some of that and they grant it to you. The verb was shifted from the souls to their owners, so the soul became a specification (tamyiz), and for this reason "nafs" is singular, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿and his heart constricted (wa-dhaqa bihim dharʻan)﴾ [Hud: 77], [al-Ankabut: 33], "and her eye is cooled (wa-qarri 'aynan)" [Maryam: 26]. It was also said: its wording is singular while its meaning is plural. ﴿Then consume it with satisfaction and pleasure﴾: wholesome and good. It is said hana'a fi al-ta'am yahna'u, with fath of the nun in the past tense and kasr in the non-past. It was also said: al-hana' is what is good and easy to swallow, not troubled by anything; and al-mari' is what has a praiseworthy outcome, fully digested, causing no harm. Abu Ja'far recited ﴿hani'an mari'an﴾ with shaddah on the ya' in both without hamz, and likewise "bari'" , "bari'un", "bari'an" and "kahayyah"; and the others pronounce them with hamz.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support﴾. The scholars differed concerning these "foolish" ones (sufaha', sing. safih, "one who is foolish or lacking in sound judgment"). A group said: they are the women. Al-Dahhak said: women are among the most foolish of the foolish. Mujahid said: He forbade men to give women their property, and they are foolish, whether they are wives, daughters, or mothers. Others said: they are the children. Al-Zuhri said: It means, do not give your foolish child your property, which is your support after Allah, the Exalted, lest he ruin it. Some of them said: they are the women and the children. Al-Hasan said: it is your foolish wife and your foolish son. Ibn 'Abbas said: Do not intend your property, which Allah has entrusted to you and made for you a livelihood, and then give it to your wife or your sons, so that they become the ones who support you, and then you look to what is in their hands. Rather, keep your property and put it in order, and be the one who spends on them for their provision and their maintenance. Al-Kalbi said: If a man knows that his wife is foolish and corrupting, and that his son is foolish and corrupting, then he should not allow either of them to have authority over his property so that they ruin it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrimah said: It refers to the property of the orphan that is in your charge. It means: do not hand it over to him, but spend on him until he reaches maturity. He attributed the property to the guardians, saying ﴿your property﴾, because they are its managers and those who take charge of it.

The foolish person to whom it is not permissible for his guardian to give his property is the one who deserves to be placed under restraint (hajr), namely one who is wasteful with his property or corrupt in his religion. So He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿And do not give the foolish﴾, that is, the ignorant of the place of right, ﴿your property which Allah has made for you a means of support﴾.

Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿qiyaman﴾ without an alif, while the others read ﴿qiyaman﴾ (with an alif), and its origin is qiwaman, so the waw was changed to ya' because of the kasra before it. It means the mainstay of the matter and that by which the matter is sustained. Here it means the means of support of your living by which you sustain yourselves. Al-Dahhak said: by it the Hajj, jihad and acts of righteousness are established, and by it the necks are freed from the Fire.

﴿And provide for them therein﴾, that is: feed them, ﴿and clothe them﴾ for those whose provision and maintenance are obligatory upon you. He said ﴿therein﴾ and did not say ﴿from it﴾, because He intended: make for them a provision within it. Indeed, provision from Allah is a gift without limit, while provision from the servants is a periodic, limited payment.

﴿And speak to them a kind word﴾, a good promise. Ata' said: If I profit, I will give you, and if I gain, I will make a share for you. It was also said: it is supplication. Ibn Zayd said: If he is not one whose maintenance is obligatory upon you, then say to him: may Allah grant you and us well-being, may Allah bless you. It was also said: a gentle word by which their souls are made content.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 6 (part 1 of 2):

The Exalted said: ﴿And test the orphans﴾ to the end of the verse. It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Rifa'ah and his paternal uncle. The reason was that Rifa'ah died and left behind his son Thabit, who was young. His uncle came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "My nephew is an orphan in my care. What is lawful for me from his property, and when should I hand over his property to him?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 137, without an isnad. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/437; al-Qurtubi: 5/34. Ibn Hajar mentioned it in similar terms in al-Isabah: 1/387 and said: "This is mursal; its narrators are trustworthy."]] ﴿And test the orphans﴾: examine them regarding their intellects, their religious conduct, and their keeping of their property. ﴿Until, when they reach marriageable age﴾: that is, the age of men and women. ﴿Then if you perceive﴾: that is, if you see, ﴿in them maturity of judgment﴾. The exegetes said: that is, intellect and righteousness in religion, preservation of property, and knowledge of what will set it right. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and al-Sha'bi said: he should not hand over his property to him, even if he is an old man, until his maturity has become evident to him.

The testing varies according to their conditions. If the orphan is one who engages in trade in the market, the guardian gives him a small amount of property and observes how he conducts himself. If he is one who does not engage in trade in the market, he is tested in the expenditure of his household, in the provision for his slaves and hired workers. A woman is tested in the affairs of her household, the safekeeping of her goods, her spinning and the management of her spinning. When he sees good management and conduct in affairs repeatedly, such that his maturity is dominant in the heart, he hands over the property to him.

Know that Allah the Exalted made the removal of restriction (hajr) from the minor and the permissibility of handing over property to him dependent on two things: puberty (bulugh) and maturity (rushd). Puberty occurs through one of ﴿four things﴾ [[In A: "al-ashya' al-arba'ah."]]: two of which are shared by men and women, and two of which are specific to women.

As for what is shared by men and women, one is age, and the second is ihtilam (wet dreams/seminal emission). As for age: when the child completes fifteen years, he is judged to have reached puberty, whether boy or girl, based on what Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "I was presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uhud when I was fourteen years old, and he rejected me. Then I was presented to him on the day of the Trench when I was fifteen years old, and he permitted me." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Shahadat, chapter on the puberty of children and their testimony: 5/276; and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the explanation of the age of puberty, no. (1868): 3/1490.]] Nafi' said: "I related this hadith to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and he said: 'This is the dividing line between the fighting men and the offspring,' and he wrote that the one who is fifteen should be assigned a stipend among the fighters, and whoever has not reached it is among the offspring." This is the view of the majority of scholars.

Abu Hanifah, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: the puberty of a girl is by completing seventeen years, and the puberty of a boy is by completing eighteen years.

As for ihtilam, we mean by it the emission of semen, whether by wet dream, by intercourse, or otherwise. If this is found after completing nine years, from either of them, he is judged to have reached puberty, based on the words of the Exalted: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission﴾. The Prophet ﷺ also said to Mu'adh regarding the jizyah when he sent him to Yemen: "Take from every adult male (halim) one dinar." [[A portion of a hadith narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Zakat, chapter on the zakat of livestock: 2/195; al-Tirmidhi in al-Zakat, chapter on what has come concerning the zakat of cattle: 3/257, and said: "This is a hasan hadith." Then he said: "Some of them narrated this hadith from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Masruq... and this is more authentic." Also narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Zakat, chapter on the zakat of cattle: 5/26; al-Daraqutni: 2/102; al-Hakim: 1/398, who authenticated it on the condition of the two Shaykhs and al-Dhahabi agreed; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/230, 233; Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/19. See what Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir: 4/122.]]

As for growth of hair (al-inbat), meaning the growth of coarse hair around the private parts, it is a sign of puberty in the children of polytheists, based on what was narrated from Atiyyah al-Qurazi who said: "I was among the captives of Banu Qurayzah. They used to examine us, and whoever had grown hair was killed, and whoever had not grown hair was not killed. I was among those who had not grown hair." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Hudud, chapter on a boy who incurs a hadd penalty: 6/233; al-Tirmidhi in al-Siyar, chapter on what has come concerning oaths: 5/208, and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; al-Nasa'i in Qat' al-Sariq, chapter on amputation on a journey: 8/92; Ibn Majah in al-Hudud, chapter on one upon whom the hadd is not obligatory, no. (2541): 2/849; al-Darimi in al-Siyar, chapter on when a child's hadd is execution: 2/223; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/310, 5/312; and Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an, p. 360.]]

Is that considered puberty for the children of Muslims? There are two opinions. One is that it is puberty, as it is for the children of disbelievers. The second is that it is not puberty, because the births of Muslims can be ascertained by referring to their fathers, whereas the births of disbelievers cannot be ascertained, and their fathers' statements about them are not accepted because of their disbelief. Therefore, growth of hair, which is the sign of puberty, was made to count as puberty in their case.

As for what is specific to women: menstruation and pregnancy. If a woman menstruates after completing nine years, she is judged to have reached puberty. Likewise, if she gives birth, she is judged to have reached puberty before delivery by six months, because that is the minimum period of pregnancy.

As for maturity (rushd): it is that he be upright in his religion and his property. Uprightness in religion is that he refrain from grave sins and acts of disobedience that remove probity ('adalah). Uprightness in property is that he not be a squanderer (mubadhdhir). Squandering (tabdhir) is that he spends his property on what has no worldly praise and no otherworldly reward, or that he does not handle it well, so that he is cheated in sales. If the child reaches puberty while corrupt in his religion and not righteous in his property, the restriction upon him remains, his property is not handed over to him, and his disposals are not valid.

According to Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him: if he is righteous in his property, the restriction is removed from him even if he is corrupt in his religion. And if he is corrupt in his property, he said: the property is not handed over to him until he reaches twenty-five years, though his disposals are valid before that. The Qur'an is a proof for the one who maintains the restriction upon him, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Until, when they reach marriageable age, then if you perceive in them maturity of judgment, hand over to them their property﴾. He commanded handing over property to them after puberty and the perception of maturity. The corrupt person is not mature, and after reaching twenty-five years, while he is corrupting his property, he is by consensus not mature. Therefore it is necessary that it is not permissible to hand over property to him, just as before reaching this age.

When he reaches puberty and maturity is perceived in him, the restriction is removed from him and property is handed over to him, whether a man or a woman, whether married or not.

According to Malik, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him: if she is a woman, property is not handed over to her until she marries. When she marries, it is handed over to her, but her disposals are not valid except with her husband's permission, unless she becomes old and has been tested.

If the child reaches maturity and the restriction is removed from him, then he becomes foolish again, it is considered: if he returns to squandering his property, he is placed under restriction. If he returns to corruption in his religion, there are two views: one is that the restriction is reimposed upon him, just as it is maintained upon him if he reached puberty in this condition. The second is that it is not reimposed, because the ruling for continuance is stronger than the ruling for initiation.

According to Abu Hanifah, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him: there is no restriction at all upon a free, sane, adult person. The evidence for establishing restriction from the consensus of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, is what was narrated from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father, that Abd Allah ibn Ja'far bought a salty land for sixty thousand dirhams. Ali said: "I will certainly go to Uthman and have you placed under restriction." Ibn Ja'far went to al-Zubayr and informed him of that. [Al-Zubayr said: "I am your partner in your sale." Then Ali came to Uthman and said: "Restrict this man."] [[Omitted in (b).]] Al-Zubayr said: "I am his partner." Uthman said: "How can I restrict a man in a sale in which al-Zubayr is his partner?" So this was an agreement among them on the permissibility of restriction, until al-Zubayr devised a means to avert it.

The Exalted said: ﴿And do not consume their property﴾ O guardians, ﴿wastefully﴾ without right, ﴿and hastily﴾, that is, by way of hurrying ﴿lest they grow up﴾. ﴿Lest﴾ is in the accusative position. That is: do not hasten their maturity and their rushd, fearing that they will reach adulthood and you will be obliged to hand their property over to them. Then He explained what is lawful for them from their property, saying: ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain﴾, that is, let him refrain from the orphan's property, so that he takes not even a little or a lot from it. Abstinence (ʿiffah) is refraining from what is not lawful. ﴿And whoever is poor﴾, needy of the orphan's property, while he guards it and looks after it, ﴿let him consume it justly﴾ (bil-ma'ruf). ٧٨/ب

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us: Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn Umar al-Sijzi informed us: the Imam Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Dasah al-Tammar informed us: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani informed us: Humayd ibn Mas'adah informed us, that Khalid ibn al-Harith related to them: Husayn, that is al-Mu'allim, informed us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I am poor and I have nothing, and I have an orphan?" He said: "Eat from the property of your orphan without extravagance, without hastening, and without accumulating wealth for yourself." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Wasaya, chapter on what the guardian of an orphan may take from the orphan's property: 4/151-152; al-Nasa'i in al-Wasaya, chapter on what the executor may take from the orphan's property when he takes charge of it: 6/256; Ibn Majah in al-Wasaya, chapter on His saying: "And whoever is poor, let him eat in a reasonable manner," no. (2718): 2/907. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/305. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar attributed it also to Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn al-Jarud and Ibn Abi Hatim, and said: its isnad is strong. See Fath al-Bari: 8/241.]]

They differed as to whether he is obliged to repay it. Some of them held that he repays it when he becomes well-off, and this is the meaning of His saying ﴿let him consume it justly﴾; so the ma'ruf is a loan, that is, he borrows from the orphan's property when he needs it, and when he becomes well-off he repays it. This is the view of Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I have placed myself with regard to the property of Allah the Exalted in the position of the orphan's property: if I am rich I abstain, and if I am in need I eat justly, and when I become well-off I repay." [[Narrated by Abu Yusuf in al-Kharaj, pp. 39, 127. Ibn Hajar said: it was narrated by Ibn Sa'd, Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Tabari, through the narration of Isra'il and Sufyan, both from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib who said... And Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated it from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: Umar said to me... See: al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 39.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: he does not eat it except when compelled to, just as one is compelled to eat carrion.

Some people said: there is no repayment obligation upon him.

Then they differed about the manner of this eating in accordance with what is ma'ruf. Ata' and Ikrimah said: he eats with the tips of his fingers, does not waste, and does not clothe himself from it; he does not wear cotton or fine garments, but only what stills hunger and covers nakedness.

Al-Hasan and a group said: he eats from the fruit of his date palms and the milk of his livestock in a reasonable manner, and there is no repayment obligation upon him. As for gold and silver, no; if he takes anything of them, he returns it.

Al-Kalbi said: the ma'ruf is riding the mount and being served by the servant, and it is not permissible for him to eat anything of his property.

Al-Sarakhsi, Abu al-Hasan, informed us; Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, that he said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: "I have an orphan, and he has camels. Am I permitted to drink from the milk of his camels?" He said: "If you are seeking the strayed camels of his, and you apply tar to their mange, and you repair their trough, and you water them on the day they come to water, then drink, without harming their offspring and without excessive milking."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 7/588. Ibn Hajar attributed it to 'Abd al-Razzaq, through the narration of Yahya ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and said: al-Tabari narrated it through his chain, and al-Tha'labi and al-Wahidi through another route from al-Qasim; al-Baghawi narrated it through the route of Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim, and it is in the Muwatta'. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. (39).]]

Some of them said: "The well-known view is that he may take from all of his property an amount equal to his labour and the wage of his work, and there is no obligation of repayment upon him. This is the view of 'A'ishah and a group of the people of knowledge."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when you hand over to them their property, then call witnesses over them.﴾ This is a command of guidance, not an obligation. It commands the guardian to call witnesses to the handing over of the property to the orphan after he has reached maturity, so that suspicion is removed from him and disputes are cut off. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾: Accounting, Recompensing and Witnessing.

The Lord's words: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave behind﴾, to the end of the verse. It was revealed concerning Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari. He died and left a wife called Umm Kujjah and three daughters by her. Two men, who were the paternal cousins of the deceased and his executors, Suwayd and Arfajah, came forward and took his property and gave nothing to his wife or his daughters. In the Jahiliyyah they did not give inheritance to women or to young children, even if the child was a boy. They gave inheritance only to men, and they said: "We give only to one who fights and seizes the spoils." Then Umm Kujjah came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Aws ibn Thabit died and left me with daughters, and I am his wife. I have nothing with which to support them. Their father left good property, and it is in the hands of Suwayd and Arfajah. They have given neither me nor my daughters anything, and the girls are in my custody. They are not fed and they are not given drink." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the two men, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, her child does not ride a horse, does not carry a burden, and does not strike an enemy." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿For men﴾, meaning: for the males among the deceased's offspring and his relatives, ﴿a share﴾, meaning a portion, ﴿of what the parents and the close relatives leave behind﴾ from the inheritance. ﴿And for women﴾, meaning the females among them, ﴿a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave behind, whether it is little﴾, meaning of the property, ﴿or much﴾ of it, ﴿a share ordained﴾. It is put in the accusative as an absolute object. It was also said: He made this a share and thus established inheritance for them, but He did not specify how much it was. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Suwayd and Arfajah: "Do not divide anything from the property of Aws ibn Thabit, for Allah, the Exalted, has made a share for his daughters from what he left, but He has not specified how much it is, until I see what is revealed concerning them." Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾. When this was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to Suwayd and Arfajah: "Give Umm Kujjah an eighth of what he left, and to his daughters two-thirds, and the remainder of the property is for you two." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 7/598. Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Isabah, in the biography of Umm Kujjah: 8/284, and said: Abu Nu'aym and Abu Musa narrated it through his chain, then through the narration of Sufyan from Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil from Jabir, who said... And he said: its narrator from Sufyan is Ibrahim ibn Harasa, who is weak. Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal contradicted him, narrating from Abdullah ibn Muhammad from Jabir, and Abu Dawud narrated it through his chain. And he said in al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 39: al-Tha'labi mentioned it, then al-Baghawi, without a chain; and al-Wahidi said: "The exegetes said..." And it is mentioned. See also: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi pp. 137–138; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/438–439.]].

The Lord's words: ﴿And when the division is attended by close relatives﴾, meaning the division of inheritances, ﴿and the orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾, meaning give them a portion of the property before the division, ﴿and speak to them kind words﴾.

The scholars differed concerning the ruling of this verse. Some said: it has been abrogated (mansukhah). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Dahhak said: this was before the verse of inheritance. When the verse of inheritance was revealed, it assigned inheritances to their rightful people, and it abrogated this verse.

Others said: it is muhkamah (firm, not abrogated). This is the view of Ibn Abbas, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i and al-Zuhri. Mujahid said: it is obligatory upon the heirs, to the extent that their souls are content to give [[See the detailed discussion of these views in: Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/7 and what follows.]].

Al-Hasan said: they used to give the chest, the vessels, worn clothing, household goods, and whatever was shameful to divide.

If some of the heirs were children, the scholars differed. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and others said: if the heirs were adults, they gave them a portion; if they were minors, they excused themselves to them, so the guardian or executor would say: "I do not own this property; it belongs to the minors. If it were mine, I would have given you something. When they grow up, they will recognize your rights." This is the "kind speech."

Others said: that is a binding right in the property of minors and adults alike. If they were adults, they themselves gave them their share; if they were minors, their guardian gave it. Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated that Ubaidah al-Salmani divided the property of orphans, ordered a sheep to be slaughtered, and prepared food for the people of this verse, and said: "Had it not been for this verse, this would have come from my own property."

Qatadah said, relating from Yahya ibn Ya'mur: "Three muhkam Madinan verses have been abandoned by people: this verse, the verse of seeking permission: ﴿O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾ [al-Nur: 58], to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿O mankind, We created you from male and female﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13], to the end of the verse."

Some of them said, and this is the most preferred of the opinions: this is by way of recommendation (nadb) and desirability (istihbab), not by way of obligation (hatm) and requirement (ijab).
