Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 9:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And let those fear who, if they should leave behind them weak offspring, would be anxious for them.﴾ "Weak offspring" means young children, whom they fear for, lest they fall into poverty. This refers to a man whom death is approaching, and those present with him say: "Look to yourself, for your children and your heirs will not avail you anything. Advance something for yourself: free slaves, give charity, and give so-and-so such-and-such, and so-and-so such-and-such," until he has disposed of most of his wealth. So Allah the Exalted forbade them from this, and commanded them to tell him to look after his child, and not to increase his bequest beyond one-third, nor to leave his heirs in want. It is as if this speaker were the one making the bequest; he would be pleased that those present with him urged him to preserve his wealth for his child, and not leave them destitute in their weakness and helplessness.

Al-Kalbi (al-Kalbi) said: This address is to the guardians of orphans. It says: whoever has an orphan in his care, let him treat him well, and let him do for him in his right what must be done for his own offspring after him.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So let them fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ That is, justice. Al-sadid (sadid) means justice and the correct speech, which is that he should instruct him to give in charity an amount less than one-third and leave the remainder to his child.

The Lord's words: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly﴾. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed concerning a man from the Banu Ghatafan called Marthad ibn Zayd, who was guardian of his nephew's property while the nephew was a young orphan, and he consumed it. So Allah the Exalted revealed concerning him: ﴿Indeed, those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly﴾ [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 138, without an isnad. See also: Tafsir al-Qurtubi, 5/53.]], meaning unlawfully, without right. ﴿They only consume fire into their bellies﴾: this informs about their final destination, meaning their outcome will be like that. ﴿And they will burn in a blaze﴾. The recitation of the common readers (al-'Ammah, the majority of reciters) is with a fatha on the yā', meaning they will enter it. It is said: ṣaliya al-nāra yaṣlāhā ṣilan (he entered the fire and burned in it). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Except one who is destined for the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 163]. Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr read it with a ḍamma on the yā', meaning they will enter the Fire and be burned. Its parallel is the Lord's words: ﴿So We will cause him to burn in a Fire﴾ [al-Nisa': 30], and: ﴿I will cast him into Saqar﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 26].

In the hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw people who had lips like the lips of camels. One of their lips was cut off and placed on their nostrils, and the other on their bellies. The guardians of the Fire were stuffing them with the embers and stones of Hell. I said: 'O Jibril, who are these?' He said: 'Those who consume the properties of orphans unjustly.'" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 8/27, in a longer form. It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and mentioned by Ibn Kathir at the beginning of the tafsir of Surat al-Isra': 3/12, and al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/443. It contains Abu Harun al-'Abdi, who is 'Imarah ibn Juwayn (with a jim, diminutive form), known by his kunya. He is abandoned (matruk), and some have accused him of lying; he is a Shi'i of the fourth tabaqah. See: al-Taqrib: 2/49. It was also mentioned by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah: 1/250, with al-Rawd al-Unuf.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 11 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God enjoins you concerning your children: a male's share is like the share of two females﴾, etc. Know that inheritance in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance) was based on manhood and strength, so they would give inheritance only to men, excluding women and children. God nullified this with His saying: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾, etc. In the Jahiliyyah and at the beginning of Islam, inheritance was also based on alliance (al-muhalafah). God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those to whom your oaths have bound you, give them their share﴾ [al-Nisa': 33]. Then inheritance became based on emigration (hijrah). God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who believed but did not emigrate, you owe them no duty of protection until they emigrate﴾ [al-Anfal: 72]. All of that was abrogated (nusikha, from naskh, abrogation), and inheritance became based on one of three things: lineage (nasab), marriage (nikah), or patronage (wala'). By lineage is meant that kin inherit from one another, according to His saying: ﴿And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 6]. By marriage is meant that one of the spouses inherits from the other. By patronage is meant that the manumitter (al-mu'tiq) and his agnates ('asabat) inherit from the freed slave (al-mu'taq). With God's help, we will now mention a brief section on who inherits among the relatives and on the manner of distributing the inheritance among the heirs. We say:

When a deceased person dies leaving property, first his burial preparations are made, then his debts are paid, then his bequests are carried out, and whatever remains is divided among the heirs. The heirs (al-warathah) are of three categories: some inherit by fixed shares (al-fard), some inherit by agnatic relation (al-ta'sib), and some inherit by both together. Whoever inherits by marriage inherits only by fixed share, and whoever inherits by patronage inherits only by agnatic relation. As for those who inherit by blood relation, some inherit by fixed share, such as the daughters, the sisters, the mothers, the grandmothers, and the maternal siblings (awlad al-umm). Some inherit by agnatic relation, such as the sons, the brothers, the sons of brothers, the paternal uncles and their sons. And some inherit by both, such as the father, who inherits by agnatic relation when the deceased has no son. If the deceased has a son, the father inherits a sixth (al-sudus) by fixed share. If the deceased has a daughter, the father inherits a sixth by fixed share and takes the remainder after the daughter's share by agnatic relation. The same applies to the grandfather. The agnatic heir (sahib al-ta'sib) is the one who takes the entire estate when alone, and takes what is left over after the holders of fixed shares (ashab al-fara'id).

The total number of heirs is seventeen: ten men and seven women. Of the men: the son, the son's son however low he may be, the father, the grandfather (the father's father) however high he may be, the brother whether full, paternal, or maternal, the full or paternal nephew (the son of a brother) and his descendants however low, the paternal uncle, full or paternal, and their sons however low, the husband, and the male freed slave's patron (mawla al-'ita'q). Of the women: the daughter, the son's daughter however low she may be, the mother, the grandmother (the mother's mother or the father's mother), the sister whether full, paternal, or maternal, the wife, and the female freed slave's patron (mawlat al-'ita'q).

Six of these heirs are never excluded (lā yalhaquhum hajb al-hirman) by another: the two parents, the two children, and the two spouses, because there is no intermediary between them and the deceased.

The causes that prevent inheritance are four: difference of religion, slavery, killing, and uncertainty of death (ammiyy al-mawt).

By difference of religion we mean that a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim, and a Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever. This is based on what 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisa'i al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabi' informed us, al-Shafi'i informed us, Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ali ibn Husayn, from 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Usamah ibn Zayd, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Fara'id, chapter "A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor a disbeliever from a Muslim": 12/50; and Muslim in al-Fara'id, no. (1614): 3/1233; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/368.]]

As for disbelievers, some of them inherit from one another despite the differences of their religions, because all disbelief is one religion, according to His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve, some of them are allies of others﴾ [al-Anfal: 73].

Some scholars held that difference of religion within disbelief prevents inheritance, so that a Jew does not inherit from a Christian, nor a Christian from a Magian. This was the view of al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "People of two different religions do not inherit from one another."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Fara'id, chapter "Does a Muslim inherit from a disbeliever": 4/181; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Fara'id, chapter "What has come concerning the nullification of inheritance between a Muslim and a disbeliever": 6/289, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith, which we do not know except from the hadith of Ibn Abi Layla"; and Ibn Majah in al-Fara'id, chapter "The inheritance of the people of Islam from the people of polytheism," no. (2731): 2/911; and al-Daraqutni in al-Fara'id: 4/75; and al-Darimi in al-Fara'id, chapter "The inheritance of the people of polytheism from the people of Islam," from 'Umar, with the wording "The people of two religions do not inherit from one another," and with the wording "Two different religions do not inherit from one another": 2/369-370. Al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/240, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; Ibn Hajar also attributed it to al-Nasa'i and Ibn al-Sakan (Talkhis al-Habir: 3/84). And al-Bayhaqi: 6/218; and Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan, chapter al-Fara'id, from Usamah, and from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, and from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: 1/65-66; and Imam Ahmad: 2/195, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/365.]] Others interpreted it as referring to Islam versus disbelief, since all disbelief is one religion, so the inheritance of some disbelievers from others does not amount to establishing inheritance between people of two different religions.

The slave does not inherit from anyone, and no one inherits from him, because he has no property. There is no difference in this between the chattel slave (al-qinn), the mudabbar (a slave promised freedom upon his master's death), the mukatab (a slave with a contract of manumission), and the umm walad (a female slave who has borne her master's child).

Killing prevents inheritance, whether intentional or by mistake, based on what is related from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The killer does not inherit."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Fara'id, chapter "What has come concerning the nullification of the killer's inheritance": 6/290, and he said: "This is a hadith that is not sound; it is not known except through this route, and Ishaq ibn Abi Farwah has been abandoned by some; and the practice of the scholars is that the killer does not inherit." It was also narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra, and by Ibn Majah in al-Diyat, chapter "The killer does not inherit," no. (2645): 2/883, all of them from al-Layth, from Ishaq, from Abi Farwah, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd, from Abu Hurayrah. Al-Zarkashi said: Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it through Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, as a marfu' report: "The killer inherits nothing." Ibn Abi 'Asim narrated it in al-Diyat, p. 108, and Isma'il's narration from the people of the Hijaz is weak. See al-Mu'tabar fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Minhaj wa'l-Mukhtasar by al-Zarkashi, p. 168; Talkhis al-Habir: 3/84-85. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/367, and weakened it.]]

By uncertainty of death (ammiyy al-mawt) we mean that when two mutual heirs die in a manner where the time of death is unknown, such as drowning in water or a building collapsing on them, and it is not known which of them died first, then neither of them inherits from the other. Rather, the inheritance of each of them goes to whoever was certainly alive after his death from among his heirs.

The fixed shares (al-sihham al-mahdudah) in the laws of inheritance are six: the half (al-nisf), the quarter (al-rub'), the eighth (al-thumun), the two-thirds (al-thuluthan), the third (al-thulth), and the sixth (al-sudus).

The half is the fixed share of three: the husband's share when there is no child; the share of a single daughter of the direct line (li'l-sulb), or of a single son's daughter when there is no child of the direct line; and the share of a single full sister or a single paternal sister when there is no full sibling.

The quarter is the husband's share when the deceased woman has a child, and the wife's share when the deceased man has no child.

The eighth is the wife's share when the deceased man has a child.

The two-thirds is the share of two or more daughters of the direct line, and of two or more sons' daughters when there is no child of the direct line; and the share of two or more full sisters or paternal sisters.

The third is the share of three: the mother's share when the deceased has no child and no two or more siblings (of either sex); except in two cases: one where there is a husband and both parents, and the other where there is a wife and both parents, in which case the mother receives a third of what remains after the husband's or wife's share. Also the share of two or more maternal siblings (awlad al-umm), males and females being equal in it; and the grandfather's share alongside siblings when there is no holder of a fixed share in the case, where the third is better for the grandfather than sharing with the siblings.

As for the sixth, it is the share of seven: the father's share when the deceased has a child; the mother's share when the deceased has a child or two or more siblings; the grandfather's share when the deceased has a child, and alongside siblings when there is a holder of a fixed share in the case, and when the sixth is better for the grandfather than sharing with the siblings; the share of grandmothers; the share of a single maternal sibling, male or female; the share of son's daughters when the deceased has one daughter of the direct line, completing the two-thirds; and the share of paternal sisters when the deceased has one full sister, completing the two-thirds.

'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us: Wuhayb informed us: Ibn Tawus informed us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Give the fixed shares to their people, and whatever remains is for the nearest male."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Fara'id, chapter "The inheritance of the child from his father and mother": 12/11; and Muslim in al-Fara'id, chapter "Give the fixed shares to their people," no. (1615): 3/1233; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/326.]]

In this hadith is evidence that some heirs exclude (hajb) others. Exclusion is of two kinds: exclusion of reduction (hajb al-nuqsan) and exclusion of deprivation (hajb al-hirman).

Exclusion of reduction is that the child and the son's child reduce the husband's share from a half to a quarter, the wife's share from a quarter to an eighth, and the mother's share from a third to a sixth. Likewise, two or more siblings reduce the mother's share from a third to a sixth.

Exclusion of deprivation is that the mother excludes the grandmothers. The maternal siblings (namely the brothers and sisters from the mother's side) are excluded by four: the father, the grandfather however high he may be, the child, and the son's child however low he may be. The full and paternal siblings are excluded by three: the father, the son, and the son's son however low they may be. The full and paternal siblings are not excluded by the grandfather according to the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, which was also the view of 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, and Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with them. This was also the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i, al-Awza'i, Ahmad, and Ishaq, may God have mercy on them.

The paternal siblings are excluded by these three and by the full brother. Some people held that all siblings are excluded by the grandfather just as they are excluded by the father. This was the view of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Ibn 'Abbas, Mu'adh, Abu al-Darda', and 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with them. It was also the view of al-Hasan, 'Ata', Tawus, and Abu Hanifah, may God have mercy on them.

The nearest agnates exclude the more distant ones in agnatic relation. The nearest of them is the son, then the son's son however low he may be, then the father, then the grandfather (the father's father) however high he may be. If there is with the grandfather one of the siblings, full or paternal, male or female, they share in the inheritance. If there is no grandfather, then the full brother, then the paternal brother, then the sons of brothers, with the nearest of them given precedence whether full or paternal. If they are equal in degree, then the one who is from the full side has precedence. Then the full paternal uncle, then the paternal uncle, then their sons in the order of the sons of brothers. Then the father's paternal uncle, then the grandfather's paternal uncle, in this same order.

If there is none of the male agnatic relatives (*'asabat al-nasab*, the agnatic residuaries, i.e., male relatives through the father's line) and the deceased has a *wala'* (patronage, the right of inheritance a manumitter holds over a freed slave), then the inheritance goes to the manumitter. If the manumitter is no longer alive, it goes to the agnatic relatives of the manumitter.

Four males make females agnatic heirs ('asabah): the son, the son's son, the full brother, and the consanguine brother. So if a man dies leaving a son and a daughter, or leaving a full or consanguine brother and a sister, the property is divided between them, with the male receiving the share of two females, and the daughter or sister is not given a fixed share (*fard*).

Likewise, the son's son makes agnatic heirs of the females in his degree, and of those above them, when they do not take any of the two-thirds. So if a man dies leaving two daughters and a son's daughter, the two daughters receive two-thirds, and the son's daughter receives nothing. If, in her degree, there is a son's son, or below her there is a son's son's son, the remainder is divided between them, with the male receiving the share of two females.

The full sister and the consanguine sister become agnatic heirs together with the daughter. So if a man dies leaving a daughter and a sister, half is for the daughter and the remainder is for the sister. If he dies leaving two daughters and a sister, the two daughters receive two-thirds, and the remainder is for the sister.

The evidence for this is what Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi reported to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi told us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us: Adam told us: Shu'bah told us: Abu Qays told us, saying: I heard Hudhayl ibn Shurahbil say: Abu Musa was asked about a daughter, a son's daughter, and a sister. He said: "The daughter has half and the sister has half. Go to Ibn Mas'ud, for he will agree with me." Ibn Mas'ud was asked, and he was told what Abu Musa had said. He said: "Then I would have gone astray, and I am not among the rightly guided. I will judge in this matter by what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) judged: for the daughter is half, and for the son's daughter is a sixth, completing two-thirds, and what remains is for the sister." We came to Abu Musa and informed him of what Ibn Mas'ud had said, may Allah be pleased with him. He said: "Do not ask me as long as this scholar is among you." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Fara'id, chapter "The inheritance of a son's daughter together with a daughter": 12/17. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/333.]

Returning to the tafsir of the verse: the scholars differed about the occasion of its revelation. Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi reported to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi told us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us: Abu al-Walid told us: Shu'bah told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to visit me while I was ill and unable to think. He performed ablution and poured some of his ablution water on me, and I regained my senses. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, to whom does the inheritance go? Only the *kalala* (one who leaves neither ascendants nor descendants) inherits from me." Then the verse of the inheritances was revealed. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surah al-Nisa, chapter "Allah enjoins you concerning your children": 8/243, and Muslim in al-Fara'id, chapter on the inheritance of the *kalala*, no. (1616): 3/1234.]

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Umm Kujjah, the wife of Aws ibn Thabit, and his daughters. [See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 137–138.]

Ata said: Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', one of the chiefs (*naqib*), was martyred on the day of Uhud and left a wife, two daughters, and a brother. The brother took the property. The wife of Sa'd came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with Sa'd's two daughters and said: "O Messenger of Allah, these are the daughters of Sa'd. Their father was killed as a martyr at Uhud, and their paternal uncle has taken their property, and they cannot be married unless they have property." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Go back, for perhaps Allah will decide in this matter." Then ﴿Allah enjoins you﴾ down to its end was revealed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called their uncle and said to him: "Give the two daughters of Sa'd two-thirds, and their mother one-eighth, and what remains is for you." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Fara'id, chapter on what has come concerning the direct line: 4/166–167; al-Tirmidhi in al-Fara'id, chapter on what has come concerning the inheritance of daughters: 6/267–268, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; Ibn Majah in al-Fara'id, chapter on the shares of the direct line, no. (2720): 2/908; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 4/334, and he authenticated it according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; and al-Wahidi narrated it with his chain from Jabir in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 139.] This is the first inheritance distributed in Islam.

The words of the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children﴾, meaning: He charges you and prescribes for you concerning your children, that is, concerning the matter of your children when you die, that the male receives the share of two females.

﴿If there are [only] women above two﴾, meaning: the children left behind are females, two or more, ﴿above﴾ being a connecting particle (*silah*), as in His saying: ﴿So strike [them] upon the necks﴾ [al-Anfal: 12]. ﴿Then for them is two-thirds of what he left. And if there is only one﴾, meaning: a daughter, ﴿[only one]﴾: the common reading is with the accusative (*nasb*) as the predicate of *kana*, while the people of Medina read it with the nominative (*raf'*), in the sense of: if one [female] occurs. ﴿Then for her is half. And for his parents﴾, meaning: the deceased's parents, a metonymy for what was not mentioned, ﴿for each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he had children﴾. He means that the father and mother each have a sixth of the inheritance when there is a child or a son's child, and the father becomes a holder of a fixed share (*sahib fard*). ﴿But if he had no children and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿fa-li-ummihi﴾ with a kasrah on the hamzah, to avoid a damma after a kasrah, while the others read it with a damma, according to the original form. ﴿And if he has brothers﴾, two or more, male or female, ﴿then for his mother is a sixth﴾. The remainder is for the father, if she is with a father, and the brothers have no inheritance alongside the father, but they block (*hajb*) the mother from a third to a sixth.

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Brothers do not block the mother from a third to a sixth unless there are three of them. He alone held this view, and he said: Because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾, and one does not say "brothers" for two. We reply: the collective noun may apply to two, since collectivity is the joining of one thing to another, and this exists in two, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then your hearts have inclined﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4], where He mentioned "the heart" in the plural form and attributed it to two.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿After any bequest he [may have] bequeathed or debt﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr read ﴿yuusa﴾ with a fatha on the sad, in the passive voice (*ma lam yusamma fa'iluh*), and so too the second, and Hafs agreed with them on the second. The others read it with a kasrah on the sad, because the mention of the deceased came earlier, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿after any bequest they [the women] bequeath﴾ and ﴿you bequeath﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "You recite the bequest before the debt, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began with the debt before the bequest." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Wasaya, chapter on what has come about beginning with the debt before the bequest: 6/314–315; Ibn Majah in al-Wasaya, chapter on the debt before the bequest, no. (1715): 2/906; Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, p. 25; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/131, from Ali; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 4/336; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 6/267, in which is al-Harith al-A'war, who is weak. Ibn Abi Usamah al-Harith narrated in his Musnad from Ibn Umar: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) judged that the debt is before the bequest, and that there is no bequest to an heir." See Nasb al-Rayah: 4/405. Ibn Kathir said: 1/460: "Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and the authors of the tafsir books narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Ishaq, from al-Harith ibn Abd Allah al-A'war, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: ..." Then al-Tirmidhi said: "We know it only from the hadith of al-Harith, and some scholars have spoken about him." I [Ibn Kathir] say: However, he was a memorizer of the laws of inheritance, careful with them and with arithmetic, and Allah knows best. And al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir: 3/95: "Although al-Harith is weak, the consensus has been established in accordance with what he narrated." Al-Albani graded the hadith as hasan in al-Irwa': 6/107. See also the tafsir of al-Tabari with the commentary of Shaykh Shakir: 8/46–47.] This is a consensus that the debt takes precedence over the bequest. The meaning of the verse is joint (*jam'*), not sequential (*tartib*). The clarification that the inheritance is deferred behind both the debt and the bequest together means: after a bequest, if there is one, or a debt, if there is one; so inheritance is deferred behind each of them.

﴿Your fathers and your sons﴾, meaning: those who inherit from you are your fathers and your sons, ﴿you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾, meaning: you do not know that they are more beneficial to you in religion and in worldly life. Among you is one who thinks that the father is more beneficial to him, so the son is more beneficial to him, and among you is one who thinks that the son is more beneficial to him, so the father is more beneficial to him. I am the One who knows who is most beneficial to you, and I have arranged your affairs according to what contains the benefit, so follow it. Abd Allah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The most obedient of you to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, whether fathers or sons, will be the highest in rank on the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted lets the believers intercede for one another. If the parent is higher in rank in Paradise, his child is raised up to him, and if the child is higher in rank, his parent is raised up to him, so that their eyes may be comforted by this." ﴿A duty from Allah﴾, meaning: what He has decreed of the inheritances. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of the affairs of the servants, ﴿Wise﴾ in establishing the rulings.

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 4, verse 12:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one-fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt.﴾ This concerns the inheritance of spouses. ﴿And for them [the wives] is one-fourth﴾, meaning: for the wives is one-fourth ﴿of what you leave, if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is one-eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt.﴾ This concerns the inheritance of wives. When a man has four wives, they share the one-fourth and the one-eighth.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance of kalala (a person with neither descendants nor ascendants), or a woman﴾, who is inherited from as kalala. The construction of the verse is: "And if there is a man or a woman who is inherited from as kalala." It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), and it was also said to be in the position of the predicate of the passive verb (mā lam yusammi fā'iluhu), and its underlying sense is: "If a man's wealth is inherited from him as kalala."

They differed concerning kalala. Most of the Companions held that kalala is one who has neither a child nor a father. It was narrated from al-Sha'bi who said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about kalala and said: "I will say something about it by my own opinion. If it is correct, it is from Allah, and if it is wrong, it is from me and from Shaytan. I think it is what remains apart from the father and the child." When 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, succeeded to the caliphate, he said: "I am truly ashamed before Allah to reject something Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, has said." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 8/54, al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 6/223–224, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir. See al-Kafi al-Shafi p. (40).]]

Tawus held that kalala is one who has no child. This is one of the two narrations from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and one of the two opinions from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/57–59.]] Those who held this view relied on the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning kalala: if a man dies leaving no child﴾. Its explanation among the common people is derived from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, because the verse was revealed concerning him, and on the day it was revealed he had neither a father nor a child, since his father 'Abd Allah ibn Haram was killed on the day of Uhud. The verse of kalala was revealed near the end of the life of the Prophet (ﷺ), so Jabir's situation became an explanation of the meaning of the verse, since it was revealed concerning him.

They differed as to whom the word kalala is a name for. Some said: it is a name for the deceased. This is the view of 'Ali and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, because he died having lost both his sides (i.e., without ascendants and descendants), so the pillar of his lineage was gone. Others said: it is a name for the heirs. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, because they surround (yatakallalūna) the deceased from his sides, and no one is in the pillar of his lineage. It is like a crown (iklīl) that encircles the head, while the middle of the head is bare. This is indicated by the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, where he said: "Only kalala inherits from me," meaning: heirs who are neither child nor parent inherit from me.

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: kalala is a name for property. Abu al-Khayr said: A man asked 'Uqba about kalala, and he said: "Do you not wonder at this man asking me about kalala? Kalala has troubled the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) as nothing else has troubled them."

'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Three matters, if the Prophet (ﷺ) had explained them to us, would be dearer to me than the world and all it contains: kalala, the caliphate, and the categories of riba (usury)." [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/303, who declared it sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, and in it is Muhammad ibn Talhah ibn Yazid ibn Rukanah. al-Dhahabi said: "Rather, neither of the two Shaykhs took from Muhammad anything, nor did he meet 'Umar." He also narrated it from 'Amr ibn Murrah from Murrah from 'Umar: 2/304, and said: "Sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs." It was also narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 10/302, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 6/225. See Kanz al-'Ummal: 11/78.]]

Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, gave a sermon and said: "I do not leave after me anything that concerns me more than kalala. I never returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about anything as much as I returned to him about kalala, and he never was harsher with me about anything than about kalala, until he poked his finger into my chest and said: 'O 'Umar, does not the verse of summer, which is at the end of Surah al-Nisa, suffice you? And if I live, I will judge in it with a judgment by which whoever reads the Qur'an and whoever does not read the Qur'an will judge.'" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Fara'id, chapter on the inheritance of kalala, no. (1617): 3/1236.]]

His saying: "Does not the verse of summer suffice you?" He meant: Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed two verses concerning kalala: one in winter, which is the one at the beginning of Surah al-Nisa, and the other in summer, which is the one at its end. The latter contains clarification that the winter verse does not have, which is why he referred him to it.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if he has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is one-sixth﴾. By this is meant a brother and a sister from the mother, by consensus. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas recited: "And he has a brother or a sister from the mother." He did not say "for them both" even though a man and a woman were mentioned earlier, following the custom of the Arabs when they mention two things and then speak about them, and they are equal in the ruling; sometimes they attribute it to one of them, and sometimes to both, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is burdensome﴾ [al-Baqarah: 153], and ﴿But if they are more than that, they share in the one-third﴾. There is consensus that children of the mother, if they are two or more, share in the one-third, males and females alike.

Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said in his sermon: "Indeed, the verse which Allah, may He be exalted, revealed at the beginning of Surah al-Nisa concerning the shares of inheritance, He revealed it concerning the child and the parent. The second verse concerns the husband, the wife and the brothers from the mother. The verse with which Surah al-Nisa ends concerns the brothers and sisters from the father and mother. The verse with which Surah al-Anfal ends was revealed concerning those of the kin (ulu al-arham): some of them are closer to others in the Book of Allah."

﴿After any bequest that is made or debt, without causing harm﴾, meaning: without bringing harm upon the heirs by exceeding the one-third in the bequest. al-Hasan said: this is to bequeath a debt that he does not owe. ﴿As a command from Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing, Most Forbearing﴾. Qatadah said: Allah disliked harm both during life and at death, forbade it, and made it a matter of severity.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 13–14:

﴿These are the limits set by Allah.﴾ That is: what He mentioned of the obligatory portions with defined limits. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, wherein he will abide forever, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾ (80/b) The people of Medina and Ibn ʿĀmir recited "nudkhiluhu jannātin" and "nudkhiluhu nāran" [with the nūn]. In Surah al-Fath [there is] ﴿nudkhiluhu﴾ and ﴿nuʿadhdhibhu﴾; in Surah al-Taghabun ﴿nukaffir﴾ and ﴿nadkhiluhu﴾; and in Surah al-Talaq ﴿nudkhiluhu﴾, all with the nūn in them. The others recited with the yā' (ya').

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 13–14:

﴿These are the limits set by Allah.﴾ That is: what He mentioned of the obligatory portions with defined limits. ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. That is the great triumph.﴾

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him into a Fire, wherein he will abide forever, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾ (80/b) The people of Medina and Ibn ʿĀmir recited "nudkhiluhu jannātin" and "nudkhiluhu nāran" [with the nūn]. In Surah al-Fath [there is] ﴿nudkhiluhu﴾ and ﴿nuʿadhdhibhu﴾; in Surah al-Taghabun ﴿nukaffir﴾ and ﴿nadkhiluhu﴾; and in Surah al-Talaq ﴿nudkhiluhu﴾, all with the nūn in them. The others recited with the yā' (ya').

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 15:

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness﴾ means: fornication (al-zina). ﴿Call to witness against them four [witnesses] from among you﴾ means: from among the Muslims. This is an address to the rulers, meaning: seek against them four witnesses. It indicates that fornication is not established except by four witnesses.

﴿If they testify, then confine them﴾ means: imprison them ﴿in houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way﴾. This was at the beginning of Islam, before the revelation of the prescribed penalties (hudud). When a woman committed fornication, she was confined in the house until she died. Then this was abrogated (nusikha, naskh) concerning the virgin, by flogging and banishment, and concerning the married person (thayyib), by flogging and stoning.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, who was told by Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal, who was told by Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, who was told by al-Rabi', who was told by al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him), who was told by Abd al-Wahhab, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Take from me, take from me: Allah has ordained a way for them. The virgin with the virgin: a hundred lashes and banishment for a year. The married person with the married person: a hundred lashes and stoning." [[Recorded by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 2/77 (Tartib al-Musnad). In it the last phrase appears as follows: "I do not know whether Abd al-Wahhab inserted it between them. It was left out of my book when I revised it, and I do not know whether it is in the original or not. The original was absent from me on the day I wrote this book." The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/276.]] Al-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said: A trustworthy transmitter (al-thiqah) told me that al-Hasan used to insert Hittan al-Raqashi between himself and Ubadah. I do not know whether Abd al-Wahhab inserted him between them, so that he was removed from my book, or not.

Our teacher, the Imam, said: The hadith is sound (sahih). Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hittan ibn Abd Allah, from Ubadah [[Recorded by Muslim in the Book of Prescribed Penalties (al-Hudud), chapter on the penalty for fornication, no. 1690: 3/1316.]]. Then the flogging was abrogated concerning the married person, and stoning remained according to the majority of scholars.

A group went to the view that both are combined. It is narrated from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that he flogged Shurahah al-Hamdaniyyah on Thursday with a hundred lashes, then stoned her on Friday, and said: "I flogged her by the Book of Allah and stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)" [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in the Book of Prescribed Penalties, chapter on stoning the married person: 12/117.]].

The majority of scholars hold that the married person is not flogged together with stoning, because the Prophet (ﷺ) stoned Ma'iz and al-Ghamidiyyah and did not flog them.

According to Abu Hanifah (may Allah be pleased with him), banishment is also abrogated concerning the virgin. The majority of scholars hold that it is established. Nafi' narrated from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (ﷺ) flogged and banished, that Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) flogged and banished, and that Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) flogged and banished [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Prescribed Penalties, chapter on what has come concerning banishment: 4/711-712, and he said: "A strange (gharib) hadith." Al-Hakim recorded it: 4/369 and declared it sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim. Al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Sunan: 8/223. Al-Albani declared it sound in al-Irwa': 8/11. See also Nasb al-Rayah: 3/331.]].

They differed over whether confinement in the house was itself a prescribed penalty that was abrogated, or whether it was detention so that the penalty could be carried out. There are two opinions on this.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 4, verse 16:

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And the two of you who commit it among you﴾. He means: the man and the woman. The pronoun in "ﷲ" refers to the lewdness (al-fahisha). Ibn Kathir recited "اللَّذَانِ" (alladhani), "وَاللَّذَيْنِ" (wallladhayni), "وَهَاتَانِ" (hatani), and "وَهَذَانَ" (hadhan) with a doubled nun (mushaddadat al-nun) for emphasis. The people of Basra agreed with him on "فَذَانِكَ" (fadhanika), while the others read it with a single nun (bi-l-takhfif). Abu 'Ubayd said: Abu 'Amr singled out "فَذَانِكَ" for doubling because the word has few letters.

﴿So harm them both﴾. Ata and Qatada said: rebuke them verbally, saying, "Do you not fear God? Are you not ashamed before God, that you committed fornication?" Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: revile them and abuse them. Ibn Abbas also said: it is by the tongue and by the hand; they are harmed by rebuke and by beating with sandals.

If it is asked: the imprisonment (al-habs) is mentioned in the first verse, and harm is mentioned in this verse, so how is the two reconciled? It is said: the first verse concerns women and this one concerns men; this is the view of Mujahid. It is also said: the first verse concerns the married (al-thayyib), and this one concerns the virgin (al-bikr).

﴿And if they both repent﴾ from the lewdness, ﴿and make amends﴾ in their conduct afterwards, ﴿then leave them alone﴾, so do not harm them. ﴿Indeed God is ever Accepting of repentance, Most Merciful.﴾

All of this was before the revelation of the prescribed punishments (al-hudud), and it was abrogated (nusikha) by flogging and stoning. Flogging is in the Qur'an, as God the Exalted says: ﴿The adulterer and the adulteress, flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾ [al-Nur: 2]. Stoning is in the Sunnah.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu 'Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Utba ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, may God be pleased with them both, that they both told him that two men disputed before the Messenger of God ﷺ. One of them said: "Judge between us, O Messenger of God, by the Book of God." The other, who was more learned in jurisprudence (afqahuhuma), said: "Yes, O Messenger of God, judge between us by the Book of God, and permit me to speak." He said: "Speak." He said: "My son was a laborer (asifan) for this man, and he committed fornication with his wife. They informed me that upon my son is stoning, so I ransomed him for a hundred sheep and a slave-girl of mine. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they informed me that upon my son is a hundred lashes and a year of exile, and that stoning is upon his wife." The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will judge between you both by the Book of God. As for your sheep and your slave-girl, they are returned to you." He flogged his son a hundred times and exiled him for a year. He commanded Unays al-Aslami to go to the other man's wife, and if she confesses, to stone her. She confessed, and he stoned her. [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Wakala, chapter on agency in the prescribed punishments: 4/491-492 and in other places; and Muslim in al-Hudud, chapter on one who confesses to committing adultery against himself, no. (1697): 3/1325; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 10/274-275.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; 'Abd al-Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah informed us; Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn Abbas, who said: 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: "God the Exalted sent Muhammad, the Messenger of God ﷺ, with the truth and revealed the Book to him. Among what God the Exalted revealed was the verse of stoning. We recited it, understood it, and memorized it. The Messenger of God ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. I fear that if a long time passes over people, someone will say, 'By God, we do not find the verse of stoning in the Book of God the Exalted,' and they will go astray by abandoning an obligation that God the Exalted revealed. Stoning in the Book of God the Exalted is a right upon whoever commits adultery when he is married (ahsana), whether man or woman, when evidence is established, or there is pregnancy, or confession." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Hudud, chapter on stoning the pregnant woman for adultery when she is married: 12/144-145, in full; and Muslim in al-Hudud, chapter on stoning the married person for adultery, no. (1691): 3/1317. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 10/280.]]

The summary of the punishment for adultery: if the adulterer is muhsan (married, meeting the conditions of ihsan), that is, one in whom four attributes are combined: sanity, puberty, freedom, and having had intercourse through a valid marriage (nikah sahih), then his punishment is stoning, whether he is Muslim or a dhimmi. This is what is meant by the married person (al-thayyib) mentioned in the hadith. The people of ra'y (Ahl al-Ra'y) held that Islam is a condition of ihsan, and that the dhimmi is not stoned. [[See: Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas: 5/98-99, where he mentions that the Prophet ﷺ stoned two Jews before Islam was made a condition of ihsan.]] It is authentically established from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he stoned two Jews who committed adultery, and they had been muhsan.

If the adulterer is not muhsan, meaning these attributes are not combined in him, then the matter is examined: if he is not of age or is insane, there is no punishment upon him. If he is free, sane, and of age, but has not had intercourse through a valid marriage, then upon him is a hundred lashes and a year of exile (taghrib). If he is a slave, then upon him is fifty lashes. Regarding his exile there are two opinions. If we say he is exiled, there are two views, the more sound of which is half a year, just as he is flogged fifty lashes, being half the punishment of a free person.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Repentance with God is only for those who do evil in ignorance﴾. Al-Hasan said: it means the repentance that He accepts, so "ʿalā" (upon) carries the sense of "ʿind" (with). It was also said: "from God."

﴿Then they repent soon after﴾. Qatada said: The Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ agreed that everything by which God is disobeyed is ignorance (jahala), whether done deliberately or not, and everyone who disobeys God is ignorant. Mujahid said: the intended meaning of the verse is deliberate wrongdoing. Al-Kalbi said: "He did not fail to know that it was a sin, but he failed to know its punishment." It was also said: the meaning of ignorance (jahala) is choosing the fleeting pleasure over the enduring pleasure.

﴿Then they repent soon after﴾. It was said: its meaning is before the evil deed encompasses their good deeds and nullifies them. As-Suddi and al-Kalbi said: "soon" (qarib) means repenting while in health, before the illness of death. ʿIkrima said: before death. ad-Dahhak said: before witnessing the Angel of Death.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us, Ibn Thawban informed us, namely Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban, from his father, from Makhul, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Indeed God, the Exalted, accepts the repentance of the servant so long as he has not begun the death rattle (gharghara)." [[Narrated by at-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter "The Door of Repentance Is Open Before the Death Rattle": 9/521, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith. And Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter "Mention of Repentance," no. (4253): 2/1420. He said in the Zawaid: its chain contains al-Walid ibn Muslim, who is a mudallis (concealer of sources) and transmitted it with ʿan'ana (using "from"), and likewise Makhul al-Dimashqi. Al-Hakim authenticated it: 4/257, and adh-Dhahabi agreed with him. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 2/132 and in other places from Ibn Umar, and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 5/90–91.]]

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, Abu al-Aswad informed us, Ibn Lahi'a informed us, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed Satan said: 'By Your might, my Lord, I will not cease to lead Your servants astray so long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord said: 'By My might, My majesty, and the loftiness of My station, I will not cease to forgive them so long as they seek My forgiveness.'" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 3/29, 41, without his words "and the loftiness of My station." Al-Hakim narrated it through another route from Darraj: 4/261, without this addition, and said: this is a hadith with a sahih chain, and adh-Dhahabi agreed. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/207: "Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and at-Tabarani in al-Awsat; one of Ahmad's chains has narrators who are the narrators of the Sahih, and likewise one of Abu Ya'la's chains." Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat: 1/221, and in it is Ibn Lahi'a from Darraj from Abu al-Haytham from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, with a wording like that of al-Baghawi, and it is in his Sharh al-Sunna: 5/76 with the same wording. This addition is munkar; Shaykh al-Albani said in Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahiha: 1/164: "The defect of this addition in my view is from Ibn Lahi'a, and it is among his confusions."]]

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Those are the ones to whom God turns in forgiveness, and God is ever Knowing, Wise﴾.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 18–19:

﴿And repentance is not [accepted] from those who do evil deeds﴾, meaning: the sins, ﴿until, when death approaches one of them﴾ and he is in the throes of death (al-nazʿ), ﴿he says, "Indeed I have repented now"﴾. This is the state of al-sawq (the death rattle), when his soul is being drawn out. Faith is not accepted from a disbeliever, nor repentance from a sinner, at that point. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir: 85]. For this reason the faith of Pharaoh did not benefit him when drowning overtook him.

﴿Nor [is repentance accepted] from those who die while they are disbelievers. For those, We have prepared﴾, i.e., We have readied and prepared, ﴿a painful punishment﴾.

﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾. It was revealed concerning the people of Madinah, who used to do this in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) and at the beginning of Islam: when a man died leaving a wife, his son from another woman, or a relative from his paternal kin (ʿasabah), would come and throw his garment over that woman and over her tent, and thereby he became more entitled to her than her own self and than anyone else. If he wished, he would marry her without a dowry, except the first dowry that the deceased had given her; and if he wished, he would marry her to someone else and take her dowry; and if he wished, he would restrain her (ʿadl) and prevent her from marrying, harming her so that she would ransom herself from him with what she had inherited from the deceased, or so that she would die and he would inherit her. If the woman went to her own family before the guardian of her husband threw his garment over her, then she was more entitled to herself. They continued in this practice until Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat al-Ansari died and left his wife Kubaysha bint Maʿn al-Ansariyya. His son from another woman, called Hisn, stood up—and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: his name was Qays ibn Abi Qays—and threw his garment over her, and thus inherited her marriage. Then he left her and did not spend on her, harming her so that she would ransom herself from him. Kubaysha came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Abu Qays died and his son inherited my marriage; he neither spends on me, nor consummates with me, nor lets me go free." He said: "Stay in your house until the command of Allah comes concerning you." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾ [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, saying: "The exegetes said: the people of Madinah were..." pp. 140–141. See also: Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/104–108, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/463.]].

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read kurhan (﴿كُرْهًا﴾) with a dammah on the kaf, here and in al-Tawbah; the rest read it with a fathah. Al-Kisa'i said: "They are two dialects." Al-Farra' said: "Al-kurh with a fathah is what one is compelled to; with a dammah it is what comes from one's own self as hardship."

﴿And do not restrain them in order to take back part of what you have given them﴾, i.e., do not prevent them from marrying, so that they become distressed and ransom themselves with part of their property. It was said: this is addressed to the guardians of the deceased. The sound view is that it is addressed to the husbands.

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: this concerns a man who has a wife whom he dislikes keeping as a companion, and she has a dowry owed to her by him; so he harms her so that she will ransom herself and return to him what he gave her as dowry. Allah the Exalted forbade that. Then He said: ﴿except when they commit a clear immorality﴾, and then it becomes lawful for you to harm them so that they will ransom themselves from you.

They differed concerning al-fahishah (the immorality). Ibn Masʿud and Qatadah said: it is nushuz (disobedience/ill conduct). Some of them, and this is the saying of al-Hasan, said: it is adultery (al-zina); meaning: if the woman acts with nushuz or commits adultery, it becomes lawful for the husband to ask her for khul' (divorce by ransom). ʿAta' said: when a man's wife committed immorality, he would take back from her what he had given her and expel her; then Allah abrogated that by the hudud (prescribed punishments).

Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read mubayyinatin and mubayyinat with a fathah on the ya'; Ahl al-Madinah and al-Basrah agreed with them on mubayyinat; the rest read them with a kasrah.

﴿And live with them in kindness﴾. Al-Hasan said: it returns to the beginning of the discourse, meaning: ﴿And give women their dowries graciously﴾ and ﴿live with them in kindness﴾. Living with them in kindness consists of gentleness in speech, in spending the night with them, and in maintenance. It was also said: it means that one should adorn himself for her just as she adorns herself for him. ﴿And if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike something while Allah has placed in it much good﴾. It was said: that is a righteous child, or that Allah will incline him toward her.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 18–19:

﴿And repentance is not [accepted] from those who do evil deeds﴾, meaning: the sins, ﴿until, when death approaches one of them﴾ and he is in the throes of death (al-nazʿ), ﴿he says, "Indeed I have repented now"﴾. This is the state of al-sawq (the death rattle), when his soul is being drawn out. Faith is not accepted from a disbeliever, nor repentance from a sinner, at that point. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir: 85]. For this reason the faith of Pharaoh did not benefit him when drowning overtook him.

﴿Nor [is repentance accepted] from those who die while they are disbelievers. For those, We have prepared﴾, i.e., We have readied and prepared, ﴿a painful punishment﴾.

﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾. It was revealed concerning the people of Madinah, who used to do this in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) and at the beginning of Islam: when a man died leaving a wife, his son from another woman, or a relative from his paternal kin (ʿasabah), would come and throw his garment over that woman and over her tent, and thereby he became more entitled to her than her own self and than anyone else. If he wished, he would marry her without a dowry, except the first dowry that the deceased had given her; and if he wished, he would marry her to someone else and take her dowry; and if he wished, he would restrain her (ʿadl) and prevent her from marrying, harming her so that she would ransom herself from him with what she had inherited from the deceased, or so that she would die and he would inherit her. If the woman went to her own family before the guardian of her husband threw his garment over her, then she was more entitled to herself. They continued in this practice until Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat al-Ansari died and left his wife Kubaysha bint Maʿn al-Ansariyya. His son from another woman, called Hisn, stood up—and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: his name was Qays ibn Abi Qays—and threw his garment over her, and thus inherited her marriage. Then he left her and did not spend on her, harming her so that she would ransom herself from him. Kubaysha came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Abu Qays died and his son inherited my marriage; he neither spends on me, nor consummates with me, nor lets me go free." He said: "Stay in your house until the command of Allah comes concerning you." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾ [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, saying: "The exegetes said: the people of Madinah were..." pp. 140–141. See also: Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/104–108, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/463.]].

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read kurhan (﴿كُرْهًا﴾) with a dammah on the kaf, here and in al-Tawbah; the rest read it with a fathah. Al-Kisa'i said: "They are two dialects." Al-Farra' said: "Al-kurh with a fathah is what one is compelled to; with a dammah it is what comes from one's own self as hardship."

﴿And do not restrain them in order to take back part of what you have given them﴾, i.e., do not prevent them from marrying, so that they become distressed and ransom themselves with part of their property. It was said: this is addressed to the guardians of the deceased. The sound view is that it is addressed to the husbands.

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: this concerns a man who has a wife whom he dislikes keeping as a companion, and she has a dowry owed to her by him; so he harms her so that she will ransom herself and return to him what he gave her as dowry. Allah the Exalted forbade that. Then He said: ﴿except when they commit a clear immorality﴾, and then it becomes lawful for you to harm them so that they will ransom themselves from you.

They differed concerning al-fahishah (the immorality). Ibn Masʿud and Qatadah said: it is nushuz (disobedience/ill conduct). Some of them, and this is the saying of al-Hasan, said: it is adultery (al-zina); meaning: if the woman acts with nushuz or commits adultery, it becomes lawful for the husband to ask her for khul' (divorce by ransom). ʿAta' said: when a man's wife committed immorality, he would take back from her what he had given her and expel her; then Allah abrogated that by the hudud (prescribed punishments).

Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read mubayyinatin and mubayyinat with a fathah on the ya'; Ahl al-Madinah and al-Basrah agreed with them on mubayyinat; the rest read them with a kasrah.

﴿And live with them in kindness﴾. Al-Hasan said: it returns to the beginning of the discourse, meaning: ﴿And give women their dowries graciously﴾ and ﴿live with them in kindness﴾. Living with them in kindness consists of gentleness in speech, in spending the night with them, and in maintenance. It was also said: it means that one should adorn himself for her just as she adorns herself for him. ﴿And if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike something while Allah has placed in it much good﴾. It was said: that is a righteous child, or that Allah will incline him toward her.

﴿And if you desire to exchange a spouse in place of a spouse﴾: by "spouse" he means the wife, and there was no rebellion (*nushuz*) or immorality on her part. ﴿And you have given one of them a qintar﴾, which is a great amount of wealth, as a dowry. ﴿Then take not from it﴾, from the qintar, ﴿anything. Would you take it﴾: this is an interrogative (*istifham*) in the sense of reproach. ﴿By slander and manifest sin﴾: the accusative of these two words is explained in two ways. One is by removing the governing preposition (*naz' al-khafid*). The second is by an implied verb, its estimated form being: you would be committing, in taking it, slander and sin. Then he said: ﴿And how could you take it?﴾

﴿And how could you take it back﴾ by way of astonishment, ﴿when you have gone in unto one another﴾. He meant by this sexual intercourse, but Allah is Bashful and uses euphemism. The root meaning of *ifda'* is reaching a thing without any intermediary.

﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾. Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: it is the guardian's statement at the marriage contract: "I have married her to you on the terms that Allah has laid down for women over men, either to keep her in kindness or to release her with good treatment." Al-Sha'bi and 'Ikrimah said: it is what has been related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Fear Allah concerning women, for you have taken them under the trust of Allah, and you have made their private parts lawful by the word of Allah." [[A portion of the hadith of Jabir concerning the Farewell Pilgrimage, narrated by Muslim in the Book of Hajj, chapter on the Pilgrimage of the Prophet (ﷺ), no. (1218): 2/886–892.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾. The people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) used to marry the wives of their fathers. Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar said: Abu Qays died, and he was among the righteous Ansar. His son Qays proposed to his father's wife, and she said: "I have taken you as a son, and you are among the righteous of your people, but I will go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and seek his counsel." She went to him and informed him, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 179, and al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/468.]] It was said: the meaning is "after what has passed." And it was said: its meaning is "but what has already passed," i.e., what occurred in the Jahiliyyah is pardoned. ﴿Indeed, it was an abomination﴾, i.e., it is an abomination, and "was" here is an extra (silah) particle. ﴿Fahishah﴾ (abomination) is the worst of sins. ﴿And hateful﴾, i.e., it brings about the hatred of Allah, and *maqt* is the most intense hatred. ﴿And evil is the way﴾, meaning that this is a wretched path. The Arabs used to call the child of a man by his father's wife *maqit* (the hated one). Among them were al-Ash'ath ibn Qays and Abu Mu'ayt ibn Abi 'Amr ibn Umayyah. [[In manuscript A: "Asad."]]

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us; Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Sijzi informed us; al-Imam Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi informed us; Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Hadrami informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-'Utaridi informed us, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: My maternal uncle passed by me carrying a banner, and I said: "Where are you going?" He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) has sent me to a man who married his father's wife, to bring his head." [[This hadith has been narrated with different wordings. It was recorded by Abu Dawud in al-Hudud, chapter on a man who commits zina with his close female relative: 6/267; al-Tirmidhi in al-Hudud, chapter on what has come concerning one who marries his father's wife: 4/598, and he said: "hasan gharib"; al-Nasa'i in al-Nikah, chapter on marrying what the fathers have married: 6/109–110; Ibn Majah in al-Hudud, chapter on one who marries his father's wife after him, no. (2607): 2/869; al-Daraqutni in al-Nikah, chapter on a man marrying his father's wife: 2/153; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/295; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/305, and he said: "this hadith is hasan gharib," and in its chain is al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar al-Kindi, who is weak (al-Taqrib). Al-Mundhiri said after citing its narrations: "This has been subject to much disagreement." Al-Shawkani said in Nayl al-Awtar: 8/322: "The hadith has many chains, and among them is one whose narrators are the narrators of the Sahih," and al-Albani authenticated it in Irwa' al-Ghalil: 8/18–22.]]

﴿And how could you take it back﴾ by way of astonishment, ﴿when you have gone in unto one another﴾. He meant by this sexual intercourse, but Allah is Bashful and uses euphemism. The root meaning of *ifda'* is reaching a thing without any intermediary.

﴿And they have taken from you a solemn covenant﴾. Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: it is the guardian's statement at the marriage contract: "I have married her to you on the terms that Allah has laid down for women over men, either to keep her in kindness or to release her with good treatment." [[A portion of the hadith of Jabir concerning the Farewell Pilgrimage, narrated by Muslim in the Book of Hajj, chapter on the Pilgrimage of the Prophet (ﷺ), no. (1218): 2/886–892.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾. The people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) used to marry the wives of their fathers. Al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar said: Abu Qays died, and he was among the righteous Ansar. His son Qays proposed to his father's wife, and she said: "I have taken you as a son, and you are among the righteous of your people, but I will go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and seek his counsel." She went to him and informed him, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed﴾. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 179, and al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Firyabi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi.
