Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us; Abu Sahl Muhammad ibn 'Amr al-Sijzi informed us; al-Imam Abu Sulayman al-Khattabi informed us; Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Hadrami informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-'Utaridi informed us, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: My maternal uncle passed by me carrying a banner, and I said: "Where are you going?" He said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) has sent me to a man who married his father's wife, to bring his head." [[This hadith has been narrated with different wordings. It was recorded by Abu Dawud in al-Hudud, chapter on a man who commits zina with his close female relative: 6/267; al-Tirmidhi in al-Hudud, chapter on what has come concerning one who marries his father's wife: 4/598, and he said: "hasan gharib"; al-Nasa'i in al-Nikah, chapter on marrying what the fathers have married: 6/109–110; Ibn Majah in al-Hudud, chapter on one who marries his father's wife after him, no. (2607): 2/869; al-Daraqutni in al-Nikah, chapter on a man marrying his father's wife: 2/153; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/295; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/305, and he said: "this hadith is hasan gharib," and in its chain is al-Ash'ath ibn Sawwar al-Kindi, who is weak (al-Taqrib). Al-Mundhiri said after citing its narrations: "This has been subject to much disagreement." Al-Shawkani said in Nayl al-Awtar: 8/322: "The hadith has many chains, and among them is one whose narrators are the narrators of the Sahih," and al-Albani authenticated it in Irwa' al-Ghalil: 8/18–22.]]

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾ and so on. In this verse Allah the Exalted explains the prohibited women on account of marital connection (al-wusla). The total number of prohibitions in the Book of Allah the Exalted is fourteen: seven by lineage (nasab) and seven by means of a cause (sabab).

As for the seven by cause, two of them are by suckling (al-rida'), four are by marital affinity (al-sihriyya), and the seventh is the married women (al-muhsanat), who are women with husbands.

As for the seven by lineage, the saying of the Exalted is: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾, the plural of "mother" (umm), which includes the grandmothers, however far up they go, on the mother's side and on the father's side. ﴿And your daughters﴾, the plural of "daughter" (bint), which includes the daughters of children, however far down they go. ﴿And your sisters﴾, the plural of "sister" (ukht), whether from the father and mother, or from one of them. ﴿And your paternal aunts﴾, the plural of "paternal aunt" ('amma), which includes all the sisters of your fathers and grandfathers, however far up they go. ﴿And your maternal aunts﴾, the plural of "maternal aunt" (khala), which includes all the sisters of your mothers and grandmothers. ﴿And the daughters of the brother and the daughters of the sister﴾, which includes the daughters of the children of the brother and the sister, however far down they go. The summary of this is that a man is forbidden his ascendants (usul), his descendants (fusul), the descendants of his first ascendants, and the first descendant of every ascendant after them. The ascendants are the mothers and grandmothers; the descendants are the daughters and the daughters of children; the descendants of his first ascendants are the sisters, and the daughters of the brothers and sisters; and the first descendant of every ascendant after them are the paternal aunts and maternal aunts, however far up they go.

As for the prohibitions by suckling, the saying of the Exalted is: ﴿And your mothers who have nursed you, and your sisters through suckling﴾.
The summary of this is that what is forbidden by lineage is forbidden by suckling. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'isha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What is forbidden by birth is forbidden by suckling." [[Narrated by Muslim in Breastfeeding (al-Radā'), chapter "What is forbidden by suckling is what is forbidden by birth," no. (1444): 4/1068, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunna: 9/73.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, saying: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from 'Amra bint 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'isha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she told her that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with her, and that she heard the voice of a man asking permission to enter the house of Hafsa. 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, if so-and-so were alive" — referring to her paternal uncle through suckling — "would he enter upon me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Yes, indeed suckling forbids what birth forbids." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Marriage, chapter "And your mothers who have nursed you," 9/139-140, and in other places, and by Muslim in Breastfeeding, chapter "What is forbidden by suckling is what is forbidden by birth," no. (1444): 4/1068, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunna: 9/72-73.]]

The prohibition by suckling is established only on two conditions. The first is that it occurs before the infant completes two years, because of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿The mothers suckle their children for two complete years﴾ [al-Baqara: 233]. It is related from Umm Salama, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Nothing is forbidden by suckling except what tears the intestines." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Breastfeeding, chapter "What has come that suckling forbids only in infancy, not beyond the two years," 4/313, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. Ibn Majah related it from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr with the wording: "There is no suckling except what tears the intestines," no. (1946): 1/626. Ibn Hibban in Marriage, no. (1250), p. 305 of Mawarid al-Zam'an, and Ibn Majah in Marriage, no. (1946): 1/626, with the wording "There is no suckling except what tears the intestines." See also Irwa' al-Ghalil: 7/221-222.]] It is also related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no suckling except what raises the bone and makes the flesh grow." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Marriage, chapter "On the suckling of an adult," 3/11. Al-Mundhiri said: Abu Hatim al-Razi was asked about Abu Musa al-Hilali, and he said: he is unknown, and his father is unknown. It was also narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 7/461, al-Daraqutni: 4/173, and Ahmad: 1/432. Al-Albani weakened the hadith in Irwa' al-Ghalil: 7/223.]] This applies only in the state of infancy.

According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, the period of suckling is thirty months, because of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And its carrying and its weaning is thirty months﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15]. According to the majority, this is based on the minimum period of pregnancy and the maximum period of suckling; the minimum period of pregnancy is six months.

The second condition is that there be five separate sucklings. This is related from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr also held this view, and al-Shafi'i, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, followed it.

Most scholars held that little suckling and much suckling both establish the prohibition. This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn 'Umar, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib held it. Sufyan al-Thawri, Malik, al-Awza'i, 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y) also followed this view. [[See: al-Ijma' ... (al-Ishraf 'ala madhahib al-'ulama' by Ibn al-Mundhir): 4/109-113.]]

Those who held that little suckling does not prohibit based their view on what Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam informed us: Anas ibn 'Iyad informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who narrates that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A single suck does not prohibit, nor do two suckings." Thus some narrated this hadith. [[See: Sunan al-Tirmidhi with Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 4/307-308, and Irwa' al-Ghalil by al-Albani: 7/220.]] 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulayka related it from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is the sound version. [[Narrated by Muslim in Breastfeeding, chapter "On a single suck and two sucks," no. (1450): 2/1073-1074, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunna: 9/81, 4/111.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, from 'Amra bint 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'isha, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "In what Allah revealed in the Qur'an there were ten known sucklings that prohibit. Then they were abrogated (nusikhna) by five known sucklings. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died while they were still among what is recited of the Qur'an." [[Narrated by Muslim in Breastfeeding, chapter "The prohibition by five sucklings," no. (1452): 2/1075, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunna: 9/80.]]

As for the prohibitions by marital affinity, the saying of the Exalted is: ﴿And the mothers of your wives﴾. The summary of this is that whoever contracts marriage with a woman, the mothers of the woman married and her grandmothers, however far up they go, whether by suckling or by lineage, become forbidden to the one who marries her by the contract itself.

﴿And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship, born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage﴾. The stepdaughters (rabā'ib) is the plural of stepdaughter (rabiba), who is the daughter of the woman. She was named rabiba because of his raising (tarbiya) of her. The saying ﴿in your guardianship﴾ means in your upbringing; it is said: "So-and-so is in the guardianship (hijr) of so-and-so" when he is in his upbringing. ﴿With whom you have consummated marriage﴾ means you have had intercourse with them.

Also forbidden to him are the daughters of the wife and the daughters of her children, however far down they go, whether by suckling or by lineage, after consummation with the wife. Even if he separates from the wife before consummating with her or she dies, it is permissible for him to marry her daughter, [but it is not permissible for him to marry her mother] [[Omitted from manuscript (a).]], because Allah the Exalted stated the prohibition of mothers absolutely, and said regarding the prohibition of stepdaughters: ﴿But if you have not consummated marriage with them, there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning: in marrying their daughters, once you have separated from them or they have died. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The mother of the woman is not forbidden except by consummation with the daughter, as with the stepdaughter.

﴿And the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾, meaning the wives of your sons. The singular is "halila" and the male is "halil." They were so named because each of them is lawful (halal) to the other, from "hulul," which means "descent," and it was also said that each of them makes lawful the other's garment (izar) from "hall," which is the opposite of "prohibition" ('aqd). [[Omitted from manuscript (a).]]

The summary is that a man is forbidden the wives of his sons and the sons of his sons, however far down they go, whether by suckling or by lineage, by the contract itself. He said "from your loins" to make clear that the wife of an adopted son (al-mutabanna) is not forbidden to the man who adopted him, for the Prophet (ﷺ) married the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha, and Zayd had been adopted by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The fourth of the prohibitions by marital affinity is the wife of the father and of the grandfather, however far up he goes. She is forbidden to the son and to the son's son by the contract itself, whether the father is so by suckling or by lineage, because of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women﴾, which has already been mentioned.

Every woman who is forbidden to you by the contract of marriage is also forbidden by intercourse through ownership of the right hand (milk al-yamin), and by intercourse through a doubtful marriage (wat' bi-shubhat al-nikah). So if he has intercourse with a woman through doubt, or with a slave-girl owned by his right hand, the mother of the one who was had intercourse with becomes forbidden to the one who had intercourse, and her daughter likewise, and the one who was had intercourse with becomes forbidden to the father of the one who had intercourse and to his son.

If a man commits fornication (zina) with a woman, the scholars have differed about it. A group held that the mother of the woman he fornicated with is not forbidden to the fornicator, nor is her daughter; but the fornicatress is forbidden to the father of the fornicator and to his son. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Urwa, and al-Zuhri also held it, and Malik and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them, followed this view.

Another group held that it establishes the prohibition. This is related from 'Imran ibn Husayn and Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with them. Jabir ibn Zayd and al-Hasan also held it, and it is the view of the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y).

If a man touches a woman with desire, or kisses her, is this treated as intercourse in establishing the prohibition of marital affinity? Likewise, if he touches a woman with desire, is it treated as intercourse in the prohibition of the stepdaughter? There are two opinions on this. The sounder of them, and the view of most scholars, is that the prohibition is established by it. The second is that it is not established, just as it is not established by looking with desire.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And that you combine two sisters﴾. It is not permissible for a man to combine two sisters in marriage, whether the sisterhood between them is by lineage or by suckling. If he marries a woman and then divorces her irrevocably (ba'in), it is permissible for him to marry her sister. Likewise, if he owns two sisters by right of ownership, it is not permissible for him to combine them in intercourse; if he has intercourse with one of them, it is not lawful for him to have intercourse with the other until he has made the first forbidden to himself.

Likewise, it is not permissible to combine a woman with her paternal aunt, nor a woman with her maternal aunt, because of what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab related to us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with them, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A woman may not be combined with her paternal aunt, nor with her maternal aunt." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Marriage, chapter "A woman may not be married while her paternal aunt is married," 9/160, and Muslim in Marriage, chapter "The prohibition of combining a woman with her paternal aunt..." no. (1408): 2/1820, and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunna: 9/66.]]

"Except what has already occurred" (illa ma qad salaf): meaning, but what has passed is pardoned, because they used to do it before Islam. 'Ata' and al-Suddi said: "Except what was done by Ya'qub (peace be upon him), for he combined between Layya, the mother of Yahudha (Judah), and Rahil (Rachel), the mother of Yusuf (Joseph), and they were two sisters."

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The Exalted Lord's saying: ﴿And all married women, except those whom your right hands possess﴾. He means: women who have husbands. It is not lawful for anyone else to marry them before they are separated from their husbands. This is the seventh of the categories of women who are forbidden [[In B: (harrimna).]] by reason of a cause.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: It was revealed concerning women who used to emigrate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while they still had husbands. Some Muslims would then marry them. Then their husbands came, having emigrated themselves, so Allah forbade the Muslims to marry them. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿except those whom your right hands possess﴾, meaning the captives (sabaya) who were taken as captives while they had husbands in the land of war. For their owner it is lawful to have intercourse with them after istibra' (the waiting period to establish that the womb is clear), because by captivity the marriage between her and her husband is dissolved [[Reference: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2 / 480.]].

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: On the day of Hunayn, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent an army to Awtas. They took captives who had husbands among the polytheists, and the Muslims disliked having intercourse with them. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Suckling, chapter on intercourse with a captive after istibra', no. (1456): 2 / 1079.]].

And 'Ata' said: By His saying ﴿except those whom your right hands possess﴾ He intended that a female slave of his should be in marriage to his slave, so that he may lawfully take her away from him.

It has also been said: By "the married women" He intended free women. The meaning is that whatever exceeds four of them is forbidden, except those whom your right hands possess, for there is no limit upon you regarding slave-girls.

The Exalted Lord's saying: ﴿The decree of Allah upon you﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive (masdar). That is, Allah has prescribed upon you the decree of Allah. It has also been said that it is in the accusative as an incitement (al-igra'), that is: adhere to the Book of Allah upon yourselves, i.e., the obligation of Allah the Exalted.

The Exalted Lord's saying: ﴿And lawful for you is what lies beyond that﴾. Abu Ja'far, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "uhilla" with the first letter dammed and the ha' kasra, in accordance with His saying ﴿are forbidden to you﴾. The others read it with a fatha, meaning: Allah has made lawful for you what lies beyond that, that is, what is other than those forbidden things which I have mentioned. ﴿That you seek﴾: that you desire, ﴿with your wealth﴾: that is, that you marry with a dowry or buy with a price. ﴿Chaste (muhsinin)﴾: that is, married (mutazawwijin) or abstaining (mutaʿaffifin). ﴿Not committing fornication (musafihin)﴾: that is, not being fornicators (zani), derived from safh al-ma' and its pouring, which is the semen. ﴿Then for what you have enjoyed of them﴾: scholars differed about its meaning. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: it means what you have benefited from and enjoyed of women through lawful marriage by intercourse. ﴿Then give them their wages (ujur)﴾: that is, their dowries (muhur). Others said: it refers to mut'ah marriage, which is that a man marries a woman for a fixed term; when that term ends, she is separated from him without divorce, she must undergo the waiting period for her womb, and there is no inheritance between them. This was permissible at the beginning of Islam, then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade it.

Ismail ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr informed us: my father informed us: 'Abd al-Aziz ibn 'Umar informed us: al-Rabi' ibn Sabra al-Juhani told me, that his father told him that he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "O people, I had permitted you to enjoy women (istimta'), but Allah the Exalted has forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection. So whoever has any of them, let him release her, and do not take back anything of what you have given them" [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Marriage, chapter on mut'ah marriage, no. (1406): 2 / 1025, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9 / 100.]].

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Abd Allah and al-Hasan, the two sons of Muhammad ibn 'Ali, from their father, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade mut'ah with women on the day of Khaybar, and forbade eating the flesh of domestic donkeys [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of Khaybar: 7 / 481, and Muslim in the Book of Marriage, chapter on mut'ah marriage, no. (1407): 2 / 1027, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9 / 99. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari: 7 / 482-483: "It has been said that there is an inversion (taqdim and ta'khir) in the hadith," and the correct reading is: he forbade on the day of Khaybar the eating of domestic donkeys and mut'ah with women; the day of Khaybar is not a time reference for mut'ah with women, since there was no enjoyment with women during the Battle of Khaybar. Then he elaborated on this in the book of Marriage.]].

And this is the view of the majority of scholars: that mut'ah marriage is forbidden, and the verse has been abrogated (mansukha).

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, held that the verse is muhkam (not abrogated) and permitted mut'ah marriage. It is narrated from Abu Nadrah who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, about mut'ah, and he said: "Do you not read in Surat an-Nisa': 'Then for what you have enjoyed of them, up to a specified term'?" I said: "I do not read it like that." Ibn 'Abbas said: "That is how Allah revealed it," three times.

It has also been said that Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, retracted that view [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Mut'ah was only at the beginning of Islam. A man would arrive in a town where he had no acquaintance, so he would marry a woman for as long as he expected to stay, and she would guard his property and tend to his affairs, until the verse was revealed: "except upon their wives or what their right hands possess." Ibn 'Abbas said: every intimate relation other than these two is forbidden. In its chain is Musa ibn 'Ubayda, who is weak. Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: 9 / 173: "It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he retracted the view permitting mut'ah, through weak chains of transmission, and his permitting mut'ah is more sound." Ibn al-Mundhir said in al-Ishraf: 4 / 75: "It is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade mut'ah marriage, and his saying: 'Beware, Allah has forbidden it until the Day of Resurrection' indicates that abrogation cannot occur concerning it. We have transmitted reports from the early generation permitting it, but it has no meaning and no benefit alongside the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Among those who forbade mut'ah was the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: its prohibition is in the Qur'an: 'And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy,' and it is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: it was abrogated by the verses of divorce, the 'idda, and inheritance. And it is narrated from 'Ali that he said the same. Ibn 'Umar said: I know it only as fornication (sifah). Ibn al-Zubayr said: mut'ah is plain adultery, and I know of no one who practices it except that I would stone him. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: mut'ah was only for three days until Allah and His Messenger ﷺ forbade it. Among those who nullified mut'ah marriage were Malik, al-Thawri, al-Shafi'i, Ishaq, Abu Thawr and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y). I know of no one today who permits mut'ah marriage except some of the Rafidah, and there is no meaning to an opinion that contradicts the Book and the Sunnah on the part of the one who holds it." Furthermore, Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, used to interpret permission of mut'ah for one compelled to it by prolonged celibacy and lack of means; then he stopped it after it was said to him: "Your fatwa has spread among the riders..." He said: "Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return! By Allah, I did not give this fatwa, nor did I intend this. I only permitted what Allah permitted, such as carrion, blood and the flesh of swine, which are only lawful for one compelled, and it is nothing but like carrion, blood and the flesh of swine." See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 5 / 129-133; Fath al-Bari: 9 / 166-174; Ma'alim al-Sunan of al-Khattabi: 3 / 18; Talkhis al-Habir: 3 / 154-156; Nayl al-Awtar: 7 / 304-310; the treatise on marriage by Shaykh Muhammad al-Hamid in his collected treatises: pp. 5-97; Khatam al-Nabiyyin by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Zahra: 2 / 1089-1097; and the general books of jurisprudence in the chapter on marriage, the first volume of Sharh Qanun al-Ahwal al-Shakhsiyyah by al-Siba'i.]].

Salim narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab ascended the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, and said: "What is wrong with men who marry this mut'ah when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden it? I will not find a man who has married it except that I will stone him with stones." And he said: "The demolisher of mut'ah is marriage, divorce, the waiting period, and inheritance" [[Narrated by Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi through the chain of Salim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar from his father. See: Fath al-Bari: 9 / 173.]].

Al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman said: I heard al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "I know of no thing in Islam that was made lawful, then forbidden, then made lawful, then forbidden, except mut'ah."

The Exalted Lord's saying: ﴿Then give them their wages (ujur)﴾, that is, their dowries (muhur), ﴿as an obligation; and there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree upon after the obligation﴾. Whoever understands the preceding part as referring to mut'ah marriage means that when the two conclude a contract for a fixed term with a payment, then when the term ends, if the woman wishes she may extend the term and the man may increase the payment; and if they do not agree, he separates from her. Whoever understands the verse as referring to enjoyment through a valid marriage says that the meaning of His saying ﴿there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree upon﴾ is remission of the dowry, khul' (compensation for divorce), and exchange (i'tiyad). ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾.

[Section on the amount of the dowry and what is recommended concerning it]

Know that there is no fixed limit on the maximum dowry, due to the Exalted Lord's saying: ﴿And if you had given one of them a heap of gold, do not take back from it anything﴾. It is recommended not to exaggerate in it. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Beware, do not exaggerate the dowries of women, for if it were a noble thing in this world and piety before Allah, the one most entitled to it would have been the Prophet of Allah ﷺ. I do not know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married any of his wives, nor gave any of his daughters in marriage, for more than twelve ounces [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Marriage, chapter on dowry: 3 / 46; al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Marriage, chapter on what has come concerning the dowries of women: 4 / 255, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; al-Nasa'i in the Book of Marriage, chapter on equity in dowries: 6 / 117; al-Darimi in the Book of Marriage, chapter on how much were the dowries of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and his daughters: 2 / 141; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 7 / 234; authenticated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2 / 175; Ibn Hibban, no. (259), p. (307) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1 / 40, 41, 48.]]."

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Muflis informed us: Harun ibn Ishaq informed us: Yahya ibn Muhammad al-Harithi informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muhammad informed us, from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hadi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah who said: I asked 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, "How much was the dowry of the Prophet ﷺ for his wives?" She said: "His dowry for his wives was twelve ounces and a nash." She said: "Do you know what the nash is?" I said: "No." She said: "Half an ounce. So that is five hundred dirhams. This was the dowry of the Prophet ﷺ for his wives" [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Marriage, chapter on the dowry, and that it may be the teaching of Qur'an or an iron ring..., no. (1426): 2 / 1042.]].

As for the minimum dowry, scholars differed about it. A group held that there is no fixed minimum; rather, whatever may be sold or used as a price may be a dowry. This is the view of Rabi'ah, Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "Three handfuls of raisins is a dowry." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "If he gave her a whip as dowry, it is valid."

Another group said: it has a fixed measure, the nisab of theft, which is the view of Malik and Abu Hanifah, except that the nisab of theft according to Malik is three dirhams, and according to Abu Hanifah ten dirhams.

The evidence that it has no fixed minimum is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi reported to us, saying: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him), that a woman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have given myself to you." She stood for a long time. Then a man stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, marry her to me, if you have no need of her." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you have anything to give as a dower (sadaq, the bridal gift)?" He said: "I have nothing but this waist-wrapper of mine." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you give it to her, you will sit without a waist-wrapper, so look for something else." He said: "I cannot find anything." He said: "Look, even if it is an iron ring." He searched but found nothing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know any of the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes, such-and-such surah and such-and-such surah," naming the surahs. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have married her to you for what you know of the Qur'an." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Nikah, Bab Tazwij al-Mu'sir (the marriage of one who is poor): 9/131, and by Muslim in Kitab al-Nikah, Bab al-Sadaq wa Jawaz Kawnihi Ta'lim Qur'an, no. (1425): 2/1040-1041, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/117.]]

In this hadith is evidence that there is no minimum for the dower, because he said: "Look for something," and this indicates that any kind of property is permissible. He also said: "even if it is an iron ring," and an iron ring has no value except a small and trifling amount.

In the hadith is also evidence that teaching the Qur'an may be given as a dower. This is the view of al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him). Some scholars held that it is not permissible, and this is the view of the People of Opinion (ashab al-ra'y). Every action for which hiring is permissible, such as building, sewing and other work, may be made a dower. Abu Hanifa (may Allah be pleased with him) did not permit the usufruct of a free person to be made a dower. The hadith is a proof for those who permit it, after Allah the Exalted related about Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) that he married his daughter to Musa (peace be upon them both) on the condition of work, when He said: ﴿I intend to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine, on condition that you serve me for eight years﴾ [al-Qasas: 27].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 25:**

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford (ṭawl)﴾, that is, excess wealth and means, ﴿to marry the chaste (muḥṣanāt) free women﴾, ﴿the believing (mu'minat)﴾. Al-Kisa'i read ﴿muḥṣināt﴾ with a kasra on the ṣād wherever it occurs, except His words in this surah, ﴿and the married women (al-muḥṣanāt) from among women﴾. The others read all of them with a fatha on the ṣād. ﴿Then from among those whom your right hands possess of your young women (fatayatikum)﴾, that is, your female slaves (imā'ikum), ﴿the believing﴾.

That is: whoever cannot afford the dower of a free believing woman, let him marry a believing slave woman.

This indicates that it is not permissible for a free man to marry a slave woman except under two conditions. The first is that he does not find the dower of a free woman. The second is that he fears for himself ʿanat (distress), which is fornication (zina), because of His words at the end of the verse: ﴿That is for whoever among you fears ʿanat﴾. This is the view of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him. Ṭawus and ʿAmr ibn Dinar also said so, and Malik and al-Shafi'i adopted it.

The people of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y) permitted a free man to marry a slave woman unless he already has a free wife. A slave, however, may marry a slave woman even if he has a free wife or a slave wife. According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, it is not permissible for a slave if he has a free wife, just as it is not for a free man.

The verse also indicates that it is not permissible for a Muslim to marry a Scripturary (kitābiyya) slave woman, because He said: ﴿from among those whom your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾. He permitted marrying a slave woman on condition that she be believing. In another place He said: "The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them, and the chaste women (al-muḥṣanāt) from among the believers and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture" [al-Ma'idah: 5]. That is, the free women. He permitted marrying a Scripturary woman on condition that she be free. The people of opinion permitted a Muslim to marry a Scripturary slave woman. By consensus it is permissible to have sexual relations with her by right of ownership.

[﴿And Allah knows best your faith﴾, that is: do not probe the inner state of faith, but take what is apparent, for Allah knows best your faith.]

﴿You are one from another﴾. It was said: some of you are brothers to others. It was also said: all of you are from one soul, so do not disdain marrying slave women. ﴿So marry them﴾, meaning the slave women, ﴿with the permission of their people﴾, that is, their masters, ﴿and give them their wages (ujūrahunna)﴾, their dowers, ﴿in a fitting manner﴾, without delay or harm, ﴿chaste (muḥṣanāt)﴾, modest through marriage, ﴿not fornicators (musāfiḥāt)﴾, that is, not adulteresses, ﴿nor taking secret lovers (akhdān)﴾, that is, lovers with whom you commit fornication in secret. Al-Hasan said: the musāfiḥa is the one who goes with anyone who calls her. The one who takes lovers is the one who is exclusive to one man and commits fornication only with him. The Arabs used to forbid the first and permit the second. ﴿And when they are chaste (uḥṣinna)﴾: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read it with a fatha on the alif and the ṣād, meaning they guarded their private parts. Ibn Mas'ud said: they embraced Islam. The others read ﴿uḥṣinna﴾ with a ḍamma on the alif and a kasra on the ṣād, meaning they were married. ﴿And if they commit a flagrant act (fāḥisha)﴾, meaning fornication, ﴿then upon them is half of the punishment (ʿadhāb) for the chaste women﴾, that is, the punishment for free unmarried women if they commit fornication, ﴿of the punishment﴾, meaning the prescribed penalty (ḥadd). So the slave who commits fornication is flogged fifty lashes. Is he also exiled? There are two opinions on this. If we say he is exiled, then he is exiled for half a year according to the more correct view. There is no stoning for slaves.

It is narrated from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabi'a, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered me, along with a group of young men from Quraysh, to flog the slave girls (walā'id) of the Imara (slave women) fifty lashes for fornication. [The walīda is the female slave.]

According to most scholars, there is no distinction in the prescribed penalty for a slave between one who is married and one who is not. Some of them held that there is no prescribed penalty for an unmarried slave who commits fornication, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿If they commit a flagrant act, then upon them is half the punishment for the chaste women﴾. This was also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, and Ṭawus said so as well.

According to the others, the meaning of iḥṣān (chastity/protected status) is Islam. Even if the intended meaning is marriage, it is not meant that marriage is a condition for the obligation of the prescribed penalty. Rather, the intention is to point out that a slave, even if he is chaste through marriage, is not to be stoned; his punishment is only flogging, unlike a free person. The prescribed penalty for a slave woman is established by this verse, and that it is by flogging is shown in the report which ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us of: Ahmad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbdullah informed us, al-Layth narrated to me, from Sa'id, meaning al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "If the slave woman of any one of you commits fornication and her fornication is clear, let him flog her the prescribed penalty and not reproach her. Then if she commits it again, let him flog her the prescribed penalty and not reproach her. Then if she commits it a third time and her fornication is clear, let him sell her even for a rope of hair." [Reported by al-Bukhari in Sales, chapter on the sale of the mudabbar (conditionally freed slave): 4/421; Muslim in Ḥudūd, chapter on stoning the People of the Covenant (Jews) for fornication, no. 1703: 3/1328; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/297.]

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿That﴾, meaning marrying a slave woman when one lacks the means, ﴿is for whoever among you fears ʿanat﴾, meaning fornication, desiring hardship due to the overpowering of desire. ﴿But if you are patient﴾ regarding marrying slave women, being chaste, ﴿it is better for you﴾, so that the child is not born a slave. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

The Almighty's statement, ﴿God desires to make clear to you﴾, means: God desires that He make clear to you. This is like His statement, ﴿And I have been commanded to act justly between you﴾ [al-Shura 42:15], meaning: that I act justly. Likewise His statement, ﴿and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-An'am 6:71], and in another place He said, "and I have been commanded to submit" [Ghafir 40:66]. Here the particle *li-* (lam of purpose, with *an* understood) and *an* (that) introduce a verbal clause that functions as the object of the verb, so the verb in *li-yubayyina* is in the subjunctive, meaning "that He may make clear."

The meaning of the verse: God desires to make clear to you, that is, to explain to you the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs. 'Ata' said: He makes clear to you what brings you close to Him. Al-Kalbi said: He makes clear to you that abstaining from marrying slave women is better for you. ﴿And guide you﴾, that is, direct you. ﴿The ways (sunan)﴾, that is, the laws (shara'i'), ﴿of those before you﴾, regarding the prohibition of mothers, daughters and sisters, for these were forbidden to those before you.

It has also been said: ﴿and guide you﴾ to the upright religion (*al-milla al-hanifiyya*), which is the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. ﴿And turn to you in forgiveness﴾, that is, overlook what you committed before He made it clear to you. It has also been said: He brings you back from the disobedience in which you were to His obedience. And it has been said: He grants you success in repentance. ﴿And God is All-Knowing﴾ of the interests of His servants in the matters of their religion and their worldly life, ﴿All-Wise﴾ in what He arranges of their affairs.

﴿And Allah desires to turn to you [in forgiveness]﴾ if any shortfall has occurred from you in the matter of your religion. ﴿But those who follow their desires want you to deviate﴾ from the truth, ﴿a tremendous deviation﴾ by your committing what He has forbidden to you. They differed about who is meant by "those who follow desires." Al-Suddi said: they are the Jews and the Christians. Some said: they are the Magians, because they permit marriage to sisters and to the daughters of a brother or of a sister. Mujahid said: they are the fornicators, who want you to deviate from the truth so that you fornicate as they do. It was said: they are all the people of falsehood.

﴿Allah desires to lighten [the burden] for you﴾, that is, to make the rulings of the Sharia easy for you. He has indeed made it easy, as His Majesty said: ﴿And He relieves them of their burden﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I have been sent with the tolerant, easy monotheistic faith (al-hanifiyya al-samha)." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/266, from Abu Umama; and al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in al-Faqih wal-Mutafaqqih: 2/204; and al-Tabarani in al-Kabir. In its chain is Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani, who is weak. See Majma' al-Zawa'id: 5/279. The hadith is sound (hasan) due to the multiplicity of its chains and corroborating reports. See al-Nahj al-Sadid fi Takhrij Ahadith Taysir al-Aziz al-Hamid, pp. 333–334.]] ﴿And man was created weak﴾. Tawus, al-Kalbi and others said, regarding the matter of women: he cannot be patient without them. Ibn Kaysan said: ﴿and man was created weak﴾ means his desire and appetite sway him. Al-Hasan said: it means that he was created from a despised water, and its explanation is the words of Allah Most High: ﴿It is Allah who created you from weakness﴾ [al-Rum: 54].

The words of Allah Most High: ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾, that is, in what is unlawful, meaning by usury (riba), gambling, usurpation, theft, embezzlement and the like. It was said: it means corrupt contracts. ﴿Except that it be trade﴾. The people of Kufa read ﴿tijaratan﴾ in the accusative, as the predicate (khabar) of kana, meaning: except that the wealth be trade. The others read it in the nominative, meaning: except that a trade takes place (tijaratun). ﴿By mutual consent among you﴾, that is, by the willing hearts of each of you.
