And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/221–222.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 30–31:

﴿And whoever does that﴾ means: what has been mentioned before of the prohibited things, ﴿out of transgression and injustice﴾. Al-'udwan (transgression) is exceeding the limit, and al-zulm (injustice) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. ﴿Then We will cause him to enter﴾ means: We will cause him to enter in the Hereafter, ﴿a Fire﴾ in which he will be burned, ﴿and that is ever for Allah an easy matter﴾, meaning effortless.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden﴾. The scholars differed concerning the major sins whose avoidance Allah made an expiation for the minor sins. Abu 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Muqatil informed us: al-Nadr informed us: Shu'bah informed us: Firas said: I heard al-Sha'bi narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The major sins are: associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, killing a soul, and the perjury of the oath (al-yamin al-ghamus)" [Reported by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Aiman wal-Nudhur, bab al-yamin al-ghamus: 11/555, and in other places; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/85.]

Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musaddad informed us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal informed us: al-Jurayri informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" He said it three times. They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and disobedience to parents," and he was reclining and then sat up and said: "Beware, and false speech, beware, and false speech," and he kept repeating it until we said, "Would that he had remained silent." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Shahadat, bab ma qila fi shahadat al-zur: 5/261, and in al-Adab; and Muslim in al-Iman, bab bayan al-kaba'ir wa akbaruha, no. (87): 1/91; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/83-84.]

Abu 'Abd Allah Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Barti informed us: Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash and Mansur and Wasil al-Ahdab, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, from 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest in the sight of Allah?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child fearing that he will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." [Then Allah revealed the confirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ words: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery﴾] [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Tafsir, tafsir surat al-Furqan, bab "and those who do not invoke with Allah another deity": 8/492, and Muslim in al-Iman, bab kawn al-shirk aqbah al-dhunub, no. (86): 1/90; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/82.] etc.

Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah informed us: Sulayman related to me, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Avoid the seven destructive things." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming riba, consuming the property of an orphan, fleeing on the day of the battle-line, and slandering chaste, believing, heedless women." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Wasaya, bab qawl Allah ta'ala: "Indeed those who consume the property of orphans unjustly": 5/393, and Muslim in al-Iman, bab al-kaba'ir, no. (89): 1/92; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/86.]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The greatest of the major sins are: associating partners with Allah, feeling secure from the plan of Allah, despairing of the mercy of Allah, and losing hope in the comfort of Allah. [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 8/242-244; al-Tabarani in al-Kabir with a sound chain, see Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/104; 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 10/459-460; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/87. Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir: 1/485, "It is sound up to Ibn Mas'ud, without doubt."]

Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Baghawi informed us: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us: Shu'bah informed us, from Sa'id ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Among the major sins is that a man curses his parents." They said: "How does a man curse his parents?" He said: "A man curses another's father, so he curses his father and curses his mother." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, bab la yasubb al-rajul walidayhi: 10/403, and Muslim in al-Iman, bab bayan al-kaba'ir, no. (90): 1/92; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/16-17.]

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that a man asked Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, about the major sins: "Are they seven?" He said: "They are nearer to seven hundred. There is no major sin with seeking forgiveness, and no minor sin with persistence." He also said: "Everything disobeyed by which Allah is disobeyed is a major sin. Whoever commits any of them should seek forgiveness, for Allah will not keep anyone of this Ummah in the Fire forever except one who has turned away from Islam, or denies an obligation, or denies the divine decree." [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 8/245.]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Whatever Allah the Exalted has forbidden in this surah up to His words: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden﴾, is a major sin.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: They are every sin which Allah concluded with a Fire, or wrath, or a curse, or a punishment.

al-Dahhak said: They are whatever Allah has threatened with a prescribed penalty in this world or a punishment in the Hereafter.

al-Hasan [in A: "al-Husayn"] ibn al-Fadl said: They are whatever Allah has named in the Qur'an as great or mighty, such as His words: ﴿Indeed, it was a great sin (hub kabir)﴾ [al-Nisa': 2], ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin (khit'an kabir)﴾ [al-Isra': 31], ﴿Indeed, associating partners is a great injustice (zulm 'azim)﴾ [Luqman: 13], ﴿Indeed, your scheming is great (kayd 'azim)﴾ [Yusuf: 28], ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander (buhtan 'azim)﴾ [al-Nur: 16], ﴿Indeed, that was with Allah an enormity (kana 'indallahi 'azima)﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53].

Sufyan al-Thawri said: The major sins are those which involve wrongs between you and the servants, and the minor sins are those between you and Allah the Exalted, because Allah is Generous and pardons. He cited what Shaykh Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Kirmani informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'id informed us: al-Husayn ibn Dawud al-Balkhi informed us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A caller will call from the depths of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection: O nation of Muhammad, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has pardoned you all, believing men and believing women. Forgive one another your wrongs and enter Paradise by My mercy." [A fabricated (mawdu') hadith; its chain includes al-Husayn ibn Dawud, Abu 'Ali al-Balkhi, of whom al-Khatib said: "He is not trustworthy, and his hadith is fabricated." See Mizan al-I'tidal: 1/534. The author reported it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/197. See also al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah wa al-Mawdu'ah of al-Albani: 3/439, no. (1279).]

Malik ibn Mighwal said: The major sins are the sins of the people of innovation, and the minor sins (sayyi'at) are the sins of the people of the Sunnah.

It has been said: The major sins are sins committed deliberately, and the minor sins are error, forgetfulness, what one is compelled to do, and the whisperings of the soul, which are lifted from this Ummah.

It has been said: The major sins are the sins of those who consider them lawful, like the sin of Iblis, and the minor sins are the sins of those who seek forgiveness, like the sin of Adam, peace be upon him.

al-Suddi said: The major sins are what Allah has forbidden among the grave sins, and the sayyi'at are their preliminaries and consequences, which both the righteous and the wicked share, such as a glance, a touch, a kiss, and the like. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The two eyes commit adultery, the two hands commit adultery, the two feet commit adultery, and the private part either confirms that or denies it." [Reported by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/412, 2/343, from Abu Hurayrah; and al-Tabarani, Abu Ya'la, al-Bazzar and Ibn Hibban from Abu Hurayrah. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' 6/256: its chain is good; al-Mundhiri said it is sound. See also Fayd al-Qadir of al-Munawi: 4/399, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/138.]

It has been said: The major sins are what people consider trivial, and the minor sins are what they regard as grave and therefore fear to commit, as Abu al-Walid informed us... as Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu al-Walid informed us: Mahdi ibn Maymun informed us, from Anas, who said: "Indeed you do deeds which in your eyes are finer than hair, yet we used to count them among the destructive sins in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, bab ma yutaqa min muhaqqarat al-dhunub: 11/329, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/398.]

It has been said: The major sins are polytheism and what leads to it, and what is below polytheism is the sayyi'at. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ (al-Nisa' 48, 116).

And His words, the Exalted: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your bad deeds (sayyi'atikum)﴾, meaning: from one prayer to the next, from one Friday to the next, and from Ramadan to Ramadan.

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Abu Sakhr, that 'Umar ibn Ishaq, client of Za'idah, narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them, when the major sins are avoided." [Reported by Muslim in al-Taharah, bab al-salawat al-khams, no. (233): 1/209; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/177.]

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We will cause you to enter an honourable entrance﴾, meaning: a good one, which is Paradise. The people of Medina read ﴿mudkhalan﴾ with a fatha on the mim here and in al-Hajj, meaning the place of entry. The rest read it with a damma as a verbal noun (masdar) in the sense of "causing to enter."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 30–31:

﴿And whoever does that﴾ means: what has been mentioned before of the prohibited things, ﴿out of transgression and injustice﴾. Al-'udwan (transgression) is exceeding the limit, and al-zulm (injustice) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. ﴿Then We will cause him to enter﴾ means: We will cause him to enter in the Hereafter, ﴿a Fire﴾ in which he will be burned, ﴿and that is ever for Allah an easy matter﴾, meaning effortless.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden﴾. The scholars differed concerning the major sins whose avoidance Allah made an expiation for the minor sins. Abu 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Muqatil informed us: al-Nadr informed us: Shu'bah informed us: Firas said: I heard al-Sha'bi narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The major sins are: associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, killing a soul, and the perjury of the oath (al-yamin al-ghamus)" [Reported by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Aiman wal-Nudhur, bab al-yamin al-ghamus: 11/555, and in other places; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/85.]

Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musaddad informed us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal informed us: al-Jurayri informed us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" He said it three times. They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and disobedience to parents," and he was reclining and then sat up and said: "Beware, and false speech, beware, and false speech," and he kept repeating it until we said, "Would that he had remained silent." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Shahadat, bab ma qila fi shahadat al-zur: 5/261, and in al-Adab; and Muslim in al-Iman, bab bayan al-kaba'ir wa akbaruha, no. (87): 1/91; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/83-84.]

Abu 'Abd Allah Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us: Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Barti informed us: Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us: Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash and Mansur and Wasil al-Ahdab, from Abu Wa'il, from 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, from 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest in the sight of Allah?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child fearing that he will eat with you." I said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." [Then Allah revealed the confirmation of the Prophet's ﷺ words: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery﴾] [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Tafsir, tafsir surat al-Furqan, bab "and those who do not invoke with Allah another deity": 8/492, and Muslim in al-Iman, bab kawn al-shirk aqbah al-dhunub, no. (86): 1/90; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/82.] etc.

Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah informed us: Sulayman related to me, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Avoid the seven destructive things." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are they?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming riba, consuming the property of an orphan, fleeing on the day of the battle-line, and slandering chaste, believing, heedless women." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Wasaya, bab qawl Allah ta'ala: "Indeed those who consume the property of orphans unjustly": 5/393, and Muslim in al-Iman, bab al-kaba'ir, no. (89): 1/92; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/86.]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The greatest of the major sins are: associating partners with Allah, feeling secure from the plan of Allah, despairing of the mercy of Allah, and losing hope in the comfort of Allah. [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 8/242-244; al-Tabarani in al-Kabir with a sound chain, see Majma' al-Zawa'id: 1/104; 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 10/459-460; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/87. Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir: 1/485, "It is sound up to Ibn Mas'ud, without doubt."]

Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Baghawi informed us: 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us: Shu'bah informed us, from Sa'id ibn Ibrahim, who said: I heard Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrate from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Among the major sins is that a man curses his parents." They said: "How does a man curse his parents?" He said: "A man curses another's father, so he curses his father and curses his mother." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, bab la yasubb al-rajul walidayhi: 10/403, and Muslim in al-Iman, bab bayan al-kaba'ir, no. (90): 1/92; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/16-17.]

And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that a man asked Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, about the major sins: "Are they seven?" He said: "They are nearer to seven hundred. There is no major sin with seeking forgiveness, and no minor sin with persistence." He also said: "Everything disobeyed by which Allah is disobeyed is a major sin. Whoever commits any of them should seek forgiveness, for Allah will not keep anyone of this Ummah in the Fire forever except one who has turned away from Islam, or denies an obligation, or denies the divine decree." [Reported by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 8/245.]

And 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: Whatever Allah the Exalted has forbidden in this surah up to His words: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden﴾, is a major sin.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: They are every sin which Allah concluded with a Fire, or wrath, or a curse, or a punishment.

al-Dahhak said: They are whatever Allah has threatened with a prescribed penalty in this world or a punishment in the Hereafter.

al-Hasan [in A: "al-Husayn"] ibn al-Fadl said: They are whatever Allah has named in the Qur'an as great or mighty, such as His words: ﴿Indeed, it was a great sin (hub kabir)﴾ [al-Nisa': 2], ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin (khit'an kabir)﴾ [al-Isra': 31], ﴿Indeed, associating partners is a great injustice (zulm 'azim)﴾ [Luqman: 13], ﴿Indeed, your scheming is great (kayd 'azim)﴾ [Yusuf: 28], ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander (buhtan 'azim)﴾ [al-Nur: 16], ﴿Indeed, that was with Allah an enormity (kana 'indallahi 'azima)﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53].

Sufyan al-Thawri said: The major sins are those which involve wrongs between you and the servants, and the minor sins are those between you and Allah the Exalted, because Allah is Generous and pardons. He cited what Shaykh Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ali al-Kirmani informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sa'id informed us: al-Husayn ibn Dawud al-Balkhi informed us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A caller will call from the depths of the Throne on the Day of Resurrection: O nation of Muhammad, indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has pardoned you all, believing men and believing women. Forgive one another your wrongs and enter Paradise by My mercy." [A fabricated (mawdu') hadith; its chain includes al-Husayn ibn Dawud, Abu 'Ali al-Balkhi, of whom al-Khatib said: "He is not trustworthy, and his hadith is fabricated." See Mizan al-I'tidal: 1/534. The author reported it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/197. See also al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah wa al-Mawdu'ah of al-Albani: 3/439, no. (1279).]

Malik ibn Mighwal said: The major sins are the sins of the people of innovation, and the minor sins (sayyi'at) are the sins of the people of the Sunnah.

It has been said: The major sins are sins committed deliberately, and the minor sins are error, forgetfulness, what one is compelled to do, and the whisperings of the soul, which are lifted from this Ummah.

It has been said: The major sins are the sins of those who consider them lawful, like the sin of Iblis, and the minor sins are the sins of those who seek forgiveness, like the sin of Adam, peace be upon him.

al-Suddi said: The major sins are what Allah has forbidden among the grave sins, and the sayyi'at are their preliminaries and consequences, which both the righteous and the wicked share, such as a glance, a touch, a kiss, and the like. The Prophet ﷺ said: "The two eyes commit adultery, the two hands commit adultery, the two feet commit adultery, and the private part either confirms that or denies it." [Reported by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/412, 2/343, from Abu Hurayrah; and al-Tabarani, Abu Ya'la, al-Bazzar and Ibn Hibban from Abu Hurayrah. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' 6/256: its chain is good; al-Mundhiri said it is sound. See also Fayd al-Qadir of al-Munawi: 4/399, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/138.]

It has been said: The major sins are what people consider trivial, and the minor sins are what they regard as grave and therefore fear to commit, as Abu al-Walid informed us... as Abu 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu al-Walid informed us: Mahdi ibn Maymun informed us, from Anas, who said: "Indeed you do deeds which in your eyes are finer than hair, yet we used to count them among the destructive sins in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, bab ma yutaqa min muhaqqarat al-dhunub: 11/329, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/398.]

It has been said: The major sins are polytheism and what leads to it, and what is below polytheism is the sayyi'at. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ (al-Nisa' 48, 116).

And His words, the Exalted: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your bad deeds (sayyi'atikum)﴾, meaning: from one prayer to the next, from one Friday to the next, and from Ramadan to Ramadan.

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: Harun ibn Sa'id al-Ayli related to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Abu Sakhr, that 'Umar ibn Ishaq, client of Za'idah, narrated to him from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: "The five daily prayers, and Friday to Friday, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what lies between them, when the major sins are avoided." [Reported by Muslim in al-Taharah, bab al-salawat al-khams, no. (233): 1/209; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/177.]

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And We will cause you to enter an honourable entrance﴾, meaning: a good one, which is Paradise. The people of Medina read ﴿mudkhalan﴾ with a fatha on the mim here and in al-Hajj, meaning the place of entry. The rest read it with a damma as a verbal noun (masdar) in the sense of "causing to enter."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 32:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾ to the end of the verse. Mujahid said: Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, men fight in battle and we do not fight, and they have double what we have of the inheritance. If only we were men, we would fight as they fight and take from the inheritance the same as they take." So this verse was revealed.

It is also said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made for the male a portion equal to the share of two females in inheritance, the women said, "We have more right to, and more need of, the increase than men, because we are weak and they are stronger and more capable of seeking livelihood." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others﴾.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: When His saying was revealed: ﴿For the male is a portion equal to the share of two females﴾, the men said, "We hope to be preferred over the women in the Hereafter through our good deeds, so that our reward will be double the reward of the women, just as we were preferred over them in inheritance." Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For men there is a share of what they have earned﴾ of reward, ﴿and for women there is a share of what they have earned﴾.

Its meaning: men and women are equal in reward in the Hereafter, because a good deed is repaid tenfold, and men and women share in this, even though men are preferred over women in this world.

It is also said: its meaning is: for men there is a share of what they have earned of the matter of jihad, and for women there is a share of what they have earned of obedience to their husbands and guarding their chastity. That is, if men have the excellence of jihad, then women have the excellence of obedience to their husbands and guarding their chastity.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾. Ibn Kathir, al-Kisa'i and others read "wasalu," "sal," and "fasal" when a waw or fa' precedes the sin, without a hamza, transferring the vowel of the hamza to the sin; the rest read it with a sukun on the sin and with a hamza. Allah the Exalted forbade wishing for what leads to envy, and envy is to wish for the removal of a blessing from its owner and to wish it for oneself, and this is forbidden. Ghibta (admiring emulation) is to wish for oneself something like what one's companion has, and this is permissible. Al-Kalbi said: a man should not wish for his brother's wealth, nor his wife, nor his servant, but let him say, "O Allah, provide me with the like of it." This is so in the Torah and so in the Qur'an. His saying: ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "And ask Allah of His bounty" means: of His provision. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: of His worship, meaning the request for success in worship. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: He did not command asking except that He would give.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to every one We have appointed heirs (mawali)﴾, meaning: and for every one of the men and the women We have appointed heirs (mawali), that is, a kinship group (ʿusbah) who receive ﴿from what the parents and the relatives leave behind﴾. "The parents and the relatives" are the ones who inherit. [It is also said: its meaning is "And to every one We have appointed heirs (mawali)", that is, inheritors (warathah); "from what [they] left" means from those whom they left behind, and "ma" carries the meaning of "min" (from). Then he explained "the mawali" by saying: "the parents and the relatives" are the inheritors.]

﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾. The people of Kufa read ﴿ʿaqadat﴾ without an alif, meaning: your oaths bound them. The others read: "ʿaqadat aymanukum" (ʿaqadat with an alif). Al-muʿaqadah means al-muhalafah (alliance) and al-muʿahadah (covenant). Al-aymān is the plural of yamīn, which means both the hand and an oath. This is because, at the time of alliance, they would take one another by the hand as a pledge of fidelity and of adherence to the covenant. The alliance among them was such that a man in the Jahiliyyah would bind himself to another man, saying: "My blood is your blood, my ruin is your ruin, my vengeance is your vengeance, my war is your war, my peace is your peace; you inherit from me and I inherit from you; you seek retribution on my behalf and I seek it on yours; you pay blood-money for me and I pay it for you." The ally would then receive a sixth (sudus) of the ally's property. This was established at the beginning of Islam. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then give them their share﴾, that is, give them their portion of the inheritance. Then this was abrogated by His saying, exalted is He: "And those related by blood are closer to one another in the Book of Allah" (al-Ahzab: 6).

Ibrahim and Mujahid said: it means "then give them their share" of support and assistance (al-nasr wa al-rifd), and there is no inheritance. On this view, this verse is not abrogated, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fulfil the contracts﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 1). The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said in his sermon on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Do not create a new alliance in Islam; and whatever alliance existed in the Jahiliyyah, hold fast to it, for Islam has only increased it in strength." [This is a composite of two hadiths. Al-Tabari narrated it from Qays ibn ʿAsim that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whatever alliance existed in the Jahiliyyah, hold fast to it" (8/283). And from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet ﷺ said in the sermon of the day of the Conquest: "Fulfil the alliance, for Islam only increases it in strength, and do not create an alliance in Islam" (8/284). On this subject, there is also a report from Jubayr ibn Mutʿim, traced to the Prophet: "There is no alliance in Islam," narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). See: al-Kafi al-Shaf by Ibn Hajar, p. 42; Tafsir al-Tabari with the annotation of Mahmud Shakir: 8/283–284; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/510.]

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: This verse was revealed concerning those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made brothers between, from the Muhajirun and the Ansar, when they came to Madinah; they used to inherit from one another by that brotherhood to the exclusion of blood-relatives. When ﴿And to every one We have appointed heirs﴾ was revealed, it was abrogated. Then He said: ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you, give them their share﴾, which is support, assistance and sincere counsel, while inheritance has gone; so he bequeaths to him. [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the commentary, Surah al-Nisa, chapter "And to every one We have appointed heirs..." (8/247). See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/511.] Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: They used to inherit through adoption (tabanni), and this verse concerned that, then it was abrogated.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness.﴾

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 4, verse 34:

His statement, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾, and the rest of the verse. It was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', who was one of the nuqaba' (chiefs of the Ansar), and his wife Habibah bint Zayd ibn Abi Zuhayr. This is related by Muqatil. Al-Kalbi said: his wife was Habibah bint Muhammad ibn Maslamah. The reason was that she showed disobedience (nushuz) toward him, so he struck her. Her father went with her to the Prophet ﷺ [and said: "I gave him my noble daughter as a bed partner, and he struck her." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Let her take retribution from her husband." So she turned back with her father] [[Omitted in manuscript (B).]] to take retribution from him. Then Jibril (peace be upon him) came [and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Return. This is Jibril; he has brought me something," and Allah revealed this verse] [[Omitted in manuscript (B).]]. The Prophet ﷺ then said: "We wanted one matter, and Allah wanted another, and what Allah wants is better," and he lifted the retaliation (qisas) [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 144.]].

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾, meaning: they have authority over disciplining them. Al-Qawwam and al-Qayyim have the same meaning, but al-Qawwam is more intensive. It means one who takes charge of their welfare, management and discipline.

﴿by that in which Allah has given preference to some of them over others﴾: meaning, Allah has preferred men over women through greater intellect, religion and guardianship. It was also said: through testimony, based on His statement: ﴿And if there are not two men, then a man and two women﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282]. It was also said: through jihad; it was said: through acts of worship such as Friday prayer and congregational prayer; and it was said: that a man may marry four wives while a woman may have only one husband; it was said: through the fact that divorce is in his hand; it was said: through inheritance; it was said: through blood money (diyah); and it was said: through prophethood.

﴿and by that which they spend from their wealth﴾: meaning, giving the bridal gift (mahr) and maintenance (nafaqah). Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us, saying: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Saffar informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Bartiyy informed us; Abu Hudhayfah informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Dhabyan, that Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If I were to command anyone to prostrate to anyone, I would command the woman to prostrate to her husband" [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Nikah, chapter on the husband's right over the wife, no. (1853): 1/595; authenticated by Ibn Hibban, no. (1290), Mawarid al-Zam'an p. 314; and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/381 from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, and 5/227-228 from Mu'adh ibn Jabal; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/158.]].

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾, meaning: obedient. ﴿guarding in secret﴾, meaning: guarding their chastity in the absence of their husbands. It was also said: guarding their husbands' secrets. ﴿by that which Allah has guarded﴾: Abu Ja'far recited it as ﴿by that which Allah has guarded﴾ with a fatha (naṣb), meaning: they guard Allah in obedience. The recitation of the majority is with a damma (raf'), meaning: by that which Allah has guarded them, through the husbands' charge concerning their rights and their command to pay the bridal gift and maintenance.

It was also said: they guard in secret by the guarding of Allah. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; Abu Abdullah ibn Fanjawayh informed us; Umar ibn al-Khattab informed us; Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Musuhi informed us; al-Harith ibn Abdullah informed us; Abu Ma'shar informed us, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The best of women is the woman who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you in her own person and in your wealth" [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Nikah, chapter on which women are best: 6/68; authenticated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/161-162 on the condition of Muslim; and al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 8/295. Ibn Hajar also attributed it to al-Bazzar with the wording "The righteous woman, when one looks at her..." and said: Abu Dawud, al-Hakim and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the transmission of Mujahid from Ibn Abbas, and there is a similar report from Abu Umamah in Ibn Majah, but its isnad is weak. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 43.]], then he recited: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women﴾, the verse.

﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz﴾: their disobedience. The root of nushuz is arrogance and elevation, from which comes nashz, meaning an elevated place. ﴿then admonish them﴾: by warning them of Allah and admonishing them with words. ﴿and forsake them﴾: meaning, if they do not desist from that through words, then forsake them ﴿in the beds﴾. Ibn Abbas said: he turns his back to her in the bed and does not speak to her. Others said: he withdraws from her to another bed. ﴿and strike them﴾: meaning, if they do not desist with the forsaking, then strike them with a strike that is not severe and not disfiguring. Ata said: a strike with a siwak (toothstick). There has come in a hadith from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The woman's right is that you feed her when you eat, clothe her when you clothe yourself, do not strike the face, do not revile her, and do not forsake her except within the house" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Nikah, chapter on the woman's right over her husband: 3/67-68; and Ibn Majah in al-Nikah, chapter on the woman's right over the husband, no. (1850): 1/594; and Ibn Hibban, no. (1286), p. 313 of Mawarid al-Zam'an; authenticated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/187-188, and al-Dhahabi agreed. al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Kubra. Imam Ahmad also narrated it in al-Musnad: 4/446-447 from Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/160.]].

﴿Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them﴾: meaning, do not inflict wrongs upon them. Ibn Uyaynah said: do not burden them with your love, for the heart is not in their hands.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Great﴾: exalted above charging His servants with what they cannot bear. The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that the husband combines admonition, forsaking and striking toward her. Some scholars adhered to its apparent meaning and said: when nushuz appears from her, he combines these actions. They interpreted fear in His statement ﴿those from whom you fear nushuz﴾ as knowledge, like His statement: ﴿And whoever fears from a testator some deviation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 182], meaning: knows. Others interpreted fear as apprehension rather than actual knowledge, like His statement: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ [al-Anfal: 58]. They said: these actions follow the order of offenses. If he fears her nushuz, meaning its signs appear in her through harshness and bad conduct, he admonishes her. If she shows nushuz, he forsakes her. If she persists in that, he strikes her.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾. That is, a breach between the spouses. [Fear here means certainty, and it is said that it means suspicion: "if you suspect a breach between them."]

The summary of this is that when a breach appears between the spouses and their situation becomes unclear, and the husband neither forgives nor separates, and the wife neither fulfils her right nor offers compensation, and they both slide into what is not permissible, in word or deed, then the ruler (al-Imam) sends an arbiter (hakam) from his family to the husband and an arbiter from her family to the wife, two free and just men. Each arbiter is to find out the opinion of the one he has been sent to, whether his desire is for reconciliation (wisla) or for separation. Then the two arbiters meet and implement whatever their joint opinion agrees upon as good. This is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause them to agree﴾. That is, the two arbiters. ﴿Allah will cause them to agree﴾, that is, the spouses. It is also said: the two arbiters.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted.﴾

[Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Kisa'i informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; al-Thaqafi informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from] [The isnad is missing from manuscript (A) between the bracketed points, and this omission continues to the end of folio 86a.] Ubaidah, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers﴾. He said: A man and a woman came to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and each of them was accompanied by a group of people. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, ordered them, and they sent an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. Then he said to the two arbiters: "Do you know what is incumbent upon you? If you see that you should bring them together, then bring them together; and if you see that you should separate them, then separate them." The woman said: "I am content with the Book of Allah, with whatever is upon me in it and whatever is mine." The man said: "As for separation, no." Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "You have lied, by Allah, until you acknowledge the same as what she has acknowledged." [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir 8/320-321; al-Shafi'i in al-Umm 5/177, where he said: "The hadith of Ali is established according to us"; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 7/305-306. Its isnad is sound. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah 9/189-190.]

There is a difference of opinion concerning whether it is permissible to send the two arbiters without the consent of the spouses. The sounder of the two views is that it is not permissible except with their consent. The husband's arbiter may not divorce without the husband's consent, and the wife's arbiter may not obtain a khul' (divorce in exchange for compensation) using her property without her permission. This is the view of the ashab al-ra'y (proponents of personal reasoning). The reason is that when the man said, "As for separation, no," Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said, "You have lied, until you acknowledge the same as what she has acknowledged." Thus it is established that the implementation of the matter depends upon his acknowledgement and consent.

The second view: it is permissible to send the two arbiters without the consent of the spouses, and the husband's arbiter may divorce without the husband's consent, and the wife's arbiter may arrange a khul' without her consent, if they see that it is good. This is like a judge who rules between two litigants even if the ruling does not conform to their wishes. This is the view of Malik. Those who hold this view say: What Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, meant when he said to the man, "until you acknowledge," is not that his consent is a condition. Rather, its meaning is that the woman was content with what is in the Book of Allah. [So the man said, "As for separation, no," meaning: separation is not in the Book of Allah.] Ali said, "You have lied," because he denied that separation is in the Book of Allah, whereas it is in the Book of Allah. [For the saying of Allah the Exalted, ﴿Allah will cause them to agree﴾, encompasses separation and other things.] This is because agreement (tawfiq) means that each of them comes out from wrongdoing, and this is sometimes by separation and sometimes by the good state of their union.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 36:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Worship Allah﴾, that is: make Him one (wahhidu-hu) and obey Him, ﴿and associate nothing with Him﴾ [Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi related to us, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bishran informed us, Ali Abu Isma'il Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi informed us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Maymun al-Awdi] [[What is between the brackets is from (A).]] from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I was riding behind the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said: "Do you know, O Mu'adh, what is the right of Allah over the people?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The right of Allah over them is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Do you know, O Mu'adh, what is the right of the people over Allah if they do that?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The right of the people over Allah is that He does not punish them." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not give good news to the people?" He said: "Leave them to work." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jihad, chapter on the names of the horse and the donkey: 6/58, and in Tawhid, chapter on what has come concerning the Prophet's (ﷺ) supplication for his community: 13/347; and Muslim in Iman, chapter on the proof that whoever dies upholding tawhid enters Paradise with certainty, nos. (48–50), 1/58–59. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/93.]].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and to parents, good treatment﴾, meaning: kindness and tenderness toward them, ﴿and to near kin﴾, that is: be good to near kin, ﴿and orphans and the needy﴾ [Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Amr ibn Zurarah informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Hazim informed us, from his father, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from the chains of these hadiths in (A).]] "I and the one who cares for an orphan will be in Paradise like this," and he pointed with his index and middle fingers and separated them slightly.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Adab, chapter on the virtue of one who supports an orphan: 10/463, and Muslim in Zuhd and Raqa'iq from Abu Hurayrah, chapter on kindness to the widow and the needy, no. (2983): 4/2287. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/43.]]

[Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i related to us, Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us, Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Khallal informed us, Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Ayyub, from Abd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from the chains of these hadiths in (A).]] from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever wipes the head of an orphan, he wipes it only for Allah's sake, he has good deeds for every hair his hand passes over; and whoever is good to an orphan girl or orphan boy in his care, I and he will be in Paradise like these two," and he joined two of his fingers. [[Narrated by Ahmad: 5/250, 265, and al-Haythami also attributed it to al-Tabarani, saying: in it is Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani, who is weak. Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/160. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/44.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the neighbor who is near of kin﴾, that is: the neighbor who is a relative, ﴿and the neighbor who is a stranger﴾, that is: the distant one with whom you have no kinship. [Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi related to us, Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, Abu al-Qasim Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni who said: I heard] Talhah say: Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have two neighbors; to which of them should I send a gift?" He said: "To the one whose door is nearer to you." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Adab, chapter on the right of the neighbor in the nearness of doors: 10/447.]]

Our teacher, the imam Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri, informed us, Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Isfarayini informed us, Abu Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq informed us, Yazid ibn Sinan informed us, Uthman ibn Umar informed us, Abu Amir al-Khazzaz informed us, from Abu Imran al-Jawni, from Abd Allah ibn al-Samit, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face; and when you cook a broth, add more water to it and give some of it to your neighbors." [[Narrated by Muslim in Birr and Silah, chapter on the recommendation of a cheerful face when meeting, abridged, no. (2626): 4/2026; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/197.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Minhal informed us, Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us, Umar ibn Muhammad informed us, from his father, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gabriel never ceased enjoining me concerning the neighbor, until I thought he would make him an heir." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Adab, chapter on the injunction concerning the neighbor: 10/441; and Muslim in Birr and Silah, chapter on the injunction concerning the neighbor and kindness to him, no. (2625): 4/2025; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/71.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the companion by your side﴾, meaning: the fellow traveler, as said by Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and a group, and Ikrimah and Qatadah. Ali, Abd Allah and al-Nakha'i said: it is the wife who is beside him. Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Zayd said: it is the one who accompanies you hoping for your benefit.

﴿and the wayfarer﴾. It was said: he is the traveler, because he is constantly on the road (al-sabil). Most scholars hold that he is the guest. Our teacher, the imam Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri, informed us, Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan al-Isfarayini informed us, Abu Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq informed us, Shu'ayb ibn Amr al-Dimashqi informed us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, that he heard Nafi' ibn Jubayr, from Abu Shurayh al-Khuza'i, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him be good to his neighbor; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, chapter on the injunction concerning the neighbor, p. 38; and Muslim in Iman, chapter on urging the honoring of the neighbor and the guest, no. (77): 1/96.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Shurayh al-Ka'bi, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbor; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or remain silent; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honor his guest: his entitlement is a day and a night, and hospitality is three days, and whatever is beyond that is charity. It is not lawful for him to stay with him until he causes him hardship." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Adab, chapter on whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should not harm his neighbor: 1/445; and Muslim in Iman, chapter on urging the honoring of the neighbor, no. (74): 1/68.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and what your right hands possess﴾, that is: the slaves, be good to them. Our teacher Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us, Abu al-Abbas al-Tahhan informed us, Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Quraysh informed us, Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Makki informed us, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us, Yazid informed us, from Hammam, from Qatadah, from Salih Abu al-Khalil, from Safinah, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he used to say during his illness: "The prayer, and what your right hands possess." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in Wasaya, chapter on whether the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a bequest: 2/900–901, from Anas and from Ali with a different wording. He said in al-Zawa'id: its chain is good, because Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam falls short of the level of those with full precision, and the rest of its narrators meet the conditions of the two shaykhs. And Ahmad narrated it: 1/78 from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and 3/17 from Anas.]] He began to speak, but his tongue could no longer express it.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Umar ibn Hafs informed us, my father informed us, al-A'mash informed us, from al-Ma'rur, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I saw him wearing a cloak, and his slave wearing a cloak. I said: "If only you took this and wore it, they would be a matching suit, and you gave him another garment." He said: "There was a dispute between me and a man, and his mother was a non-Arab, so I reviled her, and he complained of me to the Prophet (ﷺ). He said to me: 'Did you revile so-and-so?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Did you revile his mother?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'You are a man in whom is the ignorance (jahiliyyah).' I said: 'Even in my present state, at this old age?' He said: 'Yes. They are your brothers whom Allah has placed under your authority. Whoever has his brother under his control, let him feed him from what he eats, clothe him with what he wears, and not burden him with work that overwhelms him; and if he burdens him with such work, let him help him with it.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Adab, chapter on what is forbidden of insult and cursing: 10/465, and elsewhere; and Muslim in Iman, chapter on feeding the slave from what one eats…, no. (1661): 3/1282–1283; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/339–340.]]

Our teacher, the imam Abu al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, informed us, Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hafs al-Tajir informed us, Sahl ibn Ammar informed us, Yazid ibn Harun informed us, Sadaqah ibn Musa informed us, from Farqad al-Sabakhi, from Murrah al-Tayyib, from Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "One who treats his slaves badly will not enter Paradise." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Birr, chapter on what has come concerning kindness to the servant: 6/77, and he said: this is a gharib hadith; and Ibn Majah in Adab, chapter on kindness to slaves, no. (3691): 2/1271, and he said in al-Zawa'id: in its chain is Farqad al-Sabakhi, who, although Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy in one narration, he weakened him in another. Al-Bukhari and others also weakened him. Ahmad narrated it: 1/4 and in other places, and Abu Bakr al-Marwazi in Musnad al-Siddiq, nos. (97–99), pp. 138–140. Al-Haythami said: al-Bazzar and Abu Ya'la narrated it, and in it is Farqad al-Sabakhi (in al-Mizan, al-Sanji), who is weak. Majma' al-Zawa'id: 4/236. Al-Suyuti graded it hasan in al-Jami' al-Saghir; see Fayd al-Qadir: 6/449.]]

﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful﴾. Al-mukhtal: the arrogant. Al-fakhur: one who boasts over people without right, out of arrogance. He mentioned this after mentioning the rights, because the arrogant person withholds the right out of arrogance.

Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i related to us, Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us, Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "While a man was strutting in two cloaks, admiring himself, Allah caused the earth to swallow him, and he will keep sinking into it until the Day of Resurrection." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Libas, chapter on whoever trails his garment out of pride: 10/258; and Muslim in Libas and Zinah, chapter on the prohibition of strutting in walking while admiring one's clothes, no. (2088): 3/1654, and the wording is his. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/320–321.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Nafi', from Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will not look on the Day of Resurrection at one who trails his garment out of pride." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Libas, chapter on the saying of Allah, "Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants?": 10/258 and elsewhere; and Muslim in Libas, chapter on the prohibition of trailing garments out of pride, no. (2085): 3/1651. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/9–10.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 37:

﴿Those who are niggardly﴾ Al-bukhl (stinginess) in the language of the Arabs is withholding from the one who asks some of what one possesses, and in the Shari'ah (sacred law) it is withholding what is obligatory. ﴿and enjoin upon people niggardliness﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿bil-bakhal﴾ with a fatha on the ba' and the kha', and likewise in Surat al-Hadid. The others recited it with a damma on the ba' and a sukun on the kha'. It was revealed concerning the Jews who were niggardly in explaining the description of Muhammad ﷺ and concealed it [[See al-Tabari: 8/352, and Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 145-146.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: This refers to concealing knowledge [[See al-Tabari: 8/352, and Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 145-146.]].

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Ibn Zayd said: It was revealed concerning Kardam ibn Zayd, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut, Usamah ibn Habib, Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi' and Bahri ibn Amr. They used to come to men of the Ansar and mix with them, and they would say: "Do not spend your wealth, for we fear poverty for you, and you do not know what will happen." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[See al-Tabari: 8/353, Asbab al-Nuzul p. 146, al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/352.]]: ﴿and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾, meaning wealth. It is said: it means they are niggardly with charity. ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 38–40:**

﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people and do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾. The position (i'rab) of "alladhina" (those who) is accusative, in coordination with "alladhina yabkhaluna" (those who are stingy). It was also said that it is genitive, in coordination with His words, "and We have prepared for the disbelievers". It was revealed concerning the Jews. Al-Suddi said it was concerning the hypocrites. It was also said that it was concerning the polytheists of Makkah who were united in enmity against the Messenger (ﷺ). [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/539.]]

﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion﴾, meaning a friend and intimate, ﴿then evil is he as a companion﴾. That is: Satan is an evil companion. It is in the accusative as a tafsir (specification accusative). It was also said that it is an accusative of qat' (a separate accusative, not dependent on the preceding noun) with the definite article dropped, as you say: "How excellent a man is the servant of Allah" (ni`ma rajulan `abdu Allah). Likewise Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Evil is it as a substitute for the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Kahf: 50], and "evil is the example" [al-A'raf: 177].

﴿And what would it harm them﴾, that is: what would be upon them, and what harm would come to them? ﴿if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them?﴾ And Allah is ever Knowing of them.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (even) the weight of an atom﴾. [Ibn 'Abbas put his hand in the dust, then blew on it, and said: each one of these things is an atom (dharra). The meaning is that He does not wrong, neither little nor much.] [[Omitted in (b).]] Its construction is: "And what would it harm them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent? Indeed, Allah does not wrong..." That is: He does not diminish or reduce anyone's reward for his deed by the weight of an atom (mithqal dharra), the weight of an atom. The dharra is the small red ant. It was also said: the dharr are the particles of dust seen in a beam of light through a window, and each particle of it is a dharra, which has no weight. This is an example, meaning: Allah does not wrong anything. As He said in another verse: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all" [Yunus: 44].

Abu 'Abd Allah Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu 'Umar Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Muzani informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hafid informed us: al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl al-Bajali informed us: 'Affan informed us: Hammam informed us: Qatadah informed us, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong a believer a good deed, for which he is given provision in this world, and he is recompensed for it in the Hereafter." He said: "As for the disbeliever, he is fed with his good deeds in this world, until when he reaches the Hereafter, he has no good deed for which he is given anything good." [[Narrated by Muslim in Sifat al-Munafiqin, Bab Jaza' al-Mu'min bi-hasanatihi, no. (2808): 4/2162; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/310.]]

Abu al-Tayyib al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hatim al-Bazzar al-Tusi informed us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, that Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to them. 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us. (4300): 2/1437. Al-Hakim authenticated it on the condition of Muslim, 1/6, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; Ahmad 2/212; and Ibn Hibban authenticated it in al-Zuhd, Bab fi al-Khawf wa-al-Raja', no. (2523), p. (625) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 15/134.]] Some people said: this is concerning disputes between people.

It is narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will gather the first and the last, then a caller will call out: "Whoever had been seeking an injustice, let him come to his right and take it." A person will rejoice if a right he has is due from his father, his son, his wife, or his brother, and he takes it from him, even if he is young. The evidence for this in the Book of Allah the Exalted is: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101]. A servant will be brought forward, and a caller will call out before the first and the last: "This is so-and-so, son of so-and-so. Whoever has a right against him, let him come to his right and take it." And it will be said: "Give these people their rights." He will say: "My Lord, from where? The world has gone." Allah the Exalted will say to His angels: "Look at his good deeds and give them from them." If an atom's weight of good remains, the angels will say: "Our Lord, an atom's weight of good remains for him." He will say: "Double it for My servant, and admit him to Paradise by the bounty of My mercy." The evidence for this in the Book of Allah the Exalted is: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong (the weight of) an atom, and if it is a good deed He doubles it﴾. But if he is a wretched servant, the angels will say: "Our God, his good deeds are exhausted, and claimants remain?" Allah the Exalted will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write for him a certificate to the Fire." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in al-Tafsir: 8/363–364. Ibn Kathir said: part of this report has a witness in a sahih hadith.]]

So the meaning of the verse according to this interpretation is: Allah does not wrong the weight of an atom in favour of one claimant against another, but rather He takes the right for him from the other. And He does not wrong the weight of an atom that remains for him; rather He rewards him for it and multiplies it for him. This is His saying: ﴿and if it is a good deed He doubles it﴾. The people of the Hijaz read ﴿ḥasanatun﴾ with a nominative (raf') vowel, meaning: "and if a good deed is found." The others read it with an accusative (nasb) vowel, meaning: "and if the weight of the atom is a good deed, He doubles it," that is, He makes it many times over.

﴿and gives from Himself a great reward﴾. Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When Allah the Exalted says "a great reward," who can measure its measure?

﴿فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِنْ كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ﴾ [That is: how will it be, and how will they act, when We bring from every nation a witness?] [[Omitted in (B).]] Meaning: with their prophet bearing witness against them for what they did. ﴿وَجِئْنَا بِكَ يَا مُحَمَّدُ عَلَى هَؤُلَاءِ شَهِيدًا﴾ [And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against these people], a witness who testifies over all the nations, over those who saw him and over those who did not see him.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ubayda, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Recite to me." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I recite to you when it was revealed to you?" He said: "Yes." So I recited Surah al-Nisa until I reached this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you as a witness against these people?﴾ He said: "That is enough for you now." I turned to him and his eyes were shedding tears. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter "So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness...": 8/250, from Amr ibn Murra, and elsewhere; and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the virtue of listening to the Qur'an and asking a memorizer to recite, no. (800): 1/551. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunna 4/490.]]

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿On that Day﴾, that is, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾. The people of Medina and Ibn Amir read "tassawwa" with a fatha on the ta and a shadda on the sin, meaning "tatasawwa," and the second ta was assimilated into the sin. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the ta and a light sin, by dropping the ta of the reflexive form (tafa''ul), as in His saying: ﴿No soul speaks except by His permission﴾ [Hud: 11]. The rest read it with a damma on the ta and a light sin, in the passive, meaning: "if the earth were leveled over them," and they and the earth would become one thing.

Qatada and Abu Ubayda said: it means if the earth were split open, so they would sink into it and return to it, and then the earth would be leveled over them, that is, upon them.

It was also said: they wish they had not been raised, because they had only been created from dust, and the earth would have been level over them.

Al-Kalbi said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will say to the beasts, the wild animals, the birds and the predators: "Be dust," so that the earth will be leveled over them. At that point the disbeliever will wish that he were dust, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ [An-Naba: 40].

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾. Ata said: they will wish the earth were leveled over them, and that they had not concealed the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) nor his description. Others said: rather, this is a new statement, meaning: they will not conceal from Allah any statement, because what they did is not hidden from Allah and they cannot conceal it. Al-Kalbi and a group said: ﴿they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ because their limbs will bear witness against them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man said to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "I find things in the Qur'an that contradict each other for me." He said: "Tell me what contradicts you." He said: "[Allah says] ﴿So there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 101], and ﴿And they will approach one another, questioning each other﴾ [al-Tur: 25]. He also said: ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, and He said: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 23], so they did conceal. And He said: ﴿Is it the sky He built...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And the earth after that He spread out﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 27–30], so He mentioned the creation of the sky before the earth. Then He said: ﴿Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿...willingly or unwillingly﴾ [Fussilat: 9–11], so in this verse He mentioned the creation of the earth before the sky. And He said: ﴿And Allah was ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ and ﴿And Allah was ever Mighty and Wise﴾, as if He was and then passed?"

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: As for "there will be no kinship among them," that is at the first blast. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills﴾ [al-Zumar: 68]. So there will be no kinship then, nor will they ask one another. Then at the second blast: ﴿they will approach one another, questioning each other﴾. As for His saying: ﴿We were not polytheists﴾ and ﴿they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, Allah forgives the sins of the people of sincerity, so the polytheists will say: "Come, let us say we were not polytheists." Then their mouths will be sealed, and their hands will speak. At that point it became known that Allah does not conceal any statement. And in regard to Him: ﴿Those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾; and ﴿He created the earth in two days﴾, then He created the sky, then He turned to the sky and made it complete in two other days, then He spread out the earth. Its spreading out means: He brought forth from it water and pasture, and created the mountains, the hills and what is between them, in two other days. So He said: He created the earth in two days, then the earth and what is in it were made in four days, and the heavens were created in two days. ﴿And Allah was ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is, He has always been so. So the Qur'an should not seem contradictory to you, for all of it is from Allah. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in suspended form (ta'liq) in Tafsir, in the commentary on Surah Ha Mim al-Sajda, then connected it at the end of the hadith, saying: Yusuf ibn Adi related to me: Ubayd Allah ibn Amr related to us, from Zayd, from al-Minhal, with this. Also narrated by al-Tabari in Tafsir: 8/373–374.]]

Al-Hasan said: These are stages. In one stage they will not speak, and you will hear nothing but whispers. In another stage they will speak, and they will lie and say: ﴿We were not polytheists﴾ and ﴿we did not do any evil﴾. In another place they will confess against themselves, as in His saying: ﴿So they will acknowledge their sin﴾ [al-Mulk: 11]. In another place they will not question one another, and in another they will ask for a return. The last of these stages is that their mouths will be sealed and their limbs will speak, which is His saying: ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾. [[In (B), "and the last" appears as "and the worst" (wa-akhas).]]
