[86a]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 1 of 4):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾ – to the end of the verse. The intended meaning of "intoxication" (sukr), according to most scholars, is intoxication from wine (khamr). The reason is that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him) prepared a meal and invited some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), and he brought them wine. They drank it before wine was prohibited, and they became intoxicated. Then the time for the Maghrib prayer came, and they put forward a man to lead them in prayer, and he recited ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ ("I worship what you worship"), omitting the ﴿not﴾, and continued like this to the end of the surah. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and after its revelation they used to avoid intoxication at the times of the prayers, until the prohibition of wine was revealed.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Ashribah, chapter on the prohibition of wine: 5/259; and al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir, in the tafsir of Surat al-Nisa: 8/380, and he said: this is a hasan gharib sahih hadith. It is attributed in Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi to al-Nasa'i. Al-Mundhiri said: its chain contains ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib, and it is not known except through his narration. Ibn Ma'in said: his narration is not to be used as evidence, and he once distinguished between his earlier and later narrations, and Imam Ahmad agreed with this distinction. See: Mukhtasar al-Sunan of al-Mundhiri: 5/259. Ibn Hajar, in al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 44, attributed a similar report to Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Bazzar, al-Hakim and al-Tabari. See also: Tafsir al-Tabari: 8/376.]]

Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said: He meant by it the intoxication of sleep; He forbade prayer when sleep overcomes a person. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughallis informed us, Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamadhani informed us, ʿAbdah ibn Sulayman informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If one of you feels drowsy while praying, let him sleep until the sleep leaves him, for if one of you prays while drowsy, he may go to seek forgiveness and end up cursing himself."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Wudu', chapter on wudu' from sleep: 1/313, and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on ordering one who dozes in his prayer…, no. (786): 1/543. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/57.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿until you know what you are saying, nor [approach prayer while] in a state of janabah﴾ – it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: do not approach prayer while you are in a state of janabah. It is said: a man is junub, a woman is junub, and men are junub, women are junub.

The original meaning of janabah is distance, and he is called junub because he keeps away from the place of prayer, or because of his keeping away from people and his distance from them until he performs ghusl.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except as travellers, until you wash yourselves﴾ – they differed about its meaning. Some said: [except that you are travellers and do not find water, so perform tayammum; it prohibits the junub from prayer until he performs ghusl] except that he is on a journey and does not find water, so he prays with tayammum. This is the view of ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Mujahid, may Allah be pleased with them.

Others said: the intended meaning of "prayer" here is the place of prayer, as in His saying: ﴿and churches and synagogues and mosques﴾ [al-Hajj: 40]. Its meaning is: do not approach the mosque while you are junub, except passing through it in order to leave from it, such as when a person sleeps in the mosque and becomes junub, or becomes junub while water is in the mosque, or when his path lies through it, so he passes through it without staying. This is the view of ʿAbd Allah ibn Mas'ud, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, ʿIkrimah, al-Nakhaʿi and al-Zuhri. The reason is that some people of the Ansar had their doors opening into the mosque, and they would become junub while having no water, and had no way to pass except through the mosque, so they were permitted to cross through it.

The scholars differed on this: some permitted passing through it without restriction, and this is the view of al-Hasan; Malik and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them, also held this. Some prohibited it without restriction, and this is the view of the people of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y, i.e., the Hanafis). Some said: he performs tayammum for passing through it.

As for staying (al-mukth) in the mosque, it is not permitted according to most scholars, because of what we have narrated from ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Turn these houses away from the mosque, for I do not make the mosque lawful for a menstruating woman or a junub."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Taharah, chapter on the junub entering the mosque: 1/157–158, from ʿAʾishah, and Ibn Majah in al-Taharah, chapter on what has come concerning avoiding the mosque by a menstruating woman, from Umm Salamah, no. (645): 1/212. In al-Zawa'id it says: its chain is weak; Muhdaj is not authenticated, and Abu al-Khattab is unknown; and Ibn al-Qattan related from ʿAbd al-Haqq that it is a hasan hadith. See: Nasb al-Rayah: 1/194–195; Mukhtasar al-Mundhiri: 1/157–158; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 1/162.]] Ahmad permitted staying in it, and the hadith was declared weak because its narrator is unknown; al-Muzani also held this view.

It is not permitted for a junub to perform tawaf, just as he is not permitted to pray, and he is not permitted to recite the Qur'an. ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Muliḥi informed us, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us, ʿAli ibn al-Ja'd informed us, Shu'bah informed us, ʿAmr ibn Murrah informed me, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allah ibn Salamah [in the manuscript: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muslim; the correction is from Sharh al-Sunnah and al-Taqrib] say: I entered upon ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would relieve himself, eat meat with us, and recite the Qur'an, and nothing would prevent him or hold him back from reciting the Qur'an except janabah.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Taharah, chapter on the junub reciting the Qur'an: 1/156; al-Tirmidhi in al-Taharah, chapter on what has come concerning a man reciting the Qur'an in every state so long as he is not junub: 1/453–454, and he said: hasan sahih; al-Nasa'i in al-Taharah, chapter on preventing the junub from reciting the Qur'an: 1/144; Ibn Majah in al-Taharah, chapter on what has come concerning reciting the Qur'an without wudu', no. (594): 1/195; al-Hakim: 4/107, who authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed; and Imam Ahmad: 1/8 and other places. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/41–42. See also what al-Mundhiri said in Mukhtasar al-Sunan: 1/156, Ibn Hajar in Talkhis al-Habir: 1/139–140, and Irwa' al-Ghalil of al-Albani: 1/241–245.]]

Ghusl of janabah becomes obligatory by one of two matters: either by the emission of semen (al-mani), or by the meeting of the two circumcised parts (iltiqa' al-khitanayn), which is the insertion of the glans into the vagina even if there is no emission. At the beginning the ruling was that whoever had intercourse with his wife and did not ejaculate was not obliged to perform ghusl; then this ruling was abrogated (mansukh).

ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabi' informed us, al-Shafi'i informed us, Sufyan informed us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Abu Musa al-Ash'ari asked ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) about the meeting of the two circumcised parts. ʿAʾishah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the two circumcised parts meet, or the circumcised part touches the circumcised part, then ghusl has become obligatory."[[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/38 (Tartib Musnad al-Imam); and in al-Umm: 1/31; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/97 from ʿAʾishah; and Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Taharah, chapter on the obligation of ghusl when the two circumcised parts meet, as a mawquf report from ʿAʾishah: 1/46. The full hadith is in Muslim, al-Hayd, chapter on the abrogation of "water is from water…", no. (349): 1/271–272; the author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/5. See: Nasb al-Rayah: 1/84–85; Talkhis al-Habir: 1/134–135.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and if you are ill﴾ – plural of marid (sick). By it he means a sick person whose use of water would harm him, such as one with smallpox or the like, or one who has an injury on the place of his purification, fearing destruction or increased pain from using water on it. He performs prayer with tayammum even if water is available. If part of his body for purification is healthy and part is injured, he washes the healthy part and performs tayammum for the injured part. This is based on what Abu Tahir ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-Qashani informed us, Abu ʿUmar al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us, Abu ʿAli Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAmr al-Lu'lu'i informed us, Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani informed us, Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Antaki informed us, Muhammad ibn Salamah informed us, from al-Zubayr ibn Khuraygh, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: We set out on a journey, and a stone struck a man among us and wounded his head; then he had a wet dream, and he asked his companions: "Do you find a concession for me to perform tayammum?" They said: "We do not find a concession for you while you are able to use water." So he washed and died. When we came to the Prophet (ﷺ), he was informed of this, and he said: "They killed him; may Allah kill them! Why did they not ask when they did not know? The cure for ignorance is asking. It would have sufficed him to perform tayammum, and to bind or wrap a cloth over his wound – the narrator is unsure – then wipe over it and wash the rest of his body."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Taharah, chapter on the one with a skin disease performing tayammum: 1/208, from Jabir; in its chain is al-Zubayr ibn Khuraygh (diminutive), mawla of ʿAʾishah: weak in narration, fifth tier (Taqrib). Ibn Majah in al-Tayammum, chapter on the wounded one who has a junub's ghusl and fears for himself, no. (572): 1/189, from Ibn ʿAbbas in similar terms; al-Zawa'id says its chain is broken. Al-Darimi from Ibn ʿAbbas, in al-Taharah, chapter on the wounded one who has junub: 1/192; al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/178, from Ibn ʿAbbas; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/120.]]

The Ashab al-Ra'y did not permit combining tayammum and ghusl. They said: if most of his limbs are healthy, the healthy ones are washed and he does not perform tayammum over them; and if most of them are injured, he suffices with tayammum.

The hadith is a proof for those who require combining the two.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿or on a journey﴾ – he means that if he is on a journey, whether long or short, and water is unavailable, he prays with tayammum and there is no need to repeat the prayer. This is based on what is narrated from Abu Dharr, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, clean earth is the purification of the Muslim, even if he does not find water for ten years; when he finds water, let him touch his skin with it."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Taharah, chapter on the junub performing tayammum: 1/205–206; al-Tirmidhi in al-Taharah, chapter on what has come concerning tayammum for the junub when he does not find water: 1/387–388, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; al-Nasa'i in al-Taharah, chapter on one tayammum for several prayers: 1/171; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/176–177, who authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed; Ahmad: 5/146, 147. Ibn Hibban authenticated it in Mawarid al-Zam'an, no. (196), p. 75. al-Bazzar narrated it through Hisham from Ibn Sirin from Abu Hurayrah, marfu'; Ibn al-Qattan authenticated it, but al-Daraqutni said the correct version is mursal. See Fath al-Bari: 1/446.]]

As for when a man is neither ill nor on a journey, but has no water in a place where water is not generally unavailable, such as in a village whose water has been cut off, he prays with tayammum and then repeats the prayer when he finds water, according to al-Shafi'i. According to Malik and al-Awza'i, there is no need to repeat it. According to Abu Hanifah, may Allah be pleased with him, he delays the prayer until he finds water.[[According to the Hanafis: if he hopes or expects to find water, he delays the prayer until the end of the recommended time; some said he delays it until the end of the permissible time, and the first view is more correct. See: al-Fatawa al-Hindiyya: 1/30; Fath al-Qadir: 1/94.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿or one of you comes from the toilet (al-ghait)﴾ – he means by it when one has broken wudu'. Al-Ghait is the name for a low-lying piece of land, and it was the custom of the Arabs to go to the ghait for relieving themselves, so the breaking of wudu' was referred to by the ghait. ﴿Or you have touched women﴾ – Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "lamastum" here and in al-Ma'idah, while the rest read ﴿lamastum al-nisa'﴾.

They differed about the meaning of lams (touching) and mulamasah (touching). Some people said: it means intercourse; this is the view of Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah, and touching is used as a euphemism for intercourse, because intercourse does not occur except through touching.

Others said: both mean the meeting of the two skins, whether it is through intercourse or not; this is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i.

The jurists differed over the ruling of the verse. A group held that if a man's body touches any part of a woman's body with no barrier between them, both their ablutions (wudu', the ritual washing before prayer) are nullified. This was the view of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and it was also said by al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Malik, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, Ahmad and Ishaq said: if the touching is with desire, it nullifies purity; if it is without desire, it does not nullify it.

Some people said: touching never nullifies wudu'. This was the view of Ibn 'Abbas, and it was also held by al-Hasan and al-Thawri.

Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is not nullified unless erection occurs.[[The Hanafis say that wudu' is nullified by intimate touching, such as when the two are naked and erection occurs, not by erection alone. See: Ibn 'Abidin's commentary (Hashiyat Ibn 'Abidin): 1/146; al-Fatawa al-Hindiyya: 1/13.]]

Those who did not require wudu' because of touching argued with what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Nadr, client of 'Umar ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: "I used to sleep in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with my legs in the direction of his qiblah. When he prostrated, he would nudge me, and I would draw in my legs; when he stood, I would stretch them out again." She said: "And the houses at that time had no lamps."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Prayer, chapter on voluntary prayer behind a woman: 1/588; and Muslim in Prayer, chapter on passing in front of the one praying, no. (512): 1/367; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 2/457.]]

Al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, that 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "I was sleeping beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I missed him during the night. I touched him with my hand, and I placed my hand on the soles of his feet while he was prostrating, and he was saying: 'I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your displeasure, and in Your forgiveness from Your punishment, and in You from You. I cannot count Your praise; You are as You have praised Yourself.'"[[Narrated by Muslim in Prayer, chapter on what is said in bowing and prostration, no. (486): 1/352.]]

The opinion of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, differed regarding a man who touches a woman within his prohibited kin, such as his mother, daughter or sister, or touches a young non-mahram girl. The more sound of the two opinions is that it does not nullify wudu', because she is not a place of desire, just as when he touches a man.

His opinion also differed regarding whether the wudu' of the one touched is nullified, in two views. One is that it is nullified, because both share in the pleasure, just as ghusl (full ritual bath) becomes obligatory for both through sexual intercourse. The second is that it is not nullified, based on the hadith of 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, where she said: "I placed my hand on his feet while he was prostrating."

If a man touches a woman's hair, teeth or nail, his wudu' is not nullified according to him.

Know that the one in a state of minor impurity (muhdith) has no valid prayer until he performs wudu' if he finds water, or performs tayammum (dry ablution with earth) if he does not find water. Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us, Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us, 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, that Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prayer of one of you is not accepted when he has become impure (ahdatha) until he performs wudu'."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Wudu', chapter: "The prayer without purity is not accepted": 1/234; and Muslim in Purity, chapter on the obligation of purity for prayer, no. (225): 1/204; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/328.]]

Hadath (minor impurity) is the emergence of what comes out of either of the two private passages, whether it is a substance or a trace; and loss of reason through insanity or fainting, in any state. As for sleep, the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, is that it requires wudu', except if one sleeps sitting firmly, in which case there is no wudu' upon him. This is based on what 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-Aziz al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabi' informed us, al-Shafi'i informed us, the trustworthy one [narrated] from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to wait for the 'Isha' prayer and would sleep, I think he said sitting, until their heads nodded, then they would pray and not perform wudu'."[[Narrated by Muslim in Menstruation, chapter on the proof that the sleep of one sitting does not nullify wudu', with the wording: "The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to sleep, then pray without performing wudu'," no. (376): 1/284. Also narrated with the author's wording by Abu Dawud in Purity, chapter on wudu' from sleep: 1/143; al-Tirmidhi in Purity, chapter on what has come concerning wudu' from sleep: 1/253, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith"; al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/34 (Tartib al-Musnad); and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/338.]]

A group held that sleep requires wudu' in every state. This was the view of Abu Hurayra and 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with them, and it was also held by al-Hasan, Ishaq and al-Muzani. Another group held that if one sleeps standing, sitting or prostrating, there is no wudu' upon him until he sleeps lying on his side. This was held by al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak and the people of opinion (ashab al-ra'y).

They differed concerning touching the private part, one's own or another's. A group held that it requires wudu'. This was the view of 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Abu Hurayra and 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with them, and it was also held by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Sulayman ibn Yasar and 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr. It was also the view of al-Awza'i, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq. Likewise a woman touching her private part. However, al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said it is not nullified unless one touches with the palm of the hand or the pads of the fingers.

They argued with what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Hazm, that he heard 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr say: "I entered upon Marwan ibn al-Hakam and we mentioned what requires wudu'. Marwan said: 'Touching the penis requires wudu'.' 'Urwa said: 'I did not know that.' Marwan said: 'Busra bint Safwan informed me that she heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "If one of you touches his penis, let him perform wudu'."'"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Purity, chapter on wudu' from touching the penis: 1/131; al-Tirmidhi in Purity, chapter on what has come concerning wudu' from touching the penis: 1/270-272, and he said: "This is a sahih hadith"; al-Nasa'i in Purity, chapter on wudu' from touching the penis: 1/100; Ibn Majah in Purity, chapter on wudu' from touching the penis, no. (479): 1/161; Malik in Purity, chapter on wudu' from touching the private part: 1/42; al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan: 1/146-147, and he said: "sahih"; al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/34-35 (Tartib al-Musnad) and in al-Umm: 1/15; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/406; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/340.]]

A group held that it does not require wudu'. This was narrated from 'Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Abu al-Darda' and Hudhayfa, and it was held by al-Hasan. Al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak and the people of opinion also held this view.

They argued with what was narrated from Talq ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about a man touching his penis, and he said: "Is it anything other than a part of you?" It is also narrated as: "Is it anything other than a piece of flesh or a part of you?"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Purity, chapter on the concession in that (wudu' from touching the penis): 1/133, and al-Mundhiri quoted in it the statement of Yahya ibn Ma'in: "People have said much about Qays ibn Talq, and that his hadith is not to be used as proof," and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim said: "I asked my father and Abu Zur'a about this hadith, and he said: 'Qays ibn Talq is not one by whom proof is established; they weakened him and did not authenticate him.'" It is also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Purity, chapter on what has come concerning abandoning wudu' from touching the penis: 1/274; al-Nasa'i in Purity, chapter on wudu' from that: 1/101; Ibn Majah in Purity, chapter on the concession in that, no. (483): 1/163; al-Daraqutni in Purity: 1/49; Ibn Hibban in Purity, chapter on what has come concerning touching the private part, no. (207), p. (77) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; Ahmad: 4/22-23; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/342. See also: Talkhis al-Habir: 1/125; Nasb al-Raya: 1/60-76. The hadith was authenticated by al-Daraqutni, al-Tahawi, 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, Ibn al-Madini, al-Tabarani and Ibn Hazm. It was declared weak by al-Shafi'i, Abu Hatim, Abu Zur'a, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn al-Jawzi, and abrogation (naskh) was claimed for it by Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, Ibn al-'Arabi, al-Hazimi and others.]]

Whoever required wudu' from it said: this is abrogated by the hadith of Busra, because Abu Hurayra also narrates that wudu' is required from touching the penis.[[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/35 (Tartib al-Musnad) and in al-Umm: 1/15-16; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 1/133; al-Daraqutni: 1/147; authenticated by al-Hakim: 1/138, with the wording: "whoever touches his private part." Also Ibn Hibban, no. (210), p. (77) of Mawarid al-Zam'an; Ahmad: 2/333; and narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh as a statement of Abu Hurayra (mawquf). See: Nasb al-Raya: 1/56. al-Nawawi said: "Its chain has weakness, but it is strengthened by the multiplicity of its routes." See: al-Majmu': 2/37. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/341.]] And he is of later Islam, and Talq ibn 'Ali's arrival upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was at the beginning of the Hijra, when he was building the mosque.

They differed concerning the emergence of impurity from other than the two private passages, through bloodletting (fasd), cupping (hijama), and other things such as vomiting and the like. A group held that it does not require wudu'. This was narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, and it was held by 'Ata', Tawus, al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Malik and al-Shafi'i also held this view.

A group held that wudu' is required because of vomiting, nosebleed, bloodletting and cupping. Among them were Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, the people of opinion, Ahmad and Ishaq.

They agreed that a small amount of these, and the emergence of wind from other than the two passages, does not require wudu'. Had a large amount required wudu', its small amount would require it too, like the two private passages.

﴿So if you do not find water, then perform tayammum﴾. Know that tayammum is one of the distinctive features of this Ummah. Hudhayfa, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have been favoured over the people in three ways: our rows have been made like the rows of the angels; the whole earth has been made a place of prostration (masjid) for us; and its dust has been made a means of purification for us when we do not find water."[[Narrated by Muslim in Mosques and Places of Prayer, no. (522): 1/371.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 3 of 4):

The beginning of the tayammum (dry ablution) was as follows. Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on some of his journeys. When we reached al-Bayda' or Dhat al-Jaysh, my necklace broke, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stayed to search for it, and the people stayed with him, although they were not near water and had no water with them. So the people came to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: 'Do you not see what Aisha has done? She has kept the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people with him, and they are not near water and have no water with them.' Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had laid his head on my thigh and was sleeping. He said: 'You have detained the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the people, and they are not near water and have no water with them.' She said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, rebuked me and said what Allah willed him to say, and he began to poke me in the side with his hand. Nothing prevented me from moving except the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my thigh. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose in the morning without water, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed the verse of tayammum: ﴿then perform tayammum﴾. Usayd ibn Hudayr, who was one of the nuqaba' (chieftains), said: 'This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abu Bakr!' Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: 'We then made the camel I was riding rise, and we found the necklace beneath it.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tayammum, chapter "If one finds neither water nor earth": 1/431, and in other places; and by Muslim in the Book of Menstruation, chapter on tayammum, no. (367): 1/279. The author (al-Baghawi) also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/104–106.]]

And Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Ubayd ibn Isma'il informed us; Abu Usama informed us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she borrowed a necklace from Asma' and it was lost. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent some of his companions to search for it, and the time of prayer came upon them, so they prayed without ablution. When they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) they complained to him about that, and the verse of tayammum was revealed. Usayd ibn Hudayr said: "May Allah reward you with good. By Allah, no matter ever befell you but that Allah made a way out of it for you, and placed in it a blessing for the Muslims." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tayammum, chapter "If one finds neither water nor earth": 1/440, and by Muslim in the Book of Menstruation, chapter on tayammum, no. (367): 1/279.]]

﴿Then perform tayammum﴾, i.e., aim for; ﴿clean earth﴾, i.e., pure, clean dust. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: al-sa'id is the dust.

The scholars differed regarding what tayammum may be performed with. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, held that it is restricted to that to which the name "dust" applies, from which some powder clings to the hand, because the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And its dust has been made a purifier for us." [[A portion of the hadith of Hudhayfah, previously cited in Muslim, no. (522): 1/371.]]

The people of opinion (ahl al-ra'y, i.e., the Hanafi jurists) permitted tayammum with orpiment, plaster, depilatory lime and other kinds of ground surfaces, to the extent that they said: If one strikes his hands on a rock with no dust on it, or on earth, then blows on it until all of it is gone, and then wipes his face and hands with it, his tayammum is valid. They said: al-sa'id is the surface of the earth, based on what is narrated from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a purifier." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari at the beginning of the Book of Tayammum: 1/435–436, and by Muslim in the Book of Mosques and Places of Prayer, no. (521): 1/370, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/196.]]

This is general (mujmal, i.e., unspecified), while the hadith of Hudhayfah that restricts it to dust is specific (mufassar, i.e., explained), and the specific explains the general.

Some permitted tayammum with everything connected to the earth, such as trees, plants and the like, and said: al-sa'id is the name for whatever grows upon the surface of the earth.

Aiming at the dust is a condition for the validity of tayammum, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿then perform tayammum﴾, and tayammum means intention. Hence, if one stands in the path of the wind so that dust strikes his face, and he intends (it), it is not valid.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and wipe your faces and your hands; indeed Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. Know that wiping the face and the two hands is obligatory in tayammum, and they differed regarding its manner. Most scholars held that one wipes the face and the two hands together with the elbows, with two strikes: one strikes his palms on the dust and wipes his entire face, and it is not obligatory to get the dust beneath the hair. Then he strikes a second time and wipes his hands up to the elbows. This is because Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad ibn al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, from Abu al-Huwayrith, from al-A'raj, from Abu al-Summa, who said: "I passed by the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was urinating, and I gave him the greeting of peace, but he did not return it to me until he went to a wall and struck it with a stick he had with him. Then he placed his hands on the wall and wiped his face and forearms, and then returned my greeting." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tayammum, chapter "Tayammum while at home when one finds no water and fears missing the prayer": 1/441, and by Muslim in the Book of Menstruation, chapter on tayammum, no. (369): 1/281, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/115.]] In it is evidence for the obligation of wiping the two hands up to the elbows, just as washing them in ablution is obligatory up to the elbows. It is also evidence that tayammum is not valid unless some dust of the earth clings to the hand, because the Prophet (ﷺ) struck the wall with the stick, and if mere striking were sufficient, he would not have struck it with a stick.

Al-Zuhri held that one wipes the two hands up to the shoulders, based on what is narrated from Ammar, who said: "We performed tayammum up to the shoulders." This is a report of an action (of Ammar), which he did not transmit from the Prophet (ﷺ). It is also narrated that he said: "I became junub (in a state of major impurity), so I rolled in the dust, and when I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about it, he ordered me to (wipe) the face and the palms."

A group held that tayammum is a single strike for the face and the palms. This is the view of Ali and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, and it was said by al-Sha'bi, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and Makhul, and al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also took this position. They argued with what Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Adam informed us; Shu'bah informed us; al-Hakam informed us, from Dharr, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, who said: "A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: 'I became junub and did not find water.' Ammar ibn Yasir said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: 'Do you not remember that we were on a journey, you and I? As for you, you did not pray, but as for me, I rolled in the dust and prayed, and I mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It would have sufficed you to do this." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) struck the earth with his palms and blew into them, then wiped with them his face and palms.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tayammum, chapter "Does one blow into the hands?": 1/443, and by Muslim in the Book of Menstruation, chapter on tayammum, no. (368): 1/280, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/109.]]

Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us, from Shu'bah with its chain, that Ammar said to Umar, may Allah be pleased with him: "I rolled in the dust and then came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'The face and the two palms will suffice you.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tayammum, chapter "Tayammum for the face and the two palms": 1/445, and by Muslim in the Book of Menstruation, chapter on tayammum, no. (368): 1/280, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/109.]]

In the hadith is evidence that the junub who finds no water prays with tayammum, and likewise a menstruating woman and a woman in postnatal bleeding, when they become pure and have no water.

Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both, held that the junub does not pray with tayammum, but postpones the prayer until he finds water and bathes. They interpreted His saying, exalted is He: ﴿or you have touched women﴾ as touching with the hand, not sexual intercourse. The hadith of Ammar, may Allah be pleased with him, is a proof, and Umar had forgotten what Ammar had mentioned to him, so he was not satisfied with his statement. It is also reported that Ibn Mas'ud retracted his opinion and permitted tayammum for the junub. The evidence for this also is what Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyad ibn Mansur informed us, from Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, from Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them, that the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered a man who was junub to perform tayammum and then pray, and when he found water, to bathe. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tayammum, chapter "Clean earth is the ablution of the Muslim": 1/447–448, and in the Book of Prophets; and by Muslim in the Book of Mosques and Places of Prayer, chapter on making up missed prayers, at length, no. (682): 1/474–476; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/111.]]

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us; Abu al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Ali al-Lu'lu'i informed us; Abu Dawud al-Sijistani informed us; Musaddad informed us; Khalid al-Wasiti informed us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Abu Amr, from Bajdan, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: "A share of charity wealth had gathered with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'O Abu Dharr, go out to it.' So I went out to al-Rabadhah, and I used to suffer from janabah (major impurity), so I would remain (in that state) for five or six (days). I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Clean earth is the ablution of the Muslim, even if (he waits) ten years. When you find water, let it touch your skin, for that is better.'" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Purification, chapter "The junub performs tayammum": 1/205–206; and by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Purification, abridged, chapter "What has come concerning tayammum for the junub when he finds no water": 1/387, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 1/220; and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/176–177 authenticated it, and al-Dhahabi agreed.]]

The wiping of the face and the hands in tayammum is sometimes a substitute for washing the whole body, in the case of the junub, the menstruating woman, the woman in postnatal bleeding, and the deceased; sometimes it is a substitute for washing the four limbs, in the case of one who is in a minor state of impurity (muhdith); and sometimes it is a substitute for washing some of the limbs of purification, such as when one of the limbs of his purification has a wound and he cannot wash its location; then he must perform tayammum in place of washing it.

Tayammum for a prayer of the time is not valid except after the time has entered, and one may not combine two obligatory prayers with a single tayammum. This is because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿When you stand up for prayer, wash your faces﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and if you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse indicates the obligation of ablution or tayammum whenever one does not find water, at every prayer. However, the evidence has been established regarding ablution, for the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed all the prayers with one ablution on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, [[See Sahih Muslim, Book of Purification, chapter on the permissibility of performing all the prayers with one ablution, no. (277): 1/232.]] so tayammum remains on its apparent meaning. This is the view of Ali, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them. It was said by al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i and Qatadah, and Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq also took this position.

A group held that tayammum, like purification with water, may be performed before the time of the prayer, and one may pray with it whatever obligatory prayers he wishes, so long as he does not break his ablution. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan, al-Zuhri, al-Thawri and the people of opinion.

They agreed that it is permissible to perform, with a single tayammum (dry ablution), together with the obligatory prayer, as many voluntary (nafl) prayers as one wishes, both before the obligatory prayer and after it, and that one may recite the Qur'an if one is in a state of janabah (ritual impurity requiring a full bath). If the tayammum is due to the excuse of travel and the absence of water, then seeking water is a condition, and this means that one searches for it among one's baggage and companions.

If one is in an open desert with no barrier obstructing one's view, one looks around oneself. If there is a nearby barrier obstructing one's view, such as a hill or a wall, one moves away from it, because Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But if you find no water, then perform tayammum﴾. It is not said, "He did not find the water," except of one who has searched.

According to Abu Hanifah (may Allah be pleased with him), seeking water is not a condition. If one sees the water but there is a barrier between him and the water, such as an enemy or a predatory animal that prevents him from going to it, or if the water is in a well and he does not have the equipment for drawing water, then he is like one who has no water. He performs the prayer with tayammum and there is no need for him to repeat it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 44–46:

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ He means: the Jews of Madinah. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: It was revealed concerning Rifa'ah ibn Zayd and Malik ibn Dakhshum. Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke, they would twist their tongues [[In B: (lisanahuma).]] and find fault with him, so Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse. [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/593.]] ﴿They purchase﴾ means: they exchange. ﴿Error﴾ means: in place of guidance. ﴿And they want you to lose the way﴾ means: to stray from the way, O assembly of the believers.

﴿And Allah is most knowing of your enemies﴾ among you, so do not seek counsel from them, for they are your enemies. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a Protector, and sufficient is Allah as a Helper.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is, be content with Allah as a Protector, and be content with Allah as a Helper.

﴿Among those who are Jews﴾: it has been said that this is connected to His saying ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture?﴾ and ﴿among those who are Jews﴾. It has also been said that it is a new (independent) sentence, meaning: among those who are Jews are some who distort, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ [al-Saffat: 164], meaning: there is none of us who has a known station, intending "a group." ﴿They distort the words﴾ they alter the words ﴿from their places﴾ meaning: the description of Muhammad (ﷺ). Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: The Jews would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him about a matter, and he would inform them, and they would see that they accept his word; but when they departed from him they would distort his speech. ﴿And they say: we hear﴾ your saying ﴿and we disobey﴾ your command, ﴿and hear, without being made to hear﴾ meaning: hear from us, and we will not hear from you; ﴿without being made to hear﴾ meaning: without your words being accepted from you. It has also been said that they would say to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Listen," and then say to themselves: "May you not hear." ﴿And [they say] "Ra'ina"﴾ meaning: they would say "Ra'ina," intending by it a reference to ruin (ru'unah). ﴿Twisting with their tongues﴾ by distortion ﴿and defaming﴾ disparaging ﴿the religion﴾: that his saying "Ra'ina" is from consideration (al-muraa'ah), while they distort it, intending by it ruin (al-ru'unah). ﴿And if they had said, "We hear and we obey, and hear and look at us"﴾ meaning: look at us in place of their saying "Ra'ina," ﴿it would have been better for them and more upright﴾ meaning: more just and more correct. ﴿But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they do not believe, except a few﴾ meaning: except a small group of them, and they are 'Abdullah ibn Salam and those who embraced Islam with him from among them.

The Qur'an, Surah 4, verse 47:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have been given the Scripture﴾, addressing the Jews, ﴿believe in what We have sent down﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what is with you﴾, meaning the Torah. This is because the Prophet ﷺ spoke with the rabbis of the Jews, Abdullah ibn Suriya and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and said: "O assembly of Jews, fear Allah and submit. By Allah, you certainly know that what I have brought you is the truth." They said: "We do not know that," and they persisted in disbelief. So this verse was revealed. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari at length in the Book of the Virtues of the Ansar, chapter on the Hijra of the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions to Madina: 7/249-250.]]

﴿before We obliterate faces﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "We make them like the hoof of a camel." Qatada and al-Dahhak said: "We blind them." [[In A: (nʿmhā), i.e. "we blind them."]] By "face" is meant the eye. ﴿and turn them back upon their heels﴾, that is, We obliterate the face and turn it back to the nape. It was also said: We make the faces like the places where hair grows on monkeys' faces, because human hair grows on their backs and not on their faces. It was also said: the meaning is that We erase their traces and what is in them of nose, eye, mouth and brow, and make them like the nape of the neck. It was also said: We place their eyes on the nape so that he walks backwards.

It is reported that when Abdullah ibn Salam (may Allah be pleased with him) heard this verse, he came to the Prophet ﷺ before he had gone to his family, with his hand on his face, and embraced Islam, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not think I would reach you until my face was turned around to my nape." Likewise Ka'b al-Ahbar, when he heard this verse, embraced Islam in the time of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), and said: "O Lord, I have believed, O Lord, I have submitted," fearing that the threat of this verse would befall him. [[A part of the previous hadith.]]

If it is said: He threatened them with obliteration if they did not believe, and they did not believe, yet He did not do that to them?

It is said: This threat remains, and there will be obliteration and transformation among the Jews before the Hour.

It is also said: This was a conditional threat, and when Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions embraced Islam, it averted it from the rest.

It is also said: By it He meant the Resurrection. Mujahid [88a] said: by His words ﴿We obliterate faces﴾ He means: We leave them in error, so the meaning is the obliteration of the face of the heart and the turning back of the insights of guidance upon their heels, into disbelief and misguidance.

The root of "tams" is erasing, destroying and transforming. Ibn Zayd said: We erase their traces from their faces and their regions in which they are, and turn them back upon their heels, until they return to where they came from at the beginning, which is Syria. He said: That has already happened, and he interpreted it as the exile of the Banu al-Nadir to Adhruʿat and Ariha in Syria. ﴿Or We curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, so that We make them apes and swine. ﴿And the command of Allah is always accomplished.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 4, Verse 48:**

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be set up with Him﴾. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Wahshi ibn Harb and his companions. When he killed Hamza, he had been promised freedom in return for killing him, but this promise was not fulfilled for him. When he arrived in Makkah, he and his companions regretted what they had done, so they wrote to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We have indeed regretted what we did, and nothing prevents us from embracing Islam except that we heard you say, while you were in Makkah: 'And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah...' (al-Furqan 25:68) to the end of the verses. We have called upon another god along with Allah, we have killed the soul that Allah has forbidden, and we have committed adultery. So, were it not for these verses, we would have followed you." Then the verses were revealed: "Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds..." (al-Furqan 25:70-71). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent these to them. When they read them, they wrote back: "This is a severe condition; we fear that we will not be able to do righteous deeds." Then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be set up with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. He sent this to them, and they wrote back: "We fear that we will not be among those whom He wills [to forgive]." Then it was revealed: "Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah" (al-Zumar 39:53). He sent this to them, and they entered Islam and returned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he accepted them. Then he said to Wahshi: "Tell me how you killed Hamza." When he told him, he said: "Woe to you! Hide your face from me." So Wahshi went to Syria and remained there until he died. [See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 3/268.]

Abu Mijlaz reported from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): When the verse "Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves..." was revealed, a man stood up and said: "And what about shirk, O Messenger of Allah?" He remained silent, then the man stood up to him two or three times, and then the verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be set up with Him﴾. [Al-Tabari: 8/449. Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/557 as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir.]

Mutarrif ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir said: Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "During the time of Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a man died while committing a major sin, we would testify that he was among the people of the Fire, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be set up with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾. So we refrained from such testimonies." [See al-Tabari: 8/450, and al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/556.]

It is related from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) that this verse is the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an: "but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir, Surat al-Nisa: 8/399-400, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Al-Suyuti also attributed it to al-Firyabi. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/588.]

﴿And whoever sets up partners with Allah has certainly fabricated﴾, i.e., invented, ﴿a tremendous sin﴾. Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Salihi informed us: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Muhammad ibn Hammad told us: Abu Mu'awiya told us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what are the two destroying things (al-Mujibatan)?" He said: "Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah will enter Paradise, and whoever dies associating something with Allah will enter the Fire." [Narrated by Muslim in al-Iman, Chapter: Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise, no. 93, 1/94.]

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) informed us: Abu Ma'mar informed us: Abd al-Warith informed us, from al-Husayn, i.e., al-Mu'allim, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from Yahya ibn Ya'mur, that Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali told him that Abu Dhar told him, who said: I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was wearing a white garment and sleeping. Then I came to him again and he had awakened, and he said: "There is no servant who says 'There is no god but Allah' and then dies upon that, except that he will enter Paradise." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals." I said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals?" He said: "Even if he commits adultery and even if he steals, in spite of the nose of Abu Dhar." And whenever Abu Dhar narrated this, he would say: "Even in spite of the nose of Abu Dhar." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Libas, Chapter: White Garments, 10/283. Also narrated by Muslim in al-Iman, Chapter: Whoever dies without associating anything with Allah enters Paradise, no. 94, 1/95; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/96-97.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 49:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾ and the rest of the verse. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning men of the Jews, among them Bahri ibn Amr, al-Nu'man ibn Awfa and Marhab ibn Zayd. They came with their children to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, is there any sin upon these?" He said: "No." They said: "We are no different from them. What we do by day is expiated for us by night, and what we do by night is expiated for us by day." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[See Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 148, citing al-Kalbi without an isnad; Lubab al-Nuqul by al-Suyuti, p. 167; al-Durr al-Manthur 2/560. Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi, pp. 44-45, that al-Tha'labi mentioned it from al-Kalbi.]]

Mujahid and Ikrimah said: They used to bring their children forward in the prayer, claiming that they had no sins, and that was the "purification."

al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the Jews and Christians when they said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved," and "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian" [al-Baqarah 2:111]. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: It is the praising of some of them by others. Tariq ibn Shihab narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "A man sets out from his house with his religion with him, then comes to a man who possesses for himself and for himself no harm or benefit, and says: 'By Allah, you are such and such!' And he returns to his house with no part of his religion left with him." Then he recited: "Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?" and the rest of the verse.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, that is, He cleanses, absolves of sins and sets right. ﴿And they will not be wronged a fatil﴾. Fatil is the name for what is in the split of a date stone (fatil, the thread in the cleft of the date-pit). The qitmir is the name for the thin skin over the date-stone, and the naqir is the name for the small pit on the back of the date-stone. It was also said: al-fatil comes from al-fatl (twisting), which is the dirt that is rolled between two fingers when twisting.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 50–52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Look﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿how they invent lies against Allah﴾ they fabricate against Allah, ﴿the lie﴾ in their altering of His Book. ﴿And sufficient is it as a manifest sin﴾ (i.e., the lie is sufficient as a manifest sin).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in al-Jibt and at-Taghut?﴾ The scholars differed regarding them. ʿIkrimah said: they are two idols which the polytheists worshipped besides Allah. Abu ʿUbayda said: they are every object of worship that is worshipped besides Allah. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Worship Allah and avoid at-Taghut﴾ [an-Nahl: 36]. ʿUmar said: al-Jibt is magic, and at-Taghut is the devil. This is also the saying of ash-Shaʿbi and Mujahid. Mu'adh ibn Jabal was with him and said, "I have its explanation: it is replaced in one hour a hundred times." 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Thus have I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." [[Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. 45: It was narrated by Ibn 'Adi and al-Tabarani, and in its chain are Nafi' ibn Yusuf al-Sulami and Abu Harmaz, who is weak. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said in his Musnad: Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad was asked about this verse, and he informed us from Hisham from al-Hasan, who said: "Their skins are replaced every day seventy thousand times."]]

Al-Hasan said: "The Fire consumes them every day seventy thousand times. Whenever it has consumed them, it is said to them, 'Return,' and they return as they were."

Abu 'Abd Allah... [The chain follows:] 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Mu'adh ibn Usayd informed us, al-Fadl ibn Musa informed us, al-Fudayl informed us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The distance between the shoulders of the disbeliever is a three-day journey for a swift rider." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter: The Description of Paradise and Hell: 11/415; and Muslim in al-Jannah, chapter: The Fire Will Be Entered by the Tyrants, no. 2852, 4/2190; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/250. It is also transmitted as a statement (mawquf) of Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us, 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juladi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, Shurayh ibn Yunus informed us, Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Harun ibn Sa'd, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with them), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The molar, or the fang, of the disbeliever is like Uhud, and the thickness of his skin is a three-day journey." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha, chapter: The Fire Will Be Entered by the Tyrants, no. 2851, 4/2189.]]

If it is asked: How can skins be punished which did not exist in the world and did not disobey Him?

It is answered: The first skin is restored each time.

He said ﴿other skins than them﴾ only because their attributes changed, as you would say: "I made from my ring another ring, other than it." The second ring is the first, except that the workmanship and the attribute have changed. It is like a man who leaves his brother healthy, then after a time sees him sick and weak, and says: "I am not the one you knew," while he is the very same person, except that his attributes have changed.

Al-Suddi said: The skin is replaced by another skin made of the flesh of the disbeliever; then the skin is returned to flesh, and from the flesh another skin is brought forth. It was also said: The person is punished in the skin, not the skin itself, as is evident from His saying ﴿that they may taste the punishment﴾, and He did not say "that it may taste." 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya said: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, clothes the people of the Fire in skins that do not feel pain, so that it is an increase of punishment for them. Whenever a skin is burned, He replaces it with another skin, as He said: ﴿their garments of pitch﴾ [Ibrahim: 50]; the garments cause them pain while they themselves do not feel pain.

His saying: ﴿that they may taste the punishment; indeed Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾.

The Almighty said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to shade, extended shade﴾ – a shelter (*kaneenan*) that the sun does not cancel, and in which neither heat nor cold can harm them.

The Almighty said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾. It was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi of Banu Abd al-Dar, who was the *sadin* (keeper) of the Ka'bah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah on the day of the Conquest, Uthman closed the door of the House and climbed onto the roof. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for the key, and it was said to him: "It is with Uthman." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked him for it, but he refused and said: "Had I known that he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have withheld the key from him." Then Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) twisted his arm, took the key from him, and opened the door. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered the House and prayed two rak'ahs in it. When he came out, al-Abbas asked him for the key, requesting that it be given to him and that he combine for him the *siqayah* (providing water to pilgrims) and the *sidanah* (keeping the key of the Ka'bah). Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that the key be returned to Uthman and that he be apologised to. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) did so. Uthman said to him: "You coerced me and harmed me, then you came to me gently." Ali said: "Indeed Allah the Exalted revealed concerning you a Qur'an," and he recited the verse to him. Uthman said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." The key was with him, and when he died he handed it to his brother Shaybah. So the key and the *sidanah* remain with their descendants until the Day of Resurrection. [[Al-Wahidi related it in *Asbab al-Nuzul* (p. 150) without an isnad. Ibn Hajar said: "Thus al-Tha'labi and then al-Baghawi mentioned it without an isnad, and likewise al-Wahidi mentioned it in *al-Wasit* and *al-Asbab*" (*al-Kafi al-Shaf*, p. 45). See al-Tabari (8/491). In *al-Durr al-Manthur* (2/570) it is attributed to Ibn Mardawayh by way of al-Kalbi from Ibn Abbas.]]

It has been said: the meaning of the verse is all trusts. Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zarrad informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Idris al-Jurjani and Abu Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mu'allim al-Harawi informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Isa al-Malini informed us, al-Hasan ibn Sufyan al-Nasawi informed us, Shaybān ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Abu Hilal informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Rarely did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) address us without saying: 'Verily, there is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and no religion for one who has no covenant.'" [[Ahmad related it in *al-Musnad* (3/135, 154) and in *al-Sunnah* (p. 97). Diya' al-Maqdisi related it in *al-Ahadith al-Mukhtarah* by two routes from Anas, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it in *Mawarid al-Zam'an* (no. 36, p. 40). The hadith has supporting narrations, which is why al-Dhahabi said: "Its chain is strong." See *Mishkat al-Masabih* (1/17) and *Fayd al-Qadir* (6/381). The author also related it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (1/75).]]

The Almighty said: ﴿And when you judge between people, judge with justice﴾, that is, with equity. ﴿Indeed, excellent is what Allah instructs you to do﴾, that is, excellent is the thing with which He admonishes you. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Hamad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Zayyat informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, Ibn Abbad narrated to us, Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us from Amr ibn Dinar, from Amr ibn Aws, that he heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him) attribute it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The just will be near Allah upon pulpits of light, on the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both His hands are right hands. They are those who act justly in their judgement, in their families, and in what they are entrusted with." [[Muslim related it in *al-Imarah*, chapter: The virtue of the just ruler (no. 1827), 3/1458. The author also related it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (10/63).]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us, Fudayl ibn Marzuq informed us, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the most beloved of people to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and the nearest of them to Him in sitting, is a just leader. And indeed, the most hated of people to Allah and the most severe in punishment is an oppressive leader." [[Al-Tirmidhi related it in *al-Ahkam*, chapter on what has come concerning the just leader (4/559–560), and said: "A hasan gharib hadith, which we do not know except through this route." Ahmad related it (3/22, 55) from Abu Sa'id. In the chain of both, there is Atiyyah al-Awfi: truthful but makes many errors, was a Shi'i and a mudallis (*Taqrib*). The author also related it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (10/65).]]

The Almighty said: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. For them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to shade, extended shade﴾ – a shelter (*kaneenan*) that the sun does not cancel, and in which neither heat nor cold can harm them.

The Almighty said: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners﴾. It was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi of Banu Abd al-Dar, who was the *sadin* (keeper) of the Ka'bah. When the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah on the day of the Conquest, Uthman closed the door of the House and climbed onto the roof. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked him for it, but he refused and said: "Had I known that he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have withheld the key from him." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that the key be returned to Uthman and that he be apologised to. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) did so.
