So the key and the *sidanah* remain with their descendants until the Day of Resurrection. [[Al-Wahidi related it in *Asbab al-Nuzul* (p. 150) without an isnad. Ibn Hajar said: "Thus al-Tha'labi and then al-Baghawi mentioned it without an isnad, and likewise al-Wahidi mentioned it in *al-Wasit* and *al-Asbab*" (*al-Kafi al-Shaf*, p. 45). See al-Tabari (8/491). In *al-Durr al-Manthur* (2/570) it is attributed to Ibn Mardawayh by way of al-Kalbi from Ibn Abbas.]]

It has been said: the meaning of the verse is all trusts. Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ali al-Zarrad informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Idris al-Jurjani and Abu Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mu'allim al-Harawi informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Isa al-Malini informed us, al-Hasan ibn Sufyan al-Nasawi informed us, Shaybān ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Abu Hilal informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Rarely did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) address us without saying: 'Verily, there is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness, and no religion for one who has no covenant.'" [[Ahmad related it in *al-Musnad* (3/135, 154) and in *al-Sunnah* (p. 97). Diya' al-Maqdisi related it in *al-Ahadith al-Mukhtarah* by two routes from Anas, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it in *Mawarid al-Zam'an* (no. 36, p. 40). The hadith has supporting narrations, which is why al-Dhahabi said: "Its chain is strong." See *Mishkat al-Masabih* (1/17) and *Fayd al-Qadir* (6/381). The author also related it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (1/75).]]

The Almighty said: ﴿And when you judge between people, judge with justice﴾, that is, with equity. ﴿Indeed, excellent is what Allah instructs you to do﴾, that is, excellent is the thing with which He admonishes you. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing﴾. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Hamad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Zayyat informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, Ibn Abbad narrated to us, Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us from Amr ibn Dinar, from Amr ibn Aws, that he heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him) attribute it to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The just will be near Allah upon pulpits of light, on the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both His hands are right hands. They are those who act justly in their judgement, in their families, and in what they are entrusted with." [[Muslim related it in *al-Imarah*, chapter: The virtue of the just ruler (no. 1827), 3/1458. The author also related it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (10/63).]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us, Fudayl ibn Marzuq informed us, from Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the most beloved of people to Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and the nearest of them to Him in sitting, is a just leader. And indeed, the most hated of people to Allah and the most severe in punishment is an oppressive leader." [[Al-Tirmidhi related it in *al-Ahkam*, chapter on what has come concerning the just leader (4/559–560), and said: "A hasan gharib hadith, which we do not know except through this route." Ahmad related it (3/22, 55) from Abu Sa'id. In the chain of both, there is Atiyyah al-Awfi: truthful but makes many errors, was a Shi'i and a mudallis (*Taqrib*). The author also related it in *Sharh al-Sunnah* (10/65).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 59:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾. The scholars differed concerning ﴿those in authority﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them, said: They are the jurists (fuqaha') and scholars (ulama') who teach people the landmarks of their religion. This is also the view of al-Hasan, al-Dahhak and Mujahid, and its evidence is the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those who draw conclusions from it would have known it﴾ [an-Nisa: 83].

Abu Hurayrah said: They are the rulers and governors (al-umara' wa'l-wulat).

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: It is incumbent upon the imam to judge by what Allah has revealed and to render the trust. When he does so, it is incumbent upon the subjects to listen and obey.

Abu 'Ali Hassan ibn Sa'd al-Mani'i informed us; Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us; Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us; 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us; Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys the commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the commander has disobeyed me." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter "One fights behind the imam and is protected by him": 6/116, and in al-Ahkam: 13/111; and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the obligation to obey rulers in what is not sinful, no. (1835): 3/1466. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/69.]

Abu 'Abd Allah 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Musaddad informed us; Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah, who said to me: Nafi' narrated to me, from 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Listening and obedience is due from the Muslim man in what he loves and what he dislikes, so long as he is not commanded to sin. If he is commanded to sin, there is no listening and no obedience." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Ahkam, chapter on listening and obedience to the imam: 13/121, and in al-Jihad: 6/115; and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the obligation to obey rulers in what is not sinful, no. (1839): 3/1469; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/43.]

[Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahman Muhammad al-Darawardi informed us] [The words in brackets are missing from manuscript (A).] Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Yahya ibn Sa'id: 'Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn 'Ubadah informed us that his father informed him, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to listen and obey in ease and hardship, in what pleases us and what displeases us, and on being given preference over us, and that we would not dispute the command with its people, and that we would speak the truth wherever we are, fearing in Allah no blame of any blamer." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Fitan, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "You will see after me matters you will disapprove": 13/5, and in al-Ahkam: 13/192; and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the obligation to obey rulers in what is not sinful, no. (1709): 3/1470; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/46.]

Abu 'Abd Allah 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Qaffal informed us; Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn al-Fadl al-Burujirdi informed us; Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Sayrafi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Kudaymi informed us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi informed us, from Shu'bah, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Dharr: "Listen and obey, even if it is a slave from Abyssinia whose head is like a raisin." [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Adhan, chapter on the imamate of the tempted and the innovator: 2/188; and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the obligation to obey rulers in what is not sinful, no. (1837): 3/1467; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/42.]

Abu 'Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us; Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jirahi informed us; Abu al-'Abbas informed us; Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us; Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us; Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Kindi informed us; Zayd ibn al-Hubab informed us; Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed us; Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivering a sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and he said: "Fear Allah, pray your five prayers, fast your month, pay the zakat of your wealth, and obey those in authority over you, and you will enter the Garden of your Lord." [Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salat, chapter on what has been mentioned concerning the virtue of prayer, 3/238, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; and Ahmad: 5/251. Its chain is hasan. He narrated it by another route in 5/262, and in it there is weakness. Also reported by Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi, and al-Khal'i narrated it in his fawa'id. See Fayd al-Qadir: 1/130. The author also reported it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/23-24, and said: this is a hasan hadith.]

It is said: What is meant is the commanders of the expeditions (umara' al-saraya). Abu 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl informed us; Hajjaj ibn Muhammad informed us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning 'Ubayd Allah ibn Hudhafah ibn Qays ibn 'Adi, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him at the head of an expedition. [Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Tafsir, Surat al-Nisa', chapter "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger": 8/253; and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the obligation to obey rulers in what is not sinful, no. (1834): 3/1465. See also: al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 152.]

And 'Ikrimah said: By "those in authority" he meant Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both. Abu al-Muzaffar Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Taymi narrated to us; Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Uthman ibn al-Qasim informed us; Khaythamah ibn Sulayman ibn Haydarah al-Atrablusi informed us; 'Amr ibn Abi 'Arzah informed us in Kufa; Thabit ibn Musa al-'Abid informed us, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Rib'i, from Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I do not know how long I will remain among you, so follow those after me: Abu Bakr and 'Umar." [Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Manaqib: 10/149; Ibn Majah in the Muqaddimah, no. (97): 1/37; al-Hakim in abridged form: 3/75, and he authenticated it and al-Dhahabi agreed; Ahmad: 5/382, 402 from Hudhayfah; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/101, saying: a sahih hadith.] may Allah be pleased with both of them.

And 'Ata' said: They are the Muhajirun, the Ansar, and those who follow them in goodness, based on the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾, and so on. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khallal informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Isma'il al-Makki, from al-Hasan, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of my Companions among my nation is like salt in food; food is not made good except with salt." [Reported by Imam Ahmad in Fada'il al-Sahabah: 1/58, from al-Hasan as a mursal report, and in it are two defects: the unknown identity of the shaykh of Ma'mar, and the mursal transmission of al-Hasan al-Basri. Also Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, p. 200; and Abu Ya'la and al-Bazzar narrated it similarly, and in it is Isma'il ibn Muslim, who is weak. The author also reported it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/73. See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/18; Fayd al-Qadir: 5/516; Kashf al-Khafa' by al-'Ajluni: 2/257-258.] He said: al-Hasan said: "Our salt has gone, so how shall we be made good?"

His words, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿And if you dispute about anything﴾, i.e., differ, ﴿concerning a matter﴾ of your religion. Tanazu' means the difference of opinions, and its root is from al-naz' (pulling), as though the two disputants pull at and resist each other. ﴿Then refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾, i.e., to the Book of Allah and to His Messenger while he is alive, and after his death to his Sunnah. Referring to the Book and the Sunnah is obligatory if the answer is found in them; if it is not found, then the way is ijtihad (independent reasoning). It is also said: referring to Allah and the Messenger means that one says, regarding what one does not know: "Allah and His Messenger know best."

﴿If you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That﴾, i.e., referring it to Allah and the Messenger, ﴿is better and more favorable in outcome﴾, i.e., better in its end and consequence.

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah an-Nisa', verse 60:**

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to seek judgement from the *taghut* (false authority, idol, or anything worshipped or obeyed besides Allah)﴾, to the end of the verse. Al-Sha'bi said: There was a dispute between a man from the Jews and a man from the hypocrites (*munafiqun*). The Jew said, "Let us go to Muhammad, for he knows that he does not take bribes and does not show partiality in judgement." The hypocrite said, "Let us go to the Jews, for he knows that they take bribes and show partiality in judgement." They agreed to go to a soothsayer (*kahin*) in Juhaynah and have him judge between them, so this verse was revealed.[[Narrated by al-Wahidi with his chain from al-Sha'bi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 154; and by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, 8/508. Al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur, 2/580, attributes it to Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

Jabir said: The *tawaghit* to whom they would go for judgement were one in Juhaynah and one in Aslam, and in every tribe there were soothsayers.

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: It was revealed concerning a hypocrite man called Bishr, who had a dispute with a Jew. The Jew said, "Let us go to Muhammad." The hypocrite said, "Rather, let us go to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf," and he is the one whom Allah called *taghut*. The Jew refused to have his case heard by anyone but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the hypocrite saw this, he went with him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ruled in favour of the Jew. When they left his presence, the hypocrite clung to him and said, "Come with us to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him." So they came to 'Umar. The Jew said, "I and this man disputed before Muhammad, and he ruled in my favour against him, but he was not content with his ruling and claimed that he would bring the case to you." 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to the hypocrite, "Is that so?" He said, "Yes." 'Umar said to them both, "Wait here until I come out to you." 'Umar entered the house, took his sword, wrapped it around himself, then came out and struck the hypocrite with it until he was dead, and said, "This is how I judge between those who are not content with the judgement of Allah and the judgement of His Messenger." Then this verse was revealed. Jibril said, "'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, distinguished between truth and falsehood, so he was named *al-Faruq* (the Distinguisher)."[[Ibn Hajar said: al-Tha'labi mentioned it from the narration of al-Kalbi, from Abu 'Asim, from Ibn 'Abbas; al-Wahidi also mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 155.]]

Al-Suddi said: Some Jews embraced Islam, and some of them were hypocrites. In the pre-Islamic period (*jahiliyyah*), when a man from Banu Qurayzah killed a man from Banu al-Nadir, he was killed in retaliation, or his *diyah* (blood money) of one hundred *wasq* of dates was taken. But when a man from Banu al-Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, he was not killed in retaliation, and he paid the *diyah* of sixty *wasq*. The Nadir, who were allies of the Aws, were more honourable and more numerous than Qurayzah, who were allies of the Khazraj. When Allah brought Islam, and the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, a man from al-Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, and they disputed over this. Banu al-Nadir said, "We and you had agreed that we should kill from among you, but you would not kill from among us, and your *diyah* is sixty *wasq* while our *diyah* is one hundred *wasq*. So we will give you that." The Khazraj said, "This is something you did in the pre-Islamic period, because you were many and we were few, and you overpowered us. Today we and you are brothers, our religion and yours is one, so you have no superiority over us." Some of the hypocrites among them said, "Let us go to Abu Burdah, the Aslami soothsayer." Some of the Muslims from both groups said, "No, rather let us go to the Prophet (ﷺ)." The hypocrites refused and went to Abu Burdah so that he would judge between them. He said, "Make the morsel large," meaning the share. They said, "For you, ten *wasq*." He said, "No, rather one hundred *wasq* as my *diyah*." They refused to give him more than ten *wasq*, and he refused to judge between them. So Allah revealed the verse of retribution (*qisas*), and this verse: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to seek judgement from the *taghut*﴾, meaning the soothsayer or Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.[[Narrated by al-Tabari, 8/510; al-Suyuti, in al-Durr, 2/581, attributes it to Ibn Abi Hatim.]] ﴿And they have been commanded to reject it, and Satan desires to lead them far astray﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 61–62:

﴿When it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion.﴾ Meaning: they turn away from you with full aversion.

﴿How then, when a calamity befalls them﴾ This is a warning, meaning: how will they act when a calamity befalls them, ﴿because of what their hands have sent forward﴾, that is, the punishment for their aversion. It was also said: it is every calamity that strikes all the hypocrites in this world and the Hereafter. The speech ends here. Then the speech returns to what preceded, informing about their conduct, so He said: ﴿Then they come to you﴾, that is, they seek judgment from the Taghut (false judge), ﴿then they come to you﴾ [they seek your favor and swear] [[In (A) the phrase reads thus: (they come to you and fear you).]].

It was also said: he meant by the calamity the killing of the hypocrite by 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), and then they came seeking his blood-money. ﴿They swear by Allah, "We intended nothing but good will and conciliation"﴾, meaning: we did not intend by deviating from it in the judgment or by appealing to 'Umar anything but ﴿good will and conciliation﴾. Al-Kalbi said: "Only good will in speech, and conciliation: rightness." Ibn Kaysan said: "Truth and justice." Its parallel is: ﴿They will surely swear, "We intended nothing but the best."﴾ It was also said: it is the kindness of some of them toward others. It was also said: it is bringing the matter closer to the truth, not passing a ruling against the judgment of the arbiter. And tawfiq is conformity with the truth. It was also said: it is reconciliation and bringing together the two disputants.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 63–65:

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾ of hypocrisy, meaning: He knows that what is in their hearts is contrary to what is on their tongues. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning: from punishing them. It was also said: "I turn away from accepting their excuse. Admonish them with the tongue, and say to them a far-reaching word (qawlan baligh)." It was also said: this is threatening them with Allah. It was also said: that you threaten them with killing if they do not repent. Al-Hasan said: "The far-reaching word is that you say to them: 'If you manifest what is in your hearts of hypocrisy, you will be killed,' because it reaches their souls in every way." Al-Dahhak said: ﴿So turn away from them and admonish them﴾ in public, ﴿and say to them in their own selves a far-reaching word﴾ in private and in solitude. He said: it was said that this is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of fighting.

And the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah﴾, meaning: by the command of Allah, because obedience to the Messenger became obligatory by the command of Allah. Al-Zajjaj said: "To be obeyed by the permission of Allah" because Allah has permitted it and commanded it. It was also said: ﴿except to be obeyed﴾ is a complete and sufficient statement, and ﴿by the permission of Allah﴾ means: by the knowledge of Allah and His decree, i.e., the occurrence of obedience to him happens by the permission of Allah. ﴿And if, when they wronged themselves﴾ by taking their dispute to the false deity (ṭāghūt), ﴿they had come to you and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that which is in dispute between them﴾ — the verse.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us, that Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, that Abu al-Yaman informed us, that Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me: that al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with him) used to narrate that he disputed with a man of the Ansar who had witnessed Badr before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning watercourses (shirāj)[[The shirāj: channels of water flowing from the lava plains (ḥarrah) down to the plain; its singular is sharj. The ḥarrah is land with black stones, and in Medina there are a number of them.]] from the ḥarrah, with which they were both irrigating. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to al-Zubayr: "Irrigate, O Zubayr, then send [the water] to your neighbour." The Ansari became angry and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it because he is your paternal aunt's son?" The face of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) changed colour, then he said to al-Zubayr: "Irrigate, then hold back the water until it reaches the walls (al-jidr)." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then gave al-Zubayr his full right, though previously he had given a ruling in al-Zubayr's favour with an opinion that he intended as a broad allowance for both him and the Ansari. When the Ansari provoked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he gave al-Zubayr his full right in the clear judgment.

ʿUrwa said: al-Zubayr said: "By Allah, I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that which is in dispute between them﴾ — the verse."

It is also narrated that the Ansari who disputed with al-Zubayr was named Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. When they went out, he passed by al-Miqdad and said: "For whom was the judgment?" The Ansari said: "He judged in favour of his paternal aunt's son," and twisted his cheek. A Jew who was with al-Miqdad noticed this and said: "May Allah fight these people! They testify that he is the Messenger of Allah, then they accuse him in a judgment he gives between them. By Allah, we once sinned in the lifetime of Musa (peace be upon him), and Musa called us to repent of it, saying: 'Kill yourselves,' and we did so, until our slain reached seventy thousand in obedience to our Lord, until He was pleased with us." Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas said: "Indeed, by Allah, Allah knows the truth of me, and if Muhammad commanded me to kill myself, I would do it." Then Allah revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge﴾[[Al-Wahidi and his teacher al-Tha'labi and al-Mahdawi related that it was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, and their basis is what Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted as mursal with a strong chain; it was objected that Hatib, although a Badri, is among the Muhajirun, while some reports say that a man of the Ansar witnessed Badr. As for the rest of the story and their passing by the Jew, al-Tha'labi mentioned it without a chain; see Fath al-Bari: 5/35–36.]].

Mujahid and al-Sha'bi said: it was revealed concerning Bishr, the hypocrite, and the Jew who brought their dispute before ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him).[[The Hafiz Ibn Kathir mentioned a report about the story of the hypocrite and the Jew who brought their dispute before the Prophet (ﷺ) and then before ʿUmar, and ʿUmar's killing of the hypocrite. He said: "Very strange," narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/522.]]

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿But no﴾, meaning: the matter is not as they claim, that they are believers, then they are not content with your judgment. Then he resumed the oath: ﴿by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe﴾. It is permissible that ﴿lā﴾ in His saying ﴿fa-lā﴾ is an extra particle (ṣilah), as in His saying ﴿fa-lā uqsimu﴾. ﴿Until they make you judge﴾: i.e., make you an arbiter (ḥakam), ﴿concerning that which is in dispute between them﴾: i.e., that which has become disputed and confused among them of their affairs, and his ruling became unclear to them. From this comes "shajar" (tree), due to the interlacing of its branches with one another. ﴿Then they find within themselves no discomfort﴾. Mujahid said: "doubt (shakk)." Others said: "constriction (ḍīq)." ﴿Concerning what you have decided﴾. Al-Dahhak said: "sin (ithm)," meaning: they would be sinning by denying what you have decided. ﴿And submit in full submission﴾: i.e., and yield to your command with complete yielding.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 4, verses 66–69:**

Allah's words: ﴿And if We had prescribed for them, "Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes,"﴾ means: We made it obligatory and decreed it upon them, as We commanded the Children of Israel, ﴿they would not have done it, except a few of them﴾, as We commanded the Children of Israel to leave Egypt. The meaning is that We only prescribed upon them obedience to the Messenger and contentment with his judgment. Had We prescribed upon them killing and leaving their homes, they would not have done it, ﴿except a few of them﴾. It was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays, and he was among the few whom Allah excepted. Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: When this verse was revealed, Umar, Ammar ibn Yasir, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who were the few, said: "By Allah, if He had commanded us, we would have done it, and praise be to Allah who has spared us." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 70–72:

﴿That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾. That is, the reward of the Hereafter. It was also said: [the bounty is given] to those who obey the Messenger of Allah and love him. In this is a clarification that they will never attain that rank by their own obedience; they attained it only by the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib informed us: Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Be moderate and aim for correctness, and know that none of you will be saved by his deed." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy and bounty."[[A portion of a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Iman, chapter "The religion is ease": 1/93, and in other places; and by Muslim in Kitab al-Munafiqin, chapter "No one will enter Paradise by his deed", no. (1816): 4/2170, and in Kitab al-Birr wa'l-Sila; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 14/390.]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution﴾ from your enemy, that is, your troops and your weapons of war. Al-hidhr and al-hadhar are one and the same, like al-mithl and al-mathal, and al-shibh and al-shabah. ﴿Then go forth﴾ [i.e., "march out"] ﴿in separate groups﴾, that is, in detachments, one detachment after another. And al-thubat are groups in dispersion; its singular is thubah. ﴿Or go forth all together﴾, that is, assembled, all of you, with the Prophet (ﷺ).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, among you is he who will surely lag behind﴾ — it was revealed concerning the hypocrites.[[Said by Mujahid. See Ibn Kathir: 1/525.]]

He said ﴿among you﴾ only because they are gathered with the people of faith in kind, lineage, and the outward profession of Islam, not in the reality of faith. ﴿Will surely lag behind﴾, that is, will delay and be sluggish in jihad; he was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy the hypocrite. The lam in ﴿la-yubatti'anna﴾ is the lam of oath. Al-tabti'ah is delay in following a command; one says: "What delayed you?" meaning, "What held you back from us?" One says: abta'a ibti'a'an and battaa yubatti'u tabti'atan.

﴿And if a calamity strikes you﴾, that is, killing and defeat, ﴿he says: "Allah has certainly blessed me﴾ by staying behind, ﴿since I was not present among them as a witness﴾, that is, present in that battle so that I would be struck by what struck them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 73–74:

﴿And if there befalls you a bounty from Allah﴾ — a conquest and spoils — ﴿he will surely say﴾ — this is the hypocrite — and there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it. His exalted saying: ﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the worldly life for the Hereafter﴾. It was said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, and the meaning of yashrūna is yashtarūna (they buy), meaning those who choose the worldly life over the Hereafter; the meaning is: "They believed, then fought." Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah guarantees for one who strives in His way — nothing brings him out of his house except striving in His way and belief in His words — that He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to the dwelling from which he went out, along with whatever reward or spoils he has gained." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 75–77:

Allah's words: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight﴾ — i.e., do not strive (jihad) — ﴿in the cause of Allah﴾, meaning in obedience to Allah, reproaching them for abandoning jihad; ﴿and [for] the oppressed﴾ — i.e., concerning the oppressed. Ibn Shihab said: "[fight] in the cause of the oppressed, to deliver them." It was also said: "[fight] for the deliverance of the oppressed from the hands of the polytheists." There was in Makkah a group ﴿of men, women and children﴾ who suffered great harm from the polytheists, ﴿who say, "Our Lord, bring us out of this city whose people are wrongdoers"﴾ — meaning Makkah. "Its people are wrongdoers" means the polytheists; "its people" refers to the city whose characteristic is that its people are polytheists. The word ﴿wrongdoers﴾ is in the genitive (khafada) because it is an adjective (na't) of "its people"; when "its people" returned to "the city," it became as if the action belonged to the city, as one says, "I passed by a man whose beauty is [in] his eye." ﴿And appoint for us from Yourself a protector﴾ — i.e., one who will take charge of our affairs; ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾ — i.e., one who will repel the enemy from us. Allah answered their supplication, and when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he appointed Attab ibn Usayd over them, and Allah made him a helper for them, one who grants justice to the oppressed against the oppressors.

Allah's words: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah﴾ — i.e., in His obedience; ﴿and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the taghut﴾ — i.e., in the obedience of Satan; ﴿so fight, [O believers], against the allies of Satan﴾ — i.e., his party and his soldiers, who are the disbelievers; ﴿indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak﴾ — his scheming. As he did on the Day of Badr, when he saw the angels he feared they would seize him, so he fled and abandoned them.

Allah's words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"﴾ — the verse. Al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf al-Zuhri, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi, Qudamah ibn Maz'un al-Jumahi, Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, and a group who used to suffer great harm from the polytheists in Makkah before they emigrated, and who would say: "O Messenger of Allah, permit us to fight them, for they have harmed us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would say to them: "Restrain your hands, for I have not been commanded to fight them" [[al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 159–160; al-Nasa'i related it from Ibn ʿAbbas in al-Sunan: 6/3, and al-Hakim: 2/66, 307.]].

﴿And establish prayer and give zakat﴾. When they emigrated to Madinah and Allah commanded them to fight the polytheists, this was difficult for some of them. Allah said: ﴿When fighting was prescribed for them [kutiba]﴾ — i.e., made obligatory — ﴿behold, a party of them fear men as they fear Allah or [even] greater fear﴾ — meaning they fear the polytheists of Makkah, ﴿as they fear Allah﴾ — i.e., as they fear Allah; ﴿or greater in fear﴾ — more. It was also said: the meaning is "and more intense in fear." ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting [jihad]? If only [lawla] You would delay us to a near term"﴾ — meaning death; i.e., "Why did You not leave us until we die at our appointed times?"

They differed concerning those who said this. It was said: it was said by a group of the hypocrites, because the statement ﴿Why have You prescribed for us fighting?﴾ is not fitting for believers. It was also said: it was said by a group of believers who were not firmly rooted in knowledge; they said it out of fear and cowardice, not out of belief, and then they repented; and the people of faith differ in degrees of faith. It was also said: they were a people who had been believers, but when fighting was made obligatory upon them, they became hypocrites out of cowardice and held back from jihad.

﴿Say, [O Muhammad], "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah"﴾ — i.e., its benefit and the enjoyment of it is little, and the reward of the Hereafter is better and more excellent — ﴿for those who fear [Allah]﴾ from polytheism and disobedience to the Messenger; ﴿and you will not be wronged [even] by the thread [of a date-stone]﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the yaa' (yuzlamun), and the rest read it with the taa' (tuzlamun).

Abu Salih Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Mu'adhdhin informed us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mu'awiyah al-Saydalani informed us: al-Asamm informed us: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shakir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bishr al-Abdi informed us: Mis'ar ibn Kidam informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The world, in comparison to the Hereafter, is nothing but like what one of you puts his finger into the sea — let him look at what it returns with" [[Related by Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha wa Ahliha, Bab Fana' al-Dunya wa Bayan al-Hashr Yawm al-Qiyamah, no. (2858): 4/2193.]].

Allah said: ﴿When fighting was prescribed for them [kutiba]﴾ — i.e., made obligatory — ﴿behold, a party of them fear men as they fear Allah or [even] greater fear﴾ — meaning they fear the polytheists of Makkah, ﴿as they fear Allah﴾ — i.e., as they fear Allah; ﴿or greater in fear﴾ — more. It was also said: the meaning is "and more intense in fear." ﴿And they said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting [jihad]? If only [lawla] You would delay us to a near term"﴾ — meaning death; i.e., "Why did You not leave us until we die at our appointed times?"

They differed concerning those who said this. It was said: it was said by a group of the hypocrites, because the statement ﴿Why have You prescribed for us fighting?﴾ is not fitting for believers. It was also said: it was said by a group of believers who were not firmly rooted in knowledge; they said it out of fear and cowardice, not out of belief, and then they repented; and the people of faith differ in degrees of faith. It was also said: they were a people who had been believers, but when fighting was made obligatory upon them, they became hypocrites out of cowardice and held back from jihad.

﴿Say, [O Muhammad], "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah"﴾ — i.e., its benefit and the enjoyment of it is little, and the reward of the Hereafter is better and more excellent — ﴿for those who fear [Allah]﴾ from polytheism and disobedience to the Messenger; ﴿and you will not be wronged [even] by the thread [of a date-stone]﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read it with the yaa' (yuzlamun), and the rest read it with the taa' (tuzlamun).

Abu Salih Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Mu'adhdhin informed us: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Mu'awiyah al-Saydalani informed us: al-Asamm informed us: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Shakir informed us: Muhammad ibn Bishr al-Abdi informed us: Mis'ar ibn Kidam informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The world, in comparison to the Hereafter, is nothing but like what one of you puts his finger into the sea — let him look at what it returns with" [[Related by Muslim in al-Jannah wa Sifat Na'imiha wa Ahliha, Bab Fana' al-Dunya wa Bayan al-Hashr Yawm al-Qiyamah, no. (2858): 4/2193.]].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 78–79:**

His, the Mighty and Majestic's, saying: ﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you﴾, meaning: death will descend upon you. It was revealed concerning the hypocrites who said about the slain of Uhud: "If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed." So Allah refuted them with His saying: ﴿Wherever you are, death will overtake you﴾ [[al-Tabari: 9/8; al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 160; and al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/595–596.]] [91a] ﴿even if you were in towers built up high﴾. The "burooj" (towers) are the fortresses and castles. The "mushayyadah" (built up high) are those that are raised and lofty. Qatadah said: its meaning is "in fortified palaces." Ikrimah said: "plastered." The "shayd" is plaster (gypsum).

﴿And if good befalls them﴾: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the hypocrites. This is because they said, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madinah: "We have continued to notice a decrease in our fruits and our crops since this man and his companions came to us."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if good befalls them﴾, meaning the Jews, ﴿good﴾, that is, fertility and cheapness of prices, ﴿they say: "This is from Allah"﴾, meaning, for us. ﴿And if evil befalls them﴾, meaning drought and high prices, ﴿they say: "This is from you"﴾, that is, from the ill omen of Muhammad and his companions. It was also said: what is meant by "good" is victory and spoils on the day of Badr, and by "evil" is killing and defeat on the day of Uhud. "They say: 'This is from you'" means: "You are the one who brought us to this, O Muhammad." According to this view, this is the saying of the hypocrites. ﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad: ﴿"All of it is from Allah"﴾, that is, the good and the evil are all from Allah. Then He rebuked them for their ignorance, saying: ﴿So what is wrong with these people, that they hardly understand any statement?﴾, meaning the hypocrites and the Jews, ﴿that they hardly understand any statement﴾, that is, they do not comprehend speech. It was also said: "the statement" here is the Qur'an, meaning they do not understand the meanings of the Qur'an.

His saying: ﴿So what is wrong with these people﴾. Al-Farra' said: this expression ("fa-ma lil") has become so common in speech that they came to think the lam (ل) is attached to it, and that the two are one word. So in some instances they separated the lam from what follows it, and in others they joined it. The "ittisal" (joining) is the recitation (qira'ah). It is not permissible to pause on the lam, because it is a lam of jarr (the lam that governs the genitive).

His, the Mighty and Majestic's, saying: ﴿Whatever good reaches you﴾, that is, good and blessing, ﴿is from Allah; and whatever evil reaches you﴾, that is, affliction or a matter you dislike, ﴿is from yourself﴾, that is, because of your sins. The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, while the intended meaning is others. A parallel to it is His saying: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned﴾ [al-Shura: 30]. The people of qadar (the Qadariyyah, who deny divine predestination) cling to the apparent meaning of this verse, saying: Allah has negated evil from Himself and attributed it to the servant, when He said: ﴿And whatever evil reaches you is from yourself﴾. But there is no argument for them in it, because the verse does not mean the good and evil deeds that are earned, namely obedience and disobedience. Rather, it means what reaches them of blessings and trials, and that is not their own action, as evidenced by the fact that He attributed it to someone other than them, and did not attribute it to them, when He said: ﴿whatever reaches you (mā aṣābak)﴾. One does not say of obedience and disobedience "aṣābanī" (it struck me); rather one says "aṣabtuhā" (I did it). And one says of blessings "aṣābanī" (it reached me). This is evidenced by the fact that He did not mention reward or punishment for it. It is like His saying: ﴿But when good comes to them, they say, "This is ours"; and if evil befalls them, they attribute it to an omen from Moses and those with him﴾ [al-A'raf: 131]. When He mentioned the good and evil deeds that are earned, He attributed them to the servant and promised reward or punishment for them, saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever brings an evil deed will be recompensed only with its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160].

It was also said: the meaning of the verse is: whatever good reaches you of victory and triumph on the day of Badr is from Allah, that is, from the grace of Allah; and whatever evil reaches you of killing and defeat on the day of Uhud is from yourself, that is, because of the sin of your own self in opposing the Messenger ﷺ.

If it is asked: how can His saying ﴿Say: "All of it is from Allah"﴾ be reconciled with His saying ﴿from yourself﴾? It is said: His saying ﴿Say: "All of it is from Allah"﴾ means that fertility and drought, victory and defeat, are all from Allah. And His saying ﴿from yourself﴾ means: whatever evil reaches you is from Allah, but it is because of your own sin, as a punishment for you. This is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned﴾ [al-Shura: 30]. This is supported by what Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: that he recited ﴿And whatever evil reaches you is from yourself﴾ and said: "And I have written it against you."

Some of them said: this verse is connected to what precedes it, and there is an implied speech in it. Its estimated meaning is: "So what is wrong with these people, that they hardly understand any statement? They say: 'Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself.' Say: 'All of it is from Allah.'" ﴿And We have sent you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ to your sending and your truthfulness. It was also said: "And sufficient is Allah as a witness" that the good and the evil are all from Allah the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 80:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾. The reason for this is that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever loves me has loved Allah." Some of the hypocrites said: "This man only wants us to take him as a lord, just as the Christians took Jesus, son of Mary, as a lord." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [[Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (46): I have not found it.]] That is: whoever obeys the Messenger in what he commands has obeyed Allah. ﴿And whoever turns away﴾ from his obedience, ﴿then We have not sent you, O Muhammad, as a guardian over them﴾, that is, a watcher and an overseer; rather, all their affairs rest with Him, exalted is He. It is also said: Allah, mighty and majestic is He, abrogated this by the verse of the sword, and commanded him to fight whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And they say, "Obedience."﴾ That is, the hypocrites say to the Messenger (ﷺ) with their tongues: "We have believed in you, so command us." Their words, "Your command is obedience," mean: "Our affair and our state is that we obey you." The grammarians (al-nahwiyyun) said: that is, "Our command and our condition is that we obey you."

﴿Then when they go out from your presence﴾ means they leave. ﴿a group of them spends the night plotting other than what you say﴾. Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: "Bayyata" means "changed" and "altered" what the Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined upon them, so that "tabyit" (nightly planning) carries the sense of "tabdil" (substitution). Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is that they devised and plotted at night what they had promised you by day. Anything planned at night is called "tabyit." Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash said: the Arabs say of a thing that has been arranged, "qad buyyita" ("it has been plotted"), likening it to the arranging of the verses of poetry (buyut al-shi'r).

﴿And Allah records﴾ that is, He records, preserves and safeguards ﴿what they plot﴾, that is, what they falsify, alter and devise. Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means what they conceal of hypocrisy.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, O Muhammad, and do not punish them. It is also said: do not disclose their names. The Messenger (ﷺ) was forbidden from reporting the names of the hypocrites. ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as a Guardian﴾, that is: take Him as your guardian (wakil), and sufficient is Allah as a Guardian and Helper.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ That is: do they not contemplate the Qur'an? Tadabbur (reflection) is looking at the end of a matter, and the "dubr" (back/end) of everything is its last part.

﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found within it much inconsistency﴾, that is, much discrepancy and contradiction. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. It is also said: they would have found within it, in its reports of the unseen concerning what has occurred and what will occur, much divergence. Will they not then reflect on it, so that they would know, by the absence of contradiction in it and the truthfulness of what it reports, that it is the speech of Allah the Exalted, because what is not from Allah cannot be free of contradiction and divergence.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it.﴾ The reason for this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to send out expeditions (sara·ya). When they were victorious or were defeated, the hypocrites would hasten to inquire about their condition, and they would spread the news and speak of it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke of it [91/b]. They would thereby weaken the hearts of the believers. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them﴾ [[Al-Tabari: 8/570; compare al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/601–602.]], that is, the hypocrites, ﴿a matter of security﴾, that is, victory and spoils, ﴿or fear﴾, that is, killing and defeat, ﴿they spread it﴾, that is, they circulated it and made it public. ﴿But if they had referred it to the Messenger﴾, that is, if they had not spoken of it until the Prophet (ﷺ) was the one to report it, ﴿and to those of authority among them﴾, that is, the people of judgment among the Companions, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them), ﴿those who draw conclusions from it among them would have known it.﴾ That is, those who extract it, and they are the scholars. In other words, they would have known what should be concealed and what should be made public. Istinbat (drawing out) means extraction; it is said, "istanbata al-ma'" ("he extracted the water") when he brought it out. 'Ikrimah said: "yastanbitunahu" means they are eager for it and ask about it. al-Dahhak said: "yatba'unahu" (they follow it). He meant those who heard those reports from the believers and the hypocrites. If they had referred it to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to the people of judgment and knowledge, those who draw conclusions from it among them would have known it, that is, they would have loved to know it as it truly is.

﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾ all of you, ﴿except a few.﴾ If it is asked: how can He make an exception of a few when, without His bounty, all would have followed Satan? It is answered: the exception relates to what came before. It is said: the meaning is, "they spread it, except a few who did not spread it." By "the few" is meant the believers. This is the view of al-Kalbi and the preference of al-Farra', who said: because when a secret becomes known, the one who draws conclusions from it and others know it, and dissemination may occur in some cases but not in others. It is also said: "those who draw conclusions from it among them" is followed by "except a few," and then His words, ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾, form a complete statement.

It is also said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. The meaning is: were it not for that, you would have followed Satan, except a few. These were people who were guided before the coming of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the revelation of the Qur'an, such as Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqah ibn Nawfal, and a group other than these two.

Their words, "Your command is obedience," mean: "Our affair and our state is that we obey you." The grammarians (al-nahwiyyun) said: that is, "Our command and our condition is that we obey you."

﴿Then when they go out from your presence﴾ means they leave. ﴿a group of them spends the night plotting other than what you say﴾. Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: "Bayyata" means "changed" and "altered" what the Prophet (ﷺ) had enjoined upon them, so that "tabyit" (nightly planning) carries the sense of "tabdil" (substitution). Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Qutaybi said: its meaning is that they devised and plotted at night what they had promised you by day. Anything planned at night is called "tabyit." Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash said: the Arabs say of a thing that has been arranged, "qad buyyita" ("it has been plotted"), likening it to the arranging of the verses of poetry (buyut al-shi'r).

﴿And Allah records﴾ that is, He records, preserves and safeguards ﴿what they plot﴾, that is, what they falsify, alter and devise. Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: it means what they conceal of hypocrisy.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, O Muhammad, and do not punish them. It is also said: do not disclose their names. The Messenger (ﷺ) was forbidden from reporting the names of the hypocrites. ﴿And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as a Guardian﴾, that is: take Him as your guardian (wakil), and sufficient is Allah as a Guardian and Helper.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ That is: do they not contemplate the Qur'an? Tadabbur (reflection) is looking at the end of a matter, and the "dubr" (back/end) of everything is its last part.

﴿And if it had been from other than Allah, they would have found within it much inconsistency﴾, that is, much discrepancy and contradiction. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas. It is also said: they would have found within it, in its reports of the unseen concerning what has occurred and what will occur, much divergence. Will they not then reflect on it, so that they would know, by the absence of contradiction in it and the truthfulness of what it reports, that it is the speech of Allah the Exalted, because what is not from Allah cannot be free of contradiction and divergence.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it.﴾ The reason for this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to send out expeditions (sara·ya). When they were victorious or were defeated, the hypocrites would hasten to inquire about their condition, and they would spread the news and speak of it before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke of it [91/b]. They would thereby weaken the hearts of the believers. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And when there comes to them﴾ [[Al-Tabari: 8/570; compare al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/601–602.]], that is, the hypocrites, ﴿a matter of security﴾, that is, victory and spoils, ﴿or fear﴾, that is, killing and defeat, ﴿they spread it﴾, that is, they circulated it and made it public. ﴿But if they had referred it to the Messenger﴾, that is, if they had not spoken of it until the Prophet (ﷺ) was the one to report it, ﴿and to those of authority among them﴾, that is, the people of judgment among the Companions, such as Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with them), ﴿those who draw conclusions from it among them would have known it.﴾ That is, those who extract it, and they are the scholars. In other words, they would have known what should be concealed and what should be made public. Istinbat (drawing out) means extraction; it is said, "istanbata al-ma'" ("he extracted the water") when he brought it out. 'Ikrimah said: "yastanbitunahu" means they are eager for it and ask about it. al-Dahhak said: "yatba'unahu" (they follow it). He meant those who heard those reports from the believers and the hypocrites. If they had referred it to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to the people of judgment and knowledge, those who draw conclusions from it among them would have known it, that is, they would have loved to know it as it truly is.

﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾ all of you, ﴿except a few.﴾ If it is asked: how can He make an exception of a few when, without His bounty, all would have followed Satan? It is answered: the exception relates to what came before. It is said: the meaning is, "they spread it, except a few who did not spread it." By "the few" is meant the believers. This is the view of al-Kalbi and the preference of al-Farra', who said: because when a secret becomes known, the one who draws conclusions from it and others know it, and dissemination may occur in some cases but not in others. It is also said: "those who draw conclusions from it among them" is followed by "except a few," and then His words, ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan﴾, form a complete statement.

It is also said: the bounty of Allah is Islam, and His mercy is the Qur'an. The meaning is: were it not for that, you would have followed Satan, except a few. These were people who were guided before the coming of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the revelation of the Qur'an, such as Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, Waraqah ibn Nawfal, and a group other than these two.

In the verse there is evidence for the permissibility of qiyas (analogical reasoning). Some knowledge is attained through recitation and transmission, which is the explicit text (nass), and some is attained through istinbat (deduction), which is qiyas upon the meanings embedded in the texts.

Al-Baghawi's commentary (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 4, verse 84:

God Almighty says: ﴿So fight in the way of God; you are not held responsible except for yourself﴾. The reason was that the Prophet (ﷺ) had arranged with Abu Sufyan, after the Battle of Uhud, to meet at the Badr al-Sughra (the Lesser Badr) appointment in Dhu al-Qa'dah. When the appointed time arrived, he called the people to go out, but some of them disliked it. So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿So fight in the way of God; you are not held responsible except for yourself﴾. [[See Ibn Kathir's *al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya*: 4/780, and see what precedes it: pp. 137–139.]] That is: do not abandon fighting the enemy and defending the oppressed among the believers, even if you are alone, for God has promised you victory. He rebuked them for abandoning fighting. The *fa'* in His words ﴿So fight﴾ answers His words ﴿And whoever fights in the way of God and is killed or overcomes, We will bestow upon him a great reward﴾, meaning: so fight. ﴿And urge the believers﴾ to fighting, that is, urge them to striving and encourage them with the reward. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) then went out with seventy riders, and God sufficed them against fighting. Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Perhaps God will restrain the might of those who disbelieved﴾, that is, perhaps God will restrain the fighting of those who disbelieved, the polytheists. The word *'asā* (perhaps) from God is binding. ﴿And God is greater in might﴾, that is, greater in force and more mighty in authority, ﴿and greater in exemplary punishment﴾, that is, greater in punishment.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share in it, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will bear a burden of it.﴾ "A share" means a portion of it. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: The good intercession is reconciling between people, and the evil intercession is going about with tale-bearing (namimah) between people.

It has also been said: The good intercession is speaking well of people, by which one earns reward and good, and the evil is backbiting (ghibah) and speaking ill of people, by which one earns evil.

His saying ﴿a burden of it﴾ means a portion of its sin. Mujahid said: It is intercession of people on behalf of one another, and the intercessor is rewarded for his intercession even if it is not granted.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Sufyan al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Burdah, my grandfather Abu Burdah informed me, from his father, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When a man came to the Prophet ﷺ asking or seeking a need, he would turn to us with his face and say: "Intercede, so that you may be rewarded, and let Allah decree through the tongue of His Prophet what He wills."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter on the mutual cooperation of believers: 10/450, and Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on the recommendation of intercession, no. (2627): 4/2026. The lam in his saying "fal-yaqdi" is neither an imperative nor a causal particle; it may be a supplication, meaning: O Allah, decide. See Fath al-Bari: 10/451.]]

His exalted saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Muqit over all things.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: Muqit means Capable (muqtadir) and Rewarder (mujazi). The poet said: "And one who travels, I restrained myself from him, and I was capable (muqitan) of his harm."

Mujahid said: Muqit means witness (shahid). Qatadah said: Guardian (hafiz). It has also been said: its meaning is that He is Muqit over every living creature, meaning He delivers sustenance (al-qut) to it.

And there came in a hadith: "It is sufficient sin for a person that he neglects those whom he sustains and feeds" (kafa bi-l-mar'i ithman an yudayyi'a man yaquwtu wa yuqit).[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Zakat, chapter on maintaining ties of kinship: 2/261, from Abdullah ibn Amr; and Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter on the merit of spending on one's slave, no. (996): 2/692, from Abdullah ibn Amr, with the wording "It is sufficient sin for a person that he withholds from one whose sustenance he owns." Also Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/160, 193, 195. al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/342.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When you are greeted with a greeting, greet with better than it, or return it.﴾ At-tahiyyah (greeting) is the supplication for life (du'a al-hayah). What is meant by "tahiyyah" here is the salam (greeting of peace). He says: when a Muslim greets you with salam, respond with better than it, or return it the same way he greeted. So if he says, "As-salamu 'alaykum," then say, "Wa 'alaykumu as-salam wa rahmatullah." If he says, "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah," then say, "Wa 'alaykumu as-salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh." If he says, "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh," then return the same as he said.

It is related that a man greeted Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, saying, "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh," and then added something. Ibn 'Abbas said, "The salam ends in barakah."[[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab al-Salam, Bab al-'Amal fi al-Salam: 2/559. Regarding the addition in the greeting, Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: 11/6: "These weak hadiths, when combined, strengthen what has been agreed upon regarding the legitimacy of adding 'wa barakatuh.'"]]

It is also related from 'Imran ibn Husayn that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "As-salamu 'alaykum," and he returned it. Then the Prophet ﷺ said, "Ten." Then another came and said, "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah," and he returned it and sat down. He said, "Twenty." Then another came and said, "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh," and he returned it. He said, "Thirty."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Adab, Bab Kayfa as-Salam: 8/68-69, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Istidhan, Bab ma Dhukira fi Fadl as-Salam: 7/462, and he said, "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route, from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn. There are also reports on this subject from Abu Sa'id, 'Ali, and Sahl ibn Hunayf." Al-Mundhiri attributed it in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib: 3/429 to al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi with a hasan chain. See Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 7/362-363, and Ibn Kathir: 1/533.]]

Know that giving salam is a sunnah, and returning salam is an obligation (fard), and it is a communal obligation (fard kifayah). Likewise, giving salam is a sunnah of communal obligation: if one person from a group gives salam, it suffices for the sunnah. And if one person gives salam to a group and one of them returns it, the obligation falls from all of them.

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs al-Tajir informed us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn Bukayr al-Kufi informed us: Waki' informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the salam among you."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Iman, Bab Bayan annahu la yadkhulu al-Jannah illa al-Mu'minun, no. (54): 1/74, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/258.]]

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Qutaybah informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, that a man asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Which aspect of Islam is best?" He said: "That you feed the food, and greet with salam those whom you know and those whom you do not know."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, Bab Ith'am al-Ta'am min al-Islam: 1/55, and in other places, and Muslim in al-Iman, Bab Bayan Tafadul al-Islam, no. (63): 1/65, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/260.]] The meaning of his saying, "Which of Islam is best," is: which of the characteristics of Islam is best.

It was said: His saying, ﴿greet with better than it﴾, means: if the one who greeted is a Muslim; ﴿or return it﴾ with the same, if he is not a Muslim.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of the Jews greets you with salam, he only says, 'As-sam 'alaykum' (death be upon you), so say, 'Alayka' (upon you)."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Istidhan, Bab Kayfa al-Radd 'ala Ahl al-Dhimmah bi as-Salam: 11/42, and in other places, and Muslim in al-Salam, Bab al-Nahy 'an Ibtida' Ahl al-Kitab bi as-Salam wa Kayfa Yuradd 'alayhim, no. (2164): 4/1706, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/270.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Itself Accountant over all things.﴾ That is: over every matter of returning the greeting with its like or with something better than it. Hasiban means: calling to account and recompensing. Mujahid said: "Hafiza," meaning Guardian. Abu 'Ubaydah said: "Kafiyan," meaning sufficient. It is said: "Hasbi hadha," meaning this suffices me.

**Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah an-Nisa' (4), verses 87–88:**

Allah's words, ﴿Allah! There is no god but Him. He will surely gather you﴾: the lām here is *lām al-qasam* (the lām of oath). Its implied sense is: "By Allah, He will gather you in death and in the graves," ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾. The Resurrection (*al-qiyamah*) is so called because people will rise (*yaqumun*) from their graves. Allah says: ﴿the Day they come forth from the graves in haste﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:43]. It is also said that it is named for people standing (*qiyamihim*) for the reckoning. Allah says: ﴿the Day mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Mutaffifin 83:6]. ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement﴾, meaning in speech and promise. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *أَصْدَقُ* with a silent *ṣād* followed by a *dāl*, with *ishmām* of the *zāy* (a faint hint of the *z* sound in the *ṣ*).

﴿So what is [the matter] with you concerning the hypocrites, [that you are] two groups?﴾ Scholars differed regarding the occasion of its revelation. One group said: it was revealed concerning those hypocrites who turned back on the day of Uhud. When they returned, some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Kill them, for they are hypocrites." Others said: "Pardon them, for they spoke the words of Islam."

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi told us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi told us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us; Abu al-Walid told us; Shu'bah told us, from Adi ibn Thabit, who said: I heard Abd Allah ibn Yazid narrating from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ went out to Uhud, some people who had gone out with him turned back. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ became two groups: one group said, "We shall fight them," and another group said, "We shall not fight them." Then this was revealed: ﴿So what is [the matter] with you concerning the hypocrites, [that you are] two groups? And Allah has reverted them [to disbelief] for what they have earned﴾. And he (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, it [Medina] is good (*ṭaybah*); it expels sins as the fire expels the impurity of silver." [Reported by al-Bukhari in *Tafsir*, Surah an-Nisa', chapter "So what is [the matter] with you concerning the hypocrites, [that you are] two groups..." 8/256, and by Muslim at the beginning of the book on the attributes of the hypocrites, no. 2776: 4/2142.]

Mujahid said: [these were] a people who went out to Medina and embraced Islam, then apostatized, and then asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to go to Makkah to bring their merchandise, with which they traded. They went out and stayed in Makkah. The Muslims then differed about them: one said, "They are hypocrites," and another said, "They are believers." [See al-Tabari 9/9–10; al-Wahidi, *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 161.]

Others said: it was revealed concerning some people of Quraysh who came to Medina, embraced Islam, then regretted that and left, appearing as if on an outing, until they were far from Medina. They wrote to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "We remain upon the faith with which we parted from you, but we found Medina unwholesome and longed for our land." Then they went out on a trade journey towards Syria. This reached the Muslims, and some of them said, "Let us go out to them, kill them, and take what they have, for they have turned away from our religion." But a group said, "How can you kill a people who are upon your religion, if they have not left their homes?" This was happening in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, who was silent and did not forbid either group. Then this verse was revealed. [See al-Tabari 9/12–13; al-Wahidi, *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 161.]

Others said: they are a people who embraced Islam in Makkah but did not emigrate, and they used to support the polytheists; so this was revealed. [See al-Tabari 9/10–11.]

﴿So what is [the matter] with you, O assembly of believers, concerning the hypocrites, [that you have become] two groups?﴾ meaning: you have become two factions regarding them. ﴿And Allah has reverted them﴾, meaning He overturned them and returned them to disbelief, ﴿for what they have earned﴾, by their deeds that were not pure. ﴿Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray?﴾, meaning: do you wish to set on the right path? It is also said the meaning is: do you say these people are guided when Allah has sent them astray? ﴿And whomever Allah sends astray﴾, meaning whomever Allah leaves astray from guidance, ﴿you will not find for him a way﴾, meaning a path to the truth.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 89–90:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They wish﴾ means they wish (tamannaw), that is, those who turned back from the religion wish ﴿that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, and [then] you would be equal﴾ in disbelief. His saying ﴿and [then] you would be﴾ is not meant as the response to the wish (jawab al-tamanni), because the response to a wish introduced by the fa' is in the accusative (mansub). Rather, He intended coordination (al-nasaq), meaning: they wish that you would disbelieve, and they wish that you would be equal, like His saying, ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9], meaning: they wish you would compromise, and they wish you would compromise. ﴿So do not take from among them allies﴾ — this forbids allying with them — ﴿until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾ with you.

Ikrimah said: it is another emigration. Emigration is of three kinds: the emigration of the believers at the beginning of Islam, which is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿for the poor emigrants﴾ [al-Hashr: 8], and His saying, ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa': 100], and similar verses. The emigration of the hypocrites is going out in the way of Allah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), patient and seeking reward [as is related here], and He forbade allying with them until they emigrate in the way of Allah. The emigration of all the believers is what the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The emigrant is one who abandons what Allah has forbidden."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away﴾ — they turn away from monotheism and emigration — ﴿then seize them﴾, that is, take them as captives, and from this it is said of a captive, akhidh. ﴿And kill them wherever you find them﴾, within the sacred area and outside it. ﴿And take not from among them a protector or a helper.﴾ Then He excepted a group of them, saying:

﴿Except those who take refuge with a people﴾. This exception refers to killing, not to alliance, because alliance with the disbelievers and hypocrites is not permitted in any circumstance. The meaning of ﴿take refuge﴾ is: they attach themselves to them, join them, and enter among them by alliance and protection. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "They seek refuge and take shelter with a people." ﴿Between you and whom there is a covenant﴾, that is, a treaty, and they are the Aslamiyyun. That is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a truce with Hilal ibn Uwaymir al-Aslami before his departure to Makkah, on the condition that he would not help him nor help against him; and whoever reached Hilal from his people or others and sought refuge with him, they have the same protection as Hilal has.

Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas: he meant by "the people between you and whom there is a covenant" the Banu Bakr ibn Zayd ibn Manat, who were in peace and truce. Muqatil said: they are Khuza'ah.

His saying: ﴿Or those who come to you﴾, that is, they join a people who came to you, ﴿their hearts constricted﴾, that is, their hearts were straitened. Al-Hasan and Ya'qub read "hasirah" in the accusative and with tanwin, meaning: their hearts being constricted [— meaning the people who came to you, and they were Banu Mudlij, who had agreed not to fight the Muslims and had made a pact with Quraysh not to fight them; hasirat: their hearts were straitened]. ﴿From fighting you﴾, that is, from fighting you because of the covenant between you, ﴿or fighting their own people﴾, meaning: those among them who were secure. It is also possible that the meaning is that they neither fight you alongside their people nor fight their people alongside you — meaning Quraysh, whose hearts were straitened because of that.

Some of them said: "Or" is in the sense of "and" (bi-ma'na al-waw), as if he said: "to a people between you and whom there is a covenant, or who came to you with their hearts constricted," that is, their hearts were constricted from fighting you and from fighting alongside you. They were the people of Hilal al-Aslami and Banu Bakr. Allah, glorified is He, forbade fighting these apostates when they join people who have a covenant with the Muslims, because whoever joins a people under covenant takes their ruling regarding the preservation of blood.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you﴾. He mentions His favor upon the Muslims by restraining the might of the covenanted people. He says: their constriction of hearts from fighting you is because Allah cast terror into their hearts and restrained them from fighting you; and had Allah willed, He would have empowered them over you, and they would have fought you alongside their people. ﴿So if they keep away from you﴾, that is, they withdraw from fighting you, ﴿and do not fight you﴾, and whoever joins them. It is said: on the day of the conquest of Makkah. ﴿And offer you peace﴾, that is, reconciliation, so they submit and yield, ﴿then Allah has not made for you a way against them﴾, that is, a path of killing and fighting.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 89–90:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They wish﴾ means they wish (tamannaw), that is, those who turned back from the religion wish ﴿that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, and [then] you would be equal﴾ in disbelief. His saying ﴿and [then] you would be﴾ is not meant as the response to the wish (jawab al-tamanni), because the response to a wish introduced by the fa' is in the accusative (mansub). Rather, He intended coordination (al-nasaq), meaning: they wish that you would disbelieve, and they wish that you would be equal, like His saying, ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [al-Qalam: 9], meaning: they wish you would compromise, and they wish you would compromise. ﴿So do not take from among them allies﴾ — this forbids allying with them — ﴿until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾ with you.

Ikrimah said: it is another emigration. Emigration is of three kinds: the emigration of the believers at the beginning of Islam, which is His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿for the poor emigrants﴾ [al-Hashr: 8], and His saying, ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa': 100], and similar verses. The emigration of the hypocrites is going out in the way of Allah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), patient and seeking reward [as is related here], and He forbade allying with them until they emigrate in the way of Allah. The emigration of all the believers is what the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The emigrant is one who abandons what Allah has forbidden."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away﴾ — they turn away from monotheism and emigration — ﴿then seize them﴾, that is, take them as captives, and from this it is said of a captive, akhidh. ﴿And kill them wherever you find them﴾, within the sacred area and outside it. ﴿And take not from among them a protector or a helper.﴾ Then He excepted a group of them, saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 91:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿You will find others﴾. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they were the tribes of Asad and Ghatafan, who were present in Madinah. They professed Islam out of hypocrisy (riya'), while they were not Muslims. When one of them was asked by his people, "By what have you embraced Islam?", he would say, "I believe in this monkey, this scorpion, and this beetle." And when they met the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), they would say, "We are upon your religion," wishing by that to have safety from both parties.

And ad-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas: they were the Banu 'Abd al-Dar, who had this description. ﴿They wish to be safe from you﴾, so do not confront them; ﴿and to be safe from their own people﴾, so they do not confront them; ﴿Whenever they are returned to temptation﴾, meaning, invited to polytheism, ﴿they are plunged back into it﴾, meaning they return and revert to polytheism. ﴿If they do not withdraw from you﴾, meaning, if they do not refrain from fighting you until you march to Makkah; ﴿and offer you peace﴾, meaning ransom and reconciliation; ﴿and restrain their hands﴾, and do not withhold their hands from fighting you, ﴿then seize them﴾ as captives, ﴿and kill them wherever you find them﴾, meaning wherever you come upon them. ﴿Those⁠—﴾, meaning the people of this description, ﴿We have given you clear authority over them﴾, meaning [a clear, manifest proof for killing and fighting]. [[Omitted from (A).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 92:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer﴾ up to the end of the verse. It was revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿa al-Makhzumi.
