The account is that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Makkah before the Hijrah and embraced Islam, then feared to make his Islam known to his family, so he fled to Madinah and took refuge in one of its fortresses (ʿutum). His mother grieved over this with severe grief and said to her two sons, al-Harith and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, who were her sons by the same mother: "By Allah, no roof shall shade me, and I shall not taste food or drink until you bring him back to me." So the two of them went out in search of him, and al-Harith ibn Zayd ibn Abi Unaysa went out with them, until they came to Madinah. They came to ʿAyyash while he was in the fortress, and said to him: "Come down, for your mother has not been sheltered by a roof since you left, and she has sworn that she will not eat food or drink water until you return to her. (And you have the covenant of Allah) upon us that we will not compel you to anything, nor will we come between you and your religion." When they mentioned to him his mother's distress and gave him their solemn oath by Allah, he came down to them, and they took him out of Madinah, then bound him with a leather thong, and each of them lashed him one hundred times. Then they brought him back to his mother, and when he came to her she said: "By Allah, I will not untie you from your bonds until you disbelieve in the one in whom you have believed." Then they left him bound and cast out in the sun for as long as Allah willed, until he gave them what they wanted. Then al-Harith ibn Zayd came to him and said: "O ʿAyyash, is this the religion you were upon? By Allah, if it was guidance, you have abandoned guidance, and if it was misguidance, you were upon it." ʿAyyash was angered by his words and said: "By Allah, I will never meet you alone except that I kill you." Then ʿAyyash embraced Islam after that and emigrated. Then al-Harith ibn Zayd embraced Islam after him and emigrated to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while ʿAyyash was not present that day and did not know of his Islam. Then, while ʿAyyash was traveling on the outskirts of Quba, he met al-Harith and killed him. The people said: "Woe to you! What have you done? He had embraced Islam." So ʿAyyash returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what has happened between me and al-Harith is what you know, and I did not know of his Islam until I had killed him." Then it was revealed: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake﴾ [[Al-Tabari mentions the story: 9/33-34; al-Wahidi on the authority of al-Kalbi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 162. Al-Suyuti attributes it to Ibn al-Mundhir, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/615-616. See also Ibn Kathir: 1/535.]].

This is a prohibition against killing a believer, like His saying: ﴿It is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53].

﴿Except by mistake﴾ is an exception of the disconnected type (istithna' munqati'), meaning: "but if a mistake occurs." ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾, i.e., he must free a believing slave as expiation, ﴿and a blood-money paid over to his family﴾ in full, ﴿to his family﴾, i.e., to the family of the slain person who inherit from him, ﴿unless they remit it﴾, i.e., they give it as charity, pardon it and forgo the blood-money. ﴿But if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave﴾. By this is meant that if the man was a Muslim in the land of war, alone among the disbelievers, and he was killed by someone who did not know of his Islam, then there is no blood-money for him, but expiation is due. It is also said that what is meant is: if the slain was a Muslim in the land of Islam but of the lineage of a disbelieving people, whose kin in the land of war are at war with the Muslims, then expiation is due but there is no blood-money for his family. al-Harith ibn Zayd was from a disbelieving people at war with the Muslims, so freeing a slave was obligatory for him, but there was no blood-money, because there was no covenant between his people and the Muslims.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if he was from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, then a blood-money paid to his family and the freeing of a believing slave﴾. By this is meant that if the slain was a dhimmi or a mu'ahad (one with a treaty), then blood-money and expiation are obligatory. The expiation is by freeing a believing slave, whether the slain was a Muslim or a mu'ahad, a man or a woman, free or a slave, and it is from the property of the killer. ﴿But whoever does not find [the means], then fasting two consecutive months﴾. If the killer is able to find a slave, or is capable of obtaining one by having its price in excess of his own maintenance, the maintenance of his dependents, and his needs such as housing and the like, then freeing is obligatory for him, and he may not switch to fasting. If he is unable to obtain one, then he must fast two consecutive months. If he breaks the fast by a day deliberately during the two months, or forgets the intention and intends another fast, he must begin the two months afresh.

If he breaks a day due to an excuse of illness or travel, does the consecutiveness break? The scholars differ on this. Some say it breaks and he must begin the two months afresh; this is the view of al-Nakha'i and the more apparent of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, because he broke the fast by choice. Others say it does not break and he should build upon what he has done; this is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Hasan and al-Sha'bi.

If a woman menstruates during the two months, she breaks the fast on the days of menstruation, and the consecutiveness is not broken. When she becomes pure, she builds upon what she has fasted, because it is a matter written upon women which they cannot avoid.

If he is unable to fast, is he released from it by feeding sixty of the poor? On this there are two opinions: one is that he is released, as in the expiation of zihar; the other is that he is not released, because the Law did not mention a substitute for it, and so He said: ﴿then fasting two consecutive months﴾.

﴿A repentance from Allah﴾, i.e., Allah made this a repentance for the one who kills by mistake. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of the one who killed by mistake, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has ordained for you.

As for the discussion explaining the blood-money: know that killing is of three kinds: deliberate pure killing (ʿamd mahd), quasi-deliberate killing (shibh ʿamd), and pure mistaken killing (khata' mahd).

Pure deliberate killing is: that one intends to kill a person by means that are generally intended for killing, and kills him. For this there is retaliation (qisas) when equality is present, or a heavier blood-money (diyah mughallazah) owed immediately from the killer's property.

Quasi-deliberate killing is: that one intends to strike him with something that does not usually kill someone of his kind by such a blow, such as striking him with a light stick or a small stone once or twice, and he dies. There is no retaliation for it, but a heavier blood-money is obligatory upon his ʿaqilah (paternal kinsmen), deferred over three years.

Pure mistaken killing is: that one does not intend to strike him but intends something else and hits him, and he dies from it. There is no retaliation for it, but a lighter blood-money is obligatory upon his ʿaqilah, deferred over three years.

Expiation is due from the killer's property in all these kinds. According to Abu Hanifa, may Allah be pleased with him, deliberate killing does not require expiation, because it is a major sin like the other major sins.

The blood-money for a free Muslim is one hundred camels. If camels are unavailable, its value is due in dirhams or dinars according to one opinion; according to another opinion, a fixed substitute is due from them, which is one thousand dinars, or twelve thousand dirhams, based on what is related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "He imposed the blood-money on the people of gold at one thousand dinars, and on the people of silver at twelve thousand dirhams" [[See: Sunan al-Bayhaqi: 8/76. Musannaf ʿAbd al-Razzaq: 9/296.]].

Some people held that what is obligatory as blood-money is one hundred camels, or one thousand dinars, or twelve thousand dirhams. This is the view of ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr and al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Malik said likewise.

Others held that it is one hundred camels, or one thousand dinars, or ten thousand dirhams. This is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri and the Companions of opinion (ashab al-ra'y).

The blood-money of a woman is half the blood-money of a man. The blood-money of the dhimmi and the mu'ahad is one-third of the blood-money of a Muslim if he is a People of the Book; if he is a Magian, it is one-fifth of the blood-money. It is related from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The blood-money of a Jew or a Christian is four thousand dirhams, and the blood-money of a Magian is eight hundred" [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 2/107 (Tartib al-Musnad), al-Tabari in al-Tafsir: 9/54. See also Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/205.]]. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Hasan, and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, adopted it.

Others held that the blood-money of the dhimmi and the mu'ahad is equal to the blood-money of a Muslim. This is related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is the view of Sufyan al-Thawri and the Companions of opinion.

Some said: the blood-money of the dhimmi is half the blood-money of a Muslim. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, and Malik, Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them both, said likewise.

The blood-money in pure deliberate killing and quasi-deliberate killing is heavier by age: thirty hiqqah (camels in their fourth year), thirty jadha'ah (camels in their fifth year), and forty khalifah (pregnant she-camels) with their young in their wombs. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with them both, and ʿAta' said likewise, and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, adopted it, based on what ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, that ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, that Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm informed us, that al-Rabi' informed us, that al-Shafi'i informed us, that Ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from al-Qasim ibn Rabi'a, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Verily, in deliberate killing resembling mistake, by whip or stick, there are one hundred camels, heavier, of which forty are khalifah with their young in their wombs" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Diyat, bab kam al-diyah, from Ibn ʿAmr: 6/354; al-Nasa'i in al-Qasamah, bab kam diyat shibh al-ʿamd, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: 8/40; Ibn Majah in al-Diyat, bab diyat shibh al-ʿamd mughallazah, no. (2628): 2/878; al-Daraqutni in al-Hudud: 3/105; al-Shafi'i: 2/108 (Tartib al-Musnad); Ahmad: 2/11 from Ibn ʿUmar, and in other places. It was authenticated by Ibn Hibban, and Ibn al-Qattan said: it is sahih, and the difference in its transmission does not harm it. See: Talkhis al-Habir: 4/15; Nasb al-Rayah: 4/331-333. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/186.]].

Others held that the heavier blood-money is in four categories: twenty-five bint makhad, twenty-five bint labun, twenty-five hiqqah, and twenty-five jadha'ah. This is the view of al-Zuhri and Rabi'a, and Malik, Ahmad and the Companions of opinion said likewise.

As for the blood-money of mistake, it is lighter and is in fifths by agreement, though they differed on its division. Some held that it is twenty bint makhad, twenty bint labun, twenty ibn labun, twenty hiqqah, and twenty jadha'ah. This is the view of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, Sulayman ibn Yasar, al-Zuhri and Rabi'a, and Malik and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them, said likewise. Others replaced the sons of labun with daughters of makhad; this is related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, and Ahmad and the Companions of opinion said likewise.

The blood-money for limbs follows this estimate, and the blood-money for a woman in these is half that of a man. The blood-money for killing by mistake and quasi-deliberate killing is borne by the ʿaqilah, who are the male paternal relatives (ʿasabat) of the killer, and nothing of it is obligatory on the perpetrator himself, because the Prophet ﷺ made it obligatory upon the ʿaqilah.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 93:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ [to the end of the verse]. It was revealed concerning Miqyas ibn Subabah al-Kinani. He had embraced Islam together with his brother Hisham. He found his brother Hisham slain among the Banu al-Najjar, so he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent with him a man from the Banu Fihr to the Banu al-Najjar, [saying]: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands you: if you know the killer of Hisham ibn Subabah, hand him over to Miqyas so that he may take retribution from him; and if you do not know him, hand over to him his blood-money (diyah)." The Fihri conveyed this to them, and they said: "We hear and obey Allah and His Messenger. By Allah, we do not know his killer, but we will pay his blood-money." So they gave him one hundred camels. Then the two of them set out returning toward Medina. Satan came to Miqyas and whispered to him, saying: "You will accept the blood-money of your brother, and that will be a disgrace for you? Kill the one who is with you, so that one soul will be in place of another soul, and you will have the surplus of the blood-money." So he caught the Fihri off guard, struck him with a rock and crushed him. Then he mounted a camel, drove the rest of the camels, and returned to Mecca as an unbeliever. So this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 9/61-62. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/623, and Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, pp. 163-164.]] ﴿his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾ because of his disbelief and apostasy. He is the one whom the Prophet ﷺ excepted on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, among those whom he had granted safety, when he was killed while clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah is angry with him and has cursed him﴾, i.e., He has expelled him from mercy. ﴿And has prepared for him a great punishment.﴾ The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse.

It is reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the killer of a believer intentionally has no repentance. It was said to him: "Did not Allah say in Surat al-Furqan: 'And they do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right,' up to His saying: 'And whoever does that will meet a penalty; the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation, except one who repents' (al-Furqan 67-70)?" He said: "That was in the Jahiliyyah. Some people of polytheism had killed and committed adultery, then they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'What you call to is indeed good; if only you would inform us that there is an expiation for what we have done.' So there was revealed: 'And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah' up to His saying: 'except one who repents and believes' [[Narrated by al-Bukhari: in Tafsir - chapter: (O My servants who have transgressed...) 8/549. And Muslim: in Iman - chapter: that Islam demolishes what was before it, no. (122) 1/113.]]. So that verse is for those people."

As for the verse in al-Nisa', it concerns a man who knew Islam and its laws and then killed; his recompense is Hell.

Zayd ibn Thabit said: "When the verse in al-Furqan was revealed, 'And those who do not call upon another god along with Allah,' we marveled at its leniency. We remained seven months, then the harsh [verse] was revealed after the lenient one, and it abrogated the lenient one." By the harsh [verse] he meant this verse, and by the lenient one he meant the verse of al-Furqan.

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "That is a Meccan verse, and this one is Medinan; it was revealed and nothing has abrogated it."

What the majority hold, and it is the position of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah), is that the repentance of one who intentionally kills a Muslim is accepted, based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed I am Forgiving toward one who repents, believes, and does righteousness﴾ [Ta-Ha: 82], and He said: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" [al-Nisa': 48]. What is reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, is an intensification and exaggeration in deterring from killing, just as is reported from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he said: "If he has not killed, it is said to him: 'There is no repentance for you'; and if he has killed and then comes [seeking repentance], it is said: 'For you there is repentance.'" A similar thing is also reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

There is no basis in the verse for those who hold that committing major sins necessitates eternal abiding in the Fire, because the verse was revealed concerning a killer who was an unbeliever, namely Miqyas ibn Subabah. It was also said that it is a threat for one who kills a believer while regarding it as lawful to kill him because of his faith; and whoever regards the killing of the people of faith because of their faith as lawful is an unbeliever abiding eternally in the Fire. It was said concerning His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾ that its meaning is: it is his recompense if He should recompense him; but He may, if He wills, punish him, and if He wills, forgive him by His generosity, for He has promised to forgive whom He wills.

It is related that Amr ibn Ubayd came to Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' and said to him: "Does Allah break His promise?" He said: "No." He said: "Did not Allah say: ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾?" Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' said to him: "You have come from ignorance of the language, O Abu Uthman! The Arabs do not count failing to carry out a threat as breaking one's word and a blameworthy act; they only count failing to carry out a promise as breaking one's word and a blameworthy act," and he recited:

"Indeed I, if I threaten him or promise him,
am one who breaks my threat, and fulfills my promise."

The proof that other than shirk does not necessitate eternal abiding in the Fire is what we have related, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever dies not associating anything with Allah enters Paradise" [[Narrated by Muslim in Iman, chapter: whoever dies not associating anything with Allah enters Paradise, no. (93): 1/94, from Jabir. And al-Bukhari narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Whoever dies associating something with Allah enters the Fire, and I say: whoever dies not associating anything with Allah enters Paradise." Al-Bukhari in Janaiz: 3/110, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/96.]].

Abu al-Wahid Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, [who said:] Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi told us, [who said:] Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, [who said:] Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, [who said:] Abu al-Yaman told us, [who said:] Shu'ayb told us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Idris A'idh Allah ibn Abd Allah informed me that Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may Allah be pleased with him, — and he had witnessed Badr and was one of the Nuqaba' (chiefs) on the night of al-Aqabah — said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said while around him was a group of his Companions: "Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill your children, will not bring a slander that you invent between your hands and your feet, and will not disobey in what is right. Whoever of you fulfils [the pledge], his reward is with Allah; and whoever commits any of that and is punished in this world, that is an expiation for it; and whoever commits any of that and Allah conceals it, it is up to Allah: if He wills He pardons him, and if He wills He punishes him." So we pledged allegiance to him on that [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Iman, chapter: the sign of faith is love of the Ansar: 1/64, and in other places. Muslim in Hudud, chapter: the prescribed punishments are an expiation for their people, no. (1709): 3/1333. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/60-61.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 94:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully﴾ [to the end of the verse]. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Banu Murrah ibn Awf called Mirdas ibn Nahik, who was from the people of Fadak. He was a Muslim, and no one else from his people had embraced Islam. They heard of a military expedition (sariyyah) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ coming against them. The commander of the expedition was a man called Ghalib ibn Fudalah al-Laythi. So they fled, but the man remained, because he was upon the religion of the Muslims. When he saw the horses, he feared that they might be from outside the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, so he drove his sheep to the top of a mountain ridge (a'qul) and climbed the mountain himself. When the horsemen caught up, he heard them glorifying God (takbir), and when he heard the takbir he knew that they were from the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. So he too said the takbir, came down, and was saying: "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon you." Usamah ibn Zayd overtook him, killed him, and seized his sheep. Then they returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was greatly grieved by that, and the news had reached him before them. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You killed him in order to take what he had?" Then he recited this verse to Usamah ibn Zayd. Usamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me." He said: "And what will you do with 'There is no god but Allah'?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said it three times. Usamah said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept repeating it until I wished that I had not embraced Islam until that day. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked forgiveness for me after three times, and said: 'Free a slave.'" [Ibn Hajar attributed it to al-Tha'labi from the narration of al-Kalbi from Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi p. (48). It was also narrated by al-Tabari from the narration of Asbat from al-Suddi with slight variation: Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/78-79. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/632-633, Fath al-Bari 8/258.]

Abu Dhabyan related from Usamah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only said it out of fear of the weapon." He said: "Why did you not split open his heart, so that you would know whether he said it out of fear or not?" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Diyat, chapter "And whoever gives life to it": 12/191, and in other places; and Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the prohibition of killing the disbeliever after he has said: There is no god but Allah, no. (96) 1/96. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/241-242.]

And Ikrimah related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: A man from the Banu Sulaym passed by a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, and with him was his flock of sheep. He greeted them with salam. They said: "He only greeted you with salam so that he might seek refuge from you." So they rose, killed him, and took his sheep, and brought them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾ [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir of Surah al-Nisa: 8/286, and he said: this is a hasan hadith. Abu Dawud in al-Huruf: 6/4; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak authenticated it: 2/235, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir: 9/76; Ibn Abi Asim in al-Diyat p. (36); and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/229. See also al-Bukhari with al-Fath 8/258, and Ibn Kathir: 1/539.] . .

﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of Allah﴾ means: when you travel in the cause of Allah, that is, for jihad.

﴿Investigate carefully﴾ (fa-tabayyanu). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited it here in both places, and in Surah al-Hujurat, with the taa' and the thaa' from tathbit (establishing), meaning: stop until you recognise the believer from the disbeliever. The others recited it with the yaa' and the nun from tabayyun (clarification). It is said: "I clarified the matter" (tabayyantu al-amr) when I considered it carefully.

﴿And do not say to one who offers you peace (al-salam)﴾ This is the reading of the people of Madinah, Ibn Amir and Hamzah, that is, al-maqadah (submission, surrender), which is the statement "There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." The others recited al-salam, which is the greeting (salam) that is the salutation of the Muslims, because he had greeted them with it. It is also said that al-salam and al-salam are one and the same, meaning: do not say to one who greets you with salam, "You are not a believer."

﴿Seeking the transitory goods of worldly life﴾ means: you seek the spoils and the booty. "The transitory goods of worldly life" (ʿaraḍ al-ḥayat al-dunya) means its benefits and its possessions.

﴿With Allah are abundant spoils﴾ means: booty (ghana'im) in abundance. It is also said: abundant reward for one who guards against killing a believer.

﴿Thus you were before﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Thus you used to conceal your faith from the polytheists. ﴿Then Allah bestowed favour upon you﴾ by making Islam manifest. Qatadah said: You were misguided before, then Allah bestowed favour upon you with Islam and guidance.

It is also said that its meaning is: thus you were before, when you were safe among your people by saying "There is no god but Allah" before the Hijrah, so do not frighten one who says it. Then Allah bestowed favour upon you with the Hijrah. ﴿So investigate carefully﴾ lest you kill a believer.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾

I say: When the warriors see in a land or a village the symbols of Islam, they must refrain from them, for the Prophet ﷺ, when he fought a people, if he heard the adhan he withheld from them, and if he did not hear it he attacked them.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan informed us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Nawfal ibn Musahiq, from Ibn Isam, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ, whenever he sent out a military expedition (sariyyah), would say: "If you see a mosque or hear a muezzin, do not kill anyone." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on calling the polytheists (to Islam): 3/432, and al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i; al-Tirmidhi in al-Siyar, chapter "Narrated to us Muhammad ibn Yahya": 5/155, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith; al-Shafi'i: 2/116 (in the arrangement of al-Musnad); al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir at length... See: al-Isabah of Ibn Hajar: 4/500-501; Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan: 2/149-150; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/60.]

**Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on Surah 4, verse 95:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] and are not disabled, and those who strive in the way of God﴾ and so on. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Abd Allah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd al-Zuhri narrated to us: Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "I saw Marwan ibn al-Hakam sitting in the mosque, so I came and sat down beside him. He informed us that Zayd ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, had told him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dictated to him: ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home], other than those with a disability, and those who strive in the way of Allah﴾." He said: "Ibn Umm Maktum came while he was dictating it to me and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if I were able to fight, I would have fought.' He was a blind man. So Allah revealed to him while his thigh was upon my thigh, and it became so heavy on me that I feared it would crush my thigh. Then the state passed from him, and Allah revealed: ﴿other than those with a disability﴾."

[Related by al-Bukhari in *Tafsir*, Surah al-Nisa', chapter "Not equal are those believers who sit [at home] and the strivers in the way of Allah," 8/259, and by Muslim in *Imara*, chapter on the removal of the obligation of jihad from those excused, no. (1898), 3/158.]

This verse concerns jihad and exhorts to it. So He said: ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]﴾ from jihad ﴿other than those with a disability﴾. The people of Medina, Ibn Amir and al-Kisa'i read *ghayra* with a *nasb* (accusative) on the *ra'*, meaning "except those with a disability" (*illa*). The others read it with a *raf'* (nominative) on the *ra'*, as an adjective (*na't*) of "those who sit," meaning: "Not equal are those who sit who are other than those with a disability," that is, other than those with chronic affliction (*zamana*), weakness of body, or blindness. ﴿And those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives﴾ are not equal to the sitters other than those with a disability, for they are equal to the strivers, since the excuse has kept them back.

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib informed us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from the expedition (*ghazwa*) to Tabuk and drew near to Medina, he said: "Indeed, in Medina there are people who, whenever you traversed a journey or crossed a valley, were with you in it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, while they are in Medina?" He said: "Yes, while they are in Medina; the excuse has held them back."

[Related by al-Bukhari in *Jihad*, chapter "Whoever is held back by an excuse from the expedition," 6/47, and in *Maghazi*, 8/126; by Muslim in *Imara*, chapter on the reward of one held back from the expedition by illness or another excuse, no. (1911), 3/1518; and by the author in *Sharh al-Sunna*, 10/376.]

Al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit [at home]﴾ refers to [those who stayed back from] Badr, and ﴿those who go out to Badr﴾ refers to those who went out to Badr.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah has preferred the strivers with their wealth and their lives over the sitters by a degree﴾, that is, by a merit. It has been said: by "the sitters" here He means those with a disability; Allah preferred the strivers over them by a degree, because the striver engaged in jihad with intention, while those with a disability had intention but did not engage in it, so they were lower by a degree. ﴿And to each﴾, meaning the striver and the sitter, ﴿Allah has promised the best reward﴾, meaning Paradise, because of their faith. Muqatil said: it means the striver and the sitter who has an excuse. ﴿And Allah has preferred the strivers over the sitters with a great reward﴾, meaning over the sitters who have no excuse. (94a)

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 96:

﴿Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. Ibn Muhayriz said concerning this verse: "It is seventy degrees, between each two degrees is the running of a swift, well-trained horse for seventy autumns."

It is also said: "The degrees are Islam, jihad, hijrah and martyrdom; the mujahidun alone attain them." Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni informed us: Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Shurayk al-Shafi'i informed us: Abdullah ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jurbadhi informed us: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Abu Hani' al-Khawlani narrated to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Jabali, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Abu Sa'id, whoever is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Prophet, Paradise becomes obligatory for him." He said: Abu Sa'id was amazed by it and said: "Repeat it to me, O Messenger of Allah." So he did. He said: "And another thing, by which Allah raises the servant a hundred degrees in Paradise, between each two degrees is as the distance between heaven and earth." He said: "And what is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Jihad in the way of Allah, jihad in the way of Allah." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter "The best of people is a believer who strives (mujahid)": 6/6; Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter "Explanation of what Allah has prepared for the mujahidun in Paradise of degrees," no. (1884): 3/1501; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/347.]]

Al-Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu al-Qasim Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Shah informed us: my father informed us: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Mutarriz informed us: Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us: Shurayh ibn al-Nu'man informed us: Fulayh informed us, from Hilal ibn Ali, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever believes in Allah and His Messenger, establishes the prayer, and fasts Ramadan, it is a right upon Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to admit him into Paradise, whether he struggles in the way of Allah or sits in the land where he was born." They said: "Shall we not inform the people of this?" He said: "Indeed, in Paradise there are one hundred degrees which Allah has prepared for those who strive in His way; between each two degrees is as the distance between heaven and earth. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle and highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter "The degrees of those who strive in the way of Allah": 6/11, and in al-Tawhid; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/346.]]

Know that jihad in general is obligatory, but it is divided into fard al-ayn (individual obligation) and fard al-kifayah (collective obligation).

Fard al-ayn: when the disbelievers enter the abode of a people among the believers, it becomes obligatory upon every legally responsible man among the people of that town who has no excuse to go out against their enemy, whether free or slave, wealthy or poor, to repel them from themselves and from their neighbours.

For those Muslims who are far away from them, it is fard al-kifayah. If the sufficiency is not achieved by those who have been attacked, then it becomes obligatory upon those Muslims who are far away to assist them. If the sufficiency is achieved by those who are present, then there is no obligation upon the distant ones, except by way of voluntary choice. Slaves and the poor are not included in this category. Of this type is the case where the disbelievers remain in their own lands: the imam must not let a year pass without a campaign (ghazwah) that he undertakes himself or sends through his expeditionary units (sarayahu), so that jihad does not become neglected. Choosing (to go) for one who is able to fight, when sufficiency is achieved by others, is that he should not sit back from jihad, but it is not made obligatory, because Allah Most High promised the one who fights and the one who sits back the reward in this verse, saying: ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best﴾. Had it been an obligation upon all, the one who sits back would deserve punishment, not reward.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ – [the verse continues]. It was revealed concerning some people of Makkah who professed Islam but did not emigrate (hijrah). Among them were Qays ibn al-Fakih ibn al-Mughirah, Qays ibn al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and others like them. When the polytheists marched out to Badr, they went out with them and were killed alongside the disbelievers. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death﴾; by this He meant the Angel of Death and his assistants, or He meant the Angel of Death alone, as He said: ﴿Say, "The Angel of Death who has been entrusted with you will take you"﴾ [al-Sajdah: 11]. The Arabs sometimes address a single person using the plural form. ﴿Wronging themselves﴾ means by associating partners with Allah. It is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal), meaning "in the state of their wronging." It was said: that is, by remaining in the land of polytheism, because Allah the Exalted did not accept Islam after the Prophet's ﷺ migration except with migration. Then this ruling was abrogated (naskh) after the conquest of Makkah, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no hijrah after the conquest." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on the obligation of going forth (nafir): 6/37, and in al-Hajj; Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the pledge after the conquest of Makkah, no. (1353): 3/1487, and in al-Hajj; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/370, from Ibn Abbas.] These people were killed on the day of Badr, and the angels struck their faces and their backs, and said to them: "What were you in?" This is the meaning of His words: ﴿They will say, "In what were you?"﴾ – that is, "In what state were you?" Or, "In which of the two groups were you? Were you among the Muslims or among the polytheists?" It is a rebuke and reproach. They excused themselves by weakness in resisting the people of polytheism. ﴿They said, "We were oppressed (mustad'afin) in the land"﴾ – meaning weak and unable. ﴿In the land﴾ means the land of Makkah. ﴿They [the angels] said: "Was not the earth of Allah spacious, so that you could have emigrated therein?"﴾ – meaning, to Madinah, and leaving Makkah from among the people of polytheism? Allah the Exalted then refuted them and informed us of their lie, and said: ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and evil is the destination﴾ – that is, "Their abode is Hell, and wretched is the final destination to Hell."

Then He excepted from among them those with an excuse, saying: ﴿Except the oppressed among men, women and children, who are unable to devise any plan and do not find a way﴾. They are unable to devise a plan, nor have the means or the strength to leave it. ﴿And they do not find a way﴾, that is, they do not know a path to leave. Mujahid said: they do not know the way to Madinah.

﴿For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them﴾, that is, He will overlook them. "Perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is binding, because it is used to give hope, and when Allah gives a servant hope, He fulfils it. ﴿And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: My mother and I were among those whom Allah excused, meaning the oppressed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate for these oppressed ones in the prayer.

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muʿadh ibn Fudala informed us, Hisham informed us, from Yahya, who is Ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say, when he said, 'Allah hears those who praise Him, our Lord, to You belongs all praise,' in the last rak'ah of the Isha prayer, he would perform qunut: 'O Allah, deliver ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿa. O Allah, deliver al-Walid. O Allah, deliver Salama ibn Hisham. O Allah, deliver the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar. O Allah, make it years like the years of Yusuf.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surah Al ʿImran, chapter "You have no say in the matter": 8/226, and Muslim in Masajid and places of prayer, chapter on the recommendation of qunut in all prayers when a calamity befalls the Muslims, no. (675): 1/446-467. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 3/121 with the wording: "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he wished to invoke curse upon someone or supplicate for someone would perform qunut after bowing, and sometimes he said: when Allah hears those who praise Him..."]].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on the earth many a refuge and abundance﴾. ʿAli ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): ﴿murāghaman﴾ means a place of relocation to which one moves. Mujahid said: a place of withdrawing from what is disliked. Abu ʿUbayda said: al-muragham: one says "raghamtu qawmi wa hajartuhum" (I opposed my people and emigrated from them), and it means the place of movement and the way out.

It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, a man from the Banu Layth, an elderly sick old man called Jundaʿ ibn Damra, heard it and said: "By Allah, I will not spend tonight in Makkah. Take me out." They took him out carrying him on a litter until they brought him to al-Tanim, where death overtook him. He struck his right hand upon his left and said: "O Allah, this is for You and this is for Your Messenger; I pledge allegiance to You upon what Your Messenger pledged to You." Then he died. News of him reached the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "Had he reached Madinah, he would have had a more complete reward." The polytheists laughed and said: "This man did not attain what he sought." So Allah revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him﴾ [[Al-Haythami said: Abu Ya'la narrated it and its narrators are trustworthy, Majma' al-Zawa'id 7/10; al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 208; both from Ibn ʿAbbas. See al-Durr al-Manthur 2/651; al-Tabari 9/114 onward; Usd al-Ghaba of Ibn al-Athir 1/359-360.]], that is, before he reaches the place he emigrated to, ﴿then his reward has become due﴾, that is, it is obligatory, ﴿upon Allah﴾, by His making it binding upon Himself out of bounty, ﴿and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Then He excepted from among them those with an excuse, saying: ﴿Except the oppressed among men, women and children, who are unable to devise any plan and do not find a way﴾. They are unable to devise a plan, nor have the means or the strength to leave it. ﴿And they do not find a way﴾, that is, they do not know a path to leave. Mujahid said: they do not know the way to Madinah.

﴿For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them﴾, that is, He will overlook them. "Perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is binding, because it is used to give hope, and when Allah gives a servant hope, He fulfils it. ﴿And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: My mother and I were among those whom Allah excused, meaning the oppressed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate for these oppressed ones in the prayer.

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muʿadh ibn Fudala informed us, Hisham informed us, from Yahya, who is Ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say, when he said, 'Allah hears those who praise Him, our Lord, to You belongs all praise,' in the last rak'ah of the Isha prayer, he would perform qunut: 'O Allah, deliver ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿa. O Allah, deliver al-Walid. O Allah, deliver Salama ibn Hisham. O Allah, deliver the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar. O Allah, make it years like the years of Yusuf.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surah Al ʿImran, chapter "You have no say in the matter": 8/226, and Muslim in Masajid and places of prayer, chapter on the recommendation of qunut in all prayers when a calamity befalls the Muslims, no. (675): 1/446-467. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 3/121 with the wording: "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he wished to invoke curse upon someone or supplicate for someone would perform qunut after bowing, and sometimes he said: when Allah hears those who praise Him..."]].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on the earth many a refuge and abundance﴾. ʿAli ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): ﴿murāghaman﴾ means a place of relocation to which one moves. Mujahid said: a place of withdrawing from what is disliked. Abu ʿUbayda said: al-muragham: one says "raghamtu qawmi wa hajartuhum" (I opposed my people and emigrated from them), and it means the place of movement and the way out.

It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, a man from the Banu Layth, an elderly sick old man called Jundaʿ ibn Damra, heard it and said: "By Allah, I will not spend tonight in Makkah. Take me out." They took him out carrying him on a litter until they brought him to al-Tanim, where death overtook him. He struck his right hand upon his left and said: "O Allah, this is for You and this is for Your Messenger; I pledge allegiance to You upon what Your Messenger pledged to You." Then he died. News of him reached the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "Had he reached Madinah, he would have had a more complete reward." The polytheists laughed and said: "This man did not attain what he sought." So Allah revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him﴾ [[Al-Haythami said: Abu Ya'la narrated it and its narrators are trustworthy, Majma' al-Zawa'id 7/10; al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 208; both from Ibn ʿAbbas. See al-Durr al-Manthur 2/651; al-Tabari 9/114 onward; Usd al-Ghaba of Ibn al-Athir 1/359-360.]], that is, before he reaches the place he emigrated to, ﴿then his reward has become due﴾, that is, it is obligatory, ﴿upon Allah﴾, by His making it binding upon Himself out of bounty, ﴿and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Then He excepted from among them those with an excuse, saying: ﴿Except the oppressed among men, women and children, who are unable to devise any plan and do not find a way﴾. They are unable to devise a plan, nor have the means or the strength to leave it. ﴿And they do not find a way﴾, that is, they do not know a path to leave. Mujahid said: they do not know the way to Madinah.

﴿For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them﴾, that is, He will overlook them. "Perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is binding, because it is used to give hope, and when Allah gives a servant hope, He fulfils it. ﴿And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: My mother and I were among those whom Allah excused, meaning the oppressed. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate for these oppressed ones in the prayer.

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muʿadh ibn Fudala informed us, Hisham informed us, from Yahya, who is Ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) that "the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say, when he said, 'Allah hears those who praise Him, our Lord, to You belongs all praise,' in the last rak'ah of the Isha prayer, he would perform qunut: 'O Allah, deliver ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿa. O Allah, deliver al-Walid. O Allah, deliver Salama ibn Hisham. O Allah, deliver the oppressed among the believers. O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar. O Allah, make it years like the years of Yusuf.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surah Al ʿImran, chapter "You have no say in the matter": 8/226, and Muslim in Masajid and places of prayer, chapter on the recommendation of qunut in all prayers when a calamity befalls the Muslims, no. (675): 1/446-467. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 3/121 with the wording: "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he wished to invoke curse upon someone or supplicate for someone would perform qunut after bowing, and sometimes he said: when Allah hears those who praise Him..."]].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on the earth many a refuge and abundance﴾. ʿAli ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): ﴿murāghaman﴾ means a place of relocation to which one moves. Mujahid said: a place of withdrawing from what is disliked. Abu ʿUbayda said: al-muragham: one says "raghamtu qawmi wa hajartuhum" (I opposed my people and emigrated from them), and it means the place of movement and the way out.

It is narrated that when this verse was revealed, a man from the Banu Layth, an elderly sick old man called Jundaʿ ibn Damra, heard it and said: "By Allah, I will not spend tonight in Makkah. Take me out." They took him out carrying him on a litter until they brought him to al-Tanim, where death overtook him. He struck his right hand upon his left and said: "O Allah, this is for You and this is for Your Messenger; I pledge allegiance to You upon what Your Messenger pledged to You." Then he died. News of him reached the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: "Had he reached Madinah, he would have had a more complete reward." The polytheists laughed and said: "This man did not attain what he sought." So Allah revealed: ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him﴾ [[Al-Haythami said: Abu Ya'la narrated it and its narrators are trustworthy, Majma' al-Zawa'id 7/10; al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 208; both from Ibn ʿAbbas. See al-Durr al-Manthur 2/651; al-Tabari 9/114 onward; Usd al-Ghaba of Ibn al-Athir 1/359-360.]], that is, before he reaches the place he emigrated to, ﴿then his reward has become due﴾, that is, it is obligatory, ﴿upon Allah﴾, by His making it binding upon Himself out of bounty, ﴿and Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

The words of the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿And when you travel in the land﴾, that is, when you journey, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, that is, no sin or wrongdoing, ﴿if you shorten the prayer﴾, meaning from four rak'ahs to two, and this is for the Noon (Zuhr), Afternoon ('Asr), and Night ('Isha') prayers, ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, that is, will ambush you and kill you, ﴿during the prayer﴾. Its parallel is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿upon [the fear] from Pharaoh and their chiefs, that he would persecute them﴾ [Yunus: 83], meaning, that he would kill them.

﴿Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy﴾, that is, of manifest enmity.

Know that shortening the prayer while traveling is permissible by the consensus of the Muslim community (ijma', the scholarly consensus). They differed regarding the permissibility of completing the prayer in full. Most of them held that shortening is obligatory (wajib). This was the view of 'Umar, 'Ali, Ibn 'Umar, Jabir, and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them. It was also said by al-Hasan, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, and Qatadah, and it is the view of Malik and the people of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y), based on what has been related from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "The prayer was first prescribed as two rak'ahs, then the travel prayer was confirmed as it was, and the prayer of residence was made complete." [Related by al-Bukhari in Shortening (al-Taqsir), chapter "One shortens when he leaves his place": 2/569; and Muslim in the Travelers, chapter "The prayer of travelers and its shortening", no. (685): 1/478.]

Another group held that completing the prayer is permissible. This is related from 'Uthman and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with them, and al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: if he wishes he may complete it, and if he wishes he may shorten it, and shortening is more excellent.

[Imam 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, from Talhah ibn 'Amr, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did all of that: he shortened the prayer and he completed it." [Related by al-Shafi'i: 1/182 (Tartib al-Musnad), and al-Daraqutni: 2/189, by way of Talhah, and he said: "Talhah is weak." He also related it by another route and said: "This is a sound chain." The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/166.]

The apparent meaning of the Qur'an supports this view, because He said: ﴿there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾, and the wording "there is no blame" is used only for concessions (rukhas), not for what is mandatory. So the apparent meaning of the verse [requires that shortening] [[Omitted from (A).]] is not permissible except in fear, and the matter is not so. The verse was revealed concerning the majority of the Prophet's ﷺ journeys, and most of them were not free from fear of the enemy.

Shortening during travel in a state of safety is permissible according to the majority of scholars. The evidence for this is what 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Muslim ibn Khalid and 'Abd al-Majid ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Rawwad informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Ammar informed me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Babah, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who said: I said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "Allah the Exalted only said ﴿that you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, and the people are now secure." 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I wondered at what you wondered at, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'It is a charity (sadaqah) which Allah has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity.'" [Related by Muslim in the Prayer of Travelers, chapter "The prayer of travelers", no. (686): 1/478, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/168.]

'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: 'Abd al-Wahhab informed us, from Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ traveled between Makkah and Madinah, secure, fearing none but Allah, and he prayed two rak'ahs." [Related by al-Tirmidhi in Prayer, chapter "What has come concerning shortening in travel": 3/109, and he said: "This is a sound hadith (hadith sahih)"; and al-Nasa'i in Shortening the Prayer in Travel: 3/117; al-Shafi'i: 1/180; Ahmad: 1/215; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/170. Ibn Hajar said: al-Nasa'i declared it sound.]

Another group held that the two rak'ahs of the traveler are not shortening; rather, shortening is that one prays a single rak'ah in fear. This is related from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is the view of 'Ata', Tawus, al-Hasan, and Mujahid. They took the condition of fear mentioned in the verse as still applying. But most scholars held that limiting oneself to a single rak'ah is not permissible, whether one is in fear or in safety.

The scholars differed regarding the distance that permits shortening. One group said: shortening is permitted in both long and short journeys. This is related from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him. 'Amr ibn Dinar said: Jabir ibn Zayd said to me: "Shorten the prayer at 'Arafah." But the majority of jurists do not permit shortening in a short journey.

They also differed regarding the limit at which shortening becomes permissible. Al-Awza'i said: a day's march. Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, used to shorten and break their fast over four barids, which is sixteen farsakh. This is the view of Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq. The view of al-Hasan and al-Zuhri is close to this; they said: a two days' march. This is also the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: two nights' journey at a moderate pace, and he said in another place: forty-six miles by the Hashimi mile. Sufyan al-Thawri and the people of opinion said: a three days' march.

It was also said: the words ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾ are connected to what follows concerning the prayer of fear, and separate from what precedes it. This is related from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: The words ﴿there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer﴾ were revealed only to this extent. Then, after a year, they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the prayer of fear, and there was revealed: ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you; indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy﴾, ﴿and when you are among them﴾ [[Related by al-Tabari: 9/126. Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir, after attributing it to al-Tabari: "This context is very strange, but part of it has a witness in the narration of Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi, whose name is Zayd ibn al-Samit." Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/549.]] the verse. A similar construction in the Qur'an is common, in which one report is given in full and then another report is joined to it. Outwardly it appears connected to it, though it is separate from it, as in the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Now the truth has become evident. It was I who sought to seduce him, and indeed he is of the truthful﴾ [Yusuf: 51], which is a quotation from the wife of al-'Aziz, and His saying: ﴿That is so he may know that I did not betray him in his absence﴾ [Yusuf: 52], which is a report from Yusuf, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 102 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾. Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas [[Al-Hakim narrated it in its meaning in al-Mustadrak: 3/30, and declared it sound according to the condition of al-Bukhari. As-Suyuti attributed it in ad-Durr al-Manthur: 2/664 to al-Bazzar, and to al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 172, and to al-Tabari: 9/157. Shaykh Shakir said: In its chain is al-Nadr Abu Umar, who is Nadr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Khazzaz, and he is weak in hadith. Abu Nu'aym was asked about him and said: "He is not worth this," and he raised something from the ground. He used to come and sit with al-Hammani, and whatever he was asked about he would say: "Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas."]] and Jabir [[In this meaning, at greater length, in Muslim, Book of the Prayer of Travelers, chapter on the prayer of fear, no. (840): 1/575.]] , may Allah be pleased with them both, that when the polytheists saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions standing for the Dhuhr prayer in congregation, they regretted that they had not fallen upon them. Some of them said to others: "Leave them, for they have after it a prayer which is dearer to them than their fathers and their sons," meaning the Asr prayer. "When they stand in it, then rush upon them and kill them." Then Jibril, peace be upon him, descended and said: "O Muhammad, it is the prayer of fear, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾," so he taught him the prayer of fear.

Its summary: when the enemy is in their encampment in a direction other than the qiblah, the imam divides the people into two groups. One group stands facing the enemy to guard them, and the imam begins the prayer with the other group. When he has prayed one rak'ah with them, he stands and remains standing until they complete their prayer, and they go to face the enemy. Then the second group comes, and he prays the second rak'ah with them and remains seated until they complete the prayer for themselves, and then he gives the salam with them. This is the narration of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed in this way at Dhat al-Riqa'. Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq adopted this view.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from one who prayed with the Prophet ﷺ on the day of Dhat al-Riqa' the prayer of fear: that a group lined up with him and a group lined up facing the enemy. He prayed with those who were with him one rak'ah, then remained standing, and they completed for themselves. Then they departed and lined up facing the enemy, and the other group came, and he prayed with them the remaining rak'ah, then remained seated, and they completed for themselves, then he gave the salam with them [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Maghazi, chapter on the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa': 7/422, and Muslim in the Prayer of Travelers, chapter on the prayer of fear, no. (841): 1/575. See also Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/280.]]. Malik said: "That is the best of what I have heard concerning the prayer of fear" [[See: al-Muwatta': 1/185; Malik narrated the hadith on the prayer of fear in the Muwatta': 1/183.]].

And Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musaddad informed us: Yahya narrated to us from Shu'bah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ, with this [[The same previous hadith, and it is in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/279.]].

Some people held that when the imam rises to the second rak'ah, the first group goes in the middle of the prayer to face the enemy, and the second group comes, and he prays the second rak'ah with them and gives the salam while they do not give the salam, but go to face the enemy. The first group returns and completes its prayer, then the second group returns and completes its prayer. This is the narration of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed in this way. This is also the view of the Ashab al-Ra'y.

Abu Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib informed us: Yazid ibn Zuray' informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, that the Prophet ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear with one of the two groups one rak'ah, while the other group was facing the enemy. Then they departed and stood in the place of those, and those came and he prayed with them another rak'ah, then gave the salam with them. Then these stood and prayed their rak'ah [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Maghazi, chapter on the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa': 7/422, and Muslim in the Prayer of Travelers, chapter on the prayer of fear, no. (839): 1/574. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/276.]].

Both narrations are sound. Some held that this is among the permissible variations, while al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, adopted the hadith of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah because it is more in accordance with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, more cautious for the prayer, and more effective in guarding against the enemy. That is because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when they have prostrated, let them be behind you﴾, meaning: when they have prayed. Then He said: ﴿And let another group come who have not prayed﴾, and this indicates that the first group has prayed. He said: ﴿Then let them pray with you﴾, so its requirement is that they pray the complete prayer. Its apparent meaning indicates that each group separates from the imam after completing the prayer. Caution for the prayer lies in the fact that much action, going and coming, does not occur in it, and caution for the matter of war lies in the fact that when they are not in the prayer, it is easier for fighting and fleeing if they need it.

If the imam prays four rak'ahs, with each group two rak'ahs, it is permissible. Al-Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfara'ini informed us: Abu Awanah Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz informed us, he said: al-Dahhak informed us: Affan ibn Muslim informed us: Aban al-Attar narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until when we were at Dhat al-Riqa', and whenever we came upon a shady tree we left it for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: A man from the polytheists came while the sword of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was hanging on a tree, and he took the sword of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, drew it, and said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Do you fear me?" He said: "No." He said: "Who will protect you from me?" He said: "Allah protects me from you." He said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ threatened him. He said: So he sheathed the sword and hung it up, and then the call to prayer was made. He said: He prayed with one group two rak'ahs, then they withdrew, and he prayed with the other group two rak'ahs. He said: So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had four rak'ahs, and the people had two rak'ahs [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Maghazi, chapter on the expedition of Dhat al-Riqa': 7/426, and Muslim in the Prayer of Travelers, chapter on the prayer of fear, no. (843): 1/576. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/287-288.]].

Abd al-Wahhab ibn al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us: al-Rabi' informed us: al-Shafi'i informed me: the trustworthy Ibn Ulayyah or another, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them, that the Prophet ﷺ used to lead the people in the Dhuhr prayer during fear at Batn Nakhl. He prayed with one group two rak'ahs and then gave the salam, then another group came and he prayed with them two rak'ahs and then gave the salam [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/176-177, and al-Nasa'i in the Prayer of Fear: 3/178, and al-Daraqutni in the Prayer, chapter on the prayer of fear: 2/61, and in it is the an'anah of al-Hasan al-Basri.]].

It is also narrated from Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding the prayer of fear, that he prayed with these one rak'ah and with those one rak'ah, and they did not make up [the rest]. [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Prayer of Fear, chapter on whoever said: he prays with each group one rak'ah and they do not make up: 2/70, and al-Nasa'i at the beginning of the Book of the Prayer of Fear: 3/168, and al-Tahawi: 1/183, and Ibn Jarir no. (10331) 9/135, and al-Hakim declared it sound: 1/335 and al-Dhahabi agreed with him, and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/385, 399. As-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Hibban, see ad-Durr al-Manthur 2/661, and Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/284.]] Zayd ibn Thabit also narrated it and said: "The people had one rak'ah and the Prophet ﷺ had two rak'ahs" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Prayer of Fear, chapter on whoever said: he prays with each group one rak'ah: 2/71, and al-Nasa'i in the Prayer of Fear: 3/168. See also Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/285.]].

Some scholars interpreted it as the prayer in the state of extreme fear, and they said: the obligation in this state is one rak'ah.

Most scholars hold that fear does not reduce the number of rak'ahs, and if the enemy is in the direction of the qiblah in a level place, where if they charge at them they would see them, the imam prays with them all together, and they guard during the prostration. As al-Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Nu'aym al-Isfara'ini informed us: Abu Awanah al-Hafiz informed us: Ammar informed us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from Ata', from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear, and we lined up behind him in two rows, with the enemy between us and the qiblah. The Prophet ﷺ said takbir and we all said takbir, then he bowed and we all bowed, then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised ours. Then he descended for prostration, and the row next to him did too, while the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prostration and the row next to him stood, the rear row descended with the prostration [then they stood then] [[In A: "then he stood and completed."]] the rear row advanced and the front row withdrew. Then the Prophet ﷺ bowed and we all bowed, then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised ours, then he descended for prostration with the row next to him, which had been the rear row in the first rak'ah, while the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prostration and the row next to him, the rear row descended with the prostration and prostrated, then the Prophet ﷺ gave the salam and we all gave the salam. Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "As your guards do now with their commanders" [[Narrated by Muslim in the Prayer of Travelers, chapter on the prayer of fear, no. (840): 1/574, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/291.]].

Know that the prayer of fear is permissible after the Messenger ﷺ, according to the majority of scholars. It is related from some of them that it is not permissible, and there is no basis for this.

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Every hadith narrated in the chapters on the prayer of fear, acting upon it is permissible; six or seven modes have been narrated concerning it.

Mujahid [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Prayer of Fear 2/64, and al-Nasa'i in the Prayer of Fear: 3/177, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/290.]] said concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse, from Ibn Ayyash al-Zuraqi, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Usfan, and Khalid ibn al-Walid was in command of the polytheists. We prayed the Dhuhr, and the polytheists said: "We have caught them unawares; if we had charged upon them while they were in prayer!" So the verse was revealed between Dhuhr and Asr.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you are among them﴾, i.e., witnessing with them, ﴿and establish prayer for them﴾, ﴿then let a group of them stand with you﴾, i.e., let them stand [in position], as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when darkness falls upon them, they stand﴾ [al-Baqarah: 20], i.e., they stopped. ﴿And let them take their weapons﴾. They differed concerning those who take their weapons. Some said: it means those who stood with the imam to pray take up their weapons during the prayer. Accordingly, one takes it only if it does not distract him from the prayer and does not harm the one beside him. [If its movement distracts him and weighs him down from the prayer, like a quiver or a large shield, or if it harms the one beside him, like a spear, then he does not take it.] [[The text between the brackets is missing from (A).]]

وقيل: ﴿وَلْيَأْخُذُوا أَسْلِحَتَهُمْ﴾ أي: الباقون الذين قاموا في وجه العدو. ﴿فَإِذَا سَجَدُوا﴾ أي: صلّوا، ﴿فَلْيَكُونُوا مِنْ وَرَائِكُمْ﴾ يريد: مكان الذين هم وجاه العدو. ﴿وَلْتَأْتِ طَائِفَةٌ أُخْرَى لَمْ يُصَلُّوا﴾ وهم الذين كانوا في وجه العدو، ﴿فَلْيُصَلُّوا مَعَكَ وَلْيَأْخُذُوا حِذْرَهُمْ وَأَسْلِحَتَهُمْ﴾. قيل: هؤلاء الذين أتوا، وقيل: هم الذين صلّوا. ﴿وَدَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ يتمنى الكفار، ﴿لَوْ تَغْفُلُونَ﴾ أي: لو وجدوكم غافلين ﴿عَنْ أَسْلِحَتِكُمْ وَأَمْتِعَتِكُمْ فَيَمِيلُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ مَيْلَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ فيقصدونكم ويحملون عليكم حملةً واحدة.

﴿وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ كَانَ بِكُمْ أَذًى مِنْ مَطَرٍ أَوْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى أَنْ تَضَعُوا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ﴾ رخّص في وضع السلاح في حال المطر والمرض، لأن السلاح يثقل حمله في هاتين الحالتين. ﴿وَخُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ﴾ أي: راقبوا العدو كيلا يتغفّلوكم. والحِذر ما يُتّقى به من العدو.

وقال الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: نزلت في رسول الله ﷺ، وذلك أنه غزا محارباً وبني أنمار، فنزلوا ولا يرون من العدو أحداً، فوضع الناس أسلحتهم، وخرج رسول الله ﷺ لحاجة له قد وضع سلاحه، حتى قطع الوادي والسماء ترشّ، فحال الوادي بين رسول الله ﷺ وبين أصحابه، فجلس رسول الله ﷺ في ظل شجرة، فبصر به غورث بن الحارث المحاربي فقال: قتلني الله إن لم أقتله! ثم انحدر من الجبل ومعه السيف، فلم يشعر به رسول الله ﷺ إلا وهو قائم على رأسه ومعه السيف قد سلّه من غمده، فقال: يا محمد، من يعصمك مني الآن؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ: الله. ثم قال: اللهم اكفني غورث بن الحارث بما شئت. ثم أهوى بالسيف إلى رسول الله ﷺ ليضربه، فأكبّ لوجهه من زلخةٍ زلخها من بين كتفيه، وندر سيفه، فقام رسول الله ﷺ فأخذه ثم قال: يا غورث، من يمنعك مني الآن؟ قال: لا أحد. قال: تشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمداً عبده ورسوله وأعطيك سيفك؟ ٩٥/ب قال: لا، ولكن أشهد أن لا أقاتلك أبداً ولا أعين عليك عدواً، فأعطاه رسول الله ﷺ سيفه، فقال غورث: والله لأنت خير مني. فقال النبي ﷺ: أجل، أنا أحق بذلك منك. فرجع غورث إلى أصحابه فقالوا: ويلك ما منعك منه؟ قال: لقد أهويت إليه بالسيف لأضربه، فوالله ما أدري من زلخني بين كتفي فخررت لوجهي، وذكر حاله. قال: وسكن الوادي فقطع رسول الله ﷺ الوادي إلى أصحابه، فأخبرهم الخبر وقرأ عليهم هذه الآية: [[أخبره ابن كثير مختصراً في التفسير، وقال: أخرجه الإمام أحمد عن جابر، وقال: تفرد به من هذا الوجه: ١ / ٥٤٩ - ٥٥٠. وانظر: البداية والنهاية: ٤ / ٨٤.]] ﴿وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِنْ كَانَ بِكُمْ أَذًى مِنْ مَطَرٍ أَوْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضَى أَنْ تَضَعُوا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ وَخُذُوا حِذْرَكُمْ﴾ أي: من عدوكم.

وقال سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس في هذه الآية: كان عبد الرحمن بن عوف جريحاً.

﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَاباً مُهِيناً﴾ يُهانون فيه. والجُناح: الإثم، من جَنَحَتْ: إذا عدلتْ عن القصد.

﴿So when you have finished the prayer﴾ means the prayer of fear (*salat al-khawf*), that is, when you have completed it. ﴿Then remember Allah﴾ means pray to Allah ﴿standing﴾ when healthy, ﴿sitting﴾ when ill, ﴿and on your sides﴾ when you are in distress or afflicted with a chronic ailment. It was also said: remember Allah with glorification (*tasbih*), praise (*tahmid*), declaration of His oneness (*tahlil*), and exaltation (*tamjid*), in every state.

Amr ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Kashani informed us: al-Qasim ibn Ja'far al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud al-Sijistani informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Ala' informed us: Ibn Abi Za'ida informed us, from his father, from Khalid ibn Salama, from al-Zuhri, from Urwa, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to remember Allah in all his states." [[Related by al-Bukhari in the Book of the Call to Prayer (*Adhan*), chapter "Does the muezzin turn his face here and there?", from Aisha, as a *mu'allaq* (a narration without its full chain): 2/114. And in the Book of Menstruation, chapter "The menstruating woman performs all the rites except the circumambulation of the House": 1/407, from Ibn Abbas, with the wording "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to remember Allah in all his states." Muslim in the Book of Menstruation, chapter "Remembering Allah Most High in a state of major impurity (*janaba*) and other states," no. (373): 1/282.]]

﴿Then when you are secure﴾ means when you are settled and safe, ﴿then establish the prayer﴾ means complete it, four rak'ahs, with its pillars (*arkan*). ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at fixed times﴾. It was said: obligatory and prescribed, ordained in its measure: four rak'ahs when at home and two rak'ahs when traveling. Mujahid said: it means an obligation with a fixed time, which Allah set for them.

The explanation of the times of prayer has come in a hadith. Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Abu Bakr Abd Allah ibn Hashim informed us: Waki' narrated to us: Sufyan informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Zuraqi, from Hakim ibn Hakim, from Abbad ibn Hunayf, from Nafi' ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Gabriel led me in prayer at the House twice. He prayed Maghrib with me when the fasting person breaks his fast, and he prayed Isha with me when the twilight (*shafaq*) disappeared, and he prayed Fajr with me when eating and drinking became forbidden for the fasting person. Then on the next day he prayed Zuhr with me when the shadow of everything was equal to it, and he prayed Asr with me when the shadow of everything was twice its length, and he prayed Maghrib with me when the fasting person breaks his fast, and he prayed Isha with me at the first third of the night, and he prayed Fajr with me when it was bright. Then he turned to me and said: 'O Muhammad, this is the time of the prophets before you, and the time is what lies between these two times.'" [[Related by Abu Dawud in the Book of Prayer, chapter on the times (*mawaqit*): 1/231-232; and al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Prayer, chapter "What has come concerning the times of prayer": 1/464-467, and he said: a hasan sahih hadith. Al-Hakim authenticated it: 1/196; and Ahmad: 1/333. Al-Suyuti added its attribution to Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, and Ibn Khuzayma. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/668. The author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunna: 2/182-183.]]

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Waki' informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad informed us: Abd Allah ibn Hisham narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: Badr ibn Uthman narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from his father, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that a questioner came to him and asked him about the times of prayer. He said: "He did not answer him at all. Then he commanded Bilal, who called the adhan, then he commanded him, and he gave the iqama for the dawn prayer when the dawn broke, and he prayed. Then he commanded him and he gave the iqama for Zuhr, while the one saying (who was asking) said: 'The sun has passed its zenith' or 'it has not passed,' and he (the Prophet) knew better than them. Then he commanded him and he gave the iqama for Asr while the sun was high, white and pure. Then he commanded him and he gave the iqama for Maghrib when the sun had set. Then he commanded him and he gave the iqama for Isha when the twilight had fallen." He said: "He prayed Fajr the next day while the one saying (who was asking) said: 'The sun has risen' or 'it has not risen,' and he prayed Zuhr near the time of Asr of the previous day, and he prayed Asr while the one saying said: 'The sun has turned red,' and he prayed Maghrib before the red twilight disappeared, and he prayed Isha at the first third of the night."
