Then he said: "Where is the questioner about the time?" The man said: "I am here, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "The time is what lies between these two times." [[Related by Muslim in the Book of Mosques and Places of Prayer, chapter "The times of the five prayers," no. (614): 1/429; and al-Baghawi in Sharh al-Sunna: 2/184.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 104:

Allah's statement: ﴿And do not falter in pursuit of the enemy﴾ [to the end of the verse]. The occasion of its revelation was that when Abu Sufyan and his companions turned back on the day of Uhud, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment after them, and they complained of the pain of their wounds. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not falter﴾ [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit (tafsir) 3/342; Sirat Ibn Hisham with al-Rawd al-Unuf 2/144; and what preceded in the tafsir of Surat Al 'Imran.]] meaning: do not weaken ﴿in pursuit of the enemy﴾, that is, in seeking Abu Sufyan and his companions. ﴿If you suffer pain﴾, that is, if you feel the pain of the wounds, ﴿then they too suffer pain﴾, that is, they feel pain, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿as you suffer pain; but you hope from Allah what they do not hope﴾, that is: yet you, despite that, hope for reward and recompense in the Hereafter and victory in this world, which they do not hope for. Some exegetes said: the meaning of hope here is fear, because every one who hopes is fearful that he may not attain what he hopes for.

The meaning of the verse: "and you fear from Allah," that is, you fear from Allah, meaning you fear from the punishment of Allah what they do not fear. Al-Farra' (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Hope does not carry the meaning of fear except with negation, as in His statement: ﴿Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14], meaning: who do not fear. And He said: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect dignity from Allah?﴾ [Nuh: 13], meaning: you do not fear from Allah His greatness. It is not permissible to say "I hoped you" to mean "I feared you," nor "I did not fear you" while meaning "I did not hope for you."

﴿And Allah is ever Knowing, Wise﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 105:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ — and the rest of the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar called Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq, of the clan of Banu Zafar ibn al-Harith, who stole a coat of mail (dir') from a neighbour of his called Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man. The coat of mail was in a bag containing flour, and the flour kept scattering through a tear in the bag until it reached the house. Then he hid it with a Jewish man called Zayd ibn al-Samin. The coat of mail was sought from Tu'mah, and he swore by Allah that he had not taken it and had no knowledge of it. The owners of the coat of mail said: "We have seen the trace of the flour until it entered his house." When he swore, they left him and followed the trace of the flour to the house of the Jew, and they took it from him. The Jew said: "Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq gave it to me." Then the Banu Zafar, who were Tu'mah's people, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him to argue on behalf of their companion, saying to him: "If you do not do so, our companion will be disgraced." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then intended to punish the Jew. It is also related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, in another narration, that Tu'mah stole the coat of mail in a bag containing bran, and he tore the bag so that the bran was scattered along the way. He brought it to the house of Zayd al-Samin and left it at his door, and carried the coat of mail to his own house. When the owner of the coat of mail rose in the morning, he followed the trace of the bran to the house of Zayd al-Samin, took it, and brought it to the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet ﷺ then intended to cut off the hand of the Jew Zayd. Muqatil said: Zayd al-Samin had deposited a coat of mail with Tu'mah, and Tu'mah denied it, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse. [[See: al-Tabari: 9/183. Al-Tirmidhi related it at length in his commentary on Surah al-Nisa: 8/395-399, from the narration of Muhammad ibn Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, from his father, from his grandfather Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Gharib; we do not know it to be traced back from Ibn Ishaq except through Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani. Yunus and others related it from Ibn Ishaq, from Asim, as a mursal report." Al-Hakim also related it in al-Mustadrak: 4/385-388 and said: "This is a sahih hadith according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it." It is also attributed in Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi to Ibn al-Mundhir and Abu al-Shaykh al-Isfahani.]] He said: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾ — with the command, the prohibition, and the decisive judgment. ﴿That you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾ — by what Allah has taught you and revealed to you. ﴿And do not be a advocate for the treacherous﴾ — [Tu'mah] [[Omitted in (A).]] ﴿khasiman﴾ — a helper, one who argues in defence of him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 106–108:

﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ for having intended to punish the Jew. Muqatil said: "And seek forgiveness of Allah" for your disputing on behalf of Tu'mah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And do not dispute﴾ — do not argue — ﴿on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, meaning: those who wrong themselves through betrayal and theft. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual betrayer and sinner.﴾ He means: a habitual betrayer regarding the coat of mail, and a sinner in his accusing of the Jew. It was said: this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant is someone other than him, like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾. Seeking forgiveness on behalf of the prophets after prophethood is according to one of three views: either for a sin that preceded prophethood, or for the sins of his community and relatives, or for something permissible which the Law has come to prohibit [in B (to forbid)], so he abandons it by seeking forgiveness. Thus, seeking forgiveness here means: hearing and obeying the ruling of the Law.

﴿They hide from the people﴾, meaning: they conceal themselves and feel shame before the people, meaning the Banu Zafr ibn al-Harith. ﴿But they do not hide from Allah﴾, meaning: they do not conceal themselves and do not feel shame before Allah. ﴿While He is with them when they plot﴾ — they say and devise — and tabyit means planning an action at night. ﴿That which He does not approve of in speech.﴾ This is because the people of Tu'mah said among themselves: "We will refer the matter to the Prophet ﷺ, for he will hear his statement and his oath, since he is a Muslim, and will not hear from the Jew, since he is a disbeliever." So Allah did not approve of that from them. ﴿And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do.﴾ Then He says to the people of Tu'mah:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 109–114:

﴿Here you are, you who⁠ ﴾ meaning: O you (people), ﴿argued﴾ meaning: disputed, ﴿on their behalf﴾ meaning: on behalf of Ṭu'ma; in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is "on his behalf," ﴿in the life of this world﴾. Al-jidal (argumentation) is the intensity of contention, from al-jadl (twisting), which is the intense twisting; so the one arguing wants to twist the opponent away from his position by way of proof. It is also said: al-jidal derives from al-jadalah, which is the ground, as if each of the two disputants seeks to overpower his companion and throw him down onto the ground. ﴿So who will argue with God on their behalf﴾ meaning: on behalf of Ṭu'ma, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, when God seizes him with His punishment, ﴿or who will be a guardian (wakīl) over them﴾, a surety (kafīl), meaning: who is it that will defend them and take charge of their affair on the Day of Resurrection? Then he resumed and said:

﴿And whoever does evil﴾ meaning: theft, ﴿or wrongs himself﴾ by casting blame on the innocent. It is also said: "whoever does evil" means shirk, "or wrongs himself" means sin other than shirk. ﴿Then seeks forgiveness from God﴾ meaning: repents to Him and asks Him for forgiveness, ﴿he will find God Forgiving, Merciful﴾. In this verse He presents repentance to Ṭu'ma.

﴿And whoever earns a sin﴾ meaning: Ṭu'ma's false oath, that is, "I did not steal it; the Jew stole it." ﴿Then he casts it upon himself﴾, meaning: he harms himself thereby, ﴿and God is ever Knowing﴾ of the thief of the coat of mail, ﴿Wise﴾, who ruled for the amputation (of the hand) of the thief.

﴿And whoever earns a fault﴾ meaning: the theft of the coat of mail, ﴿or a sin﴾, his false oath, ﴿then casts it upon one innocent﴾ of it, which is attributing the theft to the Jew, ﴿has certainly borne a slander (buhtān) and a manifest sin﴾. His saying ﴿then casts it﴾, and not "casts them" after mentioning the fault and the sin, either returns the pronoun to the sin, or treats the fault and the sin as one thing.

It is also said that al-najwā here means the men who confer in secret, as God Most High says: ﴿when they are in secret conference﴾ [al-Isra': 47].

﴿Except one who enjoins charity﴾, meaning: urges it, ﴿or what is right﴾, meaning: obedience to God and what the Sharia recognizes; all acts of righteousness are "what is right," because the intellects recognize them. ﴿Or reconciliation between people.﴾ Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Ṣāliḥī informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Ḥīrī told us; Ḥājib ibn Aḥmad al-Ṭūsī told us; Muḥammad ibn Ḥammād told us; Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Salim, who is Ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Umm al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with her, from Abu al-Darda' who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of something better than the rank of fasting, charity and prayer?" He said: We said, "Yes." He said: "Reconciling between people. Corruption between people is the shaver (that destroys religion)." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad p. (118), Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter on reconciling between people: 7/25, al-Tirmidhi in Sifat al-Qiyamah, chapter on the evil of discord: 7/212, who said: this is a sound hadith; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/444, 445; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/116.]]

Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Ṣāliḥī informed us: Abu al-Husayn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bishran told us; Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Saffar told us; Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi told us; Abd al-Razzaq told us; Ma'mar told us, from al-Zuhri, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his mother Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah, who was among the first women emigrants, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "He is not a liar who reconciles between people, saying good or conveying good." God Most High says: ﴿And whoever does that, seeking the pleasure of God﴾, meaning: those things he mentioned, seeking His good pleasure, ﴿We will give him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿a great reward.﴾ Abu Amr and Hamzah read ﴿We will give him﴾ with the ya', meaning: God will give him; the others read it with the nun.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 109–114:

﴿Here you are, you who⁠ ﴾ meaning: O you (people), ﴿argued﴾ meaning: disputed, ﴿on their behalf﴾ meaning: on behalf of Ṭu'ma; in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is "on his behalf," ﴿in the life of this world﴾. Al-jidal (argumentation) is the intensity of contention, from al-jadl (twisting), which is the intense twisting; so the one arguing wants to twist the opponent away from his position by way of proof. It is also said: al-jidal derives from al-jadalah, which is the ground, as if each of the two disputants seeks to overpower his companion and throw him down onto the ground. ﴿So who will argue with God on their behalf﴾ meaning: on behalf of Ṭu'ma, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, when God seizes him with His punishment, ﴿or who will be a guardian (wakīl) over them﴾, a surety (kafīl), meaning: who is it that will defend them and take charge of their affair on the Day of Resurrection? Then he resumed and said:

﴿And whoever does evil﴾ meaning: theft, ﴿or wrongs himself﴾ by casting blame on the innocent. It is also said: "whoever does evil" means shirk, "or wrongs himself" means sin other than shirk. ﴿Then seeks forgiveness from God﴾ meaning: repents to Him and asks Him for forgiveness, ﴿he will find God Forgiving, Merciful﴾. In this verse He presents repentance to Ṭu'ma.

﴿And whoever earns a sin﴾ meaning: Ṭu'ma's false oath, that is, "I did not steal it; the Jew stole it." ﴿Then he casts it upon himself﴾, meaning: he harms himself thereby, ﴿and God is ever Knowing﴾ of the thief of the coat of mail, ﴿Wise﴾, who ruled for the amputation (of the hand) of the thief.

﴿And whoever earns a fault﴾ meaning: the theft of the coat of mail, ﴿or a sin﴾, his false oath, ﴿then casts it upon one innocent﴾ of it, which is attributing the theft to the Jew, ﴿has certainly borne a slander (buhtān) and a manifest sin﴾. Buhtān is bahta, which is a lie so great that one is bewildered by its enormity; ﴿and a manifest sin﴾, meaning: a clear offence. His saying ﴿then casts it﴾, and not "casts them" after mentioning the fault and the sin, either returns the pronoun to the sin, or treats the fault and the sin as one thing.

God Most High says: ﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy﴾ — He says to the Prophet ﷺ: ﴿a faction among them had certainly intended﴾, meaning: had resolved within themselves, ﴿to mislead you﴾, meaning: to make you err in judgment and confuse the matter for you so that you would defend Ṭu'ma, ﴿but they do not mislead except themselves﴾, meaning: its harm returns upon them, ﴿and they cannot harm you at all﴾, meaning: its harm returns to them. ﴿And God has sent down to you the Book﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿and wisdom﴾, meaning: judgment by revelation, ﴿and taught you what you did not know﴾ of the rulings; it is also said: of the knowledge of the unseen. ﴿And the grace of God upon you has been ever great.﴾

God Most High says: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk﴾, meaning: the people of Ṭu'ma. Mujahid said: the verse is general concerning all people. Al-najwā is secret consultation regarding a plan. It is also said: al-najwā is what a group privately plans, whether in secret or openly. The meaning of the verse is: there is no good in much of what they plot among themselves. ﴿Except one who enjoins charity﴾, meaning: except in the secret talk of one who enjoins charity. So al-najwā may be an action. It is also said: this is a disconnected exception, meaning: but (the exception is) one who enjoins charity. God Most High says: ﴿And whoever does that, seeking the pleasure of God﴾, meaning: those things he mentioned, seeking His good pleasure, ﴿We will give him﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿a great reward.﴾ Abu Amr and Hamzah read ﴿We will give him﴾ with the ya', meaning: God will give him; the others read it with the nun.

The Qur'an, 4:115: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾. It was revealed concerning Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq. When the theft became known about him, he feared for himself the cutting off of his hand and public disgrace, so he fled to Makkah and apostatised from the religion. Then God the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾, meaning: opposes him, ﴿after guidance has become clear to him﴾, meaning the tawhid (the oneness of God) and the hudud (the prescribed punishments), ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ [i.e., other than the path of the believers], ﴿We will leave him in what he has turned to﴾, meaning: We will leave him to it in this world, ﴿and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾ [[Up to this point are the narrations whose chain of transmission has dropped out of manuscript (A); we have indicated the beginning of that in folio (94b).]] (96b)

It has been related that Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq stayed with a man of the Banu Sulaym from the people of Makkah called al-Hajjaj ibn Ulat. He breached the man's house, and a stone fell upon him, so he could neither enter nor leave until morning. He was then seized to be killed. Some of them said: "Leave him, for he has sought refuge with you." So they left him, and they expelled him from Makkah. He went out with merchants of Qudaah towards Syria. They halted at a station, and he stole some of their goods and fled. They pursued him, caught him, and stoned him to death, and his grave became that heap of stones. It is also said that he boarded a ship to Jeddah, stole a purse in it containing dinars, was caught, and was thrown into the sea. It is also said that he stayed in the valley of the Banu Sulaym, worshipped an idol until he died, and God the Exalted revealed concerning him:

﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with God has certainly gone far astray﴾, meaning: he has strayed from the path and been deprived of all good.

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit by Abu Hayyan, 3/351. Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. (49): it is munqati' (disconnected).]]: this verse was revealed concerning an old man of the Bedouins who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Prophet of God, I am an old man who has indulged in sins, but I have not associated anything with God since I came to know Him and believed in Him. I have not taken any protector besides Him, I have not committed acts of disobedience out of audacity toward God, and I have never imagined, even for the blink of an eye, that I could escape God by fleeing. Indeed I am remorseful, repentant, and seeking forgiveness. So what is my state?" Then God the Exalted revealed this verse.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 117–118:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They invoke none besides Him except females﴾. It was revealed concerning the people of Makkah, meaning: they worship nothing but. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And your Lord says: Call upon Me﴾ [Ghafir: 60], meaning: worship Me, as is shown by His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disdain My worship﴾ [Ghafir: 60]. His saying ﴿besides Him﴾ means besides Allah. ﴿Except females﴾: by "females" He meant idols, because they used to name them with the names of females. They would say: al-Lat, al-Uzza and Manat. Each tribe would say of its idol: "the female of the Banu so-and-so." In each of these females there was a devil who appeared to the custodians (al-sadana, the keepers of the idol shrines) and the soothsayers (al-kahana, the diviners) and spoke to them. For this reason He said: ﴿They invoke none but a devil﴾. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

What supports this interpretation, that by "females" idols are meant, is the recitation of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿They invoke besides Him none but uthunan﴾, the plural of plural of al-wathan (idol), with the waw changed into a hamza. [See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/210; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 1/288–289.]

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "Except females" means dead things with no soul in them, because their idols were inanimate objects. He called them "females" because one speaks of dead things in the feminine just as one speaks of females, and because females are the lesser of the two sexes, just as dead things are baser than living animals.

Al-Dahhak said: By "females" He meant the angels. Some of them worshipped the angels and said: "The angels are females," as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 19].

﴿But they invoke none but a rebellious devil﴾, meaning: they worship none but a rebellious devil, because when they worship idols they have obeyed the devil. Al-Marid is the one who is extremely rebellious (al-mariduh/al-mariid), the stubborn and insolent one who has gone out of obedience. What is meant is Iblis.

﴿Allah cursed him﴾, meaning: Allah removed him far from His mercy. ﴿And he said﴾, meaning: Iblis said: ﴿I will surely take from among Your servants a designated portion﴾, meaning: an appointed share. Whatever share of obedience Iblis is given from them is his designated portion. In some tafsir books it is said: "From every thousand, one is for Allah the Exalted and nine hundred and ninety-nine are for Iblis."

The root meaning of al-fard (designation, obligation) in the language is "cutting". From it comes al-furdah in a river, which is the breach that appears in it, and fard al-qaws (the notch of the bow) and al-shiraak (the strap), meaning the cut in which the string sits and the thread with which the strap is tied.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 119–123:

﴿And I will surely lead them astray﴾, meaning: from the truth, that is, "I will surely mislead them." Iblis says this, and he means adornment (tazyin). Otherwise, he has no share in misguidance, as he said: "I will surely make [evil] appealing to them on earth" [al-Hijr: 39]. ﴿And I will surely arouse their desires﴾. It was said: "I will arouse in them the desire to follow their passions." It was also said: "I will arouse in them the belief that there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no Resurrection." It was further said: "I will arouse in them the expectation of attaining the Hereafter while committing sins." ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely slit the ears of cattle﴾, that is, they will cut them and split them. This refers to the baheera (a she-camel whose ears were slit as a sign of dedication). ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Dahhak said: it means the religion of Allah. Its parallel is the statement of the Exalted: ﴿There is no alteration to the creation of Allah﴾ [al-Rum: 30], that is, to the religion of Allah. He intends the placing of Allah's ordinances in religion by making lawful what is unlawful and unlawful what is lawful.

'Ikrimah and a group of exegetes said: ﴿they will surely alter the creation of Allah﴾ by castration, tattooing, and cutting off ears, to the point that some of them prohibited castration, while others permitted it in animals, because it serves an obvious purpose. It was also said: altering the creation of Allah is that Allah, the Exalted, created cattle for riding and eating, but they made them forbidden; and He created the sun, the moon, and the stones for the benefit of the servants, but they worshipped them besides Allah. ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah﴾, that is, as a lord whom he obeys, ﴿has surely suffered a manifest loss﴾.

﴿He promises them and arouses their desires﴾. His promise and his arousing of desires are what he places in the heart of a person: long life and the attainment of worldly gain. It may also be by frightening him with poverty, so that he withholds him from spending and from maintaining family ties, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty﴾ [al-Baqarah: 268]. He also arouses their desires by convincing them that there is no Resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire. ﴿And Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾, that is, falsehood.

﴿Those—their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it﴾, that is, no flight and no way of turning away from it.

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾

That is, beneath the chambers and dwellings. ﴿They will abide therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture﴾, the verse. Masruq, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: He meant, "It is not by your wishful thinking, O Muslims, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture," meaning the Jews and the Christians. This is because they boasted, and the People of the Scripture said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our scripture came before your scripture, so we are more entitled to Allah than you." The Muslims said: "Our prophet is the seal of the prophets, and our scripture abrogates the [previous] books. We have believed in your scripture, but you have not believed in our scripture, so we are more entitled [to Allah]." [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/228–229; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 211–212.]]

Mujahid said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking﴾, O polytheists among the People of the Scripture. This is because they said: "There is no Resurrection and no reckoning," and the People of the Scripture said: "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days" [al-Baqarah: 80], and "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians" [al-Baqarah: 111]. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking﴾ [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/693.]], that is, the matter is not by wishful thinking; rather, the matter is by righteous deeds.

﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and a group said: the verse is general in regard to every doer [of deeds].

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not done evil except you? So what is the recompense?" He said: "Some of it occurs in this world. Whoever does a good deed has ten good deeds [credited to him]; and whoever is recompensed for an evil deed, one out of ten is subtracted, and nine good deeds remain for him. Woe to him whose single [bad deeds] outweigh his tens [good deeds]. As for what is recompensed in the Hereafter, his good deeds and evil deeds are weighed against each other, and he meets, in place of every evil deed, a good deed, and he looks at the surplus, and he is given the reward in Paradise, for Allah gives every person of merit his merit." [[This report is from the narration of al-Kalbi, whom the people of hadith abandoned because he was a liar; his biography was mentioned earlier in the introduction.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Abdusi narrated to us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Faqih narrated to us in Baghdad; Yahya ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zibriqan and al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to us, both saying: Rawh—that is, Ibn 'Ubadah—narrated to us; Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us; a client of Ibn Sabba' informed me: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar narrating from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when this verse was revealed to him: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper﴾." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?" I said: "Yes." So he recited it to me. He said: "I did not know except that I felt a breaking in my back, until I stretched out from it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, which of us has not done evil? Shall we indeed be recompensed for every evil we have done?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your fellow believers, you will be recompensed for that in this world until you meet Allah, and you will have no sins. It was said: "I will arouse in them the desire to follow their passions." It was also said: "I will arouse in them the belief that there is no Paradise, no Fire, and no Resurrection." It was further said: "I will arouse in them the expectation of attaining the Hereafter while committing sins." ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely slit the ears of cattle﴾, that is, they will cut them and split them. This refers to the baheera (a she-camel whose ears were slit as a sign of dedication). ﴿And I will surely command them, and they will surely alter the creation of Allah﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and al-Dahhak said: it means the religion of Allah. Its parallel is the statement of the Exalted: ﴿There is no alteration to the creation of Allah﴾ [al-Rum: 30], that is, to the religion of Allah. He intends the placing of Allah's ordinances in religion by making lawful what is unlawful and unlawful what is lawful.

'Ikrimah and a group of exegetes said: ﴿they will surely alter the creation of Allah﴾ by castration, tattooing, and cutting off ears, to the point that some of them prohibited castration, while others permitted it in animals, because it serves an obvious purpose. It was also said: altering the creation of Allah is that Allah, the Exalted, created cattle for riding and eating, but they made them forbidden; and He created the sun, the moon, and the stones for the benefit of the servants, but they worshipped them besides Allah. ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a guardian instead of Allah﴾, that is, as a lord whom he obeys, ﴿has surely suffered a manifest loss﴾.

﴿He promises them and arouses their desires﴾. His promise and his arousing of desires are what he places in the heart of a person: long life and the attainment of worldly gain. It may also be by frightening him with poverty, so that he withholds him from spending and from maintaining family ties, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Satan threatens you with poverty﴾ [al-Baqarah: 268]. He also arouses their desires by convincing them that there is no Resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire. ﴿And Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾, that is, falsehood.

﴿Those—their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it﴾, that is, no flight and no way of turning away from it.

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾

That is, beneath the chambers and dwellings. ﴿They will abide therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture﴾, the verse. Masruq, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: He meant, "It is not by your wishful thinking, O Muslims, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Scripture," meaning the Jews and the Christians. This is because they boasted, and the People of the Scripture said: "Our prophet came before your prophet, and our scripture came before your scripture, so we are more entitled to Allah than you." The Muslims said: "Our prophet is the seal of the prophets, and our scripture abrogates the [previous] books. We have believed in your scripture, but you have not believed in our scripture, so we are more entitled [to Allah]." [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/228–229; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 211–212.]]

Mujahid said: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking﴾, O polytheists among the People of the Scripture. This is because they said: "There is no Resurrection and no reckoning," and the People of the Scripture said: "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days" [al-Baqarah: 80], and "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians" [al-Baqarah: 111]. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking﴾ [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/693.]], that is, the matter is not by wishful thinking; rather, the matter is by righteous deeds.

﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and a group said: the verse is general in regard to every doer [of deeds].

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, which of us has not done evil except you? So what is the recompense?" He said: "Some of it occurs in this world. Whoever does a good deed has ten good deeds [credited to him]; and whoever is recompensed for an evil deed, one out of ten is subtracted, and nine good deeds remain for him. Woe to him whose single [bad deeds] outweigh his tens [good deeds]. As for what is recompensed in the Hereafter, his good deeds and evil deeds are weighed against each other, and he meets, in place of every evil deed, a good deed, and he looks at the surplus, and he is given the reward in Paradise, for Allah gives every person of merit his merit." [[This report is from the narration of al-Kalbi, whom the people of hadith abandoned because he was a liar; his biography was mentioned earlier in the introduction.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-'Abdusi narrated to us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Sulayman al-Faqih narrated to us in Baghdad; Yahya ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zibriqan and al-Harith ibn Muhammad narrated to us, both saying: Rawh—that is, Ibn 'Ubadah—narrated to us; Musa ibn 'Ubaydah narrated to us; a client of Ibn Sabba' informed me: I heard 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar narrating from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when this verse was revealed to him: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper﴾." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu Bakr, shall I not recite to you a verse that was revealed to me?" I said: "Yes." So he recited it to me. He said: "I did not know except that I felt a breaking in my back, until I stretched out from it." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you, which of us has not done evil? Shall we indeed be recompensed for every evil we have done?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "As for you, O Abu Bakr, and your fellow believers, you will be recompensed for that in this world until you meet Allah, and you will have no sins. As for others, it will be accumulated for them until they are recompensed on the Day of Resurrection." [[A sound hadith by its routes and corroborations. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir of Surah al-Nisa: 8/401–402, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; there is discussion regarding its isnad. Musa ibn 'Ubaydah is weak in hadith; Yahya ibn Sa'id and Ahmad ibn Hanbal criticized him. The client of Ibn Sabba' is unknown. This hadith has been narrated from Abu Bakr by other than this route, and it has no sound isnad either." Also on this subject is a report from 'A'ishah, and al-Marwazi in Musnad Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, no. 20, pp. 58–59. Another route is narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/181; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/373; Ibn Hibban declared it sound, no. 1734, p. 429 of Mawarid al-Zam'an, from 'A'ishah; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 3/74, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/249–250. See also Kanz al-'Ummal: 1/380–381; and al-Albani's Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifah: 3/686. It is also established from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: When [the verse] "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it" was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be close [to the right course] and aim for correctness, for in every affliction that a Muslim suffers there is an expiation, even the thorn that pricks him or the setback he suffers." Narrated by Muslim in al-Birr wal-Silah, chapter on the reward of the believer for what afflicts him of hardship..., no. 2574: 4/1993.]]

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged even a naqir (a speck)﴾. That is, the measure of a naqir, which is the small pit that is on the back of a date-stone. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far, the people of Basra and Abu Bakr read ﴿yudkhalūna﴾ with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatḥah on the khā' here, and in Surat Maryam and Ḥā Mīm (al-Mu'min). Abu 'Amr added "yudkhalūnahā" in Surat Fāṭir. The others read it with a fatḥah on the yā' and a ḍammah on the khā'.

Al-A'mash narrated from Abu al-Ḍuḥā, from Masruq, who said: When the verse ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ was revealed, the People of the Book said: "We and you are equal." So this verse was revealed: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds...﴾ to the end of the verse.[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 9 / 228 - 229.]] And also revealed was:

﴿And who is better in religion﴾ (that is, more sound in religion) ﴿than one who submits his face to Allah﴾ (that is, sincerely directs his deed to Allah). It was said: he entrusts his affair to Allah. ﴿while he is a doer of good﴾ (that is, a monotheist). ﴿and follows the religion of Abraham﴾ (meaning the religion of Abraham, upon him be peace), ﴿as a ḥanīf﴾ (that is, a Muslim, sincere).

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Among the religion of Abraham is praying toward the Ka'bah, circumambulating it, and the rites of the Hajj." Abraham was singled out because he was accepted by all the nations. It was also said: because he was sent upon the religion of Abraham, and some things were added for him.

﴿And Allah took Abraham as a khalīl (close friend)﴾, meaning ṣafī (chosen). Khullah means the purity of affection. Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: Abraham, upon him be peace, was the father of guests. His dwelling was on the side of the road, and he hosted whoever passed by him of the people. A year of drought befell the people, and they gathered at the door of Abraham, upon him be peace, seeking food. Abraham's provisions came each year from a friend of his in Egypt. He sent his servants with camels to his khalīl (friend) in Egypt. His friend said to his servants: "If Abraham, upon him be peace, wanted it for himself, we would bear it for him; but the hardship that has befallen the people has also befallen us." So Abraham's messengers returned. They passed by a sandy plain and said: "If we load up some of this sand, so that people see that we have come with provisions—for we are ashamed to pass by them with our camels empty." So they filled those sacks with sand, easily. Then they came to Abraham and informed him, while Sarah was sleeping. Abraham was troubled on account of the people at his door, and his eyes overcame him, so he slept. Sarah woke up when the day had risen high, and said: "Glory be to Allah! Have the servants not come?" They said: "Yes." She said: "Did they not bring anything?" They said: "Yes." So she got up to the sacks and opened them, and behold, they were the finest, purest flour that could be. She ordered the bakers, and they baked and fed the people. Then Abraham woke up and smelled the scent of food, and said: "O Sarah, where is this from?" She said: "From your Egyptian friend." He said: "This is from your Friend, Allah." He said: "On that day Allah took him as a khalīl."[[This is from the narration of al-Kalbi, and it has been mentioned before that he is abandoned (matrūk) because of his lying.]] Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of khalīl is one in whose love there is no flaw (khalal). Khullah means friendship. He was called khalīl because Allah loved him and chose him. It was also said: it is from khallah, which means need, so he was called khalīl, that is, one in need of Allah. [Because he did not place his poverty and dependence except upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic.][[What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".]] The first view is more correct, because His words ﴿And Allah took Abraham as a khalīl﴾ imply friendship from both sides, and need cannot be conceived from both sides.

Abu al-Muẓaffar ibn Aḥmad al-Taymi narrated to us; Abu Muḥammad 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Uthmān ibn al-Qasim narrated to us; Khaythamah ibn Sulayman ibn Ḥaydarah al-Aṭrābulusi narrated to us; Abu Qilābah al-Raqqashi narrated to us; Bishr ibn 'Umar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Aḥwaṣ, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I were to take a khalīl, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a khalīl, but Abu Bakr is my brother and my companion, and Allah has indeed taken your companion as a khalīl."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Virtues of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), chapter "If I were to take a khalīl": 7 / 17, from Ibn 'Abbas, without his words "and Allah has indeed taken your companion as a khalīl"; and by Muslim in the Virtues of the Companions, chapter on the virtues of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, no. (2383): 4 / 1855; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4 / 77.]]
