Abu al-Muẓaffar ibn Aḥmad al-Taymi narrated to us; Abu Muḥammad 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Uthmān ibn al-Qasim narrated to us; Khaythamah ibn Sulayman ibn Ḥaydarah al-Aṭrābulusi narrated to us; Abu Qilābah al-Raqqashi narrated to us; Bishr ibn 'Umar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Aḥwaṣ, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If I were to take a khalīl, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a khalīl, but Abu Bakr is my brother and my companion, and Allah has indeed taken your companion as a khalīl."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Virtues of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), chapter "If I were to take a khalīl": 7 / 17, from Ibn 'Abbas, without his words "and Allah has indeed taken your companion as a khalīl"; and by Muslim in the Virtues of the Companions, chapter on the virtues of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, no. (2383): 4 / 1855; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4 / 77.]]

"His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing.﴾ That is: His knowledge encompasses all things."

The Qur'an verse: ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: "Allah gives you His ruling concerning them..."﴾ and so on. Al-Baghawi's commentary, Ma'alim al-Tanzil, on Surah 4, verse 127:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: Allah gives you His ruling concerning them﴾ and the rest of the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: This verse was revealed concerning the daughters of Umm Kujjah and their inheritance, and the story has already passed at the beginning of the surah. [See what came before, the explanation of His saying, "For men there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave" (verse 7) of Surah al-Nisa'.]

'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: It refers to the orphan girl who is in the guardianship of a man, and he is her guardian. He desires to marry her if she is beautiful and wealthy, offering less than the customary bridal gift (mahr). And if she is undesirable because of little wealth and beauty, he leaves her. In another narration: It refers to the orphan girl who is in the guardianship of a man, who has become her partner in his property. He desires to marry her because of her unattractiveness, and he dislikes that she should be married to someone else, lest that person share in his property. So he keeps her confined until she dies, and then he inherits from her. So Allah forbade them from this. [See al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, the chapter on "And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans": vol. 8, p. 239.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾, meaning: they seek information from you ﴿concerning women. Say: Allah gives you His ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book﴾. It is said that its meaning is: "and He gives you a ruling concerning what is recited to you." It is also said that its meaning is: "and We give you a ruling on what is recited to you," meaning: Allah gives you a ruling and His Book gives you a ruling concerning them. This is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And give the orphans their property﴾. His saying ﴿concerning the orphan women﴾: this is an idafah of a thing to itself, because He intended by "the orphans" the women. ﴿To whom you do not give﴾, meaning: you do not give them ﴿what has been prescribed for them﴾ of their bridal gift. ﴿And you desire to marry them﴾, meaning: in marrying them for their wealth and beauty, while offering less than their bridal gift. Al-Hasan and a group said: He meant that you do not give them their right of inheritance, because they used not to let women inherit. ﴿And you desire to marry them﴾, meaning: you refrain from marrying them because of their unattractiveness.

﴿And the weak among the children﴾: He means: and He gives you a ruling concerning the weak among the children, who are the young ones, that you give them their rights, because they used not to let young children inherit. He means what is recited to you in the matter of orphans from His saying: ﴿And give the orphans their property﴾,

meaning: by giving the rights of the young. ﴿And that you stand firm for the orphans in justice﴾, meaning: and He gives you a ruling concerning standing firm for the orphans in justice, with fairness regarding their bridal gifts and their inheritances. ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾, meaning: He will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 128:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾ to the end of the verse. It was revealed concerning Amrah, and it is said concerning Khawlah [[In A: (Khuwaylah).]] daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah, and concerning her husband Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' (and it is said Rafi' ibn Khadij). He married her when she was young, but when old age overtook her, he married another young woman over her and gave her preference, and he neglected the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslamah. So she came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and complained to him, and this verse was revealed concerning her [[See: al-Muwatta' of Imam Malik, Kitab al-Nikah, Bab Jami' al-Nikah: 2/548-549; al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 2/308; Ahkam al-Qur'an of al-Shafi'i: 1/205; al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi: 7/296; Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/275; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. (178).]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: There was a man who had a wife who had grown old, and he had children from her. He wanted to divorce her and marry another woman in her place. She said: "Do not divorce me; leave me to look after my children, and give me your turn every two months if you wish, and if you wish, do not give me a turn." He said: "If that is acceptable, then it is more beloved to me." Then he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, so Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears﴾ [[Similar in meaning from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim. See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. (175-176); al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/710-711.]], meaning: she knew, ﴿from her husband﴾, meaning: from her husband, ﴿ill-treatment﴾, meaning: hatred. Al-Kalbi said: it means abandoning her bed. ﴿Or aversion﴾, by turning his face away from her and reducing his sitting with her. ﴿There is no blame upon the two of them﴾, meaning: upon the husband and the wife, ﴿that they make terms of settlement between themselves﴾, meaning: that they reconcile. The people of Kufa read ﴿that they set things right﴾ from aslaha. ﴿A settlement, and settlement is best﴾, meaning: concerning the division (of nights) and maintenance. It is that the husband says to her: "You have advanced in years, and I wish to marry a young, beautiful woman, and I will prefer her over you in the division, by night and by day. If you are content with this, then remain; and if you dislike it, I will release you." If she is content, then she is the one who does good, and she is not compelled to this. But if she is not content, and he withholds from her her right of division, then it is incumbent upon the husband to give her her right of division and maintenance, or to release her with kindness. If he keeps her and fulfills her right despite her dislike, then he is a doer of good.

Sulayman ibn Yasar said concerning this verse, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): If she makes terms with him concerning some of her right of division and maintenance, then that is permissible so long as she is content. If she then denies it after the settlement, that is her right, and she still has her entitlement [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/712.]].

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said concerning this verse: it is that a man has an older woman under him, and he marries a young woman over her, and he says to the older one: "I will give you a portion of my wealth on condition that I divide more for this young woman than I divide for you," and she is content with what they agreed upon. But if she refuses to be content, then he must act justly between them in the division.

From Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning this verse, he said: A woman is with a man, and his eye turns away from her because of ugliness or old age, and he dislikes separation from her. If she gives him some of her wealth, it is lawful for him; and if she gives him some of her days, it is lawful for him [[Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabari. See: al-Tabari: 9/268-269; Ibn Kathir: 1/564.]].

﴿And settlement is best﴾, meaning: her remaining after his offering her the choice. Reconciling by her giving up some of her right of division and maintenance is better than separation. As it is narrated that Sawdah (may Allah be pleased with her) was an elderly woman, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to part from her. She said: "Do not divorce me; I only ask that I be raised up among your wives, and I have given my turn to Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her)." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept her, and he would divide for Aisha her day and the day of Sawdah (may Allah be pleased with her) [[See the Tabaqat of Ibn Sa'd: 8/53, 169. It is established that Sawdah gave her day to Aisha, as narrated by al-Bukhari in the Nikah, Bab al-Mar'ah Tahib Yawmaha min Zawjiha li-Darratiha: 9/312, and Muslim in al-Radha', Bab Jawaz Hibatiha Nawbatiha li-Darratiha, no. (1462): 2/1085, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/152.]].

His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And souls are present with stinginess﴾, meaning: the stinginess of each of the spouses regarding their share from the other. Stinginess (shuhh) is the worst form of miserliness, and its reality is greed in withholding good. ﴿And if you do good﴾, meaning: set things right, ﴿and guard yourselves﴾ against injustice. It was said: this is addressed to the husbands, meaning: if you do good by remaining with her despite her dislike, and guard against wronging her, ﴿then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾, so He will recompense you for your deeds.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 129:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives﴾, meaning: you will never be able to make equal between wives in love and the inclination of the heart. ﴿And even if you should strive﴾ toward justice, ﴿do not incline completely [away]﴾, meaning: toward the one you love, ﴿in [giving] total inclination﴾ in the division (of nights) and maintenance, meaning: do not let your desires dictate your actions, ﴿and leave her as if suspended﴾, meaning: so that you leave the other as if hanging, neither a widow nor a married woman. Qatadah said: "As if imprisoned." In the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "as if she were imprisoned" (kaannaha masjunah).

It is narrated from Abu Qilabah that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to divide (his time) among his wives, and he would be just, and he would say: "O Allah, this is my division in what I control, so do not blame me for what You control and I do not control." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Nikah, chapter on dividing among wives: 3/63-64, from ʿAʾishah; al-Tirmidhi in al-Nikah, chapter on what has come concerning equality among co-wives: 4/294; al-Nasa'i in ʿIshrat al-Nisa', chapter on a man's inclination toward some of his wives over others: 7/63-64; Ibn Majah in al-Nikah, chapter on dividing among wives, no. (1971): 1/633 (sic); Ibn Hibban authenticated it, no. (1305), p. 317 of Mawarid al-Zaman; al-Hakim authenticated it according to the condition of Muslim: 2/187, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; al-Darimi in al-Nikah, chapter on division among wives: 2/144. See also: Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/151. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i mentioned that it was transmitted as mursal, and al-Tirmidhi said that the mursal version is more authentic.]] Some of them narrated it from Abu Qilabah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Yazid, from ʿAʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) as a connected (muttasil) chain.

It is narrated from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever has two wives and inclines toward one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of him leaning." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the same place: 3/63; al-Tirmidhi in the same place: 4/295; al-Nasa'i in the same place: 7/63; Ibn Majah, same place, no. (1969): 1/633; al-Darimi: 2/143; Ibn Hibban authenticated it (1307), p. 317. al-Tirmidhi said: "We do not know it as marfu' except from the hadith of Hammam." al-Hakim authenticated it according to the condition of the two Shaykhs: 2/186. It is strange that the publisher of the new edition of al-Baghawi said on p. 487 of the first volume: "I have not found anyone among the imams of hadith who narrated it except al-Baghawi!!"]]

﴿And if you amend [your conduct] and fear Allah﴾ regarding injustice, ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance.﴾ That is, the husband and the wife through divorce. ﴿Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾ means from His provision: He will give the woman another husband and the husband another wife. ﴿And Allah is ever All-Encompassing, All-Wise.﴾ He is abounding in bounty and mercy, and wise in what He commands and forbids.

The ruling of the verse as a whole: if a man has two or more wives, it is obligatory for him to treat them equally in the turn (qasm, the allotted division of nights). If he fails to treat them equally in carrying out this turn, he disobeys Allah the Exalted, and he must make up the turn for the wronged wife. Equality is a condition regarding spending the night (al-baytutah). As for intercourse, it is not required, because it depends on desire, and that is not within his control. If he has a free wife and a slave wife, he spends two nights with the free wife and one night with the slave wife. If he marries a new wife while he has older wives, he gives the new wife exclusive time: seven consecutive nights if she is a virgin (bikr), or three nights if she is a previously married woman (thayyib). After that he treats all of them equally. He is not required to make up these nights for the older wives.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi related to us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us; Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil related to us; Yusuf ibn Rashid related to us; Abu Usamah related to us; Sufyan al-Thawri related to us, from Ayyub and Khalid, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "It is from the Sunnah that when a man marries a virgin in addition to a previously married woman, he stays with her seven nights and then divides his time equally. And when he marries a previously married woman, he stays with her three nights and then divides his time equally." Abu Qilabah said: "And if I wished, I could say that Anas raised it to the Prophet (ﷺ)."

[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Marriage, chapter "If he marries a virgin over a previously married woman," 9/313, and by Muslim in the Book of Suckling, chapter "The amount of time a virgin and a previously married woman are entitled to the husband's stay after the wedding," no. 1461, 2/1084. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 9/155.]

When a man intends to travel for a need, he may take some of his wives with him after drawing lots among them. He is not then obligated to make up the nights for the remaining wives during the period of his journey, however long it lasts, provided that his stay in his own town does not exceed the period of travelers. The evidence for this is what ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal related to us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm related to us, al-Rabiʿ related to us, al-Shafiʿi related to us, my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Shafiʿ related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah, from ʿAisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), that she said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to travel, he drew lots among his wives, and whichever wife's lot came out, he took her with him." But when he intended a journey of relocation, he had no right to single out some of them, neither by lot nor otherwise.

[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Gifts, chapter "A woman's gift to someone other than her husband and her manumission when she has a husband...," 5/218, and by Muslim in the Book of Repentance, chapter "On the hadith of the slander and the acceptance of the repentance of the slanderer," no. 2770, 4/2130. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah, 9/153.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 131–132:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ — as slaves and as possessions. ﴿We had already enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ — meaning: the People of the Torah and the Gospel and the rest of the earlier nations in their books — ﴿and [also] you﴾ — the People of the Qur'an in your Book — ﴿to fear Allah﴾ — that is: affirm the oneness of Allah and obey Him. ﴿But if you disbelieve﴾ in what Allah has enjoined upon you — ﴿then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. It was said: indeed, for Allah there are angels in the heavens and the earth who are more obedient to Him than you are. ﴿And Allah is ever Free of need﴾ — independent of all His creation, not in need of their obedience — ﴿Praiseworthy﴾ — praised for His blessings.

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾. ʿIkrimah related from Ibn ʿAbbas: that is, "a witness that there are slaves in them." And it was said: "a protector and one who grants refuge."

If it is asked: what is the benefit of repeating His saying, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾? It is answered: each of the two has its own purpose. As for the first, its meaning is: to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He enjoins you to piety, so accept His injunction. As for the second, it says: indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever Free of need, i.e., He is the Free of need and to Him belongs the dominion, so seek from Him what you seek. As for the third, it says: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, i.e., to Him belongs the dominion, so take Him as your Disposer and do not rely upon anyone else.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 131–132:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ — as slaves and as possessions. ﴿We had already enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ — meaning: the People of the Torah and the Gospel and the rest of the earlier nations in their books — ﴿and [also] you﴾ — the People of the Qur'an in your Book — ﴿to fear Allah﴾ — that is: affirm the oneness of Allah and obey Him. ﴿But if you disbelieve﴾ in what Allah has enjoined upon you — ﴿then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾. It was said: indeed, for Allah there are angels in the heavens and the earth who are more obedient to Him than you are. ﴿And Allah is ever Free of need﴾ — independent of all His creation, not in need of their obedience — ﴿Praiseworthy﴾ — praised for His blessings.

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾. ʿIkrimah related from Ibn ʿAbbas: that is, "a witness that there are slaves in them." And it was said: "a protector and one who grants refuge."

If it is asked: what is the benefit of repeating His saying, ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾? It is answered: each of the two has its own purpose. As for the first, its meaning is: to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He enjoins you to piety, so accept His injunction. As for the second, it says: indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever Free of need, i.e., He is the Free of need and to Him belongs the dominion, so seek from Him what you seek. As for the third, it says: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, i.e., to Him belongs the dominion, so take Him as your Disposer and do not rely upon anyone else.

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (133–135)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ ("If He wills, He will take you away"), meaning: He will destroy you. ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ ("O people"), meaning: the disbelievers. ﴿وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ ("and bring others"), meaning: others other than you, better than you and more obedient. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ ("and Allah is Able to do that"), meaning: capable.

﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ ("Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter"). It means: whoever intends by his deed some worldly gain and does not intend by it Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah gives him from the worldly gain, or repels from him in this world what Allah wills, but he has no reward in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the reward of the Hereafter, Allah gives him from this world what he loves and rewards him with Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾ ("And Allah is ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah"). It means: be those who stand firm in bearing witness with justice, that is, with fairness, for Allah. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Be those who stand firm in justice in testimony concerning whoever it is against. ﴿وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾ ("even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives") refers to kinship ties. That is: speak the truth even if it is against yourselves, by confession, or against parents and relatives. So establish it against them for the sake of Allah. Do not show favour to the rich because of his wealth, nor have mercy on the poor because of his poverty. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ ("whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of them both"), that is, from you. Establish it against the one testified against, even if he is rich, and for the one testified for, even if he is poor, for Allah is more worthy of both than you. That is, leave their affair to Allah. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that Allah knows best about them both. ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ ("So do not follow desire, lest you deviate"), that is, lest you act unjustly and incline toward falsehood away from the truth. It has also been said: its meaning is, do not follow desire in order that you be just, that is, in order that you be just, as it is said: "Do not follow your desire in order to please your Lord."

﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ ("And if you distort"), that is, you distort the testimony so as to nullify the truth. ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ ("or turn away") from it, so that you conceal it and do not establish it. It is also said: "talwu" means you obstruct in establishing the testimony; it is said: "lawaytuhu haqqahu" when you push him away from his right and delay him. It has also been said: this is addressed to the rulers, concerning their twisting of the lips; it means: "and if you twist," that is, incline toward one of the two litigants or turn away from him. Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read ﴿تَلُوُوا﴾ with a damma on the lam. It has been said: its origin is "talwu," then one of the two waws was deleted for lightness. It has also been said: its meaning is, "and if you neglect the duty of giving testimony or turn away, so you abandon giving it." ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ ("then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").

﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ (140)

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (133–135)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ ("If He wills, He will take you away"), meaning: He will destroy you. ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ ("O people"), meaning: the disbelievers. ﴿وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ ("and bring others"), meaning: others other than you, better than you and more obedient. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ ("and Allah is Able to do that"), meaning: capable.

﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ ("Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter"). It means: whoever intends by his deed some worldly gain and does not intend by it Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah gives him from the worldly gain, or repels from him in this world what Allah wills, but he has no reward in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the reward of the Hereafter, Allah gives him from this world what he loves and rewards him with Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾ ("And Allah is ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah"). It means: be those who stand firm in bearing witness with justice, that is, with fairness, for Allah. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Be those who stand firm in justice in testimony concerning whoever it is against. ﴿وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾ ("even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives") refers to kinship ties. That is: speak the truth even if it is against yourselves, by confession, or against parents and relatives. So establish it against them for the sake of Allah. Do not show favour to the rich because of his wealth, nor have mercy on the poor because of his poverty. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ ("whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of them both"), that is, from you. Establish it against the one testified against, even if he is rich, and for the one testified for, even if he is poor, for Allah is more worthy of both than you. That is, leave their affair to Allah. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that Allah knows best about them both. ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ ("So do not follow desire, lest you deviate"), that is, lest you act unjustly and incline toward falsehood away from the truth. It has also been said: its meaning is, do not follow desire in order that you be just, that is, in order that you be just, as it is said: "Do not follow your desire in order to please your Lord."

﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ ("And if you distort"), that is, you distort the testimony so as to nullify the truth. ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ ("or turn away") from it, so that you conceal it and do not establish it. It is also said: "talwu" means you obstruct in establishing the testimony; it is said: "lawaytuhu haqqahu" when you push him away from his right and delay him. It has also been said: this is addressed to the rulers, concerning their twisting of the lips; it means: "and if you twist," that is, incline toward one of the two litigants or turn away from him. Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read ﴿تَلُوُوا﴾ with a damma on the lam. It has been said: its origin is "talwu," then one of the two waws was deleted for lightness. It has also been said: its meaning is, "and if you neglect the duty of giving testimony or turn away, so you abandon giving it." ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ ("then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").

﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ (140)

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (133–135)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ ("If He wills, He will take you away"), meaning: He will destroy you. ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ ("O people"), meaning: the disbelievers. ﴿وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ ("and bring others"), meaning: others other than you, better than you and more obedient. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ ("and Allah is Able to do that"), meaning: capable.

﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ ("Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter"). It means: whoever intends by his deed some worldly gain and does not intend by it Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah gives him from the worldly gain, or repels from him in this world what Allah wills, but he has no reward in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the reward of the Hereafter, Allah gives him from this world what he loves and rewards him with Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾ ("And Allah is ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah"). It means: be those who stand firm in bearing witness with justice, that is, with fairness, for Allah. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Be those who stand firm in justice in testimony concerning whoever it is against. ﴿وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾ ("even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives") refers to kinship ties. That is: speak the truth even if it is against yourselves, by confession, or against parents and relatives. So establish it against them for the sake of Allah. Do not show favour to the rich because of his wealth, nor have mercy on the poor because of his poverty. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ ("whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of them both"), that is, from you. Establish it against the one testified against, even if he is rich, and for the one testified for, even if he is poor, for Allah is more worthy of both than you. That is, leave their affair to Allah. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that Allah knows best about them both. ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ ("So do not follow desire, lest you deviate"), that is, lest you act unjustly and incline toward falsehood away from the truth. It has also been said: its meaning is, do not follow desire in order that you be just, that is, in order that you be just, as it is said: "Do not follow your desire in order to please your Lord."

﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ ("And if you distort"), that is, you distort the testimony so as to nullify the truth. ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ ("or turn away") from it, so that you conceal it and do not establish it. It is also said: "talwu" means you obstruct in establishing the testimony; it is said: "lawaytuhu haqqahu" when you push him away from his right and delay him. It has also been said: this is addressed to the rulers, concerning their twisting of the lips; it means: "and if you twist," that is, incline toward one of the two litigants or turn away from him. Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read ﴿تَلُوُوا﴾ with a damma on the lam. It has been said: its origin is "talwu," then one of the two waws was deleted for lightness. It has also been said: its meaning is, "and if you neglect the duty of giving testimony or turn away, so you abandon giving it." ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ ("then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").

﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ (140)

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (133–135)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ ("If He wills, He will take you away"), meaning: He will destroy you. ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ ("O people"), meaning: the disbelievers. ﴿وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ ("and bring others"), meaning: others other than you, better than you and more obedient. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ ("and Allah is Able to do that"), meaning: capable.

﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ ("Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter"). It means: whoever intends by his deed some worldly gain and does not intend by it Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah gives him from the worldly gain, or repels from him in this world what Allah wills, but he has no reward in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the reward of the Hereafter, Allah gives him from this world what he loves and rewards him with Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾ ("And Allah is ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah"). It means: be those who stand firm in bearing witness with justice, that is, with fairness, for Allah. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Be those who stand firm in justice in testimony concerning whoever it is against. ﴿وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾ ("even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives") refers to kinship ties. That is: speak the truth even if it is against yourselves, by confession, or against parents and relatives. So establish it against them for the sake of Allah. Do not show favour to the rich because of his wealth, nor have mercy on the poor because of his poverty. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ ("whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of them both"), that is, from you. Establish it against the one testified against, even if he is rich, and for the one testified for, even if he is poor, for Allah is more worthy of both than you. That is, leave their affair to Allah. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that Allah knows best about them both. ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ ("So do not follow desire, lest you deviate"), that is, lest you act unjustly and incline toward falsehood away from the truth. It has also been said: its meaning is, do not follow desire in order that you be just, that is, in order that you be just, as it is said: "Do not follow your desire in order to please your Lord."

﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ ("And if you distort"), that is, you distort the testimony so as to nullify the truth. ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ ("or turn away") from it, so that you conceal it and do not establish it. It is also said: "talwu" means you obstruct in establishing the testimony; it is said: "lawaytuhu haqqahu" when you push him away from his right and delay him. It has also been said: this is addressed to the rulers, concerning their twisting of the lips; it means: "and if you twist," that is, incline toward one of the two litigants or turn away from him. Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read ﴿تَلُوُوا﴾ with a damma on the lam. It has been said: its origin is "talwu," then one of the two waws was deleted for lightness. It has also been said: its meaning is, "and if you neglect the duty of giving testimony or turn away, so you abandon giving it." ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ ("then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").
