﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").

﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ (140)

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (133–135)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ ("If He wills, He will take you away"), meaning: He will destroy you. ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ ("O people"), meaning: the disbelievers. ﴿وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ ("and bring others"), meaning: others other than you, better than you and more obedient. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ ("and Allah is Able to do that"), meaning: capable.

﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ ("Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter"). It means: whoever intends by his deed some worldly gain and does not intend by it Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah gives him from the worldly gain, or repels from him in this world what Allah wills, but he has no reward in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the reward of the Hereafter, Allah gives him from this world what he loves and rewards him with Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾ ("And Allah is ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah"). It means: be those who stand firm in bearing witness with justice, that is, with fairness, for Allah. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Be those who stand firm in justice in testimony concerning whoever it is against. ﴿وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾ ("even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives") refers to kinship ties. That is: speak the truth even if it is against yourselves, by confession, or against parents and relatives. So establish it against them for the sake of Allah. Do not show favour to the rich because of his wealth, nor have mercy on the poor because of his poverty. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ ("whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of them both"), that is, from you. Establish it against the one testified against, even if he is rich, and for the one testified for, even if he is poor, for Allah is more worthy of both than you. That is, leave their affair to Allah. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that Allah knows best about them both. ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ ("So do not follow desire, lest you deviate"), that is, lest you act unjustly and incline toward falsehood away from the truth. It has also been said: its meaning is, do not follow desire in order that you be just, that is, in order that you be just, as it is said: "Do not follow your desire in order to please your Lord."

﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ ("And if you distort"), that is, you distort the testimony so as to nullify the truth. ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ ("or turn away") from it, so that you conceal it and do not establish it. It is also said: "talwu" means you obstruct in establishing the testimony; it is said: "lawaytuhu haqqahu" when you push him away from his right and delay him. It has also been said: this is addressed to the rulers, concerning their twisting of the lips; it means: "and if you twist," that is, incline toward one of the two litigants or turn away from him. Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read ﴿تَلُوُوا﴾ with a damma on the lam. It has been said: its origin is "talwu," then one of the two waws was deleted for lightness. It has also been said: its meaning is, "and if you neglect the duty of giving testimony or turn away, so you abandon giving it." ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ ("then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").

﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ (140)

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ (133–135)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنْ يَشَأْ يُذْهِبْكُمْ﴾ ("If He wills, He will take you away"), meaning: He will destroy you. ﴿أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ ("O people"), meaning: the disbelievers. ﴿وَيَأْتِ بِآخَرِينَ﴾ ("and bring others"), meaning: others other than you, better than you and more obedient. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ قَدِيرًا﴾ ("and Allah is Able to do that"), meaning: capable.

﴿مَنْ كَانَ يُرِيدُ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا فَعِنْدَ اللَّهِ ثَوَابُ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ ("Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter"). It means: whoever intends by his deed some worldly gain and does not intend by it Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah gives him from the worldly gain, or repels from him in this world what Allah wills, but he has no reward in the Hereafter. Whoever intends by his deed the reward of the Hereafter, Allah gives him from this world what he loves and rewards him with Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾ ("And Allah is ever All-Hearing, All-Seeing").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُونُوا قَوَّامِينَ بِالْقِسْطِ شُهَدَاءَ لِلَّهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah"). It means: be those who stand firm in bearing witness with justice, that is, with fairness, for Allah. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Be those who stand firm in justice in testimony concerning whoever it is against. ﴿وَلَوْ عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَوِ الْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ﴾ ("even if it be against yourselves or parents and close relatives") refers to kinship ties. That is: speak the truth even if it is against yourselves, by confession, or against parents and relatives. So establish it against them for the sake of Allah. Do not show favour to the rich because of his wealth, nor have mercy on the poor because of his poverty. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَاللَّهُ أَوْلَى بِهِمَا﴾ ("whether he is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of them both"), that is, from you. Establish it against the one testified against, even if he is rich, and for the one testified for, even if he is poor, for Allah is more worthy of both than you. That is, leave their affair to Allah. Al-Hasan said: its meaning is that Allah knows best about them both. ﴿فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا الْهَوَى أَنْ تَعْدِلُوا﴾ ("So do not follow desire, lest you deviate"), that is, lest you act unjustly and incline toward falsehood away from the truth. It has also been said: its meaning is, do not follow desire in order that you be just, that is, in order that you be just, as it is said: "Do not follow your desire in order to please your Lord."

﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ ("And if you distort"), that is, you distort the testimony so as to nullify the truth. ﴿أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾ ("or turn away") from it, so that you conceal it and do not establish it. It is also said: "talwu" means you obstruct in establishing the testimony; it is said: "lawaytuhu haqqahu" when you push him away from his right and delay him. It has also been said: this is addressed to the rulers, concerning their twisting of the lips; it means: "and if you twist," that is, incline toward one of the two litigants or turn away from him. Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read ﴿تَلُوُوا﴾ with a damma on the lam. It has been said: its origin is "talwu," then one of the two waws was deleted for lightness. It has also been said: its meaning is, "and if you neglect the duty of giving testimony or turn away, so you abandon giving it." ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾ ("then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do").

﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ (136)

Allah's words: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger"), and the verse. Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Asad and Usayd, the two sons of Ka'b, Tha'labah ibn Qays, Salam ibn Ukht 'Abdullah ibn Salam, Salamah ibn Akhihi, and Yamin ibn Yamin. These were believers among the People of the Book, who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "We believe in you and in your Book, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and 'Uzayr, and we disbelieve in what is other than that of the books and messengers." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Rather, believe in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and the Qur'an, and in Musa and the Tawrah, and in every Book before it." So Allah revealed this verse. [Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/716; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 178–179.] ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ ("O you who believe"), in Muhammad ﷺ, the Qur'an, Musa (peace be upon him) and the Tawrah, ﴿آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ ("believe in Allah and His Messenger"), Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي نَزَلَ عَلَى رَسُولِهِ﴾ ("and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger"), meaning the Qur'an, ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ ("and the Book which He revealed before"), from the Tawrah, the Injil, the Zabur and the rest of the books. [In the margin of the Zahiriyyah manuscript (A) the following appears: It is permissible that by His words "O you who believe" is meant the time of the covenant, when they said: "Yes," "believe" now "in Allah and His Messenger," and so on.]

The readers Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿نُزِّلَ وَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with a damma on the nun and the alif. The others read ﴿نَزَلَ وَأَنْزَلَ﴾ with a fatha, meaning: Allah sent down.

﴿وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ ("And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, then he has strayed far astray"). When this verse was revealed, they said: "Then we believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Qur'an, and every messenger and book that came before the Qur'an, and the angels and the Last Day. We do not differentiate between any one of them, and we are Muslims to Him." Al-Dahhak said: it means the Jews and the Christians. It says: "O you who believe" in Musa and 'Isa, "believe" in Muhammad and the Qur'an. Mujahid said: it means the hypocrites; it says: O you who believe with the tongue, believe with the heart. Abu al-'Aliyah and a group said: this is addressed to the believers; it says: "O you who believe, believe," that is, persist and remain firm in faith, as one says to someone standing: "Stand until I return to you," meaning, remain standing. It has also been said: what is meant is the people of polytheism, that is: "O you who believe" in al-Lat and al-'Uzza, "believe" in Allah and His Messenger.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ (137) ﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ (138) ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ (139)

Allah's words: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ آمَنُوا ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ ("Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief"). Qatadah said: they are the Jews. They believed in Musa, then disbelieved after him by worshipping the calf, then they believed in the Tawrah, then they disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him), then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has been said: this applies to all the People of the Book: they believed in their prophet, then disbelieved in him, and believed in the Book revealed to him, then disbelieved in it; their disbelief in it is their abandoning it. Then they increased in disbelief toward Muhammad ﷺ.

It has also been said: this concerns a people who apostatised: they believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised, then believed, then apostatised.

Regarding such a person, is his repentance accepted? It is reported from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that his repentance is not accepted, rather he is to be killed, based on Allah's words: ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ ("Allah would not forgive them"). But most scholars hold that his repentance is accepted. Mujahid said: "Then increased in disbelief" means they died upon it. ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ means: as long as they persisted in that. ﴿وَلَا لِيَهْدِيَهُمْ سَبِيلًا﴾ ("nor would He guide them to a way"), that is, a path to the truth. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿لَمْ يَكُنِ اللَّهُ لِيَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ﴾ when it is known that He does not forgive shirk if it was the first time? It is answered: its meaning is that when a disbeliever embraces Islam for the first time and remains upon it, his previous disbelief is forgiven him. But if he embraces Islam, then disbelieves, then embraces Islam, then disbelieves, his previous disbelief is not forgiven him, which would have been forgiven had he persisted in Islam.

﴿بَشِّرِ الْمُنَافِقِينَ﴾ ("Give good tidings to the hypocrites"): inform them, O Muhammad, ﴿بِأَنَّ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا﴾ ("that for them is a painful punishment"). Al-bushra is every news that changes the appearance of the face, whether pleasing or not. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: put in place of your good tidings to them the punishment, as you say to an Arab: "Your greeting is the blow, and your reproach is the sword," that is, in place of your greeting, your destruction.

Then He described the hypocrites, saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّخِذُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ ("Those who take the disbelievers as allies"), meaning: they take the Jews as allies, helpers, or confidants ﴿مِنْ دُونِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَيَبْتَغُونَ عِنْدَهُمُ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them?"), that is, support and victory over Muhammad ﷺ and his companions. It has also been said: do they seek with them strength and dominance? ﴿فَإِنَّ الْعِزَّةَ﴾ ("Indeed, honour"), that is, dominance, strength and power, ﴿لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا﴾ ("belongs entirely to Allah").

﴿وَقَدْ نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الْكِتَابِ أَنْ إِذَا سَمِعْتُمْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ يُكْفَرُ بِهَا وَيُسْتَهْزَأُ بِهَا فَلَا تَقْعُدُوا مَعَهُمْ حَتَّى يَخُوضُوا فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ إِنَّكُمْ إِذًا مِثْلُهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَامِعُ الْمُنَافِقِينَ وَالْكَافِرِينَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ جَمِيعًا﴾ (140)

﴿And it has already been revealed to you in the Book﴾. ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read "نَزَّلَ" with a fatḥah on the nūn and the zāy, meaning "Allah has revealed." The others read "نُزِّلَ" with a ḍammah on the nūn and a kasrah on the zāy, meaning "it has been revealed to you, O assembly of Muslims." ﴿That when you hear the signs of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked﴾: "the signs of Allah" means the Qur'an. ﴿Do not sit with them﴾: that is, with those who mock, ﴿until they engage in talk other than that﴾: that is, until they turn to talk other than mocking Muhammad ﷺ and the Qur'an. This refers to what Allah revealed in Surat al-Anʿām: "And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in talk other than that" [al-Anʿām: 68].

Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both: every innovator in the religion (muḥdith) and every person who introduces innovation (mubtadiʿ) until the Day of Resurrection is included in this verse. ﴿Indeed, you would then be like them﴾: that is, if you sit with them while they engage in vain talk and mockery and you are content with it, then you are disbelievers like them. If they engage in talk other than that, there is no harm in sitting with them, though it is disliked. Ḥasan said: sitting with them is not permissible even if they engage in talk other than that, because of Allah's saying: "And if Satan causes you to forget, do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people" [al-Anʿām: 68]. Most scholars hold the first view. The verse of al-Anʿām is Meccan and this verse is Medinan, and the later revelation takes precedence. ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers together in Hell, all of them﴾.

﴿Those who wait for you﴾ [they await the turns of fortune for you], [[The text between the brackets is omitted from manuscript (a).]] meaning the hypocrites. ﴿If there is a victory for you from Allah﴾: meaning success and spoils. ﴿They say﴾ to you, ﴿"Were we not with you?"﴾ in your religion in jihad; we were with you, so give us a share of the spoils. ﴿And if the disbelievers have a share﴾: meaning a turn of fortune and dominance over the Muslims. ﴿They say﴾: meaning the hypocrites say to the disbelievers, [98/b] ﴿"Did we not gain mastery over you?"﴾. Istiḥwādh (istiḥwādh, gaining control) means seizing control and dominance. Allah says: "Satan has gained mastery over them" [al-Mujādila: 19], meaning he took control and prevailed. They say: "Did we not inform you of the weak points of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions, and make you aware of their secrets?"

al-Mubarrad said: the hypocrites say to the disbelievers, "Did we not overcome you in your opinion?" ﴿And protect you﴾ and turn you away, ﴿from the believers﴾: that is, from entering into their community. It was also said: the meaning is, "Did we not gain control over you by supporting you, and protect you from the believers?" That is, we ward off from you the assault of the believers by discouraging them from you and by sending you news of their affairs and matters. The hypocrites' purpose in these words is to display favor over the disbelievers.

﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection﴾: meaning between the people of faith and the people of hypocrisy. ﴿And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾. ʿAlī said: this refers to the Hereafter. ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it means proof (ḥujjah). It was also said: it means dominance over the companions of the Prophet ﷺ.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 142–143:**

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, but it is He who deceives them.﴾ That is, they treat Him as one treats those who deceive, while He is the One who deceives them, meaning He requites them for their deception. They will be given a light on the Day of Resurrection just as the believers are, so the believers will proceed with their light over the Sirat (the bridge laid over Hell), while the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished. ﴿And when they stand up to prayer﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿they stand up lazily﴾, that is, reluctantly, not intending Allah by it. If anyone sees them, they pray; otherwise they leave and do not pray. ﴿They show off to the people﴾, that is, they do this to be seen by the people, not in obedience to the command of Allah. ﴿And they remember Allah only a little.﴾ Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) and al-Hasan said: He only said this because they perform it out of riya' (showing off, ostentation) and sum'ah (seeking to be heard of). Had they intended by that little the Face of Allah, the Exalted, it would have been much. Qatadah said: The remembrance of the hypocrites is little because Allah, the Exalted, does not accept it, and whatever Allah accepts is abundant.

﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those.﴾ That is, they are hesitant and perplexed between disbelief and faith, ﴿belonging neither to these nor to those﴾: they are not among the believers, so that what is due to the believers is due to them, nor are they among the disbelievers, so that what is taken from disbelievers is taken from them. ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way﴾, that is, a path to guidance.

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us, he said: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna informed us, Abd al-Wahhab, that is al-Thaqafi, informed us, Abdullah ibn Umar informed us, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is like the likeness of a lone sheep wandering between two flocks of sheep: it goes to this one at one time and to that one at another time." [Related by Muslim in Sifat al-Munafiqin (Attributes of the Hypocrites), no. (2784): 4/2146.]

If anyone sees them, they pray; otherwise they leave and do not pray. ﴿They show off to the people﴾, that is, they do this to be seen by the people, not in obedience to the command of Allah. ﴿And they remember Allah only a little.﴾ Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) and al-Hasan said: He only said this because they perform it out of riya' (showing off, ostentation) and sum'ah (seeking to be heard of). Had they intended by that little the Face of Allah, the Exalted, it would have been much. Qatadah said: The remembrance of the hypocrites is little because Allah, the Exalted, does not accept it, and whatever Allah accepts is abundant.

﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those.﴾ That is, they are hesitant and perplexed between disbelief and faith, ﴿belonging neither to these nor to those﴾: they are not among the believers, so that what is due to the believers is due to them, nor are they among the disbelievers, so that what is taken from disbelievers is taken from them. ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will never find for him a way﴾, that is, a path to guidance.

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us, he said: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna informed us, Abd al-Wahhab, that is al-Thaqafi, informed us, Abdullah ibn Umar informed us, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is like the likeness of a lone sheep wandering between two flocks of sheep: it goes to this one at one time and to that one at another time." [Related by Muslim in Sifat al-Munafiqin (Attributes of the Hypocrites), no. (2784): 4/2146.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 144–147:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers.﴾ Allah forbade the believers from allying themselves with the disbelievers, and said: ﴿Do you want to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾ That is, a clear proof for punishing you. Then He mentioned the states of the hypocrites, and said, glorified is His remembrance:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire.﴾ The people of Kufa recited ﴿fi al-darki﴾ (in the depth) with the letter rā' (ر) vowelled with a sukun, while the rest read it with a fatḥa. Both are dialectal variants, like al-ẓa'n and al-ẓa'an, and al-nahr and al-nahar. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: ﴿in the lowest depth﴾ means in coffins of iron, locked, in the Fire. Abu Hurairah said: it is a locked house in which the Fire blazes above them and below them. ﴿And you will not find for them a helper﴾ meaning a protector from the punishment.

﴿Except those who repent﴾ from hypocrisy, and believe, ﴿and amend﴾ their deeds, ﴿and hold fast to Allah﴾ and trust in Allah, ﴿and make their religion sincerely for Allah﴾. He meant sincerity of the heart, because hypocrisy is disbelief of the heart, so its removal occurs through sincerity of the heart. ﴿Those will be with the believers.﴾ Al-Farra' said: that is, among the believers. ﴿And Allah will give the believers in the Hereafter a great reward﴾, meaning Paradise. The yā' is omitted in the writing from ﴿yu'ti Allah﴾ because it drops in pronunciation, and it drops in pronunciation because of the sukun on the lām in "Allah".

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?﴾ That is, if you are grateful for His blessings ﴿and believe﴾ in Him. There is an inversion in it, its meaning being: if you believe and are grateful, because gratitude does not benefit without belief. This is an interrogative in the sense of affirmation, its meaning: He does not punish the believing grateful one, for His punishing His servants does not increase His dominion, and His leaving off punishing them for their deeds does not diminish His authority. Gratitude is the opposite of disbelief, and disbelief is the concealment of a blessing, while gratitude is its manifestation. ﴿And Allah is Ever Appreciative and Knowing﴾. So gratitude from Allah, may He be exalted, is His being content with the little from His servants and multiplying the reward for it, and gratitude from the servant is obedience, and from Allah it is reward.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 148–149:

His saying: ﴿Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged﴾. He means: Allah does not like the public utterance of ugly speech except by one who has been wronged. So it is permissible for the wronged person to inform about the wrongdoer's injustice and to invoke curse upon him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿But whoever retaliates after being wronged, those—there is no path [of blame] against them﴾ [al-Shura: 41]. Al-Hasan said: His supplication against him is that he says, "O Allah, help me against him; O Allah, extract my right from him." It was also said: If he is insulted, it is permissible for him to insult in return with the like of it, without exceeding it.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kharaqi informed us, Abu al-Hasan al-Taysafuni told us, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari told us, Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani told us, 'Ali ibn Hujr told us, Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, al-'Ala' ibn 'Abd al-Rahman told us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two who revile each other—what they say falls upon the one who started, so long as the wronged one does not transgress."[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Birr wa'l-Sila, Bab al-Nahy 'an al-Sibab, no. (2587): 4/2000; also narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad p. (127), and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/133.]]

Mujahid said: This applies to the guest who comes to a people and they do not host him nor treat him well; for him it is permissible to complain and to mention what was done to him. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi told us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf told us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il told us, Qutaybah ibn Sa'id told us, al-Layth told us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that he said: We said, "O Messenger of Allah, you send us out, and we alight among a people who do not host us. What do you think?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to us: "If you alight among a people and they provide you with what is due to a guest, accept it; but if they do not do so, then take from them the due right of the guest that is owed by them."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Mazalim, Bab Qisas al-Mazlum idha wajad mal zalimihi 5/107–108, and in al-Adab; by Muslim in al-Luqatah, Bab al-Diyafah wa nahwiha, no. (1727): 3/1353; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/339.]]

Al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim and Zayd ibn Aslam recited: ﴿illa man zalama﴾ with a fatha on the ẓā' and the lām, meaning: "But the wrongdoer—publicly speak evil speech against him." It was also said that its meaning is: Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech, but the one who has been wronged may speak openly. The first reading is the well-known one. ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing﴾ of the supplication of the wronged, ﴿Knowing﴾ of the punishment of the wrongdoer.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an offense﴾: He means: a good deed; whoever does it, it is recorded for him as ten [good deeds], and if he intends it but does not do it, one good deed is recorded for him. This is His saying, ﴿or conceal it﴾. It was also said that what is meant by "good" is wealth: i.e., if you disclose charity that you give openly, or conceal it by giving it secretly, ﴿or pardon an offense﴾, that is, a wrong done to you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Powerful﴾, more worthy of overlooking [your faults] from you on the Day of Resurrection.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers﴾ to the end of the verse. It was revealed concerning the Jews, because they believed in Musa (peace be upon him), the Tawrat (Torah), and Uzayr, but disbelieved in Isa (peace be upon him), the Injil (Gospel), Muhammad, and the Qur'an. ﴿And they wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, and they say: "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and they wish to adopt a way between that﴾, meaning a religion between Judaism and Islam, and a creed they would follow.

﴿They are the disbelievers in truth﴾. He affirmed their disbelief so that it would be known that disbelief in some of them is like disbelief in all of them. ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾

﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾, all of them, ﴿and do not make a distinction between any of them﴾, meaning among the messengers, and they are the believers who say: "We do not distinguish between any of His messengers." ﴿Those, He will give them their rewards﴾ for their faith in Allah, His books, and His messengers. Hafs, on the authority of Asim, recited ﴿yu'tihim﴾ with a ya' (yāʾ, the third-person masculine prefix), meaning ﴿Allah will give them﴾, while the rest recited it with a nun (nūn, the first-person plural prefix). ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [[Omitted from (A).]]

The Almighty's saying: ﴿The People of the Scripture ask you﴾ to the end of the verse. This was because Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Finhas ibn Azura, from among the Jews, said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If you are a prophet, then bring us a book all at once from the heaven, just as Musa (peace be upon him) brought." So Allah revealed to him: ﴿The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven﴾. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/726; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 197.]]

This question from them was a question of dictation and proposal, not a question of submission, and Allah, the Exalted, does not send down signs according to the proposals of His servants. His saying: ﴿So they had asked Musa for greater than that﴾, meaning greater than that, referring to the seventy whom Musa (peace be upon him) took with him to the mountain. ﴿And they said: "Show us Allah openly"﴾, meaning face to face. Abu Ubayda said: its meaning is, they said openly, "Show us Allah." ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf﴾, meaning as a god, ﴿after the clear proofs had come to them, but We pardoned that﴾ and did not uproot them. It was said: this is an invitation to repentance; its meaning is that those who committed transgression repented, so We pardoned them; so you repent, and We will pardon you. ﴿And We gave Musa a clear authority﴾, meaning a manifest proof of miracles, and these are the nine signs.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers﴾ to the end of the verse. ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾, all of them, ﴿and do not make a distinction between any of them﴾, meaning among the messengers, and they are the believers who say: "We do not distinguish between any of His messengers." ﴿Those, He will give them their rewards﴾ for their faith in Allah, His books, and His messengers. The Almighty's saying: ﴿The People of the Scripture ask you﴾ to the end of the verse. This was because Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Finhas ibn Azura, from among the Jews, said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If you are a prophet, then bring us a book all at once from the heaven, just as Musa (peace be upon him) brought." So Allah revealed to him: ﴿The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven﴾. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/726; see also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 197.]]

This question from them was a question of dictation and proposal, not a question of submission, and Allah, the Exalted, does not send down signs according to the proposals of His servants. Surah 4, verses 158–159, in al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil):

﴿Nay, Allah raised him up to Himself.﴾ It has been said that his statement "certainly" (yaqinan) refers to what follows it. His statement ﴿And they did not kill him﴾ is a complete sentence, and its implied meaning is: "Nay, Allah raised him up to Himself, certainly." The pronoun in "they did not kill him" refers to Jesus, peace be upon him. Al-Farra' (may Allah have mercy on him) said: its meaning is, "They did not kill, with certainty, the one whom they thought was Jesus." It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) that its meaning is: "They did not kill their supposition with certainty." ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty﴾, unassailable in exacting retribution from the Jews, ﴿Wise﴾, who decreed curse and wrath upon them. So He empowered over them Dhaytus ibn Asbasyanus al-Rumi (the Roman), who killed among them a great slaughter.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death﴾. That is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in 'Isa (Jesus), peace be upon him." This is the view of the majority of the exegetes and scholars. Regarding His statement ﴿before his death﴾, they differed over the pronoun. 'Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it refers to the People of the Book (the individual Jew or Christian), and its meaning is: "There is not one of the People of the Book who will not believe in 'Isa, peace be upon him, before his death, when he falls into the calamity, at a time when his faith will not benefit him, whether he is burned, drowned, falls into a well, a wall falls on him, a beast of prey devours him, or he dies suddenly." This is a narration from Abu Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them). He said: It was said to Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father): "What if he falls from the top of a house?" He said: "He will speak it (the faith) in the air." He said: It was asked, "What if one of them has his neck struck?" He said: "His tongue will falter over it."

Another group held that the pronoun in "his death" (mawtihi) refers to 'Isa, peace be upon him. Its meaning is: "There is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in 'Isa before the death of 'Isa, peace be upon him. That will be at his descent from the heaven at the end of time, so that no one remains but he believes in him, until the religion (millah) becomes one, the religion of Islam."

We have also related from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Soon the son of Maryam (Mary) will descend among you as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah (poll tax), and wealth will overflow until no one accepts it, and all religions will perish in his time except Islam. He will kill the Dajjal (the Antichrist), then he will remain on earth for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him." Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death﴾," meaning "before the death of 'Isa ibn Maryam." Then Abu Hurayrah repeated it three times. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Anbiya', Bab Nuzul 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon them both): 6/490–491; and Muslim in Kitab al-Iman, Bab Nuzul 'Isa ibn Maryam hakiman bi-shari'ati nabiyyina Muhammad (ﷺ), no. (155): 1/135; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/80–81.]]

It is narrated from 'Ikrimah that the pronoun in His statement ﴿will surely believe in him﴾ refers to Muhammad (ﷺ). He says: no People of the Book dies until he believes in Muhammad (ﷺ).

It has also been said: the pronoun refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He says: "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, before his death, at the moment of seeing (the truth), when his faith will not benefit him."

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him, ﴿a witness﴾ that he had conveyed to them the message of his Lord, and that he acknowledged servitude to Him for himself [as Allah, exalted, said, informing about him: "And I was a witness over them while I remained among them" (al-Ma'idah: 117), and every prophet is a witness over his nation]. [[What is between the brackets is omitted from manuscript (b).]] Allah, exalted, said: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these?﴾ (al-Nisa': 41).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 160:

His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying: ﴿So for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews﴾, and this refers to what was mentioned earlier of their breaking the covenant (mithaq), their disbelief in the signs of Allah, their slander against Maryam (Mary), and their saying: "We killed the Messiah" ﴿We forbade them good things which had been made lawful for them﴾, and these are what was mentioned in Surat al-An'am [[See further on in the tafsir of the verse in Surat al-An'am.]], where He said: "And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws" [al-An'am: 146].

The structure (nazm) of the verse: "So for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews," which is what we have mentioned, ﴿and for their hindering many from the way of Allah﴾, meaning by turning away themselves and others, ﴿from the way of Allah, many [people]﴾, that is, from the religion of Allah, hindering many.

﴿And their taking of usury, although they had been forbidden from it﴾ in the Torah, ﴿and their devouring of people's wealth unjustly﴾ through bribery in judgment, and the gains they obtained from their common people. ﴿We punished them﴾ by forbidding them certain good things. So whenever they committed a major sin, some of the good things that had been lawful for them were forbidden to them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That was Our recompense to them for their transgression, and indeed We are truthful﴾ [al-An'am: 146]. ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.﴾

﴿But those firm in knowledge among them﴾ means: not all of the People of the Book are described by this attribute, but those firm (al-rasikhun, "the deeply rooted") in knowledge, the mature possessors of insight among them. By this he intends those scholars of the Jews who embraced Islam, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. ﴿And the believers﴾ means the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and the Helpers (al-Ansar). ﴿Believe in what has been revealed to you﴾ means the Qur'an, ﴿and what was revealed before you﴾ means the other revealed Books. ﴿And those who establish prayer﴾: they differed regarding its grammatical position (i'rab, the grammatical analysis of word endings). It is related from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and Aban ibn Uthman that this is a mistake by the scribe, and that it should have been written "wal-muqimun al-salah" (in the nominative). Similarly is His saying in Surat al-Ma'idah: "Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians" [al-Ma'idah: 69], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, these two are certainly magicians﴾ [Ta-Ha: 63]. They said: that is an error of the scribe. [[Imam Ibn Jarir al-Tabari (may Allah have mercy on him) refuted this view on several grounds, saying: "If that were an error of the scribe, it would have been necessary for every copy other than our codex, which the scribe who erred wrote for us, to differ from it. The agreement of our codex with the codex of Ubayy regarding this shows that what is in our codex is correct and not an error. Moreover, if this were an error in the writing, the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from whom the Qur'an was taken would not have taught those who learned it from the Muslims in a faulty way; they would have corrected it with their tongues and taught the Ummah the correct form. And the transmission of all Muslims of that as a recitation, exactly as it is written in the script, is the strongest proof of its soundness and correctness, and that the scribe had no part in it." Tafsir al-Tabari: 9/397-398, with the commentary of Shaykh Shakir. See also: al-Itqan by al-Suyuti: 2/320-321, edited by Muhammad Abu al-Fadl Ibrahim.]]

Uthman said: "There is a lahn (grammatical error) in the codex which the Arabs will correct with their tongues." It was said to him: "Will you not change it?" He said: "Leave it, for it does not make lawful what is forbidden, nor forbid what is lawful." [[Ibn al-Anbari said in his book "The Refutation of Those Who Oppose the Codex of Uthman": "The narrations transmitted from Uthman on this matter do not constitute a proof, because they are interrupted (munqati'ah) and not connected. Reason testifies that Uthman, who was the leader of the Ummah and the leader and model of the people in his time, gathered them upon the codex which is the reference (al-imam), would not see a flaw in it and observe a fault in its writing and then leave it uncorrected! No, by Allah, no one of fairness and discernment would suppose this of him. Nor does anyone believe that he deferred an error in the Book so that someone after him could correct it. The way of those who came after him is to follow its script and to stop at its ruling. Whoever claims that Uthman meant by his saying 'I see in it a lahn' that he saw in its writing a lahn which, when we recite it with our tongues, would be a lahn that does not corrupt or distort in terms of altering the words or spoiling the i'rab, has erred and is not correct, because the script indicates the pronunciation; whoever commits a lahn in writing commits one in speech. Uthman would not have deferred a corruption in the spelling of the words of the Qur'an, either in writing or in pronunciation. It is known that he was constantly studying the Qur'an and perfecting its words, and in agreement with what was written in the codices sent to the regions and provinces." See: al-Itqan fi Ulum al-Qur'an by al-Suyuti: 2/322.]]

It was also said: its position is in the genitive (khafd).

They differed regarding its analysis. Some of them said: its meaning is "But those firm in knowledge among them, and among those who establish prayer." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 163:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you﴾. This is a continuation of what preceded in His saying, "The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a Book from heaven" [An-Nisa 153]. When Allah mentioned their faults and sins, they became angry and denied everything that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had sent down, and they said: "Allah has not sent down anything to any human being." So there was revealed: "They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said, 'Allah has not sent down anything to a human being'" [Al-An'am 91]. And He revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾. So He mentioned a number of the messengers to whom He had revealed, and He began with the mention of Noah, peace be upon him, because he was the father of humanity, like Adam, peace be upon him. Allah Exalted said: ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾ [As-Saffat 77]. And also because he was the first prophet of the sacred law (shari'ah) and the first warner against polytheism, and the first whose nation was punished for rejecting his call, and the people of the earth were destroyed through his supplication. He was the longest-lived of the prophets, and his miracle was placed in his own self, for he lived a thousand years, yet no tooth of his fell out, no hair of his turned white, and no strength of his diminished. No prophet endured the harm of his people as patiently as he endured it over the length of his life.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We revealed to Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac and Jacob and the Tribes﴾, and they are the sons of Jacob, ﴿and Jesus and Job and Jonah and Aaron and Solomon, and We gave David the Psalms﴾. Al-A'mash and Hamzah read ﴿Zuburan﴾ [with a ḍammah on the zay wherever it occurs], meaning the plural of zabur, i.e., We gave David books and scrolls that were written (mazburah), that is, inscribed. The others read it with a fatḥah on the zay, and it is the name of the Book that Allah Exalted sent down to David, peace be upon him. It contained praise, glorification, and commendation of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. David would go out into the wilderness, stand, and recite the Zabur, and the scholars of the Children of Israel would stand with him, standing behind him, and the people would stand behind the scholars, and the jinn would stand behind the people, the greatest first and then the greatest, and the devils behind the jinn. The beasts that are in the mountains would come and stand before him in wonder at what they heard from him, and the birds would hover over their heads. When he committed the sin, he no longer saw that. It was said to him: "That was the intimacy of obedience, and this is the loneliness of disobedience."

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abu Bakr al-Jawzaqi informed us, Abu al-Abbas informed us, Yahya ibn Zakariyya informed us, al-Hasan ibn Hammad informed us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Umawi narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Yahya, from Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If only you had seen me last night while I was listening to your recitation; you have indeed been given one of the flutes of the family of David." He said: "As Allah is my witness, O Messenger of Allah, if I had known you were listening, I would have embellished it for you, embellished it." [Reported by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Qur'an, chapter on the beauty of voice in reciting the Qur'an: 9/92, and Muslim in Salat al-Musafirin, chapter on the recommendation of beautifying the voice with the Qur'an, no. (793): 1/546, both without Abu Musa's saying: "If I had known, I would have embellished it for you with embellishment." Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: 9/93, "Abu Ya'la also reported it through Sa'id ibn Abi Burdah from his father with an addition, mentioning the hadith and saying: 'As for me, if I had known your location, I would have adorned it for you with adornment.'"]

And when 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, saw him, he would say: "Remind us, O Abu Musa," and he would recite in his presence.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verse 164:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And messengers We have already related to you before﴾, meaning: and just as We revealed to Nuh and to the prophets after him. ﴿And messengers﴾ is in the accusative by the removal of the particle of attribution (ḥarf al-ṣifah). It was also said: its meaning is "and We related to you messengers." In the recitation of Ubayy it is read: "And messengers, We have already related them to you before." ﴿And messengers We have not related to you, and Allah spoke to Musa with direct speech﴾. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs call whatever reaches a person as speech (kalam) by whatever means it arrives, but they do not express it with the verbal noun (maṣdar) in its precise sense. When it is expressed with the verbal noun, and it is not the real meaning of speech, as with "will" (irada), one says: "So-and-so willed a willing (irada)," meaning the true sense of willing. And one says: "The wall wanted (arada)," but one does not say "it wanted a wanting (irada)," because that is a metaphorical usage and not the literal reality.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 165–167:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers.﴾ Then they would say: "You did not send us any messenger, and You did not send down to us any book." In it is evidence that Allah, the Exalted, does not punish creation before He sends a messenger. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a messenger﴾ [al-Isra: 15], ﴿And Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu Awanah informed us, Abd al-Malik informed us, from Warrad, the scribe of al-Mughirah, from al-Mughirah, who said: Sa'd ibn Ubadah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "If I saw a man with my wife, I would strike him with the sword without turning away." This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Do you marvel at the jealousy of Sa'd? By Allah, I am more jealous than he is, and Allah is more jealous than I am. Because of Allah's jealousy, He has forbidden indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden. No one loves excuse more than Allah does, and because of that He sent the warners and the bearers of good news. No one loves praise more than Allah does, and because of that He promised Paradise."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Tawhid, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), "There is no one more jealous than Allah," 13/399; and by Muslim in Kitab al-Li'an, no. (1499), 2/1136. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9/266–267.]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 9/409, from Ibn Abbas. See also Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 179.]] Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: The chiefs of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, we asked the Jews about you and about your description in their book, and they claimed that they do not recognize you." A group of Jews then entered upon him, and he said to them: "Indeed, by Allah, I know that you know that I am the Messenger of Allah." They said: "We do not know that." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾, meaning, even if they deny you and reject you, ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness, and Allah suffices as a witness.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and bar others from the way of Allah﴾, by concealing the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿have certainly strayed far astray.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 4, verses 168–171:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and do wrong﴾. It is said: he said "and did wrong" – although their wrongdoing is by their disbelief – for emphasis. It is also said: its meaning is they disbelieved in Allah and did wrong to Muhammad (ﷺ) by concealing his description. ﴿Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path﴾, meaning: the religion of Islam.

﴿Except the path of Hell﴾, meaning Judaism, ﴿abiding therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah﴾. This applies to those for whom His judgement has preceded that they will not believe.

﴿O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you﴾. Its implied meaning: "so believe, and belief will be better for you." ﴿And if you disbelieve, then indeed to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion﴾. It was revealed concerning the Christians, who are of several sects: the Ya'qubiyyah (Jacobites), the Malkaniyyah (Melkites), the Nestoriyyah (Nestorians) and the Marqusiyyah (Marcusians). The Ya'qubiyyah said: "Jesus is Allah." Likewise the Malkaniyyah. The Nestoriyyah said: "Jesus is the son of Allah." The Marqusiyyah said: "the third of three." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 218. For the sects of the Christians and their doctrines, see: Muhadarat fi al-Nasraniyyah by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Zahra, pp. 183–196.]].

It is also said: the Malkaniyyah say: "Jesus is Allah," the Ya'qubiyyah say: "the son of Allah," and the Nestoriyyah say: "the third of three." A man from the Jews called Bawlus (Paul) taught them this, and it will come in Surat al-Tawbah, Allah willing, the Exalted.

Al-Hasan said: It is possible that it was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians, for they both exceeded in the matter of Jesus: the Jews by belittling him, and the Christians by going beyond the limit. The origin of ghuluw (excess) is going beyond the limit, and in religion it is forbidden.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Do not commit excess in your religion﴾, do not be strict in your religion so that you invent lies against Allah. ﴿And do not say about Allah except the truth﴾, do not say that He has a partner and a son. ﴿The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was but a messenger of Allah and His word﴾, which is His saying "Be," and he became a human without a father, [and it is said other than this]. ﴿Which He directed to Mary﴾, meaning He informed her of it and told her, as it is said: "I conveyed to you a good word." ﴿And a soul from Him﴾. It is said: it is a soul like the other souls, except that Allah the Exalted attributed it to Himself as an honour.

(1616): 3/1234; and al-Musannif in Sharh as-Sunnah: 8/336–337.]]. The meaning of al-Kalalah and the ruling of the verse have already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah[[See above, the commentary on verse (12) of the surah.]].

In this verse is the explanation of the ruling on the inheritance of siblings, whether full siblings or paternal siblings.

His saying ﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾: i.e., they seek information from you and ask you. ﴿Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-Kalalah﴾. ﴿If a man dies leaving no child and has a sister, she receives half of what he left, and he inherits from her﴾: meaning, if the sister dies, all of her inheritance goes to the brother, ﴿if she has no child﴾. If she has a son, the brother receives nothing; and if her child is a daughter, the brother receives what remains after the daughters' prescribed share. ﴿If there are two sisters, they receive two-thirds of what he left﴾: he meant two or more, namely that whoever dies leaving sisters, they receive two-thirds. ﴿If there are brothers and sisters, men and women, the male receives the equivalent of the share of two females﴾. ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾. Al-Farra' and Abu Ubaydah, may Allah have mercy on them, said: its meaning is "lest you go astray" (i.e., "so that you do not go astray"). It was also said: its meaning is "Allah makes clear to you out of dislike that you go astray." ﴿And Allah is Knower of all things﴾.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abdullah an-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; Abdullah ibn Raja' informed us; Isra'il informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The last surah to be revealed in its entirety was Bara'ah, and the last verse to be revealed was the concluding verse of Surat an-Nisa: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-Kalalah﴾[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of Surat an-Nisa, chapter "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling...": 8/267; and Muslim in al-Fara'id, chapter on the last verse revealed, the verse of al-kalalah, no. (1618): 3/1236–1237.]]

It is also narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the last verse revealed was the verse on usury, and the last surah revealed was ﴿When the help of Allah comes and the victory﴾. It is also narrated from him that the last verse revealed was His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And fear a Day on which you will be returned to Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 281].

It is also narrated that after the revelation of Surat an-Nasr, the Prophet (ﷺ) lived for one year; and after it was revealed Surat Bara'ah, which is the last surah revealed in its entirety, the Prophet (ﷺ) lived six months after it. Then, on the road to the Farewell Pilgrimage, "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-Kalalah" was revealed, and it was called the verse of summer. Then, while he was standing at Arafat, "This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you" [al-Ma'idah: 3] was revealed, and he lived after it eighty-one days. Then the verses on usury were revealed, then "And fear a Day on which you will be returned to Allah" was revealed, and he lived after it twenty-one days[[See these reports and those who narrated them in: al-Itqan of al-Suyuti: 1/101–106.]].
